abuse-children-who-cannot-tell.en:
Imagine a four-year-old in a Pune day care who has started crying every afternoon at toilet time, or a 10-year-old boy with an intellectual disability who suddenly refuses to board the school bus and cannot say why. Neither has the words, or a listener who understands them. They are the least able to tell, but not too young to be targets: in 2024, police recorded 831 child victims of penetrative sexual assault under the age of six [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## The youngest numbers: 831 under six, 3,438 aged six to 12

Police counted 44,567 child victims of penetrative sexual assault under POCSO in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| Age of child | Victims, 2024 |
|---|---|
| Under 6 | 831 |
| 6 to 12 | 3,438 |
| 12 to 16 | 16,801 |
| 16 to 18 | 23,497 |

That is 4,269 children under 12 in one year. The rise with age does not mean small children are safer: a case enters the record only when an adult notices and reports it, and the youngest rarely disclose, so these are minimums. Boys make up a larger share of the recorded victims under 12 than of teenage victims [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## When a child cannot say it: signs in very young and non-verbal children

A toddler has no word for what happened, or for why it was wrong. A child who communicates through signs or pictures may have no way to describe it, and may depend on the person causing harm. The signs are in behaviour, measured against the child's normal.

Darkness to Light, a US child-protection nonprofit, notes that direct physical signs of sexual abuse are not common. More common are sleep problems and nightmares; unusual fear of certain people or places; regression such as bedwetting or thumb-sucking; sexual behaviour or knowledge beyond the child's age; and overly compliant behaviour [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]].

Without words, they show up as patterns: a toilet-trained three-year-old having accidents again, distress at bath time with one carer but not another, panic in one room or vehicle. Compliance deserves a second look in disabled children, who may be praised for doing exactly what adults say. Keep a dated note of what changed, with whom and where.

## Disabled children: dependence, missing words, families never told their rights

Disability adds barriers. A child who needs help to bathe, dress or use the toilet depends on adults for intimate care, so abuse can hide inside routine. A child who communicates differently may never have been taught words for private parts, or may not be understood. And families may never have been told what the law offers.

Human Rights Watch's 2018 report "Invisible Victims of Sexual Violence" documented 17 rape and gang-rape cases involving eight girls and nine women with disabilities [[hrw-invisible-victims-2018]]. In 16 of the 17, survivors and their families did not know about the disability-specific protections in POCSO or the 2013 criminal law amendments [[hrw-invisible-victims-2018]]. A right nobody explains is a right nobody can claim. Our investigation into disabled survivors goes further.

## What the law provides, and what to insist on

Learn these before you need them. This is general information, not legal advice.

- **A statement at home.** Under Section 24 of the POCSO Act, police must record a child's statement at home or a place of the child's choice, by an officer out of uniform (a woman, as far as practicable), must keep the child away from the accused, and may not hold a child at a police station at night [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].
- **Help to communicate.** Under the BNSS, when a survivor of rape or another listed sexual offence has a mental or physical disability, both the police complaint and the statement before a magistrate (as far as practicable a woman) must be recorded with an interpreter or special educator, on video. The statement before the magistrate counts as the survivor's examination-in-chief, so it need not be repeated at trial, though the survivor can be cross-examined on it [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **A child-friendly court.** In a POCSO trial, lawyers' questions go through the judge. The court must bar aggressive questioning and repeated testimony, shield the child from the accused with video links, one-way mirrors or curtains if needed, and sit in camera with a parent or trusted person present [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].
- **An offence for those with power.** Under Section 92(d) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, anyone in a position to dominate the will of a disabled child or woman who uses it to exploit her sexually faces six months to five years in prison and a fine [[gazette-rpwd-act-2016]]. Rape itself carries far heavier sentences.
- **Free treatment.** Every hospital, public or private, must treat a sexually assaulted child immediately and free of cost [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Safer routines at home, in school, in transport and day care

Safety is about access: who is alone with the child, and whether anyone would notice a change.

- **Give the child words.** Teach correct names for private parts early, in the child's own way of communicating: words, signs, pictures or a communication board, plus signs for "no" and "someone hurt me".
- **Keep intimate care to a few named adults,** and tell the child who they are. Say each step before you do it ("Now I'll wash your back"), so the child knows what normal care looks like.
- **Make "no secrets about bodies" a rule** for every adult, relatives included.
- **Ask day cares, schools and hostels** who helps children in the toilet, whether any adult is ever alone with a child, and whether parents can drop in unannounced. The head of an institution who fails to report abuse by staff can face up to a year in prison and a fine [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].
- **Know the van:** the driver and attendant by name, and whether your child is often the last one dropped.
- **Watch for change after any new adult:** a carer, tutor, therapist, driver or hostel warden.

If you notice signs, you need suspicion, not proof. Call the Child Helpline 1098 or 112 [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].
abuse-children-who-cannot-tell.hg:
Sochiye, Pune ke ek day care mein chaar saal ka ek bachcha har dopahar toilet ke waqt rone laga hai, ya intellectual disability wala 10 saal ka ek ladka achanak school bus mein chadhne se mana karne laga hai aur bata nahi paata ki kyun. Dono ke paas na shabd hain, na koi aisa sunne wala jo unhe samjhe. Yeh bachche sabse kam bata paate hain, lekin itne chhote nahi ki nishana na banein: 2024 mein police ne chhe saal se kam umar ke 831 bachchon ko penetrative sexual assault ke victims ke roop mein darj kiya [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Sabse chhote bachchon ke aankde: chhe se kam ke 831, chhe se 12 ke 3,438

2024 mein POCSO ke tahat police ne penetrative sexual assault ke 44,567 child victims gine [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| Bachche ki umar | Victims, 2024 |
|---|---|
| 6 se kam | 831 |
| 6 se 12 | 3,438 |
| 12 se 16 | 16,801 |
| 16 se 18 | 23,497 |

Yaani ek hi saal mein 12 se kam umar ke 4,269 bachche. Umar ke saath ginti badhti hai, lekin iska matlab yeh nahi ki chhote bachche zyada surakshit hain: koi case record mein tabhi aata hai jab koi adult dhyaan de aur report kare, aur sabse chhote bachche shayad hi kabhi batate hain, isliye yeh kam se kam ginti hai. 12 se kam umar ke darj victims mein ladkon ka hissa, teenage victims ke mukable zyada hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Jab bachcha bol hi na sake: bahut chhote aur non-verbal bachchon mein signs

Toddler ke paas na us cheez ke liye shabd hota hai jo hui, na yeh samajh ki woh galat thi. Jo bachcha signs ya pictures se baat karta hai, ho sakta hai uske paas yeh bataane ka koi tareeka na ho, aur woh usi insaan par nirbhar ho jo nuksaan pahuncha raha hai. Signs behaviour mein hote hain, aur unhe us bachche ke apne normal se milakar dekhna padta hai.

US ki child-protection nonprofit Darkness to Light kehti hai ki sexual abuse ke seedhe physical signs aam nahi hote. Zyada aam hain: neend ki problems aur bure sapne; kuch logon ya jagahon se ajeeb darr; chhoot chuki aadaton par laut jaana, jaise bistar geela karna ya angootha choosna; umar se aage ka sexual behaviour ya jaankari; aur had se zyada har baat maan lena [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]].

Bina shabdon ke yeh patterns ki tarah dikhte hain: toilet-trained teen saal ka bachcha phir se kapde geele karne lage, nahlate waqt ek carer ke saath pareshaan ho par doosre ke saath nahi, ya kisi ek kamre ya gaadi mein ghabra jaaye. Disabled bachchon mein har baat maan lene ko dobara dhyaan se dekhiye, kyunki ho sakta hai unhe isi baat ke liye shaabaashi milti ho ki woh adults ki har baat maante hain. Tareekh ke saath likhte rahiye ki kya badla, kiske saath aur kahan.

## Disabled bachche: nirbharta, shabdon ki kami, aur parivaar jinhe kabhi unke haq nahi bataye gaye

Disability nayi rukawatein jodti hai. Jis bachche ko nahane, kapde pehenne ya toilet jaane mein madad chahiye, woh intimate care ke liye adults par nirbhar hai, aur abuse rozmarra ki routine ke andar chhup sakta hai. Jo bachcha alag tareeke se baat karta hai, use shayad kabhi private parts ke liye shabd sikhaye hi na gaye hon, ya uski baat samjhi hi na jaaye. Aur ho sakta hai parivaar ko kabhi bataya hi na gaya ho ki kanoon kya deta hai.

Human Rights Watch ki 2018 ki report "Invisible Victims of Sexual Violence" ne rape aur gang-rape ke 17 cases document kiye, jinmein disabilities wali aath ladkiyan aur nau auratein thi [[hrw-invisible-victims-2018]]. 17 mein se 16 cases mein survivors aur unke parivaar POCSO ya 2013 ke criminal law amendments mein disability ke liye bane khaas protections ke baare mein nahi jaante the [[hrw-invisible-victims-2018]]. Jo haq koi samjhaata nahi, use koi maang bhi nahi sakta. Disabled survivors par hamari investigation is par aur gehraai se baat karti hai.

## Kanoon kya deta hai, aur kis baat par adey rahein

Zaroorat padne se pehle yeh jaan lijiye. Yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahi.

- **Ghar par statement.** POCSO Act ke Section 24 ke tahat police ko bachche ka statement uske ghar ya uski pasand ki jagah par record karna hoga, aise officer ke zariye jo uniform mein na ho (jahan tak ho sake, mahila officer). Bachche ko accused se door rakhna hoga, aur kisi bhi bachche ko raat mein police station mein roka nahi ja sakta [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].
- **Baat samajhne mein madad.** BNSS ke tahat, agar rape ya kisi aur listed sexual offence ke survivor ko mental ya physical disability hai, toh police complaint aur magistrate (jahan tak ho sake, mahila magistrate) ke saamne statement, dono interpreter ya special educator ki madad se aur video par record honge. Magistrate ke saamne record hua statement survivor ka examination-in-chief maana jaata hai, isliye use trial mein dobara dohrana nahi padta, haalaanki us par survivor se cross-examination ho sakta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Bachchon ke liye anukool court.** POCSO trial mein lawyers ke sawaal judge ke zariye poochhe jaate hain. Court ko aggressive sawaal aur baar-baar gawahi rokni hogi, zaroorat ho toh video link, one-way mirror ya parde se bachche ko accused se bachana hoga, aur sunwai in camera karni hogi, jahan parent ya koi bharose ka insaan maujood ho [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].
- **Taaqat wale logon ke liye alag offence.** Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 ke Section 92(d) ke tahat, jo bhi kisi disabled bachche ya aurat ki marzi par haavi hone ki position mein ho aur us position ka istemaal uske sexual exploitation ke liye kare, use chhe mahine se paanch saal tak ki jail aur jurmana ho sakta hai [[gazette-rpwd-act-2016]]. Rape ki saza khud isse kahin zyada sakht hai.
- **Muft ilaaj.** Har hospital, sarkari ho ya private, ko sexual assault jhelne wale bachche ka turant aur muft ilaaj karna hoga [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Ghar, school, transport aur day care mein safer routines

Hifaazat ka matlab hai pahunch par nazar: bachche ke saath akela kaun hota hai, aur kya kisi badlaav par kisi ka dhyaan jaayega.

- **Bachche ko shabd dijiye.** Private parts ke sahi naam jaldi sikhaiye, bachche ke apne baat karne ke tareeke mein: shabd, signs, pictures ya communication board, aur saath mein "na" aur "kisi ne mujhe dard diya" ke liye signs bhi.
- **Intimate care kuch chune hue adults tak rakhiye,** aur bachche ko bataiye ki woh kaun hain. Har step karne se pehle bataiye ("Ab hum peeth dhoyenge"), taaki bachcha jaane ki normal care kaisi hoti hai.
- **"Body ke baare mein koi secret nahi" ka rule** har adult par lagaiye, relatives par bhi.
- **Day care, school aur hostel se seedhe poochiye** ki toilet mein bachchon ki madad kaun karta hai, kya koi adult kabhi kisi bachche ke saath akela hota hai, aur kya parents bina bataye aa sakte hain. Jo institution head apne staff ke kiye abuse ki report nahi karta, use ek saal tak ki jail aur jurmana ho sakta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].
- **Van ko jaaniye:** driver aur attendant ko naam se jaaniye, aur dekhiye ki kya aapka bachcha aksar sabse aakhir mein utarta hai.
- **Kisi bhi naye adult ke aane ke baad badlaav par nazar rakhiye:** naya carer, tutor, therapist, driver ya hostel warden.

Agar aapko signs dikhein, toh yaad rakhiye: sabut nahi, shak kaafi hai. Child Helpline 1098 ya 112 par call kariye [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].

abuse-inside-the-family-incest.en:
Imagine a nine-year-old in a two-room home in Nagpur. The man abusing her is her mother's brother, who lives with them and pays part of the rent. To reach a police station, her story must get past her mother, who needs that rent, her grandmother, who will call it a family matter, and her own fear of breaking the house apart. In 2024, police recorded a family member as the accused in 3,658 cases of penetrative sexual assault on children, the POCSO Act's term for child rape [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Each got past a wall like that. This investigation is about the ones that did not.

## 8.3%: what the family-member column counts, and misses

NCRB's *Crime in India 2024* sorts the year's 44,126 child-rape cases under POCSO by who the accused was. Family members: 3,658, or 8.3%. Family friends, neighbours, employers and other known persons: 16,668. Friends, online friends and live-in partners: 22,308. Unknown or never identified: just 1,492 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Read the family row as a floor. It counts only FIRs, only penetrative assault (44,126 of the 69,191 POCSO cases), and each FIR once, under its most serious offence [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. It does not say which relative was accused, and it is not crossed with the age table, so nobody can tell how many of the 4,269 victims under 12 were abused at home.

A survey points further inside the house. In NFHS-5, never-married women aged 18 to 49 who had faced sexual violence most often named a relative other than a father or brother: 39% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Survey answers and police counts cannot be stacked, but in one relatives top the list, and in the other they fill fewer than one case in 10.

## Silence by design: dependence, honour and money

Under Sections 19 and 21 of POCSO, anyone who knows of a sexual offence against a child must report it to the police or the Special Juvenile Police Unit; failing to do so can mean up to 6 months in prison or a fine. A child is never punished for staying silent [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Outside the home, that rule turns teachers, doctors and neighbours into reporters. Inside it, the person who knows is often the accused's wife, mother, sister or adult son, each with reasons for silence that no law touches. He may be the only earner. The house may be in his name. The family's "honour", and its other children's marriage prospects, may be weighed against one child's safety. A mother who reports her husband can lose her home and her income in the same week.

The abuser at home also has what an outsider must work for: daily access, authority and the child's love. A child may not know it is abuse, or may fear that telling will break the family.

On paper, the relative who stays silent is committing an offence. In practice, a six-month penalty weighs little against losing a roof. What moves a family is support that makes reporting survivable.

## What the 2007 study found about trust and secrecy

The government's 2007 Study on Child Abuse surveyed 12,447 children in 13 states [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. It found that 50% of abusers were known to the child or in a position of trust and responsibility, and that most children told no one. Of the children who had been sexually assaulted, 72.1% had kept quiet; only 3.4% had gone to the police [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

Boys made up 52.94% of the children who reported sexual abuse [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. In 2024 police data, they were 892 of the 44,567 child victims of penetrative assault [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A boy abused by a male relative faces a double silence: about who did it, and about being a boy it happened to.

The sample was not random and predates POCSO, so treat its figures as signals. But its pattern, trust plus secrecy, is what abuse inside a family runs on.

## The law: an aggravated offence on paper

Under Section 64(2)(f) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), rape by a relative, guardian or teacher, or by anyone in a position of trust or authority, is aggravated, with 10 years up to imprisonment for the rest of natural life [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Under POCSO, which protects boys and girls alike, penetrative assault on a child under 16 carries at least 20 years, and aggravated penetrative assault at least 20 years up to natural life, or death. The Special Court must presume the accused committed the offence unless the contrary is proved [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

The procedure assumes the child can be kept apart from the accused. Police must record the child's statement at home or at a place of the child's choice, and make sure the child never comes into contact with the accused [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. When the accused shares that home, the promise holds only if someone moves him, or the child, out.

Then comes the wait. In 2024 the conviction rate for penetrative assault on children was 30.2%, and 1,70,455 such cases were pending trial at the end of the year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB does not publish how cases against relatives end. In them the key witnesses are often family too, and every month of waiting is another month to lean on them.

## What makes some families act

Police data cannot say why some families report and others do not. It does show that 3,658 times in 2024, someone got a case against a relative onto the record [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The reasons for silence are practical, and so are the answers the law already offers.

- **Money.** Compensation does not depend on a conviction. Under Section 396 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, a victim can apply to the Legal Services Authority even if no trial takes place, and the inquiry must end within two months [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Under NALSA's 2018 scheme for women and girls, the limits are 50% higher for a minor [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]].
- **A safe place.** Mission Vatsalya, the Centre's child-protection scheme since 2021-22, funds Child Welfare Committees, children's homes and family-based care [[mwcd-mission-vatsalya-guidelines-2022]].
- **Someone outside.** A teacher, doctor or neighbour has the same duty to report, and needs no one's permission. Child Helpline 1098 runs round the clock and is linked to the emergency number 112 [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].

It starts with the first adult the child tells. If that adult believes the child and acts, the silence breaks there.
abuse-inside-the-family-incest.hg:
Sochiye, Nagpur ke do kamron ke ek ghar mein rehne wali nau saal ki ek bachchi. Uska abuse karne wala uski maa ka bhai hai, jo unke saath rehta hai aur kiraye ka kuch hissa deta hai. Police station tak pahunchne ke liye uski baat ko kai deewarein paar karni hongi: maa, jise woh kiraya chahiye; naani, jo ise "ghar ka maamla" kahengi; aur khud uska darr ki ghar uski wajah se toot jayega. 2024 mein police ne bachchon par penetrative sexual assault ke 3,658 cases mein family member ko accused darj kiya. POCSO Act mein child rape ke liye yahi term hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Inmein se har case aisi hi ek deewar paar karke aaya. Yeh investigation un cases ke baare mein hai jo paar nahi kar paaye.

## 8.3%: family-member wala column kya ginta hai, aur kya chhod deta hai

NCRB ki *Crime in India 2024* report saal ke 44,126 POCSO child rape cases ko is hisaab se baantti hai ki accused kaun tha. Family members: 3,658, yaani 8.3%. Family friends, padosi, employer aur doosre jaan-pehchaan wale: 16,668. Dost, online dost aur live-in partners: 22,308. Anjaan, ya jinki pehchaan kabhi nahi ho payi: sirf 1,492 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Family wali row ko neeche ki seema samjhiye, poori ginti nahi. Yeh sirf FIR wale cases ginti hai, sirf penetrative assault (69,191 POCSO cases mein se 44,126), aur har FIR ko sirf ek baar, uske sabse gambhir offence ke under [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh nahi batati ki kaunsa rishtedaar accused tha. Aur yeh age wali table se cross nahi hoti, isliye koi nahi bata sakta ki 12 saal se kam umar ke 4,269 victims mein se kitnon ka abuse ghar ke kisi insaan ne kiya.

Ek survey ghar ke aur andar ki taraf ishara karta hai. NFHS-5 mein 18 se 49 saal ki unmarried auraton ne, jinhone sexual violence jheli thi, sabse zyada father ya brother ke alawa kisi aur rishtedaar ka naam liya: 39% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Survey ke jawab aur police ki ginti ko ek doosre ke upar rakh kar nahi dekha ja sakta. Lekin ek mein rishtedaar list mein sabse upar hain, aur doosre mein woh 10 mein se ek case bhi nahi bharte.

## Chuppi system mein hi bani hai: nirbharta, izzat aur paisa

POCSO ke Sections 19 aur 21 ke tahat, jise bhi kisi bachche ke khilaaf sexual offence ka pata ho, use police ya Special Juvenile Police Unit ko report karna hoga; report na karne par 6 mahine tak ki jail ya fine ho sakta hai. Chup rehne ke liye bachche ko kabhi saza nahi milti [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Ghar ke bahar, yeh rule teachers, doctors aur padosiyon ko reporter bana deta hai. Ghar ke andar, jise pata hota hai woh aksar accused ki biwi, maa, behen ya bada beta hota hai, aur har ek ke paas chup rehne ki aisi wajahein hoti hain jinhe koi law chhoota tak nahi. Ho sakta hai wahi akela kamane wala ho. Ghar uske naam par ho. Family ki "izzat" aur baaki bachchon ki shaadi ki fikr ko ek bachche ki safety ke saamne tola ja sakta hai. Jo maa apne pati ko report karti hai, woh ek hi hafte mein apna ghar aur apni income dono kho sakti hai.

Ghar ke abuser ke paas woh sab pehle se hota hai jiske liye kisi bahar wale ko mehnat karni padti hai: roz ka access, bachche par authority, aur bachche ka pyaar. Ho sakta hai bachche ko pata hi na ho ki yeh abuse hai, ya use darr ho ki batane se family toot jayegi.

Kaagaz par, jo rishtedaar jaan kar bhi chup rehta hai, woh offence kar raha hai. Asal zindagi mein, 6 mahine ki saza ka darr sar se chhat chhin jaane ke darr ke saamne halka pad jaata hai. Family ko jo cheez hilaati hai, woh dhamki kam aur aisa support zyada hai jisse report karne ke baad bhi zindagi chal sake.

## 2007 ki study ne trust aur secrecy ke baare mein kya paaya

Sarkar ki 2007 ki Study on Child Abuse ne 13 states ke 12,447 bachchon ka survey kiya [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Study ne paaya ki 50% abusers bachche ke jaan-pehchaan wale the ya trust aur zimmedari ki position mein the, aur zyadatar bachchon ne kisi ko nahi bataya. Jin bachchon ka sexual assault hua tha, unmein se 72.1% chup rahe; sirf 3.4% police tak gaye [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

Sexual abuse report karne wale bachchon mein 52.94% ladke the [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. 2024 ke police data mein, penetrative assault ke 44,567 child victims mein ladke sirf 892 the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jis ladke ka abuse kisi male rishtedaar ne kiya ho, use do chuppiyan todni padti hain: ek, ki kisne kiya; doosri, ki yeh ek ladke ke saath hua.

Study ka sample random nahi tha aur yeh POCSO se pehle ki hai, isliye iske figures ko signal samjhiye, aaj ka naap nahi. Lekin isne jo pattern dikhaya, yaani trust aur secrecy, family ke andar ka abuse usi par chalta hai.

## Law: kaagaz par aggravated offence

Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 64(2)(f) ke tahat, kisi rishtedaar, guardian ya teacher ka, ya trust ya authority ki position wale kisi bhi insaan ka kiya rape aggravated offence hai, jiski saza 10 saal se lekar baaki ki poori zindagi ki jail tak hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. POCSO ladkon aur ladkiyon dono ko barabar protect karta hai. Iske tahat 16 saal se kam umar ke bachche par penetrative assault ki saza kam se kam 20 saal hai, aur aggravated penetrative assault ki kam se kam 20 saal se lekar poori zindagi ki jail, ya maut ki saza. Special Court ko yeh maan kar chalna hota hai ki accused ne offence kiya hai, jab tak ulta saabit na ho [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Poora procedure is baat par tika hai ki bachche ko accused se alag rakha ja sakta hai. Police ko bachche ka statement ghar par ya bachche ki pasand ki jagah par record karna hota hai, aur pakka karna hota hai ki bachcha kabhi accused ke contact mein na aaye [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Jab accused usi ghar mein rehta ho, toh yeh vaada tabhi nibhta hai jab koi use, ya bachche ko, wahan se bahar le jaye.

Phir intezaar shuru hota hai. 2024 mein bachchon par penetrative assault ke cases mein conviction rate 30.2% tha, aur saal ke end mein aise 1,70,455 cases trial ke intezaar mein the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB yeh publish nahi karta ki rishtedaaron ke khilaaf cases ka kya anjaam hota hai. In cases mein zaroori gawah aksar family ke hi log hote hain, aur intezaar ka har mahina unpar dabaav daalne ka ek aur mahina ban jaata hai.

## Kuch families kadam kyun uthaati hain

Police data yeh nahi bata sakta ki kuch families report kyun karti hain aur baaki kyun nahi. Lekin yeh zaroor dikhata hai ki 2024 mein 3,658 baar kisi ne kisi rishtedaar ke khilaaf case record par laaya [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Chup rehne ki wajahein practical hain, aur law mein pehle se maujood jawab bhi utne hi practical hain.

- **Paisa.** Compensation conviction par depend nahi karta. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita ke Section 396 ke tahat, victim Legal Services Authority mein apply kar sakta hai, chahe trial ho hi na, aur inquiry do mahine ke andar khatam honi chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. NALSA ki 2018 ki scheme mein, jo auraton aur ladkiyon ke liye hai, minor victim ke liye limits 50% zyada hain [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]].
- **Ek safe jagah.** Mission Vatsalya, jo 2021-22 se Centre ki child protection scheme hai, Child Welfare Committees, children's homes aur family-based care ko fund karti hai [[mwcd-mission-vatsalya-guidelines-2022]].
- **Koi bahar wala.** Teacher, doctor ya padosi par bhi report karne ki wahi duty hai, aur unhe kisi ki permission nahi chahiye. Child Helpline 1098 din-raat chalti hai aur emergency number 112 se judi hai [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].

Shuruaat us pehle adult se hoti hai jise bachcha batata hai. Agar woh bachche ka yakeen kare aur kadam uthaye, toh chuppi wahin toot jaati hai.

abuser-in-the-family-what-to-do.en:
Imagine a mother in Ranchi. Her 11-year-old daughter tells her, in pieces, that her father comes into her room at night. He earns the family's only income, and his mother lives with them. Everything this woman has been taught says: keep it inside the house. In 2024, police recorded a family member as the accused in 3,658 of the 44,126 POCSO cases of penetrative sexual assault on children, or 8.3% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Each of those cases needed an adult who put the child first. This guide is for that adult, whether the child is a girl or a boy. It is general information, not legal advice.

## The first hours: believe, separate, keep the child safe

Believe the child, and say so: "I believe you. It is not your fault. You did right to tell me." Do not ask for details, do not make the child repeat it to relatives, and do not confront the accused in front of the child. A confrontation warns him and gives him a chance to pressure the child.

Then make sure the child does not spend another night where he can reach them. If he will not leave, take the child to someone who is on the child's side: your own parents, a sibling, a friend. If there is nowhere to go, or the child is in danger now, call 1098, the Child Helpline [[wcd-childline]], or 112; the two are linked [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].

If the abuse was recent or the child is hurt, go to a hospital. Every hospital, government or private, must treat the child immediately and free of cost, and must inform the police [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Reporting a relative: your duty and the child's protection

There is no family exception. Under Sections 19 and 21 of POCSO, anyone who knows of child sexual abuse must report it to the police or the Special Juvenile Police Unit, and failing to report can mean up to 6 months in prison or a fine. Police must then inform the Child Welfare Committee and the Special Court within 24 hours [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

The law is built to keep the child apart from the accused. The child's statement must be recorded at home or at a place the child chooses, by an officer out of uniform, a woman officer where practicable. Police must make sure the child never comes into contact with the accused, and no child may be kept at a police station at night [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. If the accused lives in your home, tell the police the statement must be taken somewhere else.

Relatives may say you are destroying a man's life. The law sees it differently. Rape by a relative or guardian is an aggravated offence under Section 64(2)(f) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, carrying 10 years up to imprisonment for the rest of natural life [[indiacode-bns-2023]], and under POCSO, penetrative assault on a child under 16 carries at least 20 years [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. The stakes for him are high, which is why the pressure on you will be too.

## Family pressure, 'compromise' and bail

Pressure can come as pleading ("he has said sorry"), money ("we will pay for her studies") or threats ("you will be on the street"). Write down every offer and threat, with the date and who made it, and give it to the investigating officer and the Special Public Prosecutor.

Do not accept a "compromise". In Aparna Bhat v. State of Madhya Pradesh (18 March 2021), the Supreme Court struck down a bail condition that required a man accused of sexual assault to ask the complainant to tie a rakhi on him. It ruled that bail conditions must not require or permit contact between the accused and the victim, and that courts must not suggest compromise or marriage [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]].

Use that ruling. When the accused applies for bail, tell the prosecutor that he lives in the same house as the child, and ask for conditions that keep him away from the child and the home. If he is accused of raping a girl under 16 under Section 65 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, he cannot get anticipatory bail [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. If he breaks a condition, or anyone pushes the child to change the statement, report it the same day.

## If home is not safe: alternative care

Sometimes no adult at home will protect the child, or you cannot leave. Police must already have informed the Child Welfare Committee within 24 hours of the report [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Tell the committee, through the police or 1098, that home is not safe, and ask whether the child can stay with a safe relative or a foster family before a children's home is considered. Mission Vatsalya, the Centre's child-protection scheme since 2021-22, funds Child Welfare Committees, family-based care and children's homes [[mwcd-mission-vatsalya-guidelines-2022]].

If a girl becomes pregnant, a Nirbhaya Fund scheme launched in November 2023 offers minor girls made pregnant by rape shelter, medical and maternity care, legal aid, counselling and education support under one roof [[mwcd-pocso-victim-support-scheme-2023]]. The abortion rules name survivors of rape or incest, and minors, among those who can end a pregnancy up to 24 weeks [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]].

## Money, lawyers and support for the long haul

If the accused was the earner, apply for compensation; it does not depend on a conviction. Under Section 396 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, a victim can apply to the District Legal Services Authority even if no trial takes place, and it must complete its inquiry within two months [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Under NALSA's 2018 scheme for women and girls, the limits are 50% higher when the victim is a minor [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]]. Ask the same authority about free legal aid and a lawyer for the child [[nalsa]].

Prepare for a long road. At the end of 2024, 1,70,455 cases of penetrative assault on children were waiting for trial [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Keep one file with every paper and date, and keep the child in school if you can. A child can love the relative who hurt them, miss the family as it was, and still need protection from him. Mixed feelings do not mean the abuse did not happen.

Counselling helps both of you. Tele-MANAS, the government's free, round-the-clock mental health helpline, is 14416 [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].
abuser-in-the-family-what-to-do.hg:
Sochiye, Ranchi ki ek maa. Uski 11 saal ki beti use tukdon-tukdon mein batati hai ki raat ko uske papa uske kamre mein aate hain. Ghar ki akeli kamai unhi ki hai, aur unki maa bhi saath rehti hain. Is aurat ko ab tak jo kuch sikhaya gaya hai, sab yahi kehta hai: baat ghar ke andar hi rakho. 2024 mein police ne bachchon par penetrative sexual assault ke 44,126 POCSO cases mein se 3,658 mein, yaani 8.3% mein, family member ko accused darj kiya [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Har ek case ke peeche koi adult tha jisne bachche ko sabse pehle rakha. Yeh guide usi adult ke liye hai, chahe bachcha ladki ho ya ladka. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Pehle kuch ghante: yakeen, doori, bachche ki safety

Bachche ka yakeen kijiye, aur bol kar kahiye: "Mujhe tum par yakeen hai. Isme tumhari koi galti nahi. Tumne batakar sahi kiya." Details mat poochiye, rishtedaaron ke saamne baat dohrane ko mat kahiye, aur bachche ke saamne accused se mat bhidiye. Bhidne se woh chaukanna ho jaata hai, aur use bachche par dabaav daalne ka mauka mil jaata hai.

Phir pakka kijiye ki bachcha ek aur raat aisi jagah na bitaye jahan woh uske paas pahunch sake. Agar woh ghar nahi chhodta, toh bachche ko kisi aise insaan ke paas le jaiye jo bachche ki taraf ho: aapke apne maa-baap, bhai-behen ya koi dost. Agar jaane ki koi jagah nahi hai, ya bachcha abhi khatre mein hai, toh Child Helpline 1098 [[wcd-childline]] ya 112 par call kijiye; dono aapas mein jude hain [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].

Agar abuse haal hi mein hua hai ya bachche ko chot lagi hai, toh hospital jaiye. Har hospital ko, sarkari ho ya private, bachche ka ilaaj turant aur free karna hoga, aur police ko inform karna hoga [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Rishtedaar ko report karna: aapki duty aur bachche ki hifazat

Family ke liye koi chhoot nahi hai. POCSO ke Sections 19 aur 21 ke tahat, jise bhi child sexual abuse ka pata ho, use police ya Special Juvenile Police Unit ko report karna hoga, aur report na karne par 6 mahine tak ki jail ya fine ho sakta hai. Uske baad police ko 24 ghante ke andar Child Welfare Committee aur Special Court ko batana hota hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Law ki banawat hi bachche ko accused se alag rakhne ke liye hai. Bachche ka statement ghar par ya bachche ki pasand ki jagah par record hona chahiye, aise officer dwara jo uniform mein na ho, aur jahan tak ho sake woman officer dwara. Police ko pakka karna hota hai ki bachcha kabhi accused ke contact mein na aaye, aur kisi bachche ko raat mein police station mein nahi rakha ja sakta [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Agar accused aapke ghar mein rehta hai, toh police ko bataiye ki statement kahin aur liya jaye.

Rishtedaar keh sakte hain ki aap ek aadmi ki zindagi barbaad kar rahe hain. Law ise alag nazar se dekhta hai. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke Section 64(2)(f) ke tahat rishtedaar ya guardian ka kiya rape aggravated offence hai, jiski saza 10 saal se lekar baaki ki poori zindagi ki jail tak hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]], aur POCSO ke tahat 16 saal se kam umar ke bachche par penetrative assault ki saza kam se kam 20 saal hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Uske liye daav bahut ooncha hai, isiliye aap par dabaav bhi utna hi zyada hoga.

## Family ka dabaav, 'compromise' aur bail

Dabaav kai roop mein aa sakta hai: guzarish ("usne sorry bol diya hai"), paisa ("hum iski padhai ka kharcha uthayenge") ya dhamki ("tum sadak par aa jaogi"). Har offer aur har dhamki ko date aur kehne wale ke naam ke saath likh lijiye, aur investigating officer aur Special Public Prosecutor ko dijiye.

"Compromise" mat maaniye. Aparna Bhat v. State of Madhya Pradesh (18 March 2021) mein Supreme Court ne ek aisi bail condition radd kar di jisme sexual assault ke accused ko complainant se request karni thi ki woh use rakhi baandhe. Court ne kaha ki bail conditions accused aur victim ke beech contact ki maang nahi kar sakti, na hi uski ijazat de sakti hain, aur courts ko compromise ya shaadi ka sujhaav nahi dena chahiye [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]].

Is faisle ka istemaal kijiye. Jab accused bail ke liye apply kare, toh prosecutor ko bataiye ki woh bachche ke saath ek hi ghar mein rehta hai, aur aisi conditions maangiye jo use bachche aur ghar dono se door rakhein. Agar us par Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke Section 65 ke tahat 16 saal se kam umar ki ladki ke rape ka aarop hai, toh use anticipatory bail nahi mil sakti [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Agar woh koi condition todta hai, ya koi bachche par statement badalne ka dabaav daalta hai, toh usi din report kijiye.

## Agar ghar safe nahi hai: doosri dekhbhaal

Kabhi-kabhi ghar ka koi bhi adult bachche ki hifazat nahi karta, ya aap ghar nahi chhod paate. Report ke 24 ghante ke andar police ko Child Welfare Committee ko pehle hi bata dena hota hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Police ya 1098 ke zariye committee ko bataiye ki ghar safe nahi hai, aur poochiye ki children's home se pehle kya bachcha kisi safe rishtedaar ya foster family ke saath reh sakta hai. Mission Vatsalya, jo 2021-22 se Centre ki child protection scheme hai, Child Welfare Committees, family-based care aur children's homes ko fund karti hai [[mwcd-mission-vatsalya-guidelines-2022]].

Agar ladki pregnant ho jaye, toh November 2023 mein shuru hui Nirbhaya Fund ki ek scheme rape se pregnant hui minor ladkiyon ko ek hi chhat ke neeche shelter, medical aur maternity care, legal aid, counselling aur padhai mein madad deti hai [[mwcd-pocso-victim-support-scheme-2023]]. Abortion ke rules mein rape ya incest survivors, aur minors, un logon mein shaamil hain jo 24 hafte tak pregnancy khatam kara sakti hain [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]].

## Paisa, vakeel aur lambe safar ke liye support

Agar accused hi kamane wala tha, toh compensation ke liye apply kijiye; yeh conviction par depend nahi karta. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita ke Section 396 ke tahat victim District Legal Services Authority mein apply kar sakta hai, chahe trial ho hi na, aur authority ko do mahine ke andar apni inquiry poori karni hoti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. NALSA ki 2018 ki scheme mein, jo auraton aur ladkiyon ke liye hai, victim minor ho toh limits 50% zyada hain [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]]. Isi authority se free legal aid aur bachche ke liye vakeel ke baare mein bhi poochiye [[nalsa]].

Lambe safar ke liye taiyaar rahiye. 2024 ke end mein bachchon par penetrative assault ke 1,70,455 cases trial ke intezaar mein the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Har kaagaz aur har date ki ek file rakhiye, aur ho sake toh bachche ka school jaari rakhiye. Bachcha us rishtedaar se pyaar bhi kar sakta hai jisne use chot pahunchayi, family ko pehle jaisa yaad bhi kar sakta hai, aur phir bhi use usse hifazat ki zaroorat hoti hai. Mixed feelings ka matlab yeh nahi ki abuse hua hi nahi.

Counselling aap dono ke kaam aati hai. Tele-MANAS, sarkar ki free aur din-raat chalne wali mental health helpline, ka number 14416 hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

adolescence-peak-age-child-abuse.en:
Much of the child-safety advice Indian families hear is pitched at small children: good touch, bad touch, never go anywhere with a stranger. That advice matters, because young children are abused and are the least able to tell. But it often stops just as the risk climbs. Three very different sources, gathered years apart and in different ways, agree on something parents of teenagers rarely hear: the sexual abuse of children builds through the pre-teen years and peaks in adolescence.

## Three sources, one curve

The first is the government's 2007 Study on Child Abuse. Abuse reported by children began as early as age 5, gained momentum from 10 and peaked between 12 and 15 [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

The second is UNICEF's first global estimate of sexual violence against children, published in October 2024. Most childhood sexual violence happens in adolescence, it found, with a significant spike between 14 and 17 [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]].

The third is India's own police data. Here is how the 44,567 child victims of penetrative sexual assault recorded under POCSO in 2024 break down by age [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| Age | Child victims, 2024 |
|---|---|
| Under 6 | 831 |
| 6 to 12 | 3,438 |
| 12 to 16 | 16,801 |
| 16 to 18 | 23,497 (52.7%) |

Each source has a blind spot. The 2007 sample was not nationally representative. Police data depends on someone reporting, and young children rarely can, so the under-12 figures are minimums [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. But a survey of children, a global estimate built mainly on national surveys and a police register all bend the same way. That is hard to wave away.

## What changes at 12: independence, phones and new adults

None of the three sources measures why the risk climbs. But look at what changes around 12. A teenager's world widens faster than the adults around her widen their protection. At 13 she may travel alone to tuition, stay late for coaching, join a team, sleep over at a friend's or move into a hostel. Each step brings new adults with access and authority, and fewer adults watching.

The phone does the same indoors. UNICEF warns that online abusers may be someone the child knows or a stranger, and often win the trust of the child or a caregiver before manipulating the child into sharing sexual images or videos [[unicef-keeping-children-safe-online-2026]]. Boys are targets too: financial sexual extortion mainly hits boys aged 13 to 17, and the move from first message to coercion can take minutes to hours [[weprotect-web-of-deceit-2024]]. Our step-by-step sextortion guide covers what to do from the first threat.

Then come crushes, first relationships and the secrets that go with them. Darkness to Light, a US child-protection nonprofit, lists grooming red flags that include special attention to one child, gifts, acting as a sympathetic listener and gaining access through the internet [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. Read that list with a 14-year-old in mind: the coach who says only he understands her, the "friend" who tops up her phone, the stranger on Instagram who listens for hours.

## The 16-18 bulge, and what it mixes

The police curve does not just rise. It bulges at 16 to 18, and the bulge mixes very different cases. In 2013, Parliament raised the age below which sex with a girl is rape regardless of consent from 16 to 18 [[prs-madhavan-sexual-offences-2013]], and POCSO treats everyone under 18 as a child [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. So a 17-year-old's "yes" is not consent in law, and a teenage relationship can become a POCSO case when a family goes to the police.

NCRB's offender table shows the mix without separating it. In 22,308 of the 44,126 penetrative assault cases registered in 2024 (50.6%), the accused was recorded as a friend, an online friend or a live-in partner "on pretext of marriage" [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That one column can hold an adult who grooms a schoolgirl online, a 25-year-old who promises marriage to a 16-year-old, and two 17-year-olds whose parents found out.

So some of the 16-18 count probably reflects teenage relationships, and NCRB does not say how much. But the 2007 study and UNICEF's estimate do not come from FIRs, and they also put the peak in the teens. The warning survives the caveat. Who counts as a child under each law is untangled in our explainer on the ages in Indian law.

## Protection that fits a teenager, not a toddler

Protection for a toddler is supervision: an adult always in sight. For a 15-year-old that is impossible, and trying can push the teenager to stop telling you things. Protection has to travel with them.

- **Map the adults with access.** Tutors, coaches, drivers, hostel staff, older cousins, online "mentors". Notice when one adult singles out one teenager for attention, gifts or private chats.
- **Make phone talk routine.** Not "give me your phone", but "if anyone asks you for photos or threatens to share something, tell me, and you will not be in trouble".
- **Agree an exit.** A code word, or a pickup with no questions asked, from anywhere, at any hour.
- **Watch for change, not bruises.** UNICEF lists signs that something online has distressed a child, including trouble sleeping, avoiding devices or being unusually secretive, and fear of going to school [[unicef-parenting-negative-online-experience-2026]].

## Talking to a 14-year-old without a lecture

Teenagers often tune out lectures; a question gets further than a warning. Start from a news story or a show rather than their life: "What would you do if a friend told you this?" Ask about their world before warning them about it: which apps, which group chats, which adults they like and which they avoid.

Say one thing often: nothing they tell you will make you stop loving them, and they will never be punished for what someone else did to them. Be honest about limits too. If abuse comes out, you will have to act, and under POCSO doctors, teachers and counsellors must report it as well [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Promise to act with them, not behind their back. Our guide to teaching consent before 18 has more words you can borrow.

Why it matters: in the 2007 study, 72.1% of children who reported sexual assault had told no one, and only 3.4% had gone to the police [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. If your teenager does tell you, stay calm, believe them, do not ask why they did not tell you sooner, and call 1098 or 112.
adolescence-peak-age-child-abuse.hg:
India mein families jo child safety advice sunti hain, uska bada hissa chhote bachchon ke liye hota hai: good touch, bad touch, kisi stranger ke saath kahin mat jaana. Yeh advice zaroori hai, kyunki chhote bachchon ka bhi abuse hota hai aur woh sabse kam bata paate hain. Lekin yeh advice aksar theek wahin ruk jaati hai jahan se risk badhna shuru hota hai. Teen bilkul alag data sources, jo saalon ke gap pe aur alag-alag tarikon se jutaye gaye, ek aisi baat pe agree karte hain jo teenagers ke parents kam hi sunte hain: bachchon ka sexual abuse umar ke saath badhta jaata hai aur teenage mein sabse zyada hota hai.

## Teen sources, ek hi curve

Pehla source sarkar ki 2007 ki Study on Child Abuse hai. Usmein bachchon ne jo abuse bataya, woh 5 saal ki age se hi shuru ho jaata tha, 10 saal ke baad tezi pakadta tha, aur 12 se 15 saal ki age mein sabse zyada tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

Doosra source UNICEF ka hai. October 2024 mein UNICEF ne pehli baar duniya bhar mein bachchon ke saath sexual violence ka estimate jaari kiya. Uske hisaab se bachpan ki zyadatar sexual violence teenage mein hoti hai, aur 14 se 17 saal ke beech ismein tez uchhaal aata hai [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]].

Teesra source India ka apna police data hai. 2024 mein POCSO ke under penetrative sexual assault ke shikaar 44,567 bachche darj hue, aur age ke hisaab se unki ginti yeh hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| Age | Shikaar bachche, 2024 |
|---|---|
| 6 saal se kam | 831 |
| 6 se 12 saal | 3,438 |
| 12 se 16 saal | 16,801 |
| 16 se 18 saal | 23,497 (52.7%) |

Har source ka ek blind spot hai. 2007 ka sample poore desh ki tasveer nahi tha. Police data is pe tika hai ki koi report kare, aur chhote bachche aksar bata hi nahi paate, isliye 12 se kam age ke numbers 'kam se kam itne' hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Lekin bachchon se poochkar ki gayi ek study, zyadatar national surveys pe bana ek global estimate, aur ek police register, teeno ek hi direction mein mudte hain. Ise ignore karna mushkil hai.

## 12 ke baad kya badalta hai: azaadi, phone aur naye adults

Teeno mein se koi bhi source yeh nahi napta ki risk kyun badhta hai. Lekin dekhiye ki 12 ke aas-paas kya badalta hai. Teenage mein bachche ki duniya jitni tezi se badi hoti hai, utni tezi se adults uski protection nahi badhate. 13 saal ki age mein woh akele tuition ja sakti hai, coaching mein der tak ruk sakti hai, kisi team mein khel sakti hai, kisi dost ke ghar raat ruk sakti hai ya hostel ja sakti hai. Har kadam ke saath naye adults aate hain jinki us tak pahunch bhi hai aur jinka us pe authority bhi hai, aur nazar rakhne wale adults kam ho jaate hain.

Ghar ke andar yahi kaam phone karta hai. UNICEF warning deta hai ki online abuse karne wala koi jaan-pehchaan ka bhi ho sakta hai aur stranger bhi, aur woh aksar pehle bachche ka ya uske gharwalon ka bharosa jeetta hai, phir bachche ko manipulate karke usse sexual photos ya videos mangwata hai [[unicef-keeping-children-safe-online-2026]]. Ladke bhi target pe hain: paise ke liye ki jaane wali sexual blackmailing, yaani sextortion, ke zyadatar shikaar 13 se 17 saal ke ladke hote hain, aur pehle message se dhamki tak pahunchne mein kuch minute se kuch ghante lagte hain [[weprotect-web-of-deceit-2024]]. Pehli dhamki aate hi kya karna hai, yeh humari step-by-step sextortion guide mein hai.

Phir aate hain pehle crush, pehle relationships, aur unke saath aane wale secrets. US ki child-protection sanstha Darkness to Light grooming ke kuch red flags batati hai. Grooming matlab abuse se pehle bachche ko dheere-dheere apne jaal mein lena. Inmein shaamil hain: kisi ek bachche pe khaas dhyan dena, gifts dena, hamdard banke baatein sunna, aur internet ke zariye bachche tak pahunch banana [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. Yeh list kisi 14 saal ki bachchi ko sochkar padhiye: woh coach jo kehta hai ki sirf wahi use samajhta hai, woh 'dost' jo uska phone recharge karwa deta hai, Instagram ka woh stranger jo ghanton uski baatein sunta hai.

## 16-18 ka bulge, aur usmein kya-kya mila hai

Police data ki line sirf upar nahi jaati. 16 se 18 saal pe woh aur phool jaati hai, aur is bulge mein bahut alag-alag tarah ke cases mile hue hain. 2013 mein Parliament ne woh age 16 se badhakar 18 kar di jisse kam age ki ladki ke saath sex rape maana jaata hai, chahe uski consent ho ya nahi [[prs-madhavan-sexual-offences-2013]]. POCSO bhi 18 se kam age ke har insaan ko child maanta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Yaani law ki nazar mein 17 saal ke kisi bhi bachche ki 'haan' consent nahi hai, aur jab family police ke paas jaati hai, toh teenage ka koi relationship bhi POCSO case ban sakta hai.

NCRB ki table yeh mix dikhati hai, par alag nahi karti. 2024 mein darj penetrative assault ke 44,126 cases mein se 22,308 cases (50.6%) mein accused ko dost, online dost ya 'shaadi ka jhansa' dene wala live-in partner darj kiya gaya [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Is ek column mein bahut alag kahaniyan ho sakti hain: ek adult aadmi jo kisi school girl ko online phansata hai, ek 25 saal ka aadmi jo 16 saal ki ladki se shaadi ka waada karta hai, aur 17-17 saal ke do bachche jinke parents ko pata chal gaya.

Toh 16-18 ki ginti ka kuch hissa shayad teenage relationships se aata hai, aur kitna, yeh NCRB nahi batata. Lekin 2007 ki study aur UNICEF ka estimate FIRs se nahi bane, aur woh bhi sabse zyada risk teenage mein hi batate hain. Yaani is caveat ke baawajood warning apni jagah kaayam hai. Kis law mein kaun 'child' hai, yeh humne Indian law ki alag-alag ages wale apne explainer mein samjhaya hai.

## Teenager ki protection, toddler jaisi nahi

Chhote bachche ki protection ka matlab hai nigrani: koi adult hamesha nazar ke saamne rahe. 15 saal ke bachche ke liye yeh possible nahi, aur aisi koshish se teenager aapko baatein batana hi band kar sakta hai. Isliye protection aisi honi chahiye jo bachche ke saath-saath chale.

- **Pehchaniye ki kin adults ki pahunch hai.** Tutors, coaches, drivers, hostel staff, bade cousins, online 'mentors'. Dhyan dijiye jab koi ek adult kisi ek teenager ko khaas attention, gifts ya private chats dene lage.
- **Phone ki baat ko normal bana dijiye.** 'Phone dikhao' nahi, balki 'agar kabhi koi tumse photos maange ya kuch share karne ki dhamki de, toh mujhe batana, tum trouble mein nahi padoge.'
- **Exit plan tay kijiye.** Ek code word, ya yeh waada ki aap bina sawaal pooche kahin se bhi, kabhi bhi lene aayenge.
- **Chot nahi, badlaav dekhiye.** UNICEF batata hai ki agar online kisi baat se bachcha pareshan hai, toh kuch signs dikh sakte hain, jaise neend na aana, phone se bachna ya ajeeb tarah se sab kuch chhupana, aur school jaane se darna [[unicef-parenting-negative-online-experience-2026]].

## 14 saal ke bachche se baat, bina lecture diye

Teenagers aksar lecture sunte hi kaan band kar lete hain; warning se zyada door ek sawaal jaata hai. Baat unki life se nahi, kisi news ya kisi show se shuru kijiye: 'Agar tumhari koi dost tumhe aisa bataye, toh tum kya karoge?' Warning dene se pehle unki duniya ke baare mein poochiye: kaun se apps, kaun se group chats, kaun se adults unhe pasand hain, aur kinse woh bachte hain.

Ek baat baar-baar kahiye: woh aapko kuch bhi batayein, aapka pyaar kam nahi hoga, aur kisi aur ne unke saath jo kiya, uski saza unhe kabhi nahi milegi. Apni limits ke baare mein bhi sach boliye. Agar abuse ki baat saamne aayi, toh aapko action lena padega, aur POCSO ke under doctors, teachers aur counsellors ko bhi iski report karni hoti hai [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Waada kijiye ki aap jo bhi karenge, unke saath milkar karenge, unki peeth peechhe nahi. 18 se pehle consent sikhane wali humari guide mein aise aur bhi words hain jo aap use kar sakte hain.

Yeh kyun zaroori hai: 2007 ki study mein jin bachchon ne sexual assault ke baare mein bataya, unmein se 72.1% ne usse pehle kisi ko kuch nahi bataya tha, aur sirf 3.4% police tak gaye the [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Agar aapka teenager aapko kuch bataye, toh calm rahiye, uski baat pe bharosa kijiye, yeh mat poochiye ki pehle kyun nahi bataya, aur 1098 ya 112 pe call kijiye.

boys-missing-from-pocso-data.en:
In 2022, police in India recorded 414 boys among 38,444 child victims of penetrative sexual assault under the POCSO Act [[ncrb-cii-2022-book1]]. In 2024, they recorded 892 boys among 44,567 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The count more than doubled in two years. Yet boys are still only about 2 in 100 child victims on record, and India's last national study of child abuse, from 2007, points to a far larger hidden number.

## 414 to 892: what changed between 2022 and 2024

Boys were about 1% of child victims of penetrative assault in 2022 [[ncrb-cii-2022-book1]]. By 2024 they were about 2%: 892 boys against 43,675 girls [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Police data cannot say why the count rose: it counts reported cases, not abuse. A rise can mean more boys are being abused, or more boys and parents are going to the police. With so much of boys' abuse never reported, better reporting is a real possibility, but the record cannot prove it.

The same table shows which boys reach the record: much younger ones than the girls. More than four in ten of the 892 boys were under 12, while fewer than one in ten girls were [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The data does not say why. Perhaps a small child's abuse is more often noticed by an adult who acts, while a teenage boy usually has to decide to tell, and much of what he hears says boys cannot be victims.

## Still about 2%: the gap with the 2007 study and UNICEF's estimate

In 2007, the Ministry of Women and Child Development surveyed 12,447 children across 13 states, and 53.22% reported at least one form of sexual abuse [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Of the children who reported abuse, 52.94% were boys and 47.06% girls. Nine of the 13 states found a higher share among boys [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

That study has real limits. Its sample was not random: it set out to include street children, working children and children in institutions, and street and working children are disproportionately boys. Its definition was broad and included non-contact abuse. It is not a national rate, and it is nearly two decades old. The two figures are not like for like, but the distance between "more than half" and "about 2 in 100" is too wide to blame on method alone.

UNICEF's global estimates, published in October 2024, say 240 to 310 million boys and men alive today, around 1 in 11, were raped or sexually assaulted in childhood [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]]. Data on boys is thinner, which is why UNICEF gives a range.

Set the three side by side. The police record shows how often the abuse of boys is reported, not how often it happens.

## Why boys do not tell

Silence is the norm for abused children. In the 2007 study, 72.1% of children who said they had been sexually assaulted had told no one, and only 3.4% had gone to the police [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Among young adults who had been sexually assaulted as children, only 26.8% had ever told anyone [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

For boys, the silence has extra layers. Consider a hypothetical. A 13-year-old in Indore is abused by his cricket coach. He has been told since he was small that boys don't cry. He has never heard anyone say this can happen to a boy, so he has no words for it. He fears being laughed at, being called weak, or being asked why he did not fight back. If he hints at it, a friend may treat it as a joke. So he says nothing, and in the police data it never happened.

Adult law repeats it. Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) defines rape as an act by "a man" against "a woman", so an adult man cannot legally be raped in India [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. A boy who grows up hearing that men cannot be victims learns early that what happened to him has no name.

## POCSO protects boys; the silence does not

For children, the law is not the gap. POCSO has been in force since 14 November 2012; it defines a child as anyone under 18 and protects boys and girls alike [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Its offences are written against "a child", not "a girl" [[pocso-act-2012]]. A boy's case goes to the same police units and Special Courts as a girl's.

What fails boys is everything before the police station: the joke, the disbelief, the shame. And at 18, the law itself steps back. The BNS has no counterpart to the old Section 377, so non-consensual penetrative sex against an adult man is not rape under the new code, and no specific offence replaced it [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. A boy abused at 17 is a victim under POCSO. A year later, the same act fits no rape charge at all.

## What parents, teachers and friends can change

The aim: make telling feel safer than silence, long before anything happens.

- **Say it out loud.** Tell sons, nephews and students that sexual abuse can happen to boys, and that it is never the child's fault.
- **Believe the first telling.** If a boy hints at something, do not laugh it off as "masti" and do not ask why he did not fight back.
- **Watch the signs, not the gender.** Darkness to Light, a US child-protection nonprofit, notes that behavioural signs are more common than physical ones: anxiety, sleep problems, unusual fear of a person or reluctance to be alone with them [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]].
- **Talk about online threats.** Financial sextortion mainly targets boys aged 13 to 17, who are usually tricked into believing they are chatting with a young woman [[weprotect-web-of-deceit-2024]]. Tell boys that a threat is a crime against them, not a secret to keep.
- **Report it.** Under POCSO, anyone who knows or suspects that a child is being sexually abused must tell the police, though a child is never punished for staying silent [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Child Helpline 1098 is there for boys exactly as it is for girls.

If you are the friend he confides in, you do not have to fix anything. Believe him, keep it from everyone except an adult who can help, and go with him to that adult or to 1098.
boys-missing-from-pocso-data.hg:
2022 mein India ki police ne POCSO Act ke tahat penetrative sexual assault ke shikaar 38,444 bachche record kiye, jinmein 414 ladke the [[ncrb-cii-2022-book1]]. 2024 mein 44,567 bachche record hue, jinmein 892 ladke the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yaani do saal mein ladkon ki ginti double se bhi zyada ho gayi. Phir bhi record mein har 100 shikaar bachchon mein lagbhag 2 hi ladke hain, aur child abuse par India ki aakhri national study, jo 2007 mein hui thi, ek kahin bade chhupe hue number ki taraf ishaara karti hai.

## 414 se 892: 2022 aur 2024 ke beech kya badla

2022 mein penetrative assault ke shikaar bachchon mein ladke lagbhag 1% the [[ncrb-cii-2022-book1]]. 2024 tak woh lagbhag 2% ho gaye: 43,675 ladkiyon ke muqable 892 ladke [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Ginti kyun badhi, yeh police data nahi bata sakta: woh report hue cases ginta hai, abuse nahi. Badhat ka matlab ho sakta hai ki zyada ladkon ka abuse hua, ya yeh ki zyada ladke aur parents police tak pahunche. Ladkon ke saath hone wala bahut sa abuse kabhi report hi nahi hota, isliye reporting badhna ek asli sambhavna hai, lekin record ise sabit nahi kar sakta.

Isi table se yeh bhi pata chalta hai ki kaun se ladke record tak pahunchte hain: ladkiyon ke muqable kahin kam umar ke. 892 ladkon mein se 10 mein 4 se zyada 12 saal se chhote the, jabki ladkiyon mein yeh hissa 10 mein 1 se bhi kam tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Data iski wajah nahi batata. Shayad chhote bachche ke saath hua abuse aksar koi bada dekh leta hai aur action leta hai, jabki teenage ladke ko khud bolne ka faisla karna padta hai, aur uske aas-paas ki zyadatar baatein use yahi sikhati hain ki ladke victim nahi ho sakte.

## Ab bhi sirf 2%: 2007 ki study aur UNICEF ke estimate se itna gap

2007 mein Ministry of Women and Child Development ne 13 states ke 12,447 bachchon ka survey kiya, aur 53.22% ne kisi na kisi tarah ke sexual abuse ki baat kahi [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Abuse report karne wale in bachchon mein 52.94% ladke the aur 47.06% ladkiyan. 13 mein se 9 states mein ladkon ka hissa zyada nikla [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

Is study ki apni limits hain. Iska sample random nahi tha: ismein jaan-boojh ke street children, kaam karne wale bachche aur institutions mein rehne wale bachche shaamil kiye gaye, aur street aur kaam karne wale bachchon mein ladkon ka hissa normal se zyada hota hai. Definition bhi badi thi, jismein bina chhue hone wala abuse bhi gina gaya. Yeh poore desh ka rate nahi hai, aur study lagbhag do decade purani hai. Dono number ek jaisi cheez nahi naapte, lekin "aadhe se zyada" aur "100 mein 2" ke beech ka faasla itna bada hai ki use sirf tareeke ka farq nahi maana ja sakta.

UNICEF ne October 2024 mein global estimates jaari kiye. Unke mutabik aaj zinda 240 million se 310 million ladke aur aadmi, yaani lagbhag 11 mein se 1, bachpan mein rape ya sexual assault ka shikaar hue [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]]. Ladkon par data kam hai, isliye UNICEF ek pakka number nahi, ek range deta hai.

Teeno ko saath rakh ke dekhiye. Police record yeh dikhata hai ki ladkon ka abuse kitna kam report hota hai, yeh nahi ki kitna kam hota hai.

## Ladke kyun nahi batate

Abuse jhelne wale zyadatar bachche chup hi rehte hain. 2007 ki study mein jin bachchon ne kaha ki unke saath sexual assault hua, unmein se 72.1% ne kisi ko nahi bataya tha, aur sirf 3.4% police tak gaye the [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Jin young adults ke saath bachpan mein sexual assault hua tha, unmein se sirf 26.8% ne kabhi kisi ko bataya tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

Ladkon ki chuppi ki aur bhi layers hain. Ek hypothetical sochiye. Indore ka ek 13 saal ka ladka hai, jiska cricket coach uska abuse karta hai. Use bachpan se sikhaya gaya hai ki ladke rote nahi. Usne kabhi kisi ko yeh kehte nahi suna ki ladke ke saath bhi aisa ho sakta hai, isliye uske paas iske liye shabd hi nahi hain. Use darr hai ki log hasenge, use kamzor kahenge, ya poochhenge ki usne virodh kyun nahi kiya. Ishaare mein kisi dost ko bataye bhi, to dost ise mazaak samajh sakta hai. To woh chup reh jaata hai, aur police data mein yeh kabhi hua hi nahi.

Badon ka kanoon bhi yahi baat dohraata hai. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ka Section 63 rape ko aisa kaam batata hai jo "a man" yaani ek aadmi, "a woman" yaani ek aurat ke saath karta hai. Matlab India mein kanooni taur par kisi adult aadmi ka rape ho hi nahi sakta [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Jo ladka yeh sunte hue bada hota hai ki mard victim nahi hote, woh jaldi seekh leta hai ki uske saath jo hua, uska koi naam hi nahi hai.

## POCSO ladkon ko bachata hai, chuppi nahi

Bachchon ke maamle mein kanoon mein kami nahi hai. POCSO 14 November 2012 se laagu hai; ismein 18 se kam umar ka har insaan bachcha hai, aur yeh ladkon aur ladkiyon ko barabar protect karta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Iske offences "a child" yaani bachche ke khilaaf likhe gaye hain, sirf ladki ke khilaaf nahi [[pocso-act-2012]]. Ladke ka case bhi unhi police units aur Special Courts mein jaata hai jahan ladki ka.

Ladkon ke saath asli na-insaafi police station se pehle hoti hai: mazaak, baat ko believe na karna, sharm. Aur 18 ka hote hi kanoon bhi peeche hat jaata hai. BNS mein purane Section 377 jaisa koi section nahi hai, isliye kisi adult aadmi ke saath zabardasti penetrative sex naye code mein rape nahi hai, aur uski jagah koi khaas offence bhi nahi banaya gaya [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. 17 saal ki umar mein abuse jhelne wala ladka POCSO mein victim hai. Ek saal baad wahi kaam kisi rape charge mein fit hi nahi hota.

## Parents, teachers aur dost kya badal sakte hain

Maqsad ek hai: kuch hone se bahut pehle hi aisa mahaul banana ki batana, chup rehne se zyada safe lage.

- **Khul ke kahiye.** Apne bete, bhatije-bhaanje aur students ko bataiye ki ladkon ka bhi sexual abuse ho sakta hai, aur ismein bachche ki kabhi galti nahi hoti.
- **Pehli baar mein hi believe kijiye.** Ladka kuch ishaara kare, to use "masti" keh ke mat taaliye, aur yeh mat poochhiye ki usne virodh kyun nahi kiya.
- **Ladka-ladki nahi, signs dekhiye.** US ki child-protection nonprofit Darkness to Light ke mutabik physical signs se zyada common behaviour ke badlaav hain: anxiety, neend ki problem, kisi khaas insaan se ajeeb darr, ya uske saath akele rehne se katraana [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]].
- **Online khatron par baat kijiye.** Paison ke liye hone wala sextortion zyadatar 13 se 17 saal ke ladkon ko target karta hai, jinhe aksar yakeen dilaya jaata hai ki woh kisi ladki se chat kar rahe hain [[weprotect-web-of-deceit-2024]]. Ladkon ko bataiye ki aisi dhamki unke khilaaf crime hai, chhupa ke rakhne wala secret nahi.
- **Report kijiye.** POCSO ke mutabik jise bhi bachche ke sexual abuse ka pata ho ya shak ho, use police ko batana hoga, lekin chup rehne ke liye kisi bachche ko kabhi saza nahi hoti [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Child Helpline 1098 ladkon ke liye bhi utni hi hai jitni ladkiyon ke liye.

Agar aap woh dost hain jise usne apni baat batayi hai, to aapko sab kuch theek nahi karna hai. Uski baat maaniye, baat kisi aur ko mat bataiye siwaye us bade ke jo madad kar sake, aur uske saath us bade ke paas ya 1098 tak jaaiye.

child-abusers-known-not-strangers.en:
Many Indian children learn one safety rule early: never take anything from a stranger. Now look at the police record. In 2024, police registered 44,126 cases of penetrative sexual assault on children, the POCSO Act's term for child rape. In 42,634 of them, or 96.6%, the accused was someone the child knew [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The rule we teach first guards against the smallest part of the danger.

## The 1,492: what the 2024 offender table actually shows

One table in NCRB's *Crime in India* report records how the accused was related to the child in cases under Sections 4 and 6 of POCSO. In 2024 it sorted the 44,126 cases like this [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| Who the accused was | Cases | Share |
|---|---|---|
| Family member | 3,658 | 8.3% |
| Family friend, neighbour, employer or other known person | 16,668 | 37.8% |
| Friend, online friend or live-in partner 'on pretext of marriage' | 22,308 | 50.6% |
| Unknown or not identified | 1,492 | 3.4% |

Strangers, together with accused whom nobody could identify, fill a single row: 1,492 cases, or 3.4%.

Two cautions before you quote this table. It covers only penetrative assault: 44,126 of the 69,191 POCSO cases registered that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. And it counts only cases that reached a police station. Abuse inside the family can be especially hard to report: the adult who would go to the police may be the accused's own wife, mother or brother. Read the family row as a floor, not a full count.

## Inside the circle: family, neighbours, employers and 'friends'

Read the rows as places in a child's life. The second row, 16,668 cases, is NCRB's group for family friends, neighbours, employers and other known people. That can mean the tuition teacher, the neighbour who drops a child home, the shopkeeper, or the employer a working child or a poor family depends on: adults whom families trust with a child, often because they have been kind.

The biggest row, 22,308 cases, mixes very different situations. Some are adults who befriend a child online and then meet her. Some are men who promise a teenager marriage. Some are sexual relationships between teenagers, which POCSO treats as an offence when either one is under 18, whatever the two of them say. More than half of all child victims of penetrative assault, 23,497 or 52.7%, were aged 16 to 18 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], and the table cannot separate an adult grooming a child from a relationship between two teenagers.

For the online part, UNICEF's warning fits: online abusers, known or unknown, often first win the trust of the child or a caregiver, and only then manipulate the child [[unicef-keeping-children-safe-online-2026]].

## Not new: a 2007 government study pointed the same way

In 2007, the Ministry of Women and Child Development surveyed 12,447 children in 13 states. It found that half of the abusers were people known to the child or in a position of trust and responsibility, and that most children told no one [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Of the children who said they had been sexually assaulted, 72.1% had kept it to themselves [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

The two sources are not directly comparable. One was a broad survey of children with a non-random sample; the other counts police cases of one offence in one year. But seventeen years apart, both put a large share of abusers inside the circle of people a child already knows. Yet many safety talks at home and in school still begin and end with strangers.

## Why 'stranger danger' feels right and fails children

Stranger danger survives because it is comfortable. A stranger is easy to picture and easy to warn against, and the warning accuses nobody at home. The idea runs so deep that the Supreme Court's 2023 handbook on gender stereotypes lists the belief that rapists are usually strangers as a false stereotype [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

A known abuser does not need to snatch a child. He already has access, trust and time. Darkness to Light, a US child-protection nonprofit, describes grooming as a deliberate process of building and keeping a secret sexual relationship with a child. Its red flags are special attention to one child, gifts, touching or hugging, playing the sympathetic listener, offering to help the family, and reaching the child through the internet [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. Most of them look like kindness.

Consider a hypothetical. A nine-year-old in Lucknow has been told never to talk to strangers. The man who is a risk to her is the neighbour who helps her father fill in bank forms, brings her chocolates and offers to drop her at tuition. When he says "this is our secret", nothing she has been taught tells her what to do.

## Safety rules built for the real risk

Rules that match the data are about access, trust and secrecy, and adults have to set them. Children cannot carry this alone.

- **No body secrets.** Teach every child that no adult, relative or not, may ask them to keep a secret about touch or their body. A surprise party is fine. A secret that feels bad must be told.
- **Visible access.** One-to-one time with a tutor, coach, driver or relative should be easy to see and easy to interrupt: open doors, unplanned drop-ins, no locked rooms.
- **Behaviour over reputation.** Watch for the red flags above, and for changes in the child. Darkness to Light notes that emotional and behavioural signs are more common than physical ones, including unusual fear of a person or reluctance to be alone with them [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]].
- **Online friends, without threats.** A child who fears losing the phone may hide the chat. Ask who they talk to, calmly and often.
- **Report.** Under Sections 19 and 21 of POCSO, anyone who knows or suspects that a child is being sexually abused must tell the police or the Special Juvenile Police Unit, and failing to report is punishable, though a child is never punished for staying silent [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Child Helpline 1098 runs around the clock and is linked to the emergency number 112 [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].

Keep teaching children about strangers. Just stop treating it as the main lesson. In 2024, strangers and unidentified accused together made up 1,492 cases out of 44,126.
child-abusers-known-not-strangers.hg:
Bahut se Indian bachche bahut jaldi ek safety rule seekh jaate hain: kisi stranger se kuch mat lena. Ab zara police record dekhiye. 2024 mein police ne bachchon par penetrative sexual assault ke 44,126 cases register kiye. POCSO Act mein child rape ko yahi naam diya gaya hai. Inmein se 42,634 cases mein, yaani 96.6% mein, accused koi aisa tha jise bachcha jaanta tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Matlab jo rule hum sabse pehle sikhate hain, woh khatre ke sabse chhote hisse se bachata hai.

## 1,492 ka sach: 2024 ki offender table asal mein kya dikhati hai

NCRB ki *Crime in India* report ki ek table mein likha hota hai ki POCSO ke Section 4 aur 6 wale cases mein accused ka bachche se kya rishta tha. 2024 ke 44,126 cases is tarah bante the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| Accused kaun tha | Cases | Hissa |
|---|---|---|
| Family member | 3,658 | 8.3% |
| Family friend, padosi, employer ya koi aur jaan-pehchaan wala | 16,668 | 37.8% |
| Friend, online friend ya 'shaadi ke bahane' live-in partner | 22,308 | 50.6% |
| Anjaan, ya jiski pehchaan nahi ho paayi | 1,492 | 3.4% |

Strangers, aur woh accused jinhe koi pehchaan hi nahi paaya, sab milake bas ek row mein aate hain: 1,492 cases, yaani 3.4%.

Yeh table kisi ko quote karne se pehle do baatein yaad rakhiye. Pehli, ismein sirf penetrative assault ke cases hain: us saal register hue POCSO ke kul 69,191 cases mein se 44,126 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Doosri, ismein sirf woh cases hain jo police station tak pahunche. Family ke andar ka abuse report karna khaas taur par mushkil ho sakta hai: jise police ke paas jaana hota, woh accused ki apni biwi, maa ya bhai ho sakta hai. Isliye family wali row ko poori ginti nahi, kam se kam ginti samjhiye.

## Circle ke andar: family, padosi, employers aur 'friends'

In rows ko bachche ki rozana zindagi ki jagahon ki tarah padhiye. Doosri row, 16,668 cases wali, NCRB ka woh group hai jismein family friends, padosi, employers aur doosre jaan-pehchaan wale aate hain. Iska matlab ho sakta hai tuition wale sir, bachche ko ghar chhodne wale padosi, dukaan wale bhaiya, ya woh employer jis par kaam karne wala bachcha ya gareeb family tiki hai: aise log jin par family bachche ke maamle mein bharosa karti hai, aksar isliye kyunki woh ab tak bahut bhale lage.

Sabse badi row mein, jismein 22,308 cases hain, bahut alag-alag situations ek saath gini gayi hain. Kuch mein koi adult online dosti karta hai aur phir bachchi se milne aata hai. Kuch mein koi aadmi kisi teenager se shaadi ka waada karta hai. Aur kuch mein do teenagers ke beech sexual rishta hota hai. Agar dono mein se koi bhi 18 se kam hai, to POCSO ise offence maanta hai, chahe dono kuch bhi kahein. Penetrative assault ke shikaar saare bachchon mein se aadhe se zyada, 23,497 yaani 52.7%, 16 se 18 saal ke the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh table bachche ko groom karne wale adult aur do teenagers ke rishte ko alag nahi kar sakti.

Online wale hisse par UNICEF ki warning bilkul fit baithti hai: online abusers, jaan-pehchaan ke hon ya anjaan, aksar pehle bachche ya ghar walon ka trust jeette hain, aur uske baad hi bachche ko manipulate karte hain [[unicef-keeping-children-safe-online-2026]].

## Nayi baat nahi: 2007 ki sarkari study ne bhi yahi ishaara kiya tha

2007 mein Ministry of Women and Child Development ne 13 states mein 12,447 bachchon ka survey kiya tha. Study mein nikla ki aadhe abusers bachche ke jaan-pehchaan wale the, ya aise log the jin par bachche ki dekhbhaal aur bharose ki zimmedari thi. Aur zyadatar bachchon ne kisi ko kuch nahi bataya [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Jin bachchon ne kaha ki unke saath sexual assault hua, unmein se 72.1% ne yeh baat apne tak hi rakhi thi [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

Dono sources ko seedha compare nahi kiya ja sakta. Ek bachchon se poochha gaya bada survey tha jiska sample random nahi tha; doosra ek saal mein ek offence ke police cases ginta hai. Phir bhi 17 saal ke gap par dono abusers ke ek bade hisse ko usi daayre ke andar dikhate hain: un logon mein jinhe bachcha pehle se jaanta hai. Iske bawajood ghar aur school mein safety ki bahut si baatein strangers se shuru hoti hain aur wahin khatam ho jaati hain.

## 'Stranger danger' sahi kyun lagta hai, aur bachchon ko kyun fail karta hai

Stranger danger isliye chalta rehta hai kyunki yeh comfortable hai. Stranger ki tasveer aasani se ban jaati hai, usse bachne ko kehna aasaan hai, aur is warning mein ghar ke kisi insaan par ungli nahi uthti. Yeh soch itni gehri hai ki Supreme Court ki 2023 ki gender stereotypes wali handbook mein bhi yeh baat galat stereotype ki list mein hai ki rapists aam taur par strangers hote hain [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Jaan-pehchaan wale abuser ko bachche ko utha ke le jaane ki zaroorat nahi padti. Uske paas pehle se access hai, trust hai aur time hai. US ki child-protection nonprofit Darkness to Light grooming ko ek sochi-samjhi process batati hai, jismein abuser dheere-dheere bachche ke saath ek secret sexual rishta banata hai aur use chhupa ke rakhta hai. Uske bataye red flags yeh hain: kisi ek bachche par special attention, gifts, touch karna ya gale lagana, hamdard ban ke sunna, family ki madad ki offer, aur internet ke zariye bachche tak pahunchna [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. Dhyaan dijiye, inmein se zyadatar cheezein kindness jaisi dikhti hain.

Ek hypothetical sochiye. Lucknow mein ek nau saal ki bachchi ko sikhaya gaya hai ki strangers se baat mat karna.
