Lekin uske liye khatra woh padosi hai jo uske papa ke bank forms bharne mein madad karta hai, uske liye chocolates laata hai aur use tuition chhodne ki baat karta hai. Jab woh kehta hai "yeh hamara secret hai", tab bachchi ko sikhayi gayi koi baat kaam nahi aati.

## Asli khatre ke hisaab se bane safety rules

Jo rules data se match karte hain, woh access, trust aur secrecy par tike hain, aur yeh rules badon ko banane honge. Yeh bojh bachche akele nahi utha sakte.

- **Body ka koi secret nahi.** Har bachche ko sikhaiye ki koi bhi bada, relative ho ya nahi, unse touch ya body se judi baat secret rakhne ko nahi keh sakta. Surprise party theek hai. Jo secret bura lage, woh batana hi hai.
- **Akele ka time nazar mein rahe.** Tutor, coach, driver ya relative ke saath one-to-one time aisa ho jise koi bhi dekh sake aur jismein koi bhi beech mein aa sake: darwaza khula, bina bataye drop-in, koi band kamra nahi.
- **Reputation nahi, behaviour dekhiye.** Upar wale red flags par nazar rakhiye, aur bachche mein aaye badlaav par bhi. Darkness to Light kehti hai ki physical signs se zyada common emotional aur behavioural signs hote hain, jaise kisi khaas insaan se ajeeb sa darr, ya uske saath akele rehne se katraana [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]].
- **Online friends par baat, bina dhamki ke.** Jis bachche ko phone chhin jaane ka darr hoga, woh chat chhupa sakta hai. Aaram se aur baar-baar poochhiye ki woh kisse baat karta hai.
- **Report kijiye.** POCSO ke Section 19 aur 21 ke mutabik jise bhi bachche ke sexual abuse ka pata ho ya shak ho, use police ya Special Juvenile Police Unit ko batana hi hoga. Report na karne par saza ho sakti hai, lekin chup rehne ke liye kisi bachche ko kabhi saza nahi hoti [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Child Helpline 1098 din-raat chalti hai aur emergency number 112 se judi hai [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].

Bachchon ko strangers ke baare mein zaroor sikhaiye. Bas ise sabse bada lesson mat maaniye. 2024 mein strangers aur jin accused ki pehchaan nahi ho paayi, dono milake 44,126 mein se sirf 1,492 cases the.

child-grooms-men-married-before-21.en:
Imagine a wedding in a village near Nashik. The bride is 17, and a few guests whisper that she is too young. The groom is 19, and nobody whispers about him. In law, both are children: the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 defines a child as a girl under 18 or a boy under 21, and any marriage involving one as a child marriage [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. By that measure, India's newest national survey finds that 15.9% of men aged 25-29 had married before 21 [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. They are almost never part of the conversation.

## 15.9%: the boys inside the child marriage data

The figure comes from the provisional NFHS-6 fact sheets for 2023-24. In NFHS-5 (2019-21) it was 17.7% [[nfhs5-india-report-2021]]. NFHS-6 interviewed far fewer men than women, so treat it with some care.

For women, the survey asks a different question: how many women aged 20-24 married before 18. In 2023-24 the answer was 20.1% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. The two use different ages and legal lines, so they cannot be ranked, but both show a large minority marrying before the law allows.

NFHS-5's detailed tables show that most men in this group who married before 21 did so at 18, 19 or 20, not as young boys [[nfhs5-india-report-2021]]. The typical underage groom has reached majority, yet the marriage law still calls him a child. That is why he is so easy to overlook. Worldwide, UNICEF counts child marriage at 18 for both sexes and finds it among boys at one sixth the level among girls [[unicef-child-marriage-topic-page]]. India draws the boys' line three years higher.

## Villages and cities: 19.0% against 9.7%

In rural India, 19.0% of men aged 25-29 had married before 21; in urban India, 9.7% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. A village man is about twice as likely to have married below the legal age.

Girls show the same split: 23.3% of rural women aged 20-24 had married before 18, against 11.4% of urban women [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Boys' and girls' early marriages are not separate problems. Both are concentrated in rural India, and a wedding that families fix can involve an underage bride, an underage groom or both.

In NFHS-6, 6.7% of women aged 15-19 were already mothers or pregnant: 7.9% in rural areas, 3.4% in urban ones [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. The figure includes women of 18 and 19, who are adults, so it measures early childbearing and not only pregnancies under 18. Behind each of those pregnancies is a man, and the public conversation rarely asks how old he is.

## What the 2006 law says about boys under 21

This is general information, not legal advice. The Act sees an underage groom three ways.

As a child who can undo the marriage. A child marriage is voidable: the person who was a child at the wedding can ask a district court to annul it, but only until two years after reaching majority [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. Majority comes at 18, so on the Act's wording the deadline falls at 20. A man married at 19 has months at most, and on this reading one married at 20 has no window at all, a mismatch our explainer on the ages at which Indian law stops treating you as a child sets out.

As a child who can be protected before the wedding. A magistrate can issue an injunction, and a marriage held in breach of one is void [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. In October 2024 the Supreme Court told magistrates to use this power on their own, especially around "auspicious days" for mass weddings [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]].

As an offender. The groom's offence applies to "a male adult above eighteen years of age" who contracts a child marriage [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. A 19-year-old who marries a 17-year-old is a child in one section and an adult offender in another. The heavier law sits elsewhere: since the Supreme Court's 2017 Independent Thought ruling, sex with a wife under 18 is rape [[sc-independent-thought-2017]], and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) keeps that line [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Who gets punished, and who does not

The Act sets one maximum for the adult groom, for whoever performs the wedding and for whoever promotes or permits it: two years' rigorous imprisonment and a fine of up to Rs 1 lakh, with no minimum sentence [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. A court can let the groom off with a fine alone.

Few are punished at all. Police registered 1,499 cases under the Act across India in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Courts that year convicted in 209 cases and acquitted in 625, a conviction rate of 25.0%, with 8,553 cases awaiting trial at year-end [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Back in Nashik, in our hypothetical, the 19-year-old did not choose the date, the bride or the priest; his parents did. Yet he can be prosecuted alongside them, he commits rape if he has sex with his 17-year-old wife, and he has only until he turns 20 to challenge the marriage. None of this helps him if nobody tells him.

## Why leaving boys out keeps child marriage alive

A message aimed only at daughters leaves out half of every wedding, and the attitudes young husbands bring into it. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 44% of men aged 15-49 said a husband is justified in beating his wife in at least one of seven situations, up from 42% in NFHS-4; among women the share fell from 52% to 45% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. And 35.1% of men agreed that "contraception is women's business and a man should not have to worry about it" [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Those views land on teenage wives. Only 28.1% of currently married women aged 15-19 used any contraceptive method [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. UNICEF says girls who marry before 18 are more likely to face domestic violence and less likely to stay in school [[unicef-child-marriage-topic-page]].

Schooling points to a way out. By wives' reports, husbands with 12 or more years of schooling were half as likely as husbands with no schooling to be violent: 22% against 43% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. That does not prove cause and effect, but keeping a boy in school and out of a wedding at 19 may also protect the girl he one day marries.

Counting boys takes nothing away from girls. It puts the whole wedding in view: the groom's age, his family's role and his right to say no.
child-grooms-men-married-before-21.hg:
Sochiye, Nashik ke paas ek gaon mein shaadi ho rahi hai. Dulhan 17 saal ki hai, aur kuch mehmaan dheere se kehte hain ki woh bahut chhoti hai. Dulha 19 saal ka hai, aur uske baare mein koi kuch nahi kehta. Law ki nazar mein dono bachche hain. Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 ke hisaab se 18 se kam umar ki ladki ya 21 se kam umar ka ladka child hai, aur jis shaadi mein inmein se koi ek ho, woh child marriage hai [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. Is paimaane se, India ka sabse naya national survey batata hai ki 25-29 saal ke 15.9% mardon ki shaadi 21 se pehle ho chuki thi [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Inki baat lagbhag kabhi nahi hoti.

## 15.9%: child marriage data ke andar chhupe ladke

Yeh figure 2023-24 ki provisional NFHS-6 fact sheets se aaya hai. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein yeh 17.7% tha [[nfhs5-india-report-2021]]. NFHS-6 ne women ke muqable kahin kam mardon ka interview kiya, isliye is number ko thodi saavdhaani se padhiye.

Women ke liye survey alag sawaal poochta hai: 20-24 saal ki kitni women ki shaadi 18 se pehle hui. 2023-24 mein jawaab tha 20.1% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Dono mein umar aur legal line alag hai, isliye inki aapas mein ranking nahi ho sakti. Lekin dono dikhate hain ki ek badi minority law ki izaazat se pehle shaadi kar rahi hai.

NFHS-5 ki detailed tables dikhati hain ki is group ke jin mardon ki shaadi 21 se pehle hui, unmein se zyadatar ki shaadi 18, 19 ya 20 saal mein hui, chhote ladkon ke roop mein nahi [[nfhs5-india-report-2021]]. Aam underage dulha balig ho chuka hota hai, phir bhi shaadi ka law use child kehta hai. Isiliye use nazarandaaz karna itna aasaan hai. Duniya bhar mein UNICEF ladke aur ladki dono ke liye child marriage ki line 18 pe rakhta hai, aur paata hai ki ladkon mein child marriage ladkiyon ke muqable sirf chhatha hissa hai [[unicef-child-marriage-topic-page]]. India ladkon ki line teen saal upar kheenchta hai.

## Gaon aur shehar: 19.0% vs 9.7%

Gaon ke India mein 25-29 saal ke 19.0% mardon ki shaadi 21 se pehle hui thi; shehri India mein 9.7% ki [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Yaani gaon ke mard ki shaadi legal umar se pehle hone ke chances lagbhag dugne hain.

Ladkiyon mein bhi yahi bantwara dikhta hai: gaon ki 20-24 saal ki 23.3% women ki shaadi 18 se pehle hui thi, jabki shehar ki 11.4% ki [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Ladkon aur ladkiyon ki jaldi shaadiyan alag-alag problems nahi hain. Dono zyadatar gaon ke India mein hoti hain, aur families jo shaadi tay karti hain, usmein dulhan underage ho sakti hai, dulha underage ho sakta hai, ya dono.

NFHS-6 mein 15-19 saal ki 6.7% women ya toh maa ban chuki thi ya pregnant thi: gaon mein 7.9%, shehar mein 3.4% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Is figure mein 18 aur 19 saal ki women bhi hain, jo adult hain, isliye yeh jaldi maa banne ko naapta hai, sirf 18 se kam umar ki pregnancies ko nahi. Har aisi pregnancy ke peeche ek mard hai, aur public baatchit mein shaayad hi koi poochta hai ki uski umar kitni hai.

## 2006 ka law 21 se kam umar ke ladkon ke baare mein kya kehta hai

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi. Yeh Act underage dulhe ko teen tarah se dekhta hai.

Ek child ki tarah, jo shaadi ko khatam karwa sakta hai. Child marriage voidable hoti hai: jo insaan shaadi ke waqt child tha, woh district court se use annul karne ko keh sakta hai, lekin sirf balig hone ke do saal baad tak [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. Balig 18 pe hote hain, isliye Act ke shabdon ke hisaab se deadline 20 saal pe khatam ho jaati hai. 19 saal mein byaahe mard ke paas zyada se zyada kuch mahine hote hain, aur is reading ke hisaab se 20 saal mein byaahe mard ke paas koi window bachti hi nahi. Yeh mismatch humare us explainer mein samjhaya gaya hai jo batata hai ki Indian law kis umar mein aapko bachcha maanna band karta hai.

Ek child ki tarah, jise shaadi se pehle bachaya ja sakta hai. Magistrate injunction jaari kar sakta hai, aur injunction todkar ki gayi shaadi void hoti hai, yaani shuru se hi maanya nahi [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. October 2024 mein Supreme Court ne magistrates se kaha ki woh is power ka istemaal khud se karein, khaaskar mass weddings wale "auspicious days", yaani shubh muhurat ke dino ke aas-paas [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]].

Ek offender ki tarah. Dulhe wala offence "a male adult above eighteen years of age" pe lagta hai, yaani 18 saal se upar ka woh balig mard jo child marriage karta hai [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. 17 saal ki ladki se shaadi karne wala 19 saal ka ladka ek section mein child hai aur doosre mein adult offender. Isse bhaari law kahin aur hai: Supreme Court ke 2017 ke Independent Thought faisle ke baad se, 18 se kam umar ki patni ke saath sex rape hai [[sc-independent-thought-2017]], aur Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ne bhi yahi line rakhi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Kise saza milti hai, aur kise nahi

Act balig dulhe, shaadi karwane wale, aur shaadi ko badhava dene ya hone dene wale, sabke liye ek hi maximum saza rakhta hai: do saal ki rigorous imprisonment aur Rs 1 lakh tak ka fine, aur koi minimum saza nahi [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. Court dulhe ko sirf fine lagakar bhi chhod sakta hai.

Saza milti hi bahut kam logon ko hai. 2024 mein poore India mein police ne is Act ke under 1,499 cases darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Us saal courts ne 209 cases mein conviction diya aur 625 mein accused bari hue, yaani conviction rate 25.0%. Saal ke end mein 8,553 cases trial ke intezaar mein the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Ab wapas Nashik chaliye, humare hypothetical mein. 19 saal ke ladke ne na date chuni, na dulhan, na pandit; yeh sab uske maa-baap ne kiya. Phir bhi unke saath us par bhi case chal sakta hai. Agar woh apni 17 saal ki patni ke saath sex karta hai, toh woh rape hai. Aur shaadi ko challenge karne ke liye uske paas sirf 20 saal ka hone tak ka waqt hai. Agar koi use yeh sab bataye hi nahi, toh inmein se kuch bhi uske kaam nahi aata.

## Ladkon ko bahar rakhna child marriage ko zinda kyun rakhta hai

Jo message sirf betiyon ke liye bana hai, woh har shaadi ka aadha hissa chhod deta hai, aur woh soch bhi jo young pati shaadi mein lekar aate hain. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein 15-49 saal ke 44% mardon ne kaha ki saat mein se kam se kam ek situation mein pati ka patni ko maarna sahi hai. NFHS-4 mein yeh 42% tha. Women mein yeh hissa 52% se girkar 45% ho gaya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Aur 35.1% mard is baat se sehmat the ki "contraception is women's business and a man should not have to worry about it", yaani contraception auraton ka kaam hai aur mard ko iski fikr nahi karni chahiye [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Yeh soch teenage patniyon pe aakar padti hai. 15-19 saal ki shaadi-shuda women mein se sirf 28.1% koi bhi contraceptive method use kar rahi thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. UNICEF kehta hai ki jin ladkiyon ki shaadi 18 se pehle hoti hai, unke domestic violence jhelne ke chances zyada hote hain aur school mein tike rehne ke chances kam [[unicef-child-marriage-topic-page]].

Padhai ek raasta dikhati hai. Patniyon ki reports ke hisaab se, jo pati 12 ya usse zyada saal padhe the, unmein violence ka chance bilkul na padhe patiyon ke muqable aadha tha: 22% vs 43% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Isse cause aur effect saabit nahi hota. Lekin ladke ko 19 saal mein shaadi ke mandap ki jagah padhai mein rakhna shaayad us ladki ko bhi bacha sakta hai jisse woh ek din shaadi karega.

Ladkon ko ginne se ladkiyon se kuch nahi chhinta. Isse poori shaadi nazar mein aati hai: dulhe ki umar, uski family ka role, aur uska mana karne ka haq.

child-marriage-law-fir-gap.en:
Telangana told the Supreme Court it had recorded 4,440 child marriage cases over three years, and filed 149 FIRs [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. Across India in 2024, police registered 1,499 cases under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], while 20.1% of women aged 20-24 surveyed in 2023-24 had been married before 18 [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Every offence under the Act is cognisable and non-bailable [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. It is still barely used. This investigation asks why, and whether more FIRs are the answer.

## 1,499 FIRs against one in five young women married as children

UNICEF India estimates that at least 1.5 million girls under 18 are married in India every year, though its page does not say how the estimate was made [[unicef-india-end-child-marriage]]. Police registrations under the Act came to 1,002 in 2022, 6,038 in 2023 and 1,499 in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Even if that estimate is far off, registered cases are a tiny fraction of it.

Courts did even less. In 2024, 209 cases under the Act ended in conviction and 625 in acquittal, a conviction rate of 25.0%, and 8,553 cases were pending trial at the end of the year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Three in four trials that finished ended without a conviction.

One caveat cuts the other way. NCRB counts each FIR once, under its most serious offence [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Since the Supreme Court's 2017 Independent Thought ruling, sex with a wife under 18 is rape [[sc-independent-thought-2017]], so an FIR about a consummated child marriage may be counted under POCSO, the child sexual abuse law, instead. The true number of FIRs linked to child marriage is probably higher than 1,499, by an amount the tables do not show.

## What the states told the Supreme Court

On 18 October 2024, in a case brought by the Society for Enlightenment and Voluntary Action, the Supreme Court set out figures states had given it for the previous three years [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]:

| State | Child marriage cases reported | FIRs |
|---|---|---|
| Tamil Nadu | 8,966 | 2,392 |
| Telangana | 4,440 | 149 |
| Andhra Pradesh | about 3,400, most of them weddings stopped | 10 |
| Maharashtra | 2,043 weddings prevented | 178 |

States count differently, so this is not a league table. Many of these "cases" were weddings stopped in time, which may not need an FIR at all.

Still, the same law, over similar periods, led to an FIR in roughly one case in four in Tamil Nadu, about one in 30 in Telangana, and 10 out of about 3,400 in Andhra Pradesh. The court read Maharashtra's numbers as a sign of "limited legal follow-through" [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]].

## Assam 2023: one state's spike, then the fall

The one national spike of recent years came from a single state. Of the 6,038 cases registered across India in 2023, Assam registered 5,267 [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. In 2024 Assam registered 471, and the national total fell back to 1,499 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

A count that jumps sixfold in a year and falls back the next is measuring police decisions, not weddings. West Bengal (36.4%) and Bihar (34.6%) have India's highest shares of young women married as children [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]], yet the most cases in 2024 were registered in Assam (471) and Tamil Nadu (408), not in either of them [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Did Assam's 2023 cases stop child marriages? Nobody can say yet. NFHS-6 counts women aged 20-24, all of whom had turned 18 by the end of 2022, so every child marriage in its figures took place before 2023. Assam's survey rate did fall, to 25.3% in 2023-24 [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]], but that fall was already under way before the cases were filed. Only a later survey will tell.

## Why police and families avoid the law

Start with who the accused are. The Act punishes an adult groom, anyone who performs a child marriage and anyone who promotes or permits one [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. In an arranged child marriage, that can include the girl's own parents. A complaint may not name a stranger at all, but her own family.

Consider this situation. A police officer gets a call on the eve of a wedding: the bride is 16. If he stops the ceremony, takes an undertaking from the parents and leaves, the girl is safe tonight and nobody is booked. If he files an FIR, it names her father, the elders and the person conducting the ceremony, for an offence that carries at most two years' rigorous imprisonment and a fine of up to Rs 1 lakh, with no minimum sentence [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. On 2024's numbers, the trial is three times as likely to end in acquittal as in conviction. The Supreme Court itself observed that the absence of a minimum sentence has weakened enforcement [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]].

The law's design gives families room too. A child marriage is not automatically void: only the person who was a child can ask a district court to annul it, and only until two years after reaching adulthood [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. The Act says nothing about betrothals; the Supreme Court urged Parliament to consider outlawing them, because they can be used to evade the law [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Prosecution or prevention?

The Supreme Court's answer is prevention first. Its October 2024 guidelines put "prevention before protection and protection before penalisation", and warn that enforcement "must not be solely focused on increasing prosecutions" [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. They direct states to appoint district Child Marriage Prohibition Officers with no other duties and publish their quarterly reports online, and tell magistrates to stop child marriages with injunctions on their own, especially around "auspicious days" for mass weddings [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]].

That is the right order. A wedding stopped is worth more than a conviction afterwards, because a conviction does not unmarry a girl. But prevention still needs a record. If 4,440 cases in Telangana led to 149 FIRs, someone should be able to say what happened to the other girls: whether their weddings were stopped for good, or simply moved to another date and another district. The quarterly reports were meant to make that visible. Whether your state publishes them is something you can check.

A law that is never used tells families that nobody is watching. A law used only to punish teaches them to hide the wedding. The Supreme Court asked for neither. It asked states to show their work.
child-marriage-law-fir-gap.hg:
Telangana ne Supreme Court ko bataya ki usne teen saal mein 4,440 child marriage cases record kiye, aur 149 FIR darj ki [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. 2024 mein poore India mein police ne Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 ke tahat 1,499 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]], jabki 2023-24 mein survey ki gayi 20-24 saal ki 20.1% women ki shaadi 18 se pehle ho chuki thi [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Is Act ka har offence cognisable aur non-bailable hai [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. Phir bhi iska istemaal na ke barabar hota hai. Yeh investigation poochhti hai ki aisa kyun hai, aur kya zyada FIR hi iska jawab hain.

## 1,499 FIR, jabki har paanch mein se ek young woman ki shaadi bachpan mein hui

UNICEF India ka estimate hai ki India mein har saal 18 se kam umar ki kam se kam 1.5 million ladkiyon ki shaadi hoti hai, haalanki uska page yeh nahi batata ki yeh estimate kaise nikala gaya [[unicef-india-end-child-marriage]]. Is Act ke tahat police registrations 2022 mein 1,002, 2023 mein 6,038 aur 2024 mein 1,499 rahe [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Agar woh estimate kaafi galat bhi nikle, tab bhi registered cases uska ek bahut chhota hissa hain.

Courts ne isse bhi kam kiya. 2024 mein is Act ke 209 cases conviction par khatam hue aur 625 acquittal par, yaani conviction rate 25.0% raha, aur saal ke ant mein 8,553 cases trial mein pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jo trials poore hue, unmein har chaar mein se teen bina conviction ke khatam hue.

Ek caveat ulti disha mein kaam karta hai. NCRB har FIR ko ek hi baar ginta hai, uske sabse gambhir offence ke under [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Supreme Court ke 2017 ke Independent Thought ruling ke baad se, 18 se kam umar ki patni ke saath sex rape hai [[sc-independent-thought-2017]]. Isliye jis child marriage mein pati ne ladki ke saath sex kiya ho, uski FIR is Act ke bajaye POCSO, yaani child sexual abuse law, ke under gini ja sakti hai. Child marriage se judi FIR ki asli sankhya shayad 1,499 se zyada hai; kitni zyada, yeh tables nahi dikhati.

## States ne Supreme Court ko kya bataya

18 October 2024 ko, Society for Enlightenment and Voluntary Action ke laaye case mein, Supreme Court ne woh figures saamne rakhe jo states ne use pichhle teen saal ke liye diye the [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]:

| State | Report hue child marriage cases | FIR |
|---|---|---|
| Tamil Nadu | 8,966 | 2,392 |
| Telangana | 4,440 | 149 |
| Andhra Pradesh | lagbhag 3,400, jinmein se zyadatar roki gayi shaadiyan | 10 |
| Maharashtra | 2,043 shaadiyan roki gayi | 178 |

States alag-alag tareeke se ginte hain, isliye yeh koi league table nahi hai. Inmein se kai "cases" woh shaadiyan thi jo time par rok di gayi, aur jinke liye shayad FIR ki zaroorat hi na ho.

Phir bhi, ek hi law ne, lagbhag ek jaise periods mein, Tamil Nadu mein mote taur par har chaar mein se ek case mein FIR karwai, Telangana mein lagbhag har 30 mein se ek mein, aur Andhra Pradesh mein lagbhag 3,400 mein se 10 mein. Court ne Maharashtra ke numbers ko "limited legal follow-through" ka sanket maana, yaani kanooni karwai aage nahi badhi [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]].

## Assam 2023: ek state ka spike, phir giravat

Haal ke saalon ka akela national spike ek hi state se aaya. 2023 mein poore India mein register hue 6,038 cases mein se 5,267 Assam ne register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. 2024 mein Assam ne 471 register kiye, aur national total wapas 1,499 par aa gaya [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Jo ginti ek saal mein chhah guna uchhal jaaye aur agle saal wapas gir jaaye, woh police ke faislon ko naap rahi hai, shaadiyon ko nahi. West Bengal (36.4%) aur Bihar (34.6%) mein bachpan mein byaahi gayi young women ka share India mein sabse zyada hai [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]], phir bhi 2024 mein sabse zyada cases Assam (471) aur Tamil Nadu (408) mein register hue, in dono mein se kisi mein nahi [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Kya Assam ke 2023 ke cases ne child marriages roki? Abhi koi nahi keh sakta. NFHS-6, 20-24 saal ki women ko ginta hai, aur woh sab 2022 ke ant tak 18 ki ho chuki thi, isliye uske figures ki har child marriage 2023 se pehle hui thi. Assam ka survey rate gira zaroor, 2023-24 mein 25.3% tak [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]], lekin yeh giravat cases darj hone se pehle hi shuru ho chuki thi. Iska jawab koi baad ka survey hi dega.

## Police aur parivaar is law se kyun bachte hain

Shuruaat isse kijiye ki accused kaun hote hain. Yeh Act adult dulhe ko, child marriage karwane wale ko, aur use promote ya permit karne wale har vyakti ko saza deta hai [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. Arranged child marriage mein ismein ladki ke apne maa-baap bhi aa sakte hain. Complaint mein shayad kisi ajnabi ka nahi, balki uske apne parivaar ka naam aaye.

Is situation ko sochiye. Shaadi se ek raat pehle ek police officer ko call aata hai: dulhan 16 saal ki hai. Agar woh ceremony rokta hai, maa-baap se undertaking leta hai aur chala jaata hai, toh ladki aaj raat safe hai aur kisi par case nahi banta. Agar woh FIR darj karta hai, toh usmein ladki ke pita, ghar ke bade aur ceremony karwane wale ka naam aata hai, ek aise offence ke liye jiski saza zyada se zyada do saal ki rigorous imprisonment aur Rs 1 lakh tak ka fine hai, aur jismein koi minimum sentence nahi hai [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. 2024 ke numbers ke hisaab se, trial ke acquittal par khatam hone ke chances conviction se teen guna hain. Supreme Court ne khud kaha ki minimum sentence na hone se enforcement kamzor hua hai [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]].

Law ka design bhi parivaaron ko jagah deta hai. Child marriage apne aap void nahi hoti: sirf woh vyakti jo shaadi ke waqt child tha, district court se use annul karwane ki maang kar sakta hai, aur woh bhi adult hone ke sirf do saal baad tak [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. Act betrothal, yaani sagai, ke baare mein kuch nahi kehta; Supreme Court ne Parliament se kaha ki woh sagai ko gair-kanooni banane par vichaar kare, kyunki iska istemaal law se bachne ke liye ho sakta hai [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Prosecution ya prevention?

Supreme Court ka jawab hai: pehle prevention. Uski October 2024 ki guidelines "prevention before protection and protection before penalisation" ko priority deti hain, aur warn karti hain ki enforcement "must not be solely focused on increasing prosecutions" [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. Yaani pehle rokna, phir bachana, phir saza dena; aur sirf prosecutions badhana maqsad nahi ho sakta. Guidelines states ko direct karti hain ki woh har district mein aise Child Marriage Prohibition Officers appoint karein jinke paas koi aur duty na ho, aur unki quarterly reports online publish karein. Magistrates se woh kehti hain ki khud pehal karke injunctions se child marriages rokein, khaas kar mass weddings ke "auspicious days" ke aas-paas [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]].

Yahi sahi kram hai. Roki gayi shaadi baad ki conviction se zyada keemti hai, kyunki conviction kisi ladki ki shaadi ko wapas nahi palat sakti. Lekin prevention ko bhi record chahiye. Agar Telangana mein 4,440 cases se 149 FIR nikli, toh kisi ko yeh bata paana chahiye ki baaki ladkiyon ka kya hua: unki shaadiyan hamesha ke liye ruki, ya bas kisi aur date aur kisi aur district mein shift ho gayi. Quarterly reports isi ko saamne laane ke liye thi. Aapka state unhe publish karta hai ya nahi, yeh aap khud check kar sakte hain.

Jis law ka kabhi istemaal hi nahi hota, woh parivaaron ko batata hai ki koi dekh nahi raha. Jis law ka istemaal sirf saza dene ke liye hota hai, woh unhe shaadi chhupana sikhata hai. Supreme Court ne in dono mein se kuch nahi maanga. Usne states se kaha ki woh apna kaam dikhayein.

child-marriage-map-nfhs6-states.en:
India's headline figure is 20.1%: one in five women aged 20-24 surveyed in 2023-24 had been married before 18, down from 23.3% in 2019-21, according to provisional fact sheets from the sixth National Family Health Survey (NFHS-6) [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. But an average is not a map. In Kerala and Lakshadweep the figure is 2.9%; in West Bengal it is 36.4% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Where a girl is born, and whether she grows up in a village or a town, still decides a great deal about whether she will be married as a child.

## The hotspot belt: Bengal, Bihar, Tripura, Jharkhand

The six states with the highest figures all stand well above the national average. Five of them run across eastern and north-eastern India; the sixth is Andhra Pradesh. Here is the share of women aged 20-24 married before 18 in each, in the last two survey rounds [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]:

| State | NFHS-5 (2019-21) | NFHS-6 (2023-24) |
|---|---|---|
| West Bengal | 41.6% | 36.4% |
| Bihar | 40.8% | 34.6% |
| Tripura | 40.1% | 34.0% |
| Jharkhand | 32.2% | 28.1% |
| Assam | 31.8% | 25.3% |
| Andhra Pradesh | 29.3% | 25.1% |

In 2019-21, West Bengal, Bihar and Tripura were all above 40%. Each has since fallen by roughly five to six percentage points, faster than India as a whole. The fall has not changed their rank, or the basic fact: in each of the three, more than one young woman in three was married as a child. Jharkhand, wedged between Bihar and Bengal, completes the belt.

What sets these states apart? The fact sheets do not say, but one pattern stands out: the same places top a second list. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), the highest shares of women aged 15-19 who had already begun childbearing were in Tripura (21.9%), West Bengal (16.4%), Andhra Pradesh (12.6%), Assam (11.7%) and Bihar (11.0%) [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Five of the six child marriage hotspots of 2023-24 are the five states with the most teenage childbearing in the previous round. Early marriage and early motherhood sit on the same map.

## Assam and Andhra Pradesh: the second tier

Assam (25.3%) and Andhra Pradesh (25.1%) form a second tier, with Rajasthan just behind at 24.6% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Assam's fall, from 31.8% to 25.3%, is the steepest of the six. Andhra Pradesh, the only southern state on the list, also had the third-highest rate of teenage childbearing in 2019-21 [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

The second tier matters too. A state where about one young woman in four was married as a child is not a success because its neighbour is worse.

## Villages and cities: 23.3% against 11.4%

Across India, 23.3% of rural women aged 20-24 had married before 18, against 11.4% in towns and cities [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Village India in 2023-24 stands exactly where India as a whole stood in 2019-21, when the national figure was also 23.3%.

Inside the hotspot states the gap is starker. In rural West Bengal, 41.5% of young women had married before 18; in the state's towns and cities, 21.7% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Consider two cousins born in the same year in West Bengal, one in a village and one in a town. On these numbers, the village girl is about twice as likely to have been married as a child, and even the town girl's odds are worse than the national average.

## Married by 15: the 4.8% at the sharpest end

The under-18 measure hides a harder number. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 4.8% of Indian women aged 20-24 had been married by 15 [[nfhs5-india-report-2021]], about one young woman in 20. These are girls married before they would have sat a Class 10 board exam.

There is nothing grey about these marriages in law. Since the Supreme Court's 2017 Independent Thought judgment, sex with a wife under 18 is rape [[sc-independent-thought-2017]]. A wedding does not make a 14-year-old an adult; it moves her into the home of a man the law treats as an offender if he has sex with her.

## What has moved the numbers where they fell

All six hotspot states fell between the two rounds, as did India as a whole. The survey does not say why, and three cautions apply: the NFHS-6 figures are provisional, the urban sampling frame changed from NFHS-5, and small states have small samples [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

The fall was not universal either. The share rose in eight states and union territories, including Nagaland (5.6% to 10.2%), Himachal Pradesh (5.4% to 7.9%), Delhi (9.9% to 11.4%) and Punjab (8.7% to 10.2%) [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Some of those rises may be within the margin of error. They deserve scrutiny, not silence.

The survey also looks backwards. Every woman in NFHS-6's 20-24 age group had turned 18 by the end of 2022, so every marriage it counts took place before 2023. Nothing done since, including the Supreme Court's October 2024 guidelines on enforcing the child marriage law [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]], can be credited with these falls.

What can? Worldwide, UN Women attributes the faster decline of the past decade largely to girls' education, economic empowerment and poverty reduction [[unwomen-gender-snapshot-2026]]. Police action is not on its list. Nor do Indian police records follow this map: in 2024 the most cases under the child marriage law were registered in Assam (471) and Tamil Nadu (408) [[ncrb-cii-2024]], and Tamil Nadu is not among the seven states with the highest survey rates.

The map's lesson is concentration. A national figure falling by a few points can sit beside villages in West Bengal where four in ten young women were married as children. Protection has to go where the map is darkest, and it has to arrive before the wedding. For a girl already married, the law offers a way out: she can ask a district court to annul the marriage until two years after she turns 18 [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. This is general information, not legal advice.
child-marriage-map-nfhs6-states.hg:
India ka headline figure 20.1% hai: 2023-24 mein survey ki gayi 20-24 saal ki har paanch mein se ek woman ki shaadi 18 se pehle ho chuki thi, jabki 2019-21 mein yeh 23.3% tha. Yeh sixth National Family Health Survey (NFHS-6) ki provisional fact sheets se aata hai [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Lekin average koi naksha nahi hota. Kerala aur Lakshadweep mein yeh figure 2.9% hai; West Bengal mein 36.4% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Ladki kahan paida hoti hai, aur gaon mein badi hoti hai ya shehar mein, yeh aaj bhi kaafi had tak tay karta hai ki uski shaadi bachpan mein hogi ya nahi.

## Hotspot belt: Bengal, Bihar, Tripura, Jharkhand

Sabse oonche figures wale chhah states national average se kaafi upar hain. Inmein se paanch eastern aur north-eastern India mein hain; chhatha Andhra Pradesh hai. Neeche har state mein 20-24 saal ki un women ka share hai jinki shaadi 18 se pehle hui, pichhle do survey rounds mein [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]:

| State | NFHS-5 (2019-21) | NFHS-6 (2023-24) |
|---|---|---|
| West Bengal | 41.6% | 36.4% |
| Bihar | 40.8% | 34.6% |
| Tripura | 40.1% | 34.0% |
| Jharkhand | 32.2% | 28.1% |
| Assam | 31.8% | 25.3% |
| Andhra Pradesh | 29.3% | 25.1% |

2019-21 mein West Bengal, Bihar aur Tripura teeno 40% se upar the. Tab se har ek mein lagbhag paanch se chhah percentage points ki giravat aayi hai, jo poore India ki giravat se tez hai. Lekin isse na unki rank badli, na buniyaadi sach: teeno states mein har teen mein se ek se zyada young woman ki shaadi bachpan mein hui thi. Bihar aur Bengal ke beech basa Jharkhand is belt ko poora karta hai.

In states ko baaki se alag kya banata hai? Fact sheets yeh nahi batati, lekin ek pattern saaf dikhta hai: wahi jagahein ek doosri list mein bhi sabse upar hain. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein 15-19 saal ki un women ka share, jo childbearing shuru kar chuki thi, sabse zyada Tripura (21.9%), West Bengal (16.4%), Andhra Pradesh (12.6%), Assam (11.7%) aur Bihar (11.0%) mein tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. 2023-24 ke chhah child marriage hotspots mein se paanch wahi states hain jahan pichhle round mein teenage childbearing sabse zyada thi. Jaldi shaadi aur jaldi maa banna, dono ek hi nakshe par baithe hain.

## Assam aur Andhra Pradesh: doosra tier

Assam (25.3%) aur Andhra Pradesh (25.1%) doosra tier banate hain, aur Rajasthan 24.6% ke saath thoda hi peeche hai [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Assam ki giravat, 31.8% se 25.3%, in chhah states mein sabse tez hai. Andhra Pradesh, is list ka akela southern state, 2019-21 mein teenage childbearing mein bhi teesre number par tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Doosra tier bhi maayne rakhta hai. Jis state mein lagbhag har chaar mein se ek young woman ki shaadi bachpan mein hui, woh sirf isliye success nahi ban jaata ki uska padosi usse bhi bura hai.

## Gaon aur shehar: 23.3% vs 11.4%

Poore India mein gaon ki 20-24 saal ki 23.3% women ki shaadi 18 se pehle hui thi, jabki towns aur cities mein 11.4% ki [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Yaani 2023-24 ka gaon wala India theek wahin khada hai jahan 2019-21 mein poora India tha, jab national figure bhi 23.3% tha.

Hotspot states ke andar yeh gap aur bhi bada hai. Rural West Bengal mein 41.5% young women ki shaadi 18 se pehle hui thi; state ke towns aur cities mein 21.7% ki [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Sochiye, West Bengal mein ek hi saal paida hui do cousins, ek gaon mein aur ek town mein. In numbers ke hisaab se gaon wali ladki ki shaadi bachpan mein hone ke chances lagbhag dugne hain, aur town wali ladki ke chances bhi national average se zyada hain.

## 15 tak shaadi: sabse sakht kinare par 4.8%

18 se pehle wala measure ek aur sakht number chhupa leta hai. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein 20-24 saal ki 4.8% Indian women ki shaadi 15 saal tak ho chuki thi [[nfhs5-india-report-2021]], yaani lagbhag har 20 mein se ek. Yeh woh ladkiyan hain jinki shaadi Class 10 ka board exam dene se bhi pehle ho gayi.

Law mein in shaadiyon ke baare mein kuch bhi grey nahi hai. Supreme Court ke 2017 ke Independent Thought judgment ke baad se, 18 se kam umar ki patni ke saath sex rape hai [[sc-independent-thought-2017]]. Shaadi kisi 14 saal ki ladki ko adult nahi bana deti; woh use ek aise aadmi ke ghar pahuncha deti hai jise law offender maanta hai agar woh uske saath sex kare.

## Jahan numbers gire, wahan unhe kisne hilaaya

Chhah ke chhah hotspot states mein dono rounds ke beech giravat aayi, aur poore India mein bhi. Survey yeh nahi batata ki kyun, aur teen saavdhaaniyan zaroori hain: NFHS-6 ke figures provisional hain, urban sampling frame NFHS-5 se badal gaya hai, aur chhote states ke samples chhote hain [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

Giravat har jagah aayi bhi nahi. Aath states aur union territories mein share badha, jinmein Nagaland (5.6% se 10.2%), Himachal Pradesh (5.4% se 7.9%), Delhi (9.9% se 11.4%) aur Punjab (8.7% se 10.2%) shaamil hain [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Inmein se kuch badhotri margin of error ke andar ho sakti hai. Phir bhi in par sawaal uthne chahiye, chuppi nahi.

Survey peeche ki taraf bhi dekhta hai. NFHS-6 ke 20-24 age group ki har woman 2022 ke ant tak 18 saal ki ho chuki thi, isliye yeh jo bhi shaadi ginta hai, woh 2023 se pehle hui thi. Uske baad jo kuch hua, Supreme Court ki October 2024 wali guidelines samet jo child marriage law ko lagu karne ke liye di gayi thi [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]], use in giravaton ka credit nahi diya ja sakta.

Toh credit kise jaata hai? Duniya bhar ke liye UN Women pichhle dashak ki tez giravat ka zyadatar credit ladkiyon ki padhai, economic empowerment aur gareebi kam hone ko deta hai [[unwomen-gender-snapshot-2026]]. Police action is list mein nahi hai. Aur Indian police records bhi is nakshe ke hisaab se nahi chalte: 2024 mein child marriage law ke tahat sabse zyada cases Assam (471) aur Tamil Nadu (408) mein register hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]], jabki Tamil Nadu survey ke sabse oonche rates wale saat states mein bhi nahi hai.

Is nakshe ka sabak hai concentration. Kuch points girta hua national figure West Bengal ke un gaon ke saath-saath khada ho sakta hai jahan das mein se chaar young women ki shaadi bachpan mein hui thi. Suraksha wahan pahunchni chahiye jahan naksha sabse gehra hai, aur shaadi se pehle pahunchni chahiye. Jis ladki ki shaadi ho chuki hai, uske liye law ek raasta deta hai: woh 18 ki hone ke do saal ke andar district court se shaadi annul karwane ki maang kar sakti hai [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

child-marriage-only-poor-states-myth.en:
Ask in a Delhi office or a Chandigarh college where child marriage happens, and the usual answer points somewhere else: a poor state, a remote village, a family without schooling. The newest national data does not fit that map. In the provisional fact sheets of the National Family Health Survey 2023-24 (NFHS-6), 20.1% of Indian women aged 20-24 said they had married before 18, down from 23.3% in 2019-21 [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. But in eight states and union territories the share went up, and the list includes the national capital.

## The myth: a problem of poverty and remote villages

The myth has a true core. Child marriage is far more common in some states than in others. West Bengal (36.4%), Bihar (34.6%), Tripura (34.0%), Jharkhand (28.1%), Assam (25.3%) and Andhra Pradesh (25.1%) had the highest shares in 2023-24, while Kerala and Lakshadweep had the lowest, at 2.9% each [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Villages remain worse than cities: 23.3% of rural women aged 20-24 had married before 18, against 11.4% of urban women [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

Even the top of the list does not match the stereotype neatly. It includes Andhra Pradesh in the south, while Rajasthan comes seventh [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

The national curve has also bent a long way. The share was 47.4% in 2005-06, 26.8% in 2015-16, 23.3% in 2019-21 and 20.1% in 2023-24 [[ceda-genderstats-underage-marriage-2021]]. Gains like that make it easy to believe the problem is shrinking into a few distant pockets.

## The truth: rises in Delhi, Punjab, Himachal and Nagaland

Against the national fall, the share rose in eight states and union territories between NFHS-5 (2019-21) and NFHS-6 (2023-24) [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]:

| Place | 2019-21 | 2023-24 |
|---|---|---|
| Delhi | 9.9% | 11.4% |
| Punjab | 8.7% | 10.2% |
| Himachal Pradesh | 5.4% | 7.9% |
| Nagaland | 5.6% | 10.2% |

The other four were Goa, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh and Lakshadweep [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

These are not the places the myth points to. Delhi is the national capital. Punjab and Himachal Pradesh are rarely described as poor or backward. Yet in 2023-24, about one young woman in nine in Delhi, and one in ten in Punjab, had been married as a child. Delhi's share is nearly four times Kerala's.

## Cities are not immune: the 11.4% urban figure

The urban number deserves more attention than it gets. In 2023-24, 11.4% of women aged 20-24 living in India's towns and cities had married before 18 [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. That is roughly one in nine. It is half the rural rate, but it is not a rounding error. It is exactly Delhi's figure, and higher than Punjab's.

Consider a hypothetical. A 16-year-old in a Delhi colony talks to a boy her parents do not approve of. Over the summer holidays, a wedding is fixed with a family from their home district. Her school sees a girl who did not come back after Class 10. The neighbours see a family function. Nobody uses the words "child marriage", because that is supposed to happen somewhere else.

The survey does not record why families marry daughters early, so these figures cannot say what is driving the rises. What they do show is that living in a city, or in a state outside the usual list, has not ended the practice.

## Reading a provisional survey: samples and margins

Honest reading needs three cautions. First, these are provisional fact sheets, not the final survey report. Second, small states and union territories have small samples and wide margins of error, so rises there may not be statistically significant [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Nagaland's near-doubling and Lakshadweep's rise could partly be sampling noise. Third, the survey changed how it samples urban areas after NFHS-5, which makes comparing city figures across rounds harder [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

So which rises look solid? None can yet be called certain. But two features make the northern rises hard to wave away. Delhi and Punjab are not small union territories like Lakshadweep or Ladakh, where the survey itself warns that samples are small. And five of the eight places that rose (Delhi, Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh) are in north India, all moving the same way while the country moved the other. A single jump can be chance; a regional pattern is a warning.

The survey also looks backwards: women aged 20-24 were describing weddings from years earlier, when they were under 18. Whatever pushed these numbers up was already happening then.

## Why this myth delays action

A myth about where a harm happens decides where help is sent. If child marriage is "a village problem", a Delhi school counsellor does not ask why a Class 10 girl stopped coming, and a neighbour in Ludhiana does not call anyone.

The law draws no such line. In October 2024 the Supreme Court directed states to appoint district Child Marriage Prohibition Officers with no other duties and to publish their quarterly reports online [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. That covers Delhi, Punjab and Himachal Pradesh as much as Bihar. Yet police across India registered just 1,499 cases under the child marriage law in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], in a country where one young woman in five had been married as a child.

The places where the share is rising have schools, hospitals, police stations and phones within reach. What is missing is the belief that it could happen there. Drop the myth first. Then make the call, to 1098 or 112, before the wedding date rather than after it.
child-marriage-only-poor-states-myth.hg:
Delhi ke kisi office ya Chandigarh ke kisi college mein poochiye ki child marriage kahan hoti hai, toh jawaab aksar kahin aur ishaara karta hai: koi gareeb state, koi door ka gaon, koi family jahan padhai-likhai nahi hui. Sabse naya national data is naqshe mein fit nahi baithta. National Family Health Survey 2023-24 (NFHS-6) ki provisional fact sheets mein 20-24 saal ki 20.1% Indian women ne bataya ki unki shaadi 18 se pehle hui thi, jo 2019-21 ke 23.3% se kam hai [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Lekin aath states aur union territories mein yeh hissa badha, aur is list mein desh ki rajdhani bhi hai.

## Myth: gareebi aur door-daraz gaon ki problem

Is myth mein sach ka ek hissa hai. Kuch states mein child marriage baaki states se kahin zyada hoti hai. 2023-24 mein sabse zyada hissa West Bengal (36.4%), Bihar (34.6%), Tripura (34.0%), Jharkhand (28.1%), Assam (25.3%) aur Andhra Pradesh (25.1%) mein tha, jabki sabse kam Kerala aur Lakshadweep mein, dono jagah 2.9% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Gaon ab bhi shehron se peeche hain: gaon ki 20-24 saal ki 23.3% women ki shaadi 18 se pehle hui thi, jabki shehar ki 11.4% ki [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

Lekin list ka top bhi stereotype se poori tarah match nahi karta. Usmein south ka Andhra Pradesh hai, jabki Rajasthan saatve number pe aata hai [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

Desh ka curve bhi kaafi neeche aaya hai. Yeh hissa 2005-06 mein 47.4% tha, 2015-16 mein 26.8%, 2019-21 mein 23.3% aur 2023-24 mein 20.1% [[ceda-genderstats-underage-marriage-2021]]. Itni badi giravat ke baad yeh maan lena aasaan hai ki problem simat kar kuch door ke kono mein reh gayi hai.

## Sach: Delhi, Punjab, Himachal aur Nagaland mein badhat

Desh bhar ki giravat ke ulat, NFHS-5 (2019-21) aur NFHS-6 (2023-24) ke beech aath states aur union territories mein yeh hissa badha [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]:

| Jagah | 2019-21 | 2023-24 |
|---|---|---|
| Delhi | 9.9% | 11.4% |
| Punjab | 8.7% | 10.2% |
| Himachal Pradesh | 5.4% | 7.9% |
| Nagaland | 5.6% | 10.2% |

Baaki chaar the Goa, Jammu aur Kashmir, Ladakh aur Lakshadweep [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

Yeh woh jagahein nahi hain jinki taraf myth ishaara karta hai. Delhi desh ki rajdhani hai. Punjab aur Himachal Pradesh ko shayad hi kabhi gareeb ya pichhda state kaha jaata hai. Phir bhi 2023-24 mein Delhi ki lagbhag har nau mein se ek, aur Punjab ki har das mein se ek young woman ki shaadi bachpan mein ho chuki thi. Delhi ka hissa Kerala se lagbhag chaar guna hai.

## Shehar bhi bache nahi hain: 11.4% ka urban figure

Urban number pe jitni baat hoti hai, usse kahin zyada honi chahiye. 2023-24 mein India ke towns aur cities mein rehne wali 20-24 saal ki 11.4% women ki shaadi 18 se pehle hui thi [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Yaani lagbhag har nau mein se ek. Yeh gaon ke rate ka aadha hai, lekin koi chhoti-moti ginti nahi. Yeh bilkul Delhi ka figure hai, aur Punjab se zyada.

Ek hypothetical sochiye. Delhi ki ek colony mein 16 saal ki ek ladki ek ladke se baat karti hai jo uske parents ko pasand nahi. Garmiyon ki chhuttiyon mein unke apne gaon-district ki ek family ke saath uski shaadi tay ho jaati hai. School ko bas itna dikhta hai ki ladki Class 10 ke baad wapas nahi aayi. Padosiyon ko ek family function dikhta hai. Koi "child marriage" shabd istemaal nahi karta, kyunki woh toh kahin aur hoti hai.

Survey yeh record nahi karta ki families betiyon ki shaadi jaldi kyun karti hain, isliye yeh figures nahi bata sakte ki badhat ke peeche kya hai. Lekin itna zaroor dikhate hain ki shehar mein rehna, ya usual list se bahar ke state mein rehna, is practice ko khatam nahi kar paaya.

## Provisional survey ko kaise padhein: sample aur margins

Imaandaari se padhne ke liye teen saavdhaaniyan zaroori hain. Pehli, yeh provisional fact sheets hain, final survey report nahi. Doosri, chhote states aur union territories ke samples chhote hote hain aur margins of error bade, isliye wahan ki badhat statistically significant na bhi ho [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Nagaland ka lagbhag dugna hona aur Lakshadweep ki badhat kuch had tak sampling ka shor ho sakti hai. Teesri, NFHS-5 ke baad survey ne shehri ilaakon ka sample chunne ka tareeka badla, jisse dono rounds ke city figures ki tulna mushkil ho jaati hai [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

Toh kaunsi badhat pakki lagti hai? Abhi kisi ko bhi pakka nahi kaha ja sakta. Lekin do baatein north ki badhat ko nazarandaaz karna mushkil banati hain. Delhi aur Punjab, Lakshadweep ya Ladakh jaise chhote union territories nahi hain, jahan survey khud warning deta hai ki samples chhote hain. Aur jin aath jagahon pe hissa badha, unmein se paanch (Delhi, Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu aur Kashmir, aur Ladakh) north India mein hain, sab ek hi disha mein ja rahe the jabki desh doosri disha mein. Ek akeli chhalaang ittefaq ho sakti hai; poore ilaake ka pattern ek warning hai.

Survey peeche ki taraf bhi dekhta hai: 20-24 saal ki women saalon pehle ki shaadiyon ki baat kar rahi thi, jab woh 18 se chhoti thi. In numbers ko jo bhi upar dhakel raha tha, woh tab bhi ho raha tha.

## Yeh myth action ko kaise rokta hai

Koi nuksaan kahan hota hai, is baare mein bana myth hi tay karta hai ki madad kahan bheji jaaye. Agar child marriage "gaon ki problem" hai, toh Delhi ka school counsellor yeh nahi poochta ki Class 10 ki ladki ne aana kyun band kar diya, aur Ludhiana ka padosi kisi ko call nahi karta.

Law aisi koi lakeer nahi kheenchta. October 2024 mein Supreme Court ne states ko direction di ki woh district level pe aise Child Marriage Prohibition Officers appoint karein jinka koi aur kaam na ho, aur unki quarterly reports online publish karein [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. Yeh Delhi, Punjab aur Himachal Pradesh pe utna hi laagu hota hai jitna Bihar pe. Phir bhi 2024 mein poore India ki police ne child marriage law ke tahat sirf 1,499 cases darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]], us desh mein jahan har paanch mein se ek young woman ki shaadi bachpan mein ho chuki thi.

Jin jagahon pe yeh hissa badh raha hai, wahan school, hospital, police station aur phone sab paas hain. Kami hai toh bas is yakeen ki ki yeh wahan bhi ho sakta hai. Pehle myth chhodiye. Phir call kijiye, 1098 ya 112 pe, shaadi ki date ke baad nahi, usse pehle.

child-marriage-valid-until-challenged.en:
India's child marriage law contains a contradiction most families never hear about. Performing a child marriage is a crime. The marriage itself usually is not cancelled. It stays valid until the person married as a child goes to court to undo it, and that door closes two years after she becomes an adult. This explainer walks through the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, clause by clause. It is general information, not legal advice.

## Offence and marriage: why both can be true at once

The Act defines a child as a man under 21 or a woman under 18, and a child marriage as one in which either party is a child [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. Performing or promoting such a marriage is an offence. But the law treats the wedding and the marriage separately: the wedding can be punished, while the marriage it creates usually stays legally valid until someone challenges it.

In 2023-24, 20.1% of women aged 20-24 said they had married before 18 [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. In 2024, police across the country registered 1,499 cases under the Act [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Most child marriages never become a case, and nothing in the law ends them on its own.

## Voidable, not void: the two-year window

Section 3 makes every child marriage "voidable at the option of the contracting party who was a child at the time of the marriage". Only that person can petition a district court to annul it, and only "before the child filing the petition completes two years of attaining majority" [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. Majority is 18, so the window closes at 20.

There are exceptions. A child marriage is void from the start if the child was taken or enticed away, forced or deceived into it, or sold for marriage, or was sold, trafficked or used for immoral purposes after it [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. It is also void if it was held in breach of a court injunction [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. Outside these situations, the marriage stands.

Think about whom this rule asks to act. Imagine a girl married at 16 who turns 18 in her husband's family home. She may have left school, have a baby and have no money of her own. To end the marriage she must, before she turns 20, find a lawyer and file a case against a marriage her own parents arranged. If she misses the deadline, this Act's route to annulment is closed to her. The Act puts the work of undoing a child marriage on the person it was meant to protect.

## Two years, no minimum: the penalties

The Act punishes three groups: an adult man who marries a child; anyone who performs, conducts, directs or abets a child marriage; and anyone who promotes or permits one, parents included. The maximum for all three is two years' rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs 1 lakh, with no minimum sentence, and every offence is cognisable and non-bailable [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. A court can let the groom off with a fine alone [[indiacode-pcma-2006]], and the Act bars prison for women who promote or permit a child marriage [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]].

In October 2024 the Supreme Court said the lack of a minimum sentence "has led to ineffective enforcement of the PCMA" [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. In 2024, trials under the Act ended in 209 convictions and 625 acquittals, a conviction rate of 25.0%, and 8,553 cases were still pending at the end of the year [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## What the Act leaves out: betrothals and personal laws

The Act says nothing about betrothals. A family can fix a child's marriage years ahead, in public, without breaking it. In its October 2024 judgment the Supreme Court said marriages fixed in childhood violate a child's "free choice, autonomy, agency and childhood", and that Parliament "may consider outlawing child betrothals which may be used to evade penalty under the PCMA" [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. That is a recommendation, not an order.

The second gap is personal law: whether the Act prevails over a community's personal-law rules on marriage. The court did not decide it. It noted that the Prohibition of Child Marriage (Amendment) Bill, 2021, introduced on 21 December 2021, would raise women's minimum age of marriage from 18 to 21 and make the Act override any other law, custom or practice, and called the issue "pending consideration before Parliament" [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. But a Bill pending in the Lok Sabha lapses when the House is dissolved, as the 17th Lok Sabha was in June 2024, and the Bill's current status could not be confirmed.

## Married under 18: what Independent Thought changed

When Parliament raised the age of consent to 18 in 2013, it kept a marital exception for wives aged 15 and above, so from 2013 until 2017 a husband's sex with a 15-to-17-year-old wife was not legally rape [[indiacode-cla-2013]].

On 11 October 2017, in Independent Thought v. Union of India, the Supreme Court read that exception down: sex with a wife under 18 is rape [[sc-independent-thought-2017]]. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which replaced the Indian Penal Code on 1 July 2024, keeps the line. Its marital exception, in Section 63, covers only a wife "not being under eighteen years of age" [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The child sexual abuse law, POCSO, also applies: sexual activity with anyone under 18 is an offence, married or not.

So a girl married at 16 lives inside a marriage the law allows to stand, while the law treats sex within it as a crime against her. She is never the offender. But the ruling helps only if someone tells her, believes her and acts: a teacher, a doctor, a police officer, a neighbour who calls 1098. The cleaner fix lies with Parliament, in a law that does not wait for a child to undo her own marriage.
child-marriage-valid-until-challenged.hg:
India ke child marriage law mein ek aisa virodhabhaas hai jiske baare mein zyadatar families ne kabhi suna hi nahi. Child marriage karwana crime hai. Lekin shaadi khud aam taur pe cancel nahi hoti. Woh tab tak valid rehti hai jab tak jis insaan ki shaadi bachpan mein hui, woh court jaakar use khatam na karwaye, aur yeh darwaza adult hone ke do saal baad band ho jaata hai. Yeh explainer Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 ko clause by clause samjhata hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Offence aur shaadi: dono ek saath sach kaise

Act ke hisaab se 21 se kam umar ka ladka ya 18 se kam umar ki ladki child hai, aur jis shaadi mein inmein se koi ek child ho, woh child marriage hai [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. Aisi shaadi karwana ya uska badhawa dena offence hai. Lekin law shaadi ki rasm aur shaadi ke rishte ko alag-alag dekhta hai: rasm ke liye saza ho sakti hai, jabki usse bana rishta aam taur pe tab tak legally valid rehta hai jab tak koi use challenge na kare.

2023-24 mein 20-24 saal ki 20.1% women ne bataya ki unki shaadi 18 se pehle hui thi [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. 2024 mein poore desh ki police ne is Act ke tahat 1,499 cases darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Zyadatar child marriages kabhi case nahi banti, aur law mein aisa kuch nahi jo unhe apne aap khatam kar de.

## Voidable, void nahi: do saal ki window

Section 3 har child marriage ko "voidable at the option of the contracting party who was a child at the time of the marriage" banata hai, yaani jo insaan shaadi ke waqt child tha, woh chahe toh use radd karwa sakta hai. Sirf wahi insaan district court mein annulment ki petition daal sakta hai, aur sirf "before the child filing the petition completes two years of attaining majority", yaani adult hone ke do saal poore hone se pehle [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. Majority 18 pe aati hai, isliye yeh window 20 pe band ho jaati hai.

Kuch exceptions hain. Child marriage shuru se hi void hai agar bachche ko bhagaya ya behlaaya gaya, zabardasti ya dhokhe se shaadi karwayi gayi, ya shaadi ke liye becha gaya, ya shaadi ke baad use becha gaya, traffic kiya gaya ya "immoral purposes" ke liye istemaal kiya gaya [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. Agar shaadi court ke injunction ko todkar hui, toh bhi woh void hai [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. In haalaton ke alawa shaadi bani rehti hai.

Sochiye yeh rule kisse action lene ko kehta hai. Ek ladki ki kalpana kijiye jiski shaadi 16 mein hui aur jo apne pati ke ghar mein 18 ki hoti hai. Ho sakta hai uska school chhoot gaya ho, uska ek bachcha ho, aur uske paas apna koi paisa na ho. Shaadi khatam karne ke liye use 20 ki hone se pehle lawyer dhoondhna hoga, aur us shaadi ke khilaaf case karna hoga jo uske apne maa-baap ne karwayi thi. Agar deadline nikal gayi, toh is Act ke tahat annulment ka raasta uske liye band ho jaata hai. Act child marriage ko khatam karne ka bojh usi insaan pe daal deta hai jise bachane ke liye woh bana tha.

## Do saal, koi minimum nahi: sazaayein

Act teen tarah ke logon ko saza deta hai: woh adult mard jo kisi child se shaadi kare; jo bhi child marriage karwaye, chalaye, direct kare ya usmein madad kare; aur jo bhi uska badhawa de ya use hone de, maa-baap samet. Teenon ke liye maximum saza do saal ki rigorous imprisonment aur Rs 1 lakh ka jurmana hai, koi minimum saza nahi hai, aur har offence cognisable aur non-bailable hai [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. Court dulhe ko sirf jurmana lagakar chhod sakti hai [[indiacode-pcma-2006]], aur jo women shaadi ka badhawa deti hain ya use hone deti hain, unhe Act jail nahi bhejne deta [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]].

October 2024 mein Supreme Court ne likha ki minimum saza na hone se is law ka enforcement kamzor raha: "has led to ineffective enforcement of the PCMA" [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. 2024 mein is Act ke trials 209 convictions aur 625 acquittals pe khatam hue, yaani conviction rate 25.0%, aur saal ke end tak 8,553 cases ab bhi pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Act mein kya chhoot gaya: sagaai aur personal laws

Act sagaai yaani betrothal ke baare mein kuch nahi kehta. Koi family saalon pehle, sabke saamne, bachche ki shaadi tay kar sakti hai, aur koi law nahi tootta. October 2024 ke apne judgment mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki bachpan mein tay ki gayi shaadiyan bachche ki "free choice, autonomy, agency and childhood" ka ulanghan karti hain, aur Parliament "may consider outlawing child betrothals which may be used to evade penalty under the PCMA", yaani Parliament child betrothals ko ban karne pe vichaar kar sakti hai, kyunki inka istemaal saza se bachne ke liye ho sakta hai [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. Yeh ek sujhaav hai, order nahi.

Doosri kami personal law ki hai: kya yeh Act shaadi se jude kisi community ke personal-law rules se upar hai? Court ne iska faisla nahi kiya. Usne note kiya ki Prohibition of Child Marriage (Amendment) Bill, 2021, jo 21 December 2021 ko pesh hua, women ki shaadi ki minimum umar 18 se badhakar 21 karta aur Act ko har doosre law, custom ya practice se upar rakhta, aur kaha ki yeh mudda "pending consideration before Parliament" hai [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. Lekin Lok Sabha mein pending Bill House dissolve hone pe lapse ho jaata hai, aur 17th Lok Sabha June 2024 mein dissolve hui thi; Bill ka abhi ka status confirm nahi ho saka.

## 18 se pehle shaadi: Independent Thought ne kya badla

Jab Parliament ne 2013 mein age of consent 18 kiya, tab usne 15 ya usse zyada umar ki patniyon ke liye marital exception bana rehne diya. Isliye 2013 se 2017 tak 15 se 17 saal ki patni ke saath pati ka sex legally rape nahi maana jaata tha [[indiacode-cla-2013]].

11 October 2017 ko Independent Thought v. Union of India case mein Supreme Court ne us exception ko read down kiya: 18 se kam umar ki patni ke saath sex rape hai [[sc-independent-thought-2017]]. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), jisne 1 July 2024 se Indian Penal Code ki jagah li, yahi lakeer rakhti hai. Section 63 mein uska marital exception sirf us patni pe laagu hota hai jo "not being under eighteen years of age" ho, yaani 18 se kam na ho [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Bachchon ke sexual abuse ka law, POCSO, bhi laagu hota hai: 18 se kam umar ke kisi bhi insaan ke saath sexual activity offence hai, shaadi ho ya na ho.

Toh 16 mein byahi gayi ladki ek aisi shaadi mein jeeti hai jise law bana rehne deta hai, jabki usi shaadi ke andar sex ko law uske khilaaf crime maanta hai. Woh kabhi offender nahi hai. Lekin yeh ruling tabhi kaam aati hai jab koi use bataye, uski baat maane aur kuch kare: koi teacher, doctor, police officer, ya 1098 pe call karne wala padosi. Asli hal Parliament ke paas hai: aisa law jo kisi bachche ke apni hi shaadi khatam karne ka intezaar na kare.

child-protection-system-map-explained.en:
Consider this situation. A 13-year-old in Bhopal tells her class teacher that the man who comes home to tutor her has been touching her. From that moment the teacher has a legal duty, and the girl's family is about to enter a system of acronyms, offices and deadlines that nobody explains to them. This is the map they are rarely handed. It is general information, not legal advice.

## The first call: 1098, 112 and the police

Anyone can start the chain. The 1098 Child Helpline runs 24x7 under the Centre's Mission Vatsalya scheme, through state and district child-protection staff, and is linked with the 112 emergency system [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]. When its operating procedures were issued in March 2023, it covered 568 districts, 135 railway stations and 11 bus stands, and was to reach every district. Call 112 if a child is in danger right now [[mha-erss]]; call 1098 for any child at risk [[wcd-childline]].

The teacher has no choice about reporting. Under Sections 19 and 21 of POCSO, anyone who knows of a sexual offence against a child must report it to the Special Juvenile Police Unit (SJPU), the police unit for cases involving children, or to the local police. Not reporting can mean up to six months in prison or a fine, and the head of a school or other institution who fails to report abuse by staff faces up to a year [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Police who fail to record the case can be punished under the same section. Once they record it, they must inform the Child Welfare Committee and the Special Court within 24 hours [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

The family can report at any police station, whichever area the abuse happened in, and must get a free copy of the FIR; our Zero FIR guide explains how [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Every hospital, government or private, must treat the child immediately and free of cost, and inform the police [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## The Child Welfare Committee and district child-protection unit

The Child Welfare Committee (CWC) is the district committee for children who need care and protection, and the police must tell it about every POCSO case within 24 hours [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. That makes it the office to press on the child's safety: in our example, whether the tutor can still reach her.

The District Child Protection Unit (DCPU) is the district's child-protection office. Both are funded by Mission Vatsalya, the scheme that replaced Child Protection Services from 2021-22 and also pays for Juvenile Justice Boards, child care institutions such as children's homes, family-based care and the helpline. The Centre pays 60% and most states 40%; in the north-eastern and Himalayan states and Jammu & Kashmir the split is 90:10 [[mwcd-mission-vatsalya-guidelines-2022]]. When a committee or a home is not working, both governments answer for it.

## The Special Court and the Juvenile Justice Board

POCSO cases are tried in a designated Special Court in each district. It must record the child's evidence within 30 days of taking up the case and finish the trial, as far as possible, within one year [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. The trial is held in camera, before a woman judge where practicable, and nothing about it may be published without the court's permission [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Under the central fast-track scheme, 399 courts were hearing only POCSO cases in November 2026 [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]].

If the accused is under 18, the case goes to the Juvenile Justice Board (JJB) instead. For a 16- or 17-year-old accused of what the law calls a "heinous offence", one with a minimum sentence of seven years or more, the Board makes a "preliminary assessment" and can send the case to a Children's Court to be tried as an adult [[gazette-juvenile-justice-act-2015]].

## Money and lawyers: Legal Services Authorities

Help does not depend on winning the case. Under Section 396 of the BNSS, every state must run a victim compensation scheme. The family can apply directly to the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) even if the offender is never traced and no trial takes place, and the authority must finish its inquiry within two months [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Compensation is also possible after an acquittal. Under NALSA's 2018 scheme for women and girls, the limits are 50% higher when the victim is a minor [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]]. The same legal services authorities provide free legal aid, so a family that cannot afford a lawyer can ask for one [[nalsa]].

## Where the chain breaks, and how to push it

On paper, every link has a deadline. In the records, the backlog grows. At the end of 2024, 2,86,903 POCSO cases were waiting for trial, up from 2,62,089 a year earlier and 87.7% of all POCSO cases before the courts that year; another 21,256 were still pending investigation [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB does not say how many of those investigations had passed the two-month mark, and the law sets no consequence when police miss it [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Sometimes the break is inside the system itself. A Tata Institute of Social Sciences audit of Bihar's children's homes, submitted to the state government in April 2018, flagged sexual abuse at several institutions, including a state-funded girls' shelter home in Muzaffarpur [[newslaundry-tiss-audit-bihar-2018]]. There, 34 minor girls had been sexually abused [[sc-handbook-child-rights-2025]]. A child placed in care still needs someone outside the system checking on her.

Families can push each link using the law's own words:

- At the police station, ask for the free copy of the FIR on the spot. If one station refuses, go to another.
- If the police have not updated you on the investigation within 90 days, ask in writing; the BNSS requires that update [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- Ask the CWC in writing what it has decided about the child's safety.
- Apply to the DLSA for compensation and a lawyer now, not after the verdict.
- If any office stalls, call 1098 again, and keep a copy of every letter you send.
child-protection-system-map-explained.hg:
Ek situation sochiye. Bhopal ki ek 13 saal ki ladki apni class teacher ko batati hai ki ghar par tuition padhane aane wala aadmi use galat tarah se chhoota hai. Usi pal se teacher par ek legal duty aa jaati hai, aur ladki ki family ek aise system mein kadam rakhne wali hai jismein acronyms hain, offices hain, deadlines hain, par samjhane wala koi nahi. Yeh wahi map hai jo aisi families ke haath shayad hi kabhi lagta hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Pehla call: 1098, 112 aur police

Yeh chain koi bhi shuru kar sakta hai. 1098 Child Helpline 24x7 chalti hai. Ise Centre ki Mission Vatsalya scheme ke under state aur district ka child-protection staff chalata hai, aur yeh 112 emergency system se judi hai [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]. March 2023 mein jab iske operating procedures aaye, tab yeh 568 districts, 135 railway stations aur 11 bus stands par thi, aur ise har district tak pahunchana tha. Agar bachcha abhi khatre mein hai, toh 112 par call kariye [[mha-erss]]. Kisi bhi bachche par khatra ho, toh 1098 par [[wcd-childline]].

Teacher ke paas "bataun ya na bataun" ka option hi nahi hai. POCSO ke Section 19 aur 21 kehte hain ki jise bhi kisi bachche ke saath sexual offence ka pata hai, use Special Juvenile Police Unit (SJPU), yaani bachchon ke cases dekhne wali police unit, ya local police ko batana hoga. Na batane par chhe mahine tak ki jail ya fine ho sakta hai, aur kisi school ya institution ka head agar apne staff ka kiya abuse report na kare, toh use ek saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Agar police case record na kare, toh us par bhi isi section mein saza ho sakti hai. Case record hone ke 24 ghante ke andar police ko Child Welfare Committee aur Special Court ko batana hota hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Family kisi bhi police station mein report kar sakti hai, chahe incident kisi bhi area mein hua ho, aur use FIR ki copy free milni chahiye. Yeh kaise hota hai, hamare Zero FIR guide mein samjhaya gaya hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Har hospital, sarkari ho ya private, bachche ka ilaaj turant aur free karega, aur police ko khabar dega [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Child Welfare Committee aur District Child Protection Unit

Child Welfare Committee (CWC) district ki woh committee hai jo care aur protection ki zaroorat wale bachchon ke liye bani hai, aur police ko har POCSO case ki khabar 24 ghante ke andar ise deni hoti hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Isliye bachche ki safety ka sawaal yahin zor se uthaiye. Hamari misaal mein sawaal yeh hoga: kya woh tutor ab bhi ladki tak pahunch sakta hai?

District Child Protection Unit (DCPU) district ka child-protection office hai. Dono ka paisa Mission Vatsalya se aata hai. Yeh scheme 2021-22 se purani Child Protection Services scheme ki jagah aayi, aur Juvenile Justice Boards, children's homes jaise child care institutions, family-based care aur helpline ka kharcha bhi uthati hai. Zyadatar states mein 60% paisa Centre deta hai aur 40% state. North-east aur Himalayan states aur Jammu & Kashmir mein yeh split 90:10 hai [[mwcd-mission-vatsalya-guidelines-2022]]. Isliye agar koi committee ya home theek se kaam nahi kar raha, toh jawab dono sarkaron ko dena hai.

## Special Court aur Juvenile Justice Board

POCSO cases ka trial har district ki ek designated Special Court mein hota hai. Court ko case haath mein lene ke 30 din ke andar bachche ka bayan record karna hota hai, aur jahan tak ho sake, ek saal mein trial poora karna hota hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Trial band kamre mein, yaani in camera, hota hai, aur jahan mumkin ho, woman judge ke saamne. Court ki permission ke bina trial ki koi baat publish nahi ki ja sakti [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. November 2026 mein Centre ki fast-track scheme ke 399 courts sirf POCSO cases sun rahe the [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]].

Agar accused 18 se chhota hai, toh case Juvenile Justice Board (JJB) ke paas jaata hai. Agar accused 16 ya 17 saal ka hai aur us par kanoon ki bhasha mein "heinous offence" ka aarop hai, yaani aisa crime jiski minimum saza saat saal ya usse zyada hai, toh Board pehle ek "preliminary assessment" karta hai. Uske baad woh case Children's Court bhej sakta hai, jahan us par adult ki tarah trial chal sakta hai [[gazette-juvenile-justice-act-2015]].

## Paisa aur lawyer: Legal Services Authorities

Madad case jeetne par tiki nahi hai. BNSS ka Section 396 kehta hai ki har state ko victims ke liye compensation scheme chalani hogi. Family seedha District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) mein application de sakti hai, chahe offender kabhi pakda na jaaye aur trial kabhi na ho. Authority ko do mahine mein apni inquiry poori karni hoti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Accused bari ho jaaye, tab bhi compensation mil sakta hai. NALSA ki 2018 wali scheme, jo women aur girls ke liye hai, kehti hai ki victim minor ho toh compensation ki limit 50% zyada hoti hai [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]]. Yahi Legal Services Authorities free legal aid bhi deti hain, toh jo family lawyer afford nahi kar sakti, woh inse lawyer maang sakti hai [[nalsa]].

## Chain kahan tootti hai, aur use kaise kheenchein

Kaagaz par har kadi ki ek deadline hai. Records mein backlog badhta ja raha hai. 2024 ke end mein 2,86,903 POCSO cases, yaani us saal courts ke saamne aaye saare POCSO cases ka 87.7%, trial ka intezaar kar rahe the. Ek saal pehle yeh ginti 2,62,089 thi. Iske alawa 21,256 cases ki investigation baaki thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB yeh nahi batata ki inmein se kitni investigations do mahine ki deadline paar kar chuki thin, aur police deadline tod de, toh kanoon mein uska koi nateeja tay nahi hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Kabhi-kabhi chain system ke andar hi toot-ti hai. Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS) ne Bihar ke children's homes ka audit kiya tha. April 2018 mein state government ko di gayi is report mein kai institutions mein sexual abuse saamne aaya, jinmein Muzaffarpur ka ek state-funded girls' shelter home bhi tha [[newslaundry-tiss-audit-bihar-2018]]. Wahan 34 minor ladkiyon ka sexual abuse hua tha [[sc-handbook-child-rights-2025]]. Matlab, sarkari care mein rakhe gaye bachche ko bhi kisi aise insaan ki zaroorat hai jo system ke bahar se uska haal poochta rahe.

Families kanoon ke apne shabdon se har kadi ko kheench sakti hain:

- Police station mein usi waqt FIR ki free copy maangiye. Ek station mana kare, toh doosre station jaaiye.
- Agar 90 din mein police ne investigation ka update nahi diya, toh likhkar maangiye; BNSS ke hisaab se yeh update dena zaroori hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- CWC se likhkar poochiye ki bachche ki safety par usne kya faisla liya.
- Compensation aur lawyer ke liye DLSA mein abhi application dijiye, verdict ke baad nahi.
- Koi office atkaaye, toh 1098 par dobara call kariye, aur jo bhi letter bhejein, uski ek copy apne paas rakhiye.

child-still-close-to-abuser-myth.en:
Consider this situation. An 11-year-old in a joint family in Jaipur tells her aunt that her uncle touches her in ways she does not like when nobody else is home. The aunt raises it, carefully, with the elders. Someone points out that the girl ran to hug the same uncle at Diwali and rode happily on his scooter last Sunday. The verdict comes fast: she is imagining things. In that room, the child's affection has become evidence for the defence. It is a familiar way for adults to talk themselves out of believing a child.

## The myth: an abused child would avoid the abuser

The myth sounds like common sense: if someone hurts you, you stay away from them. But it imagines a child with an adult's choices.
