Children do not decide where they live, who picks them up from school, who looks after them, or who sits at the family table on festivals. An adult can quit a job or block a number. An 11-year-old cannot move out of her uncle's house.

It also imagines abuse as obvious violence that a child would instantly recognise and fear. Much child sexual abuse arrives wrapped in attention, gifts and affection, from someone the child has been taught to respect.

## Who the abusers are: family, neighbours, people children love

The police record shows who is on the other side of that hug. In 2024, police in India registered 44,126 cases of penetrative sexual assault on children under the POCSO Act. The accused was a family member in 3,658 cases and a family friend, neighbour, employer or other known person in 16,668. A friend, online friend or live-in partner "on pretext of marriage" accounted for another 22,308; that group also includes teenage relationships, which POCSO treats as an offence below 18. Only 1,492 cases named an unknown or unidentified person [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

These figures cover penetrative assault only, not every POCSO offence, but the pattern is not new. The government's 2007 Study on Child Abuse found that 50% of abusers were known to the child or in a position of trust and responsibility, and that most children told no one [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Boys are part of this picture too: they made up 52.94% of the children who reported sexual abuse in that study [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

These are the people a child calls Mama, Chacha, Bhaiya or Sir. Avoiding them is often impossible, and a child who refuses to visit is often scolded for being rude.

## Loyalty, fear and dependence: why children stay close

**Grooming is designed to look like closeness.** Darkness to Light, a US child-protection nonprofit, describes grooming as a deliberate process by which an offender gradually builds and keeps a secret sexual relationship with a child. On the surface, it notes, grooming can look like a close relationship between the adult, the child and even the child's caregivers. Its red flags include special attention to one child, gifts, touching or hugging, acting as a sympathetic listener and offering to help the family [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. The hug the family points to may be part of what the abuser built.

**Love and harm can sit together.** A child can love an uncle and hate what he does, both at once. He may be the adult who listens, brings sweets and praises them when nobody else does. Losing him can feel like a second injury.

**Fear and dependence keep things "normal".** Children fear not being believed, being blamed or breaking the family. When the abuser pays the school fees or keeps the household running, they also fear what will happen to everyone else. Acting normal around him can feel like the safest choice a child has.

Some children do show fear. Darkness to Light lists unusual fear of a person, or reluctance to be alone with them, among the possible signs of abuse [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. So avoidance can be a warning. Its absence proves nothing.

## What judges are now told about 'real victim' behaviour

The Supreme Court has named this reasoning as a stereotype. Its 2023 Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes lists as false the beliefs that a genuine survivor cries incessantly or never speaks to the accused again [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. It states plainly: "There is no 'correct' or 'appropriate' way in which a survivor or victim behaves" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

> If judges must not expect an adult woman to cut off the man she accuses, families and police officers have even less reason to expect it of a child.

The handbook was written about women. For a child, whose food, schooling and home may depend on the adult in question, its reasoning applies with even more force.

## Protecting a child who still loves the person hurting them

Protection cannot wait for the child to reject the abuser. Creating distance is the adults' job:

- **Separate quietly.** End unsupervised time with the person. Never force a child to hug, sit with or visit anyone, relatives included.
- **Do not demand anger.** Say: "You can love him and still tell me. What he did is not your fault." A child forced to choose between loving someone and being believed will often choose silence.
- **Report.** Under Sections 19 and 21 of POCSO, anyone who knows of a sexual offence against a child must report it, and failing to do so can mean up to six months in prison or a fine [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Call 1098 or 112. Police must record the child's statement at home or at a place the child chooses, as far as practicable through a woman officer not in uniform, and must make sure the child never comes into contact with the accused [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. This is general information, not legal advice.
- **Expect mixed feelings.** The child may miss the person, ask about him, or cry if he is arrested. None of that means the child lied. It means the child is a child.
child-still-close-to-abuser-myth.hg:
Yeh situation sochiye. Jaipur ki ek joint family mein 11 saal ki ek ladki apni bua ko batati hai ki jab ghar par koi nahi hota, to uske chacha use aise chhoote hain jo use achha nahi lagta. Bua dhyaan se yeh baat ghar ke badon ke saamne rakhti hai. Koi yaad dilata hai ki Diwali par yahi ladki daud kar chacha ke gale lagi thi, aur pichhle Sunday unke scooter par khushi-khushi ghoom rahi thi. Faisla turant ho jaata hai: yeh sab iske mann ka vehem hai. Us kamre mein bachche ka pyaar accused ke bachaav ka saboot ban gaya. Badon ke liye bachche ki baat na maanne ka yeh ek jaana-pehchana tareeka hai.

## Myth: abuse jhelne wala bachcha abuser se door bhaagega

Yeh myth common sense jaisa lagta hai: jo aapko nuksaan pahunchaye, aap usse door rehte ho. Lekin yeh bachche ko ek adult jitne options wala maan leta hai. Bachche tay nahi karte ki woh kahan rahenge, school se unhe kaun laayega, unki dekhbhaal kaun karega, ya tyohaaron par family ki table par kaun baithega. Ek adult naukri chhod sakta hai ya number block kar sakta hai. 11 saal ki bachchi apne chacha ke ghar se nikal kar kahin nahi ja sakti.

Yeh myth abuse ko khuli violence ki tarah bhi dekhta hai, jise bachcha turant pehchaan le aur jisse dare. Lekin bachchon ka bahut sa sexual abuse attention, gifts aur pyaar mein lipta hua aata hai, aise insaan se jiski izzat karna bachche ko sikhaya gaya hai.

## Abusers kaun hain: family, padosi, aur woh log jinse bachche pyaar karte hain

Police ka record batata hai ki us gale lagne ke doosri taraf kaun khada hai. 2024 mein India mein police ne POCSO Act ke tahat bachchon par penetrative sexual assault ke 44,126 cases register kiye. 3,658 cases mein accused family member tha, aur 16,668 mein family friend, padosi, employer ya koi aur jaan-pehchaan wala. Dost, online dost ya 'shaadi ke bahane' saath rehne wala live-in partner 22,308 aur cases mein accused tha; is group mein teenagers ke rishte bhi shaamil hain, jinhe POCSO 18 se kam umar mein offence maanta hai. Sirf 1,492 cases mein accused anjaan tha ya pehchana nahi ja saka [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Yeh figures sirf penetrative assault ke hain, POCSO ke har offence ke nahi, lekin yeh pattern naya nahi hai. Sarkar ki 2007 ki Study on Child Abuse mein nikla tha ki 50% abusers aise the jinhe bachcha jaanta tha ya jo bharose aur zimmedari ki position mein the, aur zyadatar bachchon ne kisi ko kuch nahi bataya [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Ladke bhi is tasveer ka hissa hain: us study mein sexual abuse report karne wale bachchon mein 52.94% ladke the [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

Yeh woh log hain jinhe bachcha Mama, Chacha, Bhaiya ya Sir kehta hai. Inse bachna aksar namumkin hota hai, aur jo bachcha inke ghar jaane se mana kare, use aksar badtameezi ke liye daant padti hai.

## Wafadari, darr aur dependence: bachche kareeb kyun rehte hain

**Grooming ko closeness jaisa dikhne ke liye banaya jaata hai.** Darkness to Light, US ki ek child-protection nonprofit, grooming ko ek soch-samajhkar kiya gaya process batati hai, jismein abuser dheere-dheere bachche ke saath ek secret sexual rishta banata hai aur use chhupa kar rakhta hai. Sanstha kehti hai ki upar se grooming adult, bachche aur yahan tak ki bachche ke parents ke beech ek close rishte jaisi dikh sakti hai. Iske red flags mein shaamil hain: kisi ek bachche par khaas dhyaan, gifts, chhoona ya gale lagana, hamdard sunne wala banna, aur family ki madad ki offer [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. Family jis gale lagne ki taraf ishaara kar rahi hai, ho sakta hai woh bhi abuser ka hi banaya hua ho.

**Pyaar aur nuksaan saath-saath reh sakte hain.** Bachcha apne chacha se pyaar bhi kar sakta hai aur unki harkat se nafrat bhi, dono ek saath. Ho sakta hai wahi woh adult ho jo uski baat sunta hai, mithai laata hai, aur tab taarif karta hai jab koi aur nahi karta. Use khona ek doosre zakhm jaisa lag sakta hai.

**Darr aur dependence sab kuch 'normal' rakhte hain.** Bachchon ko darr hota hai ki unki baat nahi maani jaayegi, ilzaam unhi par aayega, ya ghar toot jaayega. Jab abuser hi school ki fees bharta ho ya ghar chalata ho, to unhe yeh darr bhi hota hai ki baaki sab ka kya hoga. Uske saamne normal behave karna bachche ko sabse safe raasta lag sakta hai.

Kuch bachche darr dikhaate bhi hain. Darkness to Light abuse ke possible signs mein kisi insaan se ajeeb sa darr, ya uske saath akele rehne se katraana bhi ginati hai [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. Yaani door rehna ek warning ho sakta hai. Lekin door na rehna kuch bhi saabit nahi karta.

## 'Asli victim' ke behaviour par judges ko ab kya bataya jaata hai

Supreme Court is soch ko stereotype keh chuka hai. Uski 2023 ki Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes in maanyataon ko galat batati hai ki asli survivor lagataar rota rehta hai, ya accused se phir kabhi baat nahi karta [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Handbook saaf kehti hai: "There is no 'correct' or 'appropriate' way in which a survivor or victim behaves", yaani survivor ya victim ke behave karne ka koi 'sahi' ya 'uchit' tareeka nahi hota [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

> Agar judges ek adult mahila se yeh ummeed nahi kar sakte ki woh jis aadmi par ilzaam laga rahi hai usse har rishta tod de, to families aur police ke paas ek bachche se yeh ummeed karne ki wajah aur bhi kam hai.

Yeh handbook mahilaon ke baare mein likhi gayi thi. Ek bachche ka khana, padhai aur ghar shayad usi adult par tika ho, isliye bachche ke case mein yeh tark aur bhi zor se laagu hota hai.

## Us bachche ko kaise bachayein jo ab bhi nuksaan pahunchane wale se pyaar karta hai

Bachche ki hifazat is baat ka intezaar nahi kar sakti ki bachcha pehle abuser ko thukra de. Doori banana badon ka kaam hai:

- **Chupchaap doori banaiye.** Us insaan ke saath bachche ka bina nigrani wala waqt khatam kijiye. Kisi bhi bachche ko kisi ke gale lagne, paas baithne ya unke ghar jaane ke liye majboor mat kijiye, rishtedaar bhi shaamil.
- **Gussa dikhane ki maang mat kijiye.** Kahiye: "Tum unse pyaar karte hue bhi mujhe bata sakte ho. Unhone jo kiya, usmein tumhari koi galti nahi." Jis bachche ko kisi se pyaar karne aur apni baat ka yakeen dilane mein se ek chunna pade, woh aksar chuppi chunta hai.
- **Report kijiye.** POCSO ke Section 19 aur 21 ke tahat jise bhi kisi bachche ke khilaaf sexual offence ka pata ho, use report karna hoga, aur report na karne par chhe mahine tak ki jail ya jurmana ho sakta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. 1098 ya 112 par call kijiye. Police ko bachche ka statement uske ghar par ya uski pasand ki jagah par lena hota hai, jahan tak ho sake bina uniform wali mahila officer se, aur yeh pakka karna hota hai ki bachcha kabhi accused ke sampark mein na aaye [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.
- **Mile-jule ehsaason ke liye taiyaar rahiye.** Ho sakta hai bachcha us insaan ko yaad kare, uske baare mein pooche, ya uski giraftari par roye. Iska matlab yeh nahi ki bachche ne jhooth bola. Iska matlab bas itna hai ki woh ek bachcha hai.

close-in-age-exception-pocso-debate.en:
Imagine a 17-year-old boy and a 16-year-old girl in Indore who have been seeing each other since Class 11. Her parents find their messages and go to the police. In law, her "yes" counts for nothing. He is accused of penetrative sexual assault on a child, which carries at least 10 years for an adult [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Because he is 16 or older and the Juvenile Justice Act classes the offence as "heinous", a Juvenile Justice Board can assess whether he should be tried as an adult [[gazette-juvenile-justice-act-2015]]. Should the law treat this couple the way it treats a man who grooms a child? That is the close-in-age debate. This article is general information, not legal advice.

## The law since 2013: no 'yes' below 18

The POCSO Act, in force since 14 November 2012, calls everyone under 18 a child and protects boys and girls alike [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, in force from 3 February 2013, then made sex with a girl under 18 rape whether or not she consented [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. Until then, the rape law's age of consent had been 16. The Justice Verma Committee had recommended 16; Parliament chose 18 [[prs-madhavan-sexual-offences-2013]].

The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) kept that line: sex with a girl under 18 is rape "with or without her consent" [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. POCSO adds two rules that weigh heavily on teenage cases. Penetrative sexual assault carries at least 10 years, and at least 20 if the child is under 16 [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. And the Special Court must presume that the accused committed the offence unless the contrary is proved [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

## What the 2024 data show, and cannot show

Of 44,567 child victims of penetrative sexual assault recorded under POCSO in 2024, 23,497, or 52.7%, were aged 16 to 18; another 16,801 were 12 to 16 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In 22,308 of the 44,126 cases (50.6%), police recorded the accused as a "friend, online friend or live-in partner on pretext of marriage", the largest of the four groups [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

It is tempting to read this as proof that POCSO mainly prosecutes teenage couples. The data cannot carry that weight. The "friends" column mixes adults who groomed a child online, men who promised marriage and boyfriends of the same age. NCRB does not count adolescent relationships or elopements separately, and it publishes victims' ages and the accused's relationship to them in separate tables [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. So these tables cannot say how many cases involve two teenagers close in age, or how old the accused in any group were. Both sides argue across that hole.

## The case for keeping the line at 18

Supporters of the current law start with who those "friends" can be. UNICEF warns that online abusers, whether known to the child or strangers, often first win the trust of the child or a caregiver before manipulating the child into sharing sexual images [[unicef-keeping-children-safe-online-2026]]. In online gaming spaces, offenders can pull children into high-risk grooming conversations within 19 seconds of a first message, and within 45 minutes on average, according to data cited by the WeProtect Global Alliance [[weprotect-gta-2023]]. A groomed teenager, they argue, may sincerely say she agreed. A line at 18 means her "yes" is never put on trial.

They also worry about the "pretext of marriage" cases. An exception written loosely could hand any adult a new defence: it was a relationship. And a trial that asks whether a 16-year-old truly agreed would put the girl, not the accused, back at the centre of the courtroom.

## The case for a close-in-age exception

Critics start with the boy in Indore. Had his girlfriend been 15, the minimum for an adult would be 20 years [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. With her consent irrelevant and the burden of proof reversed, his defence shrinks to disputing her age or denying that anything happened.

They point next to the courts. POCSO trials completed in 2024 ended in 12,672 convictions, 25,476 acquittals and 1,101 discharges, a conviction rate of 32.3% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The NCRB table gives outcomes, not reasons. Critics argue that many collapse when a girl will not testify against a boy she chose, while 2,86,903 POCSO cases were still pending trial at the end of 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Supporters reply that witnesses also turn hostile under pressure from the accused's family.

The sharpest argument is about health. Anyone who learns of a sexual offence against a child, including a doctor, must report it to the police [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. In 2022 the Supreme Court observed that this leaves a pregnant minor and her guardian choosing between a registered doctor, with possible criminal proceedings, and an unqualified provider [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. For abortions, the court let doctors leave the girl's name out of the report if she and her guardian ask, but the report itself remains [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

## What any change must protect

An exception worth the name would cover only teenagers close to each other in age, and only where both truly agreed. It would change nothing for the adult "online friend", the man who promised marriage, the teacher, the coach or the relative. Force or threats would still make it rape: the BNS defines consent as an "unequivocal voluntary agreement" [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Unless it was written in, it would not touch the separate offence of creating or downloading sexually explicit material depicting children [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. And it would not fix the data.

Both sides agree on more than the shouting suggests. Adults who exploit teenagers must be prosecuted. NCRB should publish the age of the accused alongside the age of the victim, so that this debate can rest on evidence. And teenagers need to know what consent and grooming look like before anyone tests them: in 2024 the Supreme Court recommended comprehensive sex education covering consent [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. A 16-year-old who can spot a groomer is safer under any version of the law.
close-in-age-exception-pocso-debate.hg:
Socho, Indore mein ek 17 saal ka ladka aur ek 16 saal ki ladki hain, jo Class 11 se saath hain. Ladki ke parents unke messages dekh lete hain aur police ke paas chale jaate hain. Kanoon ki nazar mein ladki ki "haan" ki koi keemat nahi hai. Ladke par ek bachche ke saath penetrative sexual assault ka aarop hai, jiski saza ek adult ke liye kam se kam 10 saal hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Kyunki woh 16 ya usse bada hai aur Juvenile Justice Act is offence ko "heinous" maanta hai, Juvenile Justice Board yeh assess kar sakta hai ki us par adult ki tarah trial chalna chahiye ya nahi [[gazette-juvenile-justice-act-2015]]. Kya kanoon ko is couple ke saath waisa hi bartaav karna chahiye jaisa ek bachche ko groom karne wale aadmi ke saath? Yahi hai close-in-age debate. Yeh article general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## 2013 se kanoon: 18 se kam umar mein koi 'haan' nahi

POCSO Act, jo 14 November 2012 se laagu hai, 18 se kam umar ke har insaan ko bachcha maanta hai aur ladkon aur ladkiyon dono ko barabar protect karta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Phir Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, jo 3 February 2013 se laagu hua, ne 18 se kam umar ki ladki ke saath sex ko rape bana diya, chahe usne consent diya ho ya nahi [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. Usse pehle rape law mein age of consent 16 thi. Justice Verma Committee ne 16 ki sifarish ki thi; Parliament ne 18 chuna [[prs-madhavan-sexual-offences-2013]].

Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ne yahi line rakhi: 18 se kam umar ki ladki ke saath sex rape hai, "with or without her consent", yaani uski marzi ho ya na ho [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. POCSO do aur rules jodta hai jo teenage cases par bahut bhaari padte hain. Penetrative sexual assault ki saza kam se kam 10 saal hai, aur agar bachcha 16 se kam ho toh kam se kam 20 saal [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Aur Special Court ko yeh maan kar chalna hota hai ki accused ne offence kiya hai, jab tak ulta saabit na ho jaaye [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

## 2024 ka data kya dikhata hai, aur kya nahi dikha sakta

2024 mein POCSO ke tahat penetrative sexual assault ke 44,567 child victims darj hue. Inmein se 23,497, yaani 52.7%, 16 se 18 saal ke the, aur 16,801 bachche 12 se 16 saal ke the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 44,126 cases mein se 22,308 (50.6%) mein police ne accused ko "friend, online friend or live-in partner on pretext of marriage", yaani dost, online dost ya shaadi ke bahane wala live-in partner likha. Chaaron groups mein yeh sabse bada tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

In numbers ko is baat ka saboot maan lena aasaan hai ki POCSO zyada tar teenage couples par case chalata hai. Par data itna bojh nahi utha sakta. "Friends" wale column mein sab mila hua hai: woh adults jinhone kisi bachche ko online groom kiya, woh aadmi jinhone shaadi ka vaada kiya, aur hum-umar boyfriends bhi. NCRB adolescent relationships ya ghar se bhaagne (elopement) wale cases alag se nahi ginta, aur victims ki umar aur accused ke saath unka rishta alag-alag tables mein chhaapta hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Isliye yeh tables nahi bata sakte ki kitne cases mein do hum-umar teenagers the, ya kisi bhi group mein accused ki umar kya thi. Dono side isi khaali jagah ke aar-paar behes karti hain.

## 18 ki line banaye rakhne ke haq mein

Abhi ke kanoon ke supporters yahan se shuru karte hain ki yeh "friends" kaun ho sakte hain. UNICEF warning deta hai ki online abusers, chahe bachche ke jaan-pehchaan wale hon ya ajnabi, aksar pehle bachche ya uske caregiver ka bharosa jeetate hain, aur phir bachche ko sexual images share karne ke liye manipulate karte hain [[unicef-keeping-children-safe-online-2026]]. Online gaming spaces mein offenders pehle message ke sirf 19 seconds ke andar bachchon ko high-risk grooming conversations mein kheench sakte hain, aur average 45 minutes mein. Yeh data WeProtect Global Alliance ne pesh kiya hai [[weprotect-gta-2023]]. Unki daleel hai ki jis teenager ko groom kiya gaya ho, woh poori sachchai se keh sakti hai ki usne haan kaha tha. 18 ki line ka matlab hai ki uski "haan" kabhi trial par nahi chadhti.

Unhe "shaadi ke bahane" wale cases ki bhi fikar hai. Dheele dhang se likha gaya exception har adult ko ek naya bachaav thama sakta hai: "yeh toh relationship tha". Aur jo trial yeh poochega ki kya 16 saal ki ladki ne sach mein haan kaha tha, woh courtroom ke beech mein accused ki jagah phir se ladki ko hi khada kar dega.

## Close-in-age exception ke haq mein

Critics Indore wale ladke se shuru karte hain. Agar uski girlfriend 15 saal ki hoti, toh adult ke liye minimum saza 20 saal hoti [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Jab ladki ki consent ka koi matlab na ho aur proof ka bojh ulta ho, toh ladke ka bachaav bas itna reh jaata hai ki woh ladki ki umar par sawaal uthaye ya kahe ki kuch hua hi nahi.

Phir woh courts ki taraf ishaara karte hain. 2024 mein jo POCSO trials poore hue, unmein 12,672 convictions, 25,476 acquittals aur 1,101 discharges hue, yaani conviction rate sirf 32.3% raha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB ka table sirf nateeje deta hai, wajah nahi. Critics kehte hain ki kai cases tab gir jaate hain jab ladki us ladke ke khilaaf gawahi dene se mana kar deti hai jise usne khud chuna tha, jabki 2024 ke ant mein 2,86,903 POCSO cases ab bhi trial ke intezaar mein the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Supporters jawab dete hain ki gawah accused ki family ke dabaav mein bhi palat jaate hain.

Sabse tez daleel health se judi hai. Jise bhi kisi bachche ke saath sexual offence ka pata chale, doctor samet, use police ko report karna hi hoga [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. 2022 mein Supreme Court ne khud kaha ki is wajah se pregnant minor aur uske guardian ke saamne do hi raaste bachte hain: registered doctor ke paas jaayein aur criminal proceedings ka risk lein, ya kisi unqualified provider ke paas jaayein [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Abortion ke maamle mein court ne doctors ko ijaazat di ki agar ladki aur uske guardian kahein toh report mein ladki ka naam na likhein, lekin report phir bhi jaati hai [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

## Koi bhi badlaav kin cheezon ko bachaaye

Sahi maayne mein exception sirf un teenagers par laagu hoga jo umar mein ek-doosre ke kareeb hon, aur sirf tab jab dono ne sach mein haan kaha ho. Adult "online friend", shaadi ka vaada karne wale aadmi, teacher, coach ya rishtedaar ke liye kuch nahi badlega. Zor-zabardasti ya dhamki se hua sex tab bhi rape hoga: BNS consent ko "unequivocal voluntary agreement", yaani saaf aur apni marzi se di gayi sahmati, maanta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Jab tak alag se likha na jaaye, yeh exception bachchon ko dikhane wala sexually explicit material banane ya download karne ke alag offence ko chhuega bhi nahi [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Aur yeh data ki kami bhi door nahi karega.

Shor-sharaabe ke bawajood dono side kai baaton par sehmat hain. Teenagers ka shoshan karne wale adults par case chalna hi chahiye. NCRB ko victim ki umar ke saath accused ki umar bhi chhaapni chahiye, taaki yeh behes saboot par tike. Aur teenagers ko consent aur grooming ki pehchaan us din se pehle ho jaani chahiye jab koi unhe aazmaye: 2024 mein Supreme Court ne consent samet comprehensive sex education ki sifarish ki thi [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Jo 16 saal ka teenager groomer ko pehchaan sake, woh kanoon ke kisi bhi version mein zyada safe hai.

crimes-against-children-2024-numbers.en:
Police in India registered 1,87,702 crimes against children in 2024, up 5.9% from 1,77,335 in 2023; in 2022 the count was 1,62,449 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Public debate about that total usually starts and ends with POCSO, the child sexual abuse law. But the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) table is much wider, and POCSO is not even its biggest line. Here is the 2024 count, line by line, with what each number can and cannot tell you.

## 1,87,702: the headline and the rate

The total works out to 42.3 cases for every lakh children, up from 39.9 a year earlier [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Read it for what it is: 1,87,702 FIRs, complaints that reached a police station and were written down. It is not a count of children harmed.

Two things shape the number before anyone reads it. NCRB counts each FIR once, under its most serious offence, so the lesser crimes in the same FIR vanish from the table [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. And NCRB itself warns that a "rise in crime" and an "increase in registration of crime by police" are two different things; a new e-FIR facility or a women's helpdesk can push numbers up [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. So the 5.9% rise could mean more harm, more reporting, or both. The table cannot say which.

## Kidnapping, 40.0%: the biggest line in the table

POCSO made up 36.9% of the total: 69,191 cases involving 70,132 children [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Kidnapping and abduction of children was bigger, at 40.0% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Roughly two in every five crimes against children recorded in 2024 began with a child taken, or a child gone.

Part of the reason is a recording rule. Under a 2013 Supreme Court direction in *Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India*, every complaint about a missing child must be registered as an FIR, with an initial presumption that the child was abducted or trafficked [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. So a family's worst night at a police station is registered, at least at first, as a kidnapping case.

The kidnapping count on its own does not say how many of these children came home. The missing-children figures come closer.

## Missing, trafficked, married, exploited online: the numbers beyond POCSO

| Counted in 2024 | Number |
|---|---|
| Children reported missing | 98,375 |
| Children recorded as trafficked | 2,297 |
| Cyber crimes against children | 1,753 |
| Child marriage cases registered | 1,499 |

**Missing.** 98,375 children were reported missing in 2024, up 7.8% from 91,296 in 2023: 75,603 girls, 22,768 boys and 4 transgender children [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Police traced 98,826 children that year, including some who had gone missing earlier. Yet, counting those earlier cases, 48,349 children were still untraced at the end of 2024, 36,352 of them girls [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**Trafficked.** Of 6,018 people recorded as trafficked, 2,297 (38%) were children: 1,384 boys and 913 girls [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Across all ages, courts convicted in just 43 of the 586 trafficking trials that ended in 2024, a conviction rate of 7.3% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**Exploited online.** Police recorded 1,753 cyber crimes against children, and 1,099 of them involved sexually explicit material depicting children [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In the same year, the US-based National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) attributed 22,52,528 CyberTipline reports to India, 15,21,666 of them with enough information for police action [[ncmec-cybertipline-by-country-2024]]. These reports are not a count of abuse, and a single report can be made available to more than one country. Still, the distance between the two figures is not a rounding error.

**Married.** Cases under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act went from 1,002 in 2022 to 6,038 in 2023, then back to 1,499 in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Most of the 2023 jump came from one state: Assam registered 5,267 of the 6,038 [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. When one state can swing the national line like that, the line is measuring enforcement, not how many weddings happened. Meanwhile, 20.1% of women aged 20-24 surveyed in 2023-24 had been married before 18 [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. One young woman in five, against 1,499 FIRs.

## Courts: 33.9% convicted, 6,44,887 waiting

Registration is only the first door. Across all crimes against children, courts convicted in 33.9% of the trials that ended in 2024, and 6,44,887 cases were still pending trial at the end of the year, a pendency rate of 91.1% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. More than nine in ten child-crime cases before the courts were left waiting, and about two in three trials that did end closed without a conviction.

Imagine a 13-year-old whose POCSO case reached a Special Court in 2024. The law says the court should record her evidence within 30 days of taking cognisance and finish the trial within a year, as far as possible [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Yet at the end of 2024, 2,86,903 POCSO cases, 87.7% of those before the courts, were still pending trial [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Hers would most likely be one of them. Every month of waiting is another month in which she may be asked to retell it, or pressed to "compromise".

Child marriage cases show the same pattern: 209 convictions against 625 acquittals in 2024, with 8,553 cases pending [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## What these numbers cannot tell you

They cannot tell you how many children were harmed, because they only count harm that reached a police station. Most never does. In the government's 2007 study, 72.1% of children who had been sexually assaulted had told no one, and only 3.4% had gone to the police [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. India has not run a national survey on child sexual abuse since then, a gap we examine in a separate investigation.

They cannot show overlap either. Because only the most serious offence is counted, a minor bride who is also sexually abused may be recorded under POCSO and disappear from the child marriage line [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. And they cannot rank states fairly: NCRB says comparing states on these numbers alone "will be too simplistic and is best avoided" [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. A state that registers more FIRs may simply be one where families are taken seriously.

What the numbers can do is show where the system leaks: children who go missing and stay missing, trafficking trials that collapse, child marriages that never become cases, and courts that cannot keep up. Each leak can be pushed on, by a parent who insists on an FIR, a neighbour who calls 1098 before a wedding, or a reader who reports abuse material instead of forwarding it.
crimes-against-children-2024-numbers.hg:
2024 mein India ki police ne bachchon ke khilaaf 1,87,702 crimes darj kiye. Yeh 2023 ke 1,77,335 se 5.9% zyada hai; 2022 mein yeh ginti 1,62,449 thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Is total pe jab bhi baat hoti hai, woh zyadatar POCSO pe aakar ruk jaati hai, yaani bachchon ko sexual abuse se bachane wala law. Lekin National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) ki yeh table kaafi badi hai, aur POCSO iski sabse badi line bhi nahi hai. Chaliye, 2024 ki ginti ko line by line dekhte hain: har number kya bata sakta hai, aur kya nahi.

## 1,87,702: headline number aur uska rate

Har ek lakh bachchon pe yeh 42.3 cases banta hai. Ek saal pehle yeh rate 39.9 tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Is number ko sahi nazar se padhiye. Yeh 1,87,702 FIRs hain, yaani woh complaints jo police station tak pahunchi aur likhi gayi. Yeh un bachchon ki ginti nahi hai jinke saath kuch bura hua.

Is number pe do cheezon ka asar padta hai. Pehla, NCRB har FIR ko sirf ek baar ginta hai, uske sabse serious offence ke naam pe. Usi FIR ke baaki crimes table se gayab ho jaate hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Doosra, NCRB khud warning deta hai ki "rise in crime" aur "increase in registration of crime by police" do alag baatein hain, yaani crime badhna aur police ka zyada case darj karna ek cheez nahi. Naya e-FIR system ya thane mein women helpdesk khulne se bhi numbers badh sakte hain [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. Toh 5.9% ki badhat ka matlab zyada crime ho sakta hai, zyada reporting ho sakti hai, ya dono. Table yeh nahi bata sakti ki sach kya hai.

## Kidnapping, 40.0%: table ki sabse badi line

Total mein POCSO ka hissa 36.9% tha: 69,191 cases, jinmein 70,132 bachche shaamil the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Lekin bachchon ki kidnapping aur abduction ka hissa isse bhi bada tha, poore 40.0% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Mote taur pe, 2024 mein darj har paanch mein se do crimes yahin se shuru hue ki koi bachcha uthaya gaya, ya koi bachcha ghar nahi lauta.

Iski ek wajah record karne ka ek rule hai. 2013 mein Supreme Court ne *Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India* case mein direction di thi ki missing bachche ki har complaint pe FIR darj hogi. Aur shuruaat mein yahi maana jaayega ki bachche ka abduction ya trafficking hua hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Isliye jis raat koi family ghabrakar police station pahunchti hai, woh raat record mein, kam se kam shuru mein, kidnapping ka case ban jaati hai.

Kidnapping ki ginti akele yeh nahi batati ki inmein se kitne bachche ghar laute. Missing bachchon ke figures is sawaal ke zyada kareeb pahunchte hain.

## Missing, trafficked, married, online exploit hue: POCSO ke bahar ke numbers

| 2024 mein kya gina gaya | Number |
|---|---|
| Missing report hue bachche | 98,375 |
| Trafficking ke shikaar darj bachche | 2,297 |
| Bachchon ke khilaaf cyber crimes | 1,753 |
| Child marriage ke darj cases | 1,499 |

**Missing.** 2024 mein 98,375 bachchon ke missing hone ki report darj hui, jo 2023 ke 91,296 se 7.8% zyada hai. Inmein 75,603 ladkiyan, 22,768 ladke aur 4 transgender bachche the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Us saal police ne 98,826 bachchon ko trace kiya, jinmein kuch pichhle saalon se missing the. Phir bhi, pichhle saalon ke cases milakar, 2024 ke end tak 48,349 bachchon ka koi pata nahi chala, aur inmein 36,352 ladkiyan thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**Trafficked.** 2024 mein 6,018 logon ki trafficking darj hui. Inmein 2,297 (38%) bachche the: 1,384 ladke aur 913 ladkiyan [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Har age ke cases milakar, 2024 mein trafficking ke jin 586 cases ka trial poora hua, unmein se sirf 43 mein conviction hua, yaani conviction rate bas 7.3% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**Online exploit hue.** Police ne bachchon ke khilaaf 1,753 cyber crimes darj kiye, aur inmein se 1,099 cases bachchon ki sexual photos ya videos se jude the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Usi saal US ki sanstha National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) ne India se judi 22,52,528 CyberTipline reports ginin, jinmein se 15,21,666 mein itni jaankari thi ki police action le sake [[ncmec-cybertipline-by-country-2024]]. Yeh reports abuse ki ginti nahi hain, aur ek hi report ek se zyada deshon ko bhi bheji ja sakti hai. Phir bhi in dono numbers ke beech ka gap koi chhoti-moti baat nahi hai.

**Married.** Prohibition of Child Marriage Act ke under cases 2022 mein 1,002 the, 2023 mein badhkar 6,038 ho gaye, aur 2024 mein wapas 1,499 pe aa gaye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 2023 ka zyadatar jump ek hi state se aaya tha: 6,038 mein se 5,267 cases akele Assam mein darj hue [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. Jab ek state poore desh ki line ko itna upar-neeche kar de, toh samajh lijiye ki yeh number police ki sakhti naap raha hai, shaadiyon ki asli ginti nahi. Doosri taraf, 2023-24 ke survey mein 20-24 saal ki 20.1% women ki shaadi 18 se pehle ho chuki thi [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Yaani har paanch mein se ek young woman, aur saamne sirf 1,499 FIRs.

## Courts: 33.9% conviction, 6,44,887 cases intezaar mein

Case darj hona bas pehla darwaza hai. Bachchon ke khilaaf saare crimes milakar, 2024 mein jin cases ka trial khatam hua, unmein se 33.9% mein conviction hua. Saal ke end mein 6,44,887 cases ab bhi trial ka intezaar kar rahe the, yaani pendency rate 91.1% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Seedhi baat: courts ke saamne bachchon se jude har das mein se nau se zyada cases atke rahe. Aur jin trials ka faisla aaya, unmein se lagbhag teen mein se do bina conviction ke khatam hue.

Sochiye, ek 13 saal ki bachchi hai jiska POCSO case 2024 mein Special Court tak pahuncha. Law kehta hai ki court case ka cognisance lene ke 30 din ke andar uska bayaan record kare, aur jahan tak ho sake, ek saal mein trial poora kare [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Lekin 2024 ke end mein 2,86,903 POCSO cases, yaani courts ke saamne aaye 87.7% cases, ab bhi trial ka intezaar kar rahe the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Bahut mumkin hai ki uska case bhi inmein se ek ho. Intezaar ka har mahina ek aur mahina hai jismein usse sab kuch dobara batane ko kaha ja sakta hai, ya "compromise" ke liye pressure daala ja sakta hai.

Child marriage cases mein bhi yahi haal hai: 2024 mein 209 convictions, 625 acquittals, aur 8,553 cases pending [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Yeh numbers kya nahi bata sakte

Yeh numbers yeh nahi bata sakte ki asal mein kitne bachchon ko nuksaan pahuncha, kyunki yeh sirf wahi harm ginte hain jo police station tak pahuncha. Zyadatar wahan tak pahunchta hi nahi. Sarkar ki 2007 ki study mein jin bachchon ke saath sexual assault hua tha, unmein se 72.1% ne kisi ko kuch nahi bataya tha, aur sirf 3.4% police tak gaye the [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Uske baad se India ne child sexual abuse pe koi national survey nahi karaya. Is gap pe humne ek alag investigation ki hai.

Yeh numbers overlap bhi nahi dikhate. Kyunki sirf sabse serious offence gina jaata hai, koi minor dulhan jiska sexual abuse bhi hua, POCSO mein gini ja sakti hai aur child marriage ki line se gayab ho sakti hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Aur yeh states ki sahi ranking bhi nahi karte. NCRB khud kehta hai ki sirf in numbers pe states ko compare karna "will be too simplistic and is best avoided", yaani yeh bahut simplistic hoga aur isse bachna hi behtar hai [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. Ho sakta hai jis state mein zyada FIRs darj hoti hain, wahan bas families ki baat zyada seriously suni jaati ho.

Haan, yeh numbers yeh zaroor dikhate hain ki system mein kahan-kahan chhed hain: bachche jo missing hote hain aur missing hi reh jaate hain, trafficking ke cases jo court mein toot jaate hain, child marriages jo kabhi case bante hi nahi, aur courts jo speed nahi pakad paate. Har chhed pe pressure daala ja sakta hai: parents jo FIR likhwane pe tike rahein, padosi jo shaadi se pehle 1098 pe call kar de, ya aap jaise readers jo abuse wala video forward karne ki jagah uski report karein.

death-penalty-child-rape-known-abusers.en:
In April 2018, amid national protests over the Kathua and Unnao cases, the government made the rape of a girl under 12 punishable by death, and the Act of Parliament that replaced the ordinance received assent that August [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]]. In 2019, POCSO extended death to aggravated penetrative sexual assault on any child [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. The promise was simple: the harshest punishment for the worst crime. This investigation asks a narrower, harder question. Most children are abused by people they know. Does the threat of death protect them, or does it make it harder for their families to speak? This is general information, not legal advice.

## 2018 and 2019: how death entered child-rape law

The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018, in force from 21 April 2018, added Section 376AB to the IPC: rape of a girl under 12 became punishable with at least 20 years, imprisonment for the rest of natural life, or death. Gang rape of a girl under 12 (Section 376DB) carried natural-life imprisonment or death [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]]. Since 1 July 2024, Section 65 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita has carried the same punishment for the rape of a girl under 12, and directs that any fine goes to the victim [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The IPC change covered girls. The 2019 POCSO amendment, in force from 16 August 2019, reached every child, boys included: aggravated penetrative sexual assault now carries at least 20 years, up to natural life, or death [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

How many children are in that youngest group? In 2024, police recorded 4,269 child victims of penetrative assault under 12: 831 under six and 3,438 aged 6 to 12 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## What the Verma Committee warned in 2013

Parliament had been advised otherwise. The Justice J.S. Verma Committee, set up after the 2012 Delhi gang rape, advised against the death penalty for rape in its January 2013 report, noting that it "may not have a deterrent effect" [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Our case file on the committee covers the rest of its advice.

A deterrent needs two things that a harsher maximum does not supply: a good chance that the abuse is reported, and a good chance that a report ends in conviction. For a child abused at home, both are low.

## When the accused is an uncle: the cost of reporting

In 96.6% of POCSO penetrative-assault cases registered in 2024, the accused was someone the child knew: a family member in 3,658 cases, and a family friend, neighbour, employer or other known person in 16,668 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB publishes ages and relationships in separate tables, so it cannot show how many of the under-12 cases involved a relative.

Consider this situation. A nine-year-old in a joint family in Indore tells her mother what her uncle, her father's younger brother, has been doing to her. Reporting it once meant prison for him. Now the family hears he could face death. Her grandparents call it the end of the family; her father is asked whether he wants his brother's death on his conscience. The question is no longer only whether she will be believed, but whether the family will risk one of its own being executed.

No table can count the families who chose silence, because unreported abuse never reaches one. What is known is how quiet children already were. In the government's 2007 Study on Child Abuse, the last national study of its kind and built on a non-random sample, 72.1% of children who reported sexual assault had told no one, and only 3.4% had gone to the police [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. That was before POCSO and its duty to report, but it shows how high the wall was. A heavier sentence risks making it higher, though no Indian data measures that effect.

## What the 2024 conviction data show

Six years on, most cases that reach a verdict still end without a conviction. In 2024, courts convicted in 32.3% of POCSO trials completed, with 12,672 convictions against 25,476 acquittals [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. For penetrative sexual assault under Sections 4 and 6, the category that includes the offences punishable by death, the rate was 30.2%, and 1,70,455 such cases were waiting for trial at the end of the year [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The 2018 law also set deadlines: two months to investigate a rape, six months to decide an appeal [[indiacode-cla-2018]]. No deadline makes a frightened family testify. When the accused is a relative, the harshness itself can feed acquittals: a family that did report may still step back in court rather than see one of its own face death.

## What would protect more children

If the aim is fewer children abused and more abusers convicted, the data in this story points away from severity and towards certainty, speed and support.

- **Speed.** POCSO already requires the child's evidence within 30 days and the trial within a year where possible [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], yet 2,86,903 POCSO cases were pending trial at the end of 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Every month of delay is a month of family pressure.
- **Support for the parent who reports,** often a mother choosing between her child and her household: shelter, money, legal aid and one case worker who stays.
- **Early disclosure.** In 2024 the Supreme Court recommended comprehensive sex education covering consent and child sexual exploitation [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. A child with words for abuse can tell sooner.
- **A reporting system families can survive.** Anyone who knows of child sexual abuse must report it under POCSO [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], and Child Helpline 1098 runs 24x7 [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].

A death sentence is a promise about the end of a case. Most abused children need help at the beginning: someone who believes them, and a family that can afford to.
death-penalty-child-rape-known-abusers.hg:
April 2018 mein, Kathua aur Unnao cases pe desh bhar mein ho rahe protests ke beech, sarkar ne 12 saal se kam umar ki bachchi ke rape ko maut ki saza wala crime bana diya, aur ordinance ki jagah lene wale Parliament ke Act ko usi August assent mil gaya [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]]. 2019 mein POCSO ne kisi bhi bachche pe aggravated penetrative sexual assault ke liye bhi maut ki saza jod di [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Waada seedha tha: sabse bure crime ke liye sabse sakht saza. Yeh investigation ek chhota par mushkil sawaal poochhti hai. Zyadatar bachchon ka abuse jaan-pehchaan wale karte hain. Kya maut ki saza ka darr unhe bachata hai, ya unki family ke liye bolna aur mushkil bana deta hai? Yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahi.

## 2018 aur 2019: child rape ke kanoon mein maut ki saza kaise aayi

Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018, jo 21 April 2018 se lagu hua, ne IPC mein Section 376AB joda: 12 se kam umar ki bachchi ke rape ki saza kam se kam 20 saal, baaki poori zindagi ki qaid, ya maut ho gayi. 12 se kam umar ki bachchi ke gang rape (Section 376DB) ke liye poori zindagi ki qaid ya maut ki saza thi [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]]. 1 July 2024 se Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ka Section 65 12 se kam umar ki bachchi ke rape ke liye yahi saza deta hai, aur kehta hai ki koi bhi fine victim ko diya jaaye [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

IPC wala badlaav sirf ladkiyon ke liye tha. 2019 ka POCSO amendment, jo 16 August 2019 se lagu hua, har bachche tak pahuncha, ladkon samet: aggravated penetrative sexual assault ki saza ab kam se kam 20 saal, poori zindagi tak ki qaid, ya maut hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Sabse chhote bachchon ke is group mein kitne bachche hain? 2024 mein police ne penetrative assault ke 4,269 aise child victims record kiye jo 12 saal se chhote the: 831 bachche 6 saal se kam ke, aur 3,438 bachche 6 se 12 saal ke [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## 2013 mein Verma Committee ne kya chetaya tha

Parliament ko ulti salah mili thi. 2012 ke Delhi gang rape ke baad bani Justice J.S. Verma Committee ne January 2013 ki apni report mein rape ke liye death penalty ke khilaaf salah di thi, yeh kehte hue ki iska "may not have a deterrent effect", yaani shayad isse darr paida na ho [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Committee ki baaki salah hamari case file mein hai.

Kisi bhi saza ka darr tabhi kaam karta hai jab do cheezein hon, jo sakht maximum saza nahi de sakti: achha chance ki abuse report hoga, aur achha chance ki report conviction tak pahunchegi. Ghar ke andar abuse jhel rahe bachche ke liye dono hi kam hain.

## Jab accused chacha ho: report karne ki keemat

2024 mein register hue POCSO penetrative assault cases mein se 96.6% mein accused koi aisa tha jise bachcha jaanta tha: 3,658 cases mein family member, aur 16,668 mein family friend, padosi, employer ya koi aur jaan-pehchaan wala [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB umar aur rishte alag-alag tables mein chhaapta hai, isliye woh nahi dikha sakta ki 12 se kam umar wale kitne cases mein koi rishtedaar shaamil tha.

Ek situation sochiye. Indore ki ek joint family mein 9 saal ki ek bachchi apni maa ko batati hai ki uske chacha, yaani uske papa ke chhote bhai, uske saath kya karte rahe hain. Pehle report karne ka matlab tha chacha ko jail. Ab family sunti hai ki unhe maut ki saza bhi ho sakti hai. Dada-dadi kehte hain ki isse family khatam ho jaayegi; papa se poochha jaata hai ki kya woh apne bhai ki maut apne sar lena chahte hain. Ab sawaal sirf yeh nahi ki bachchi pe bharosa hoga ya nahi, balki yeh bhi ki kya family apne hi ek insaan ko maut ki saza tak pahunchane ka risk legi.

Koi table un familyon ko nahi gin sakti jinhone chup rehna chuna, kyunki report na hua abuse kisi table tak pahunchta hi nahi. Jo pata hai, woh yeh ki bachche pehle se kitne chup the. Sarkar ki 2007 ki Study on Child Abuse mein, jo apni tarah ki aakhri national study hai aur non-random sample pe bani thi, sexual assault batane wale 72.1% bachchon ne tab tak kisi ko kuch nahi bataya tha, aur sirf 3.4% police tak gaye the [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Yeh POCSO aur uski report karne ki zimmedari se pehle ki baat hai, lekin isse pata chalta hai ki chuppi ki deewar kitni oonchi thi. Sakht saza use aur ooncha karne ka risk rakhti hai, halaanki koi Indian data is asar ko naapta nahi hai.

## 2024 ka conviction data kya dikhata hai

Chhe saal baad bhi, verdict tak pahunchne wale zyadatar cases bina conviction ke khatam hote hain. 2024 mein courts ne poore hue POCSO trials mein se 32.3% mein conviction diya: 12,672 convictions, 25,476 acquittals ke muqable [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Section 4 aur 6 ke penetrative sexual assault cases mein, jis category mein maut ki saza wale offences bhi aate hain, rate 30.2% tha, aur saal ke end mein aise 1,70,455 cases trial ka intezaar kar rahe the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

2018 ke kanoon ne deadlines bhi tay ki thi: rape ki investigation ke liye do mahine, appeal ke faisle ke liye chhe mahine [[indiacode-cla-2018]]. Lekin koi deadline dari hui family se gawahi nahi dilwa sakti. Jab accused rishtedaar ho, to saza ki sakhti khud acquittals badha sakti hai: jis family ne report kiya bhi, woh court mein peeche hat sakti hai, bajaye iske ki apne hi kisi ko maut ki saza ka saamna karte dekhe.

## Zyada bachchon ko kya bachayega

Agar maqsad yeh hai ki kam bachchon ka abuse ho aur zyada abusers convict hon, to is story ka data sakhti se door, certainty, speed aur support ki taraf ishaara karta hai.

- **Speed.** POCSO pehle se kehta hai ki bachche ka bayaan 30 din mein record ho aur trial jahan tak ho sake ek saal mein poora ho [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], phir bhi 2024 ke end mein 2,86,903 POCSO cases trial ka intezaar kar rahe the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Deri ka har mahina family pe pressure ka ek aur mahina hai.
- **Report karne wale maa ya baap ka saath,** jo aksar ek maa hoti hai jise apne bachche aur apne ghar mein se ek ko chunna padta hai: rehne ki jagah, paise, legal aid, aur ek case worker jo aakhir tak saath rahe.
- **Jaldi bata paana.** 2024 mein Supreme Court ne aisi comprehensive sex education ki sifaarish ki jo consent aur bachchon ke sexual exploitation ko cover kare [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Jis bachche ke paas abuse ke liye shabd hain, woh jaldi bata sakta hai.
- **Aisa reporting system jise family jhel sake.** POCSO ke tahat child sexual abuse ke baare mein jaanne wale har insaan ko report karna hota hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], aur Child Helpline 1098 24x7 chalti hai [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].

Maut ki saza case ke ant ka waada hai. Zyadatar abused bachchon ko madad shuruaat mein chahiye: koi jo unki baat maane, aur ek family jo aisa karne ki haalat mein ho.

global-child-marriage-decline-india-role.en:
Somewhere in the world, a girl is married every three seconds. That is UNFPA's way of describing the roughly 12 million girls married before 18 every year [[unfpa-child-marriage-2025]]. Yet the United Nations now reports that the trend is improving, and faster than before. Its explanation points to our region. Of all the women alive today who were married as children, one in three lives in India [[un-sdg-report-2024-goal5]]. So any honest account of the world's curve, and of the distance still left, has to look closely at India's own.

## 22% to 18%: a decade of global decline

In 2015, 22% of young women worldwide had been married before 18. The 2026 Gender Snapshot from UN Women and UN DESA, the UN's Department of Economic and Social Affairs, puts the figure at 18%, and says the pace of reduction almost doubled in the last decade compared with the one before [[unwomen-gender-snapshot-2026]]. The UN's SDG Report 2026 agrees: the decline during 2015-2024 was double that of the previous decade [[un-sdg-report-2026-goal5]].

The long view is larger still. One in five girls is now married before 18, against one in four 25 years ago, and 68 million child marriages were averted in that time [[un-sdg-report-2024-goal5]].

A note on the measure. It asks women aged 20 to 24 whether they married before 18, so a figure published in 2026 describes weddings from years earlier. The child marriages happening today will show up in the data only years from now.

## Southern Asia: the region that moved the world

The SDG Report 2025 is plain about where the progress came from: child marriage has become less common worldwide "largely due to progress in Southern Asia" [[un-sdg-report-2025-goal5]]. Sub-Saharan Africa, where 31% of young women were married as children, is the warning. The number of child brides there is projected to rise by 2030 [[un-sdg-report-2025-goal5]].

India's weight shows in one figure. Of an estimated 640 million girls and women alive today who were married in childhood, one third live in India [[un-sdg-report-2024-goal5]]. That count includes grandmothers married decades ago, which is why it is so large. But it shows how much of the global burden sits in one country. The UN credits the region, not any one country, and its figures do not separate out India's share of the fall. India's own survey is the place to look.

## From 47.4% to 20.1%: India's own curve

India tracks child marriage through the National Family Health Survey (NFHS), using the same age yardstick [[ceda-genderstats-underage-marriage-2021]].

| Survey round | Women aged 20-24 married before 18 |
|---|---|
| NFHS-3 (2005-06) | 47.4% |
| NFHS-4 (2015-16) | 26.8% |
| NFHS-5 (2019-21) | 23.3% |
| NFHS-6 (2023-24), provisional | 20.1% |

In a single decade, India went from almost one young woman in two married as a child to about one in four. Then the fall slowed: in the eight years after 2015-16, the share dropped far more slowly. The UN's global figures and India's survey rounds are separate series covering different years, so one cannot be read off the other. But India's own numbers are clear. The steep part of its fall is behind it.

The national average also hides extremes. In 2023-24 the rate was 23.3% in villages and 11.4% in towns and cities [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. West Bengal (36.4%) and Bihar (34.6%) are higher today than India as a whole was in 2015-16. Kerala is at 2.9% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

## What the UN credits: school, work, income

UN Women names three drivers of the faster global decline: girls' education, economic empowerment and poverty reduction [[unwomen-gender-snapshot-2026]]. Prosecutions are not on the list. Each driver changes the calculation a family makes about a daughter: what she could earn, and what another year at home will cost.

Indian data show how tightly early life events follow money and schooling. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 10.0% of girls aged 15-19 in the poorest households had already begun childbearing, against 2.2% in the richest. Among girls with no schooling, it was 17.6% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Early motherhood is a different measure from early marriage, but it follows the same lines.

Money also works through dowry. UNFPA notes that where the bride's family pays dowry, younger brides typically command smaller ones, which pushes poor parents to marry daughters early [[unfpa-child-marriage-2025]]. UNICEF adds what follows: girls who marry before 18 are more likely to face domestic violence and less likely to stay in school [[unicef-child-marriage-topic-page]]. The link runs both ways: schooling is one of the drivers the UN credits for fewer child marriages, and marriage is linked to girls leaving school.

Consider a hypothetical. Two sisters, five years apart, in a village where the nearest secondary school is a long bus ride away. The elder leaves after Class 8 and is married at 16, "while a good family is asking". By the time the younger finishes Class 8, there is a school nearer home, a cousin earning in a city and an aunt who talks about jobs. Her parents discuss college before marriage. The law did not change between the two sisters. Almost everything around it did.

## The distance left: 25% in Southern Asia, 12 million girls a year

Progress is not arrival. Southern Asia still has one of the world's two highest rates: 25% of young women there were married as children, behind only sub-Saharan Africa's 31% [[un-sdg-report-2026-goal5]]. Worldwide, 4% of girls are married before they turn 15 [[unfpa-child-marriage-2025]].

In India, one in five women aged 20-24 in 2023-24 had married before 18, by provisional NFHS-6 data [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. UNICEF India puts the number at no fewer than 1.5 million girls under 18 married every year, though its page does not say how or when that estimate was made [[unicef-india-end-child-marriage]].

Finishing the job will look less like a courtroom than a secondary school within reach, a job a girl can picture for herself, and a family that need not trade her future for a smaller dowry. The law matters at the moment a wedding is being fixed, yet it is barely used: police registered 1,499 cases under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act across India in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], a gap our investigation of the law's FIR numbers sets out. And a falling national average can hide places that may be going the other way. In Delhi, Punjab and Himachal Pradesh the provisional NFHS-6 rate is higher than in NFHS-5, though these figures are provisional and such rises may not be statistically significant [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

The world's curve bent largely because Southern Asia's did. Whether it keeps bending will depend heavily on India finishing what it started two decades ago.
global-child-marriage-decline-india-role.hg:
Duniya mein kahin na kahin har teen second mein ek ladki ki shaadi ho jaati hai. UNFPA isi tarah un lagbhag 12 million ladkiyon ki baat samjhata hai jinki shaadi har saal 18 se pehle ho jaati hai [[unfpa-child-marriage-2025]]. Phir bhi United Nations ab bata raha hai ki trend sudhar raha hai, aur pehle se tezi se. Aur iski wajah humare region ki taraf ishaara karti hai. Bachpan mein byaahi gayi jitni women aaj zinda hain, unmein se har teen mein se ek India mein rehti hai [[un-sdg-report-2024-goal5]]. Isliye duniya ke curve ki, aur jo raasta abhi baaki hai uski, koi bhi imaandaar padtaal India ke apne curve ko dhyaan se dekhe bina poori nahi ho sakti.

## 22% se 18%: ek dashak ki giravat

2015 mein duniya bhar ki 22% young women ki shaadi 18 se pehle ho chuki thi. UN Women aur UN DESA, yaani UN ke Department of Economic and Social Affairs, ka 2026 Gender Snapshot yeh figure 18% batata hai, aur kehta hai ki pichhle dashak mein giravat ki raftaar usse pehle wale dashak ke muqable lagbhag doguni ho gayi [[unwomen-gender-snapshot-2026]]. UN ki SDG Report 2026 bhi yahi kehti hai: 2015-2024 ke beech ki giravat pichhle dashak se doguni thi [[un-sdg-report-2026-goal5]].

Lambi nazar se dekhein toh tasveer aur badi hai. Aaj har paanch mein se ek ladki ki shaadi 18 se pehle hoti hai, jabki 25 saal pehle yeh har chaar mein se ek thi. Is dauraan 68 million child marriages hone se ruk gayi [[un-sdg-report-2024-goal5]].

Is measure ke baare mein ek baat samajh lijiye. Yeh 20 se 24 saal ki women se poochta hai ki kya unki shaadi 18 se pehle hui thi. Isliye 2026 mein chhapa figure kai saal pehle hui shaadiyon ki baat karta hai. Aaj jo child marriages ho rahi hain, woh data mein kai saal baad dikhengi.

## Southern Asia: woh region jisne duniya ko badla

SDG Report 2025 saaf kehti hai ki progress kahan se aayi: duniya bhar mein child marriage "largely due to progress in Southern Asia" kam hui hai, yaani zyadatar Southern Asia ki progress ki wajah se [[un-sdg-report-2025-goal5]]. Sub-Saharan Africa, jahan 31% young women ki shaadi bachpan mein hui thi, ek chetavani hai. Wahan 2030 tak child brides ki ginti badhne ka anumaan hai [[un-sdg-report-2025-goal5]].

India ka wazan ek figure mein dikhta hai. Andaazan 640 million ladkiyan aur women aaj zinda hain jinki shaadi bachpan mein hui thi, aur unmein se ek-tihai India mein rehti hain [[un-sdg-report-2024-goal5]]. Is ginti mein woh daadi-naani bhi hain jinki shaadi dashakon pehle hui thi, isliye yeh itni badi hai. Lekin yeh dikhati hai ki duniya ka kitna bojh ek hi desh mein hai. UN credit region ko deta hai, kisi ek desh ko nahi, aur uske figures giravat mein India ka hissa alag se nahi dikhate. Iske liye India ka apna survey dekhna hoga.

## 47.4% se 20.1%: India ka apna curve

India child marriage ko National Family Health Survey (NFHS) ke zariye track karta hai, aur umar ka paimaana wahi hai [[ceda-genderstats-underage-marriage-2021]].

| Survey round | 20-24 saal ki women jinki shaadi 18 se pehle hui |
|---|---|
| NFHS-3 (2005-06) | 47.4% |
| NFHS-4 (2015-16) | 26.8% |
| NFHS-5 (2019-21) | 23.3% |
| NFHS-6 (2023-24), provisional | 20.1% |

Sirf ek dashak mein India mein bachpan mein byaahi gayi young women ka hissa lagbhag har do mein se ek se ghatkar lagbhag har chaar mein se ek reh gaya. Phir giravat dheemi pad gayi: 2015-16 ke baad ke aath saalon mein yeh hissa kahin zyada dheere gira. UN ke global figures aur India ke survey rounds alag-alag series hain aur alag saalon ko cover karte hain, isliye ek ko doosre se nahi padha ja sakta. Lekin India ke apne numbers saaf hain. Uski giravat ka tez hissa peeche chhoot chuka hai.

National average extremes ko bhi chhupa leta hai. 2023-24 mein yeh rate gaon mein 23.3% tha aur towns aur cities mein 11.4% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. West Bengal (36.4%) aur Bihar (34.6%) aaj us level se bhi upar hain jahan poora India 2015-16 mein tha. Kerala 2.9% pe hai [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

## UN kise credit deta hai: school, kaam, kamaai

UN Women duniya mein tez giravat ke teen drivers ginata hai: ladkiyon ki padhai, economic empowerment aur gareebi mein kami [[unwomen-gender-snapshot-2026]]. Is list mein mukadme, yaani prosecutions, nahi hain. Har driver us hisaab ko badalta hai jo ek family apni beti ke baare mein lagati hai: woh kitna kama sakti hai, aur ghar mein ek aur saal rakhne ka kharcha kitna padega.

Indian data dikhata hai ki zindagi ke yeh jaldi aane wale mod paise aur padhai se kitni kas ke jude hain. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein sabse gareeb gharon ki 15-19 saal ki 10.0% ladkiyan maa ban chuki thi ya pehli baar pregnant thi, jabki sabse ameer gharon mein yeh 2.2% tha. Jo ladkiyan kabhi school nahi gayi, unmein yeh 17.6% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Jaldi maa banna aur jaldi shaadi alag measures hain, lekin dono ek hi lakeeron pe chalte hain.

Paisa dahej ke raaste bhi kaam karta hai. UNFPA bataata hai ki jahan dulhan ki family dahej deti hai, wahan kam umar ki dulhan ka dahej aam taur pe kam hota hai, aur yeh baat gareeb maa-baap ko betiyon ki jaldi shaadi ki taraf dhakelti hai [[unfpa-child-marriage-2025]]. UNICEF aage ki baat jodta hai: jin ladkiyon ki shaadi 18 se pehle hoti hai, unke domestic violence jhelne ke chances zyada hote hain aur school mein tike rehne ke chances kam [[unicef-child-marriage-topic-page]]. Yeh rishta dono taraf chalta hai: UN kam child marriages ka credit jin drivers ko deta hai, unmein padhai ek hai, aur shaadi ka rishta ladkiyon ke school chhodne se juda hai.

Ek hypothetical sochiye. Do behnein, umar mein paanch saal ka farak, ek aise gaon mein jahan sabse paas ka secondary school bus se lambe safar ki doori pe hai. Badi behen Class 8 ke baad padhai chhod deti hai, aur 16 saal mein uski shaadi ho jaati hai, "jab tak achha ghar rishta maang raha hai". Jab tak chhoti behen Class 8 khatam karti hai, ghar ke paas ek school khul chuka hai, ek cousin shehar mein kama raha hai, aur ek mausi naukri ki baatein karti hai. Uske maa-baap shaadi se pehle college ki baat karte hain. Dono behnon ke beech law nahi badla. Uske aas-paas lagbhag sab kuch badal gaya.

## Kitna raasta baaki hai: Southern Asia mein 25%, har saal 12 million ladkiyan

Progress ka matlab manzil pe pahunch jaana nahi hai. Southern Asia ka rate ab bhi duniya ke do sabse oonche rates mein se ek hai: wahan 25% young women ki shaadi bachpan mein hui thi, aur isse aage sirf sub-Saharan Africa hai, 31% pe [[un-sdg-report-2026-goal5]]. Duniya bhar mein 4% ladkiyon ki shaadi 15 saal ki hone se pehle hi ho jaati hai [[unfpa-child-marriage-2025]].

India mein, provisional NFHS-6 data ke hisaab se, 2023-24 mein 20-24 saal ki har paanch mein se ek woman ki shaadi 18 se pehle ho chuki thi [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. UNICEF India ke mutaabik har saal kam se kam 1.5 million ladkiyon ki shaadi 18 se pehle hoti hai, haalaanki uska page yeh nahi batata ki yeh andaaza kaise aur kab lagaya gaya [[unicef-india-end-child-marriage]].

Yeh kaam poora karna courtroom jaisa kam, aur kuch aisa zyada dikhega: paas mein ek secondary school, ek aisi naukri jiska sapna ladki khud apne liye dekh sake, aur ek aisi family jise chhote dahej ke badle uska future na bechna pade. Jab shaadi tay ho rahi hoti hai, us waqt law zaroor matter karta hai, lekin uska istemaal na ke barabar hota hai: 2024 mein poore India mein police ne Prohibition of Child Marriage Act ke under 1,499 cases darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Is gap ko is law ke FIR numbers pe humari investigation samjhati hai. Aur girta national average un jagahon ko chhupa sakta hai jo shaayad ulti disha mein ja rahi hain. Delhi, Punjab aur Himachal Pradesh mein provisional NFHS-6 rate NFHS-5 se zyada hai, haalaanki yeh figures provisional hain aur ho sakta hai aisi badhat statistically significant na ho [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

Duniya ka curve zyadatar isliye muda kyunki Southern Asia ka curve muda. Woh aage bhi mudta rahega ya nahi, yeh kaafi had tak is baat pe tika hai ki India do dashak pehle shuru kiya hua kaam poora karta hai ya nahi.

health-workers-spot-child-abuse.en:
Consider an eight-year-old boy brought to a district hospital OPD in Nagpur because he has started wetting the bed again. His mother mentions that he has stopped going to tuition and screams when she insists. The examination is normal. A busy doctor writes "reassured" and calls the next patient. Abused children rarely arrive with a disclosure: in the government's 2007 Study on Child Abuse, 72.1% of children who had been sexually assaulted had told no one [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. This guide is for the nurses, ASHAs, ANMs and young doctors who see them first. It is general information, not legal advice.

## Why the clinic is often the first place abuse shows

A child who cannot tell a parent may still be brought to you, with a recurring stomach ache, sleeplessness, falling marks or a pregnancy at 14. The abuse often comes from inside the circle that brings the child. In 2024, 3,658 cases of penetrative sexual assault on children named a family member as the accused, and 16,668 a family friend, neighbour, employer or other known person [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Two consequences follow. The adult answering for the child may be the one harming them, and your OPD, ward or home visit may be the only place where an adult outside that circle looks closely.

## Signs to notice, and questions that do not lead

The US nonprofit Darkness to Light notes that emotional and behavioural signs of sexual abuse are more common than physical ones: anxiety or depression, nightmares and sleep problems, unusual fear of a person or reluctance to be alone with them, regression such as bedwetting, changes in mood or attitude to school, and sexual knowledge beyond the child's age [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. UNICEF lists headaches, stomach aches and appetite changes among the signs of a child distressed by something that happened online [[unicef-parenting-negative-online-experience-2026]]. None of these proves abuse. Each is a reason to ask.

How you ask decides what you hear, and what a court can later rely on.

- If an older child agrees, see them alone for part of the visit. "I see every patient your age on their own for a few minutes" accuses nobody.
- Use open prompts: "Tell me about that." "What happened next?" Never "Did your uncle touch you here?"
- Do not show shock or disbelief, and do not make the child repeat the story to colleagues.
- Do not promise total secrecy. Say what you will do: "I will need to tell people whose job is to keep you safe."

## Free treatment, consent and the banned two-finger test

Under Section 397 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), every hospital, public or private, must immediately give free first aid or treatment to victims of rape and of POCSO offences, and inform the police [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. A hospital in-charge who breaks this rule faces up to a year in prison under Section 200 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Never send a child away to come back with an FIR.

Some care cannot wait. HIV post-exposure prophylaxis must start as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after exposure [[who-pep]]. For an adolescent girl, emergency contraception works up to five days after, and sooner is better [[who-ec]].

For the forensic examination, BNSS Section 184 requires police to send a rape survivor to a doctor within 24 hours of being informed, makes her consent a precondition, and gives the doctor 7 days to send the report to the investigating officer [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. With a child, explain each step in words they understand, and stop if they ask.

Never perform the two-finger test. In 2013 the Supreme Court held that it violates survivors' right to privacy, physical and mental integrity and dignity [[barandbench-lillu-2013]]. On 31 October 2022 it said the test "has no scientific basis and neither proves nor disproves allegations of rape", ordered it out of medical curricula, and held that anyone who conducts it is guilty of misconduct [[theprint-sc-two-finger-test-2022]].

## Your duty to report, and what the 2022 ruling allows

Under POCSO, anyone who knows or suspects that a child sexual offence has been, or is likely to be, committed must report it to the Special Juvenile Police Unit or the local police [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Failing to report or record a case can mean up to 6 months in prison or a fine, and the head of an institution who fails to report abuse by a subordinate faces up to 1 year and a fine [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Every pregnancy in a girl under 18 falls under this duty. In 2022 the Supreme Court observed that pregnant minors and their guardians therefore face a choice between a registered doctor and possible criminal proceedings, or an unqualified provider. It ruled that a doctor terminating a minor's pregnancy need not disclose her identity or personal details in the POCSO report if she and her guardian ask [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. The report itself remains mandatory. Tell girls and families about this option early: it may keep them away from quacks.

## Documentation, referral and keeping the child's trust

Write notes the same day, as if a court will read them, because one may. Record the child's words in quotation marks, the questions you asked, who was present, the child's behaviour, findings in plain description, treatment given, and whom you informed and when. Record facts, not conclusions such as "no abuse".

Refer, do not investigate. Inform the police, and call 1098, the 24x7 Child Helpline linked to the emergency number 112 [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]. ASHAs and ANMs who notice something on a home visit can call too, and should tell the medical officer. For a girl made pregnant by rape, a central scheme launched in 2023 offers shelter, medical and maternity care, legal aid, counselling and education support [[mwcd-pocso-victim-support-scheme-2023]].

Keeping a child's trust does not mean keeping secrets. It means telling them honestly, in advance, what happens next; letting them choose who stays in the room; sharing their name only with those who must know; and being there at the follow-up. A calm, believing first response is part of the treatment.
health-workers-spot-child-abuse.hg:
Sochiye, Nagpur ke ek district hospital ki OPD mein ek aath saal ke ladke ko laaya jaata hai, kyunki woh phir se bistar geela karne laga hai. Uski maa baaton-baaton mein bata deti hai ki usne tuition jaana chhod diya hai, aur zabardasti karne par woh cheekhne lagta hai. Examination normal hai. Ek busy doctor "reassured" likhta hai aur agle patient ko bula leta hai. Abuse jhel rahe bachche shayad hi kabhi khud bata kar aate hain: sarkar ki 2007 ki Study on Child Abuse mein, jin bachchon ka sexual assault hua tha, unmein se 72.1% ne kisi ko kuch nahi bataya tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Yeh guide un nurses, ASHAs, ANMs aur young doctors ke liye hai jo inhe sabse pehle dekhte hain. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Abuse aksar sabse pehle clinic mein kyun dikhta hai

Jo bachcha parents ko nahi bata paata, use bhi aapke paas laaya ja sakta hai: baar-baar hone wale pet dard, neend na aane, girte marks ya 14 saal ki umar mein pregnancy ke saath. Abuse aksar usi daayre ke andar se hota hai jo bachche ko lekar aata hai. 2024 mein bachchon par penetrative sexual assault ke 3,658 cases mein accused family ka hi koi sadasya tha, aur 16,668 mein koi family friend, padosi, employer ya doosra jaan-pehchaan wala [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Iske do matlab hain. Bachche ki taraf se jawab dene wala adult hi shayad use nuksaan pahuncha raha ho, aur aapki OPD, ward ya home visit shayad woh akeli jagah ho jahan us daayre ke bahar ka koi adult bachche ko dhyaan se dekhta hai.

## Kin sanketon par dhyaan dein, aur aise sawaal jo leading na hon

US ki nonprofit Darkness to Light ke mutabik sexual abuse ke emotional aur behavioural sanket physical sanketon se zyada common hain: anxiety ya depression, bure sapne aur neend ki dikkat, kisi insaan se ajeeb sa darr ya uske saath akele rehne se katraana, phir se bistar geela karne jaisi chhoot chuki aadaton par laut jaana, mood ya school ke prati ravaiye mein badlaav, aur umar se zyada sexual jaankari [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. UNICEF online kuch bura hone se pareshaan bachche ke sanketon mein sir dard, pet dard aur bhookh mein badlaav ginata hai [[unicef-parenting-negative-online-experience-2026]]. Inmein se koi bhi sanket abuse ka sabut nahi hai. Har ek, poochhne ki wajah hai.

Aap kaise poochhte hain, isi se tay hota hai ki aap kya sunenge, aur court baad mein kis baat par bharosa kar paayega.

- Agar bada bachcha maan jaaye, toh visit ke kuch hisse mein usse akele mil kar baat kariye. "Main tumhari umar ke har patient se kuch minute akele mein milta hoon" kehne se kisi par ilzaam nahi lagta.
- Open prompts use kariye: "Is baare mein batao." "Phir kya hua?" Kabhi nahi: "Kya tumhare uncle ne tumhe yahan chhua?"
- Shock ya avishvaas mat dikhaiye, aur bachche se colleagues ke saamne kahani dobara mat bulwaiye.
- Poori tarah secret rakhne ka vaada mat kariye. Bataiye ki aap kya karenge: "Mujhe un logon ko batana hoga jinka kaam tumhe safe rakhna hai."

## Muft ilaaj, consent aur banned two-finger test

Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ke Section 397 ke under har hospital, sarkari ho ya private, rape aur POCSO offences ke victims ko turant muft first aid ya ilaaj dega, aur police ko soochit karega [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Jo hospital in-charge is rule ko todta hai, use Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke Section 200 ke under ek saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Kisi bachche ko "pehle FIR lekar aao" keh kar kabhi waapas mat bhejiye.

Kuch ilaaj intezaar nahi kar sakta. HIV post-exposure prophylaxis jitni jaldi ho sake shuru honi chahiye, aur exposure ke 72 ghante ke andar hi [[who-pep]]. Kisi teenage ladki ke liye emergency contraception paanch din tak kaam karti hai, aur jitni jaldi li jaaye utna behtar [[who-ec]].

Forensic examination ke liye BNSS Section 184 kehta hai ki police ko jaankari milne ke 24 ghante ke andar rape survivor ko doctor ke paas bhejna hoga, uski consent ke bina examination nahi ho sakta, aur doctor ko 7 din ke andar report investigating officer ko bhejni hogi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Bachche ko har step uski samajh ke shabdon mein samjhaiye, aur agar woh rukne ko kahe toh ruk jaiye.

Two-finger test kabhi mat kariye. 2013 mein Supreme Court ne kaha tha ki yeh test survivors ke privacy, sharirik aur maansik integrity aur dignity ke adhikaar ka ulanghan hai [[barandbench-lillu-2013]]. 31 October 2022 ko court ne kaha ki is test ka koi scientific aadhaar nahi hai aur yeh rape ke aarop ko na saabit karta hai, na galat; court ne ise medical curriculum se hatane ka aadesh diya, aur kaha ki jo bhi yeh test karega woh misconduct ka doshi hoga [[theprint-sc-two-finger-test-2022]].

## Report karne ki aapki zimmedari, aur 2022 ka faisla kya chhoot deta hai

POCSO ke under, jise bhi pata ho ya shak ho ki kisi bachche ke khilaaf sexual offence hua hai ya hone ki sambhavna hai, use Special Juvenile Police Unit ya local police ko report karna hoga [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Report na karna ya case record na karna 6 mahine tak ki jail ya fine dila sakta hai, aur jo institution head apne under kaam karne wale ke abuse ki report nahi karta, use 1 saal tak ki jail aur fine ho sakta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

18 saal se kam umar ki ladki ki har pregnancy is zimmedari ke daayre mein aati hai. 2022 mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki isi wajah se pregnant minors aur unke guardians ke saamne ek mushkil choice hoti hai: registered doctor ke paas jaayein aur criminal case ka risk lein, ya kisi unqualified insaan ke paas jaayein. Court ne faisla diya ki minor ki pregnancy terminate karne wale doctor ko, agar minor aur uske guardian kahein, POCSO report mein uski pehchaan ya personal details batane ki zaroorat nahi [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Report karna phir bhi zaroori hai. Ladkiyon aur unke parivaaron ko is option ke baare mein jaldi bataiye: isse woh jhola-chhaap doctors se bach sakti hain.

## Documentation, referral aur bachche ka bharosa banaye rakhna

Notes usi din likhiye, yeh maan kar ki court unhe padhega, kyunki shayad padhe bhi. Bachche ke shabd quotation marks mein likhiye; aapne kya sawaal poochhe, kaun maujood tha, bachche ka bartaav, findings seedhe shabdon mein, kya ilaaj diya, aur kise kab soochit kiya. Facts likhiye, "no abuse" jaise nateeje nahi.

Refer kariye, khud investigation mat kariye. Police ko soochit kariye, aur 1098 par call kariye, jo 24x7 Child Helpline hai aur emergency number 112 se judi hai [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].
