Home visit par kuch notice karne wali ASHAs aur ANMs bhi call kar sakti hain, aur unhe medical officer ko bhi batana chahiye. Rape se pregnant hui ladki ke liye 2023 mein shuru hui ek central scheme shelter, medical aur maternity care, legal aid, counselling aur padhai mein madad deti hai [[mwcd-pocso-victim-support-scheme-2023]].

Bachche ka bharosa banaye rakhne ka matlab secrets rakhna nahi hai. Iska matlab hai use pehle se, imaandaari se batana ki aage kya hoga; use chunne dena ki kamre mein kaun rahe; uska naam sirf unhi ko batana jinhe zaroorat hai; aur follow-up par maujood rehna. Shaant aur bharosa karne wala pehla reaction bhi ilaaj ka hissa hai.

household-rules-prevent-child-abuse.en:
Consider an ordinary weekday for a nine-year-old in Pune. The school van at seven. Tuition at five. A driver who fetches her from dance class. An uncle sleeping over for a cousin's wedding. She chose none of these arrangements; adults did. That matters because of who harms children. In 2024 police in India recorded 44,126 cases of penetrative sexual assault on children under POCSO. In 3,658 the accused was a family member, and in 16,668 a family friend, neighbour, employer or other known person. Only 1,492 involved someone unknown [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. This guide is about those arrangements, and the rules adults can set for them.

## Why the rules are for adults, not children

Body-safety lessons teach children to say no, get away and tell. They matter, but they hand the job to the smallest person in the room. In 2024, 831 child victims of penetrative sexual assault were under six and 3,438 were aged 6-12 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Young children rarely disclose, so these counts are minimums. A six-year-old cannot refuse the van her parents booked or the tutor they pay.

The government's 2007 Study on Child Abuse found that half of abusers were known to the child or in a position of trust, and that most children told no one [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

Grooming runs on things adults can see. The US nonprofit Darkness to Light lists its red flags as special attention to one child, gifts, touching or hugging, being the sympathetic listener, offers to help the family, and access through the internet [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. Most of them need time alone, a gift or a secret, and adults decide who gets those.

The only early warning may be a change in behaviour: nightmares, bedwetting again, unusual fear of one person or reluctance to be alone with them, signs Darkness to Light says are more common than physical ones [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. A house rule that no child must go with someone they do not want to turns that warning into action, instead of "Don't be rude to Uncle."

## Time alone: tuition, coaching and 'special' attention

Home tuition belongs at the dining table or in a room with the door open, while another adult at home walks past at no fixed time. If classes are at the tutor's home, find out who else is there, and collect your child from the door. "Extra help" for one child alone, after hours or at a teacher's flat, is the first flag on that list; ask for it in a group, within class hours.

Time alone now includes the phone. UNICEF warns that online abusers may be someone the child knows, and often first win the trust of the child or a caregiver [[unicef-keeping-children-safe-online-2026]]. Tutors, coaches and drivers should message parents, not children; class groups should include a parent; phones charge outside bedrooms at night.

At home, no adult gets unplanned "special" time alone with one child, and nobody gives your children gifts you do not know about. Surprises are fine, because everyone finds out soon; secrets from parents are not.

## Bathing, sleepovers and overnight guests

Once children can bathe and use the toilet on their own, let them, door closed. When a young child needs help, it comes from a parent or one named caregiver, not a visiting relative or an older cousin. Use the correct names for body parts, so a child can say exactly what happened.

Weddings, festivals and long family visits are when Indian homes are most crowded and least watched, and children sleep wherever there is floor space. Make one rule for these nights: children sleep with their parents or with children their own age, in a room adults can look into, never in a bed with an adult guest.

Before a sleepover at a friend's home, ask who else will be there overnight: older brothers, uncles, staff. Tell your child they can call at any hour and you will come, no questions asked.

Sons need the same rules as daughters: in the 2007 government study, boys made up 52.94% of the children who reported sexual abuse [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. That sample included many working and street children, who are more often boys, but it is a reminder that boys are not safe by default.

## Drivers, domestic staff and the school van

Police data does not count drivers, van staff or domestic workers separately [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

For the school van, learn the driver's and attendant's names and numbers, and ask the operator whether a second adult rides on every trip. Find out which child is dropped last, because that child ends every journey alone with the driver. If it is yours, change the route, the seat or the pick-up. Young children sit at the back.

At home, no driver or domestic worker should be the only adult with a child behind a closed door, bathe a school-age child, or take a child out without you knowing where. Police verification checks a record, not intentions. And these rules are not about suspecting the people who work in your home: they bind the visiting uncle and the trusted neighbour too.

## Introducing rules without accusing anyone

Present each rule as household policy, not a verdict on a person: "In our house, tuition happens at the dining table." Apply it to everyone, starting with the people you trust most, because that is where the data says the risk sits.

Tell children the rules too, so they notice when one is broken: "No grown-up should ask you to keep a secret from us, or to be alone with them. If anyone does, tell us. You will not be in trouble."

If a child suddenly refuses tuition, cries before the van or avoids one relative, do not force it. Change the arrangement first and ask open questions later. Darkness to Light cautions that such signs can look like any other childhood stress; they call for attention, not conclusions [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]].

If a child tells you something has happened, this is no longer about rules. Under POCSO, reporting child sexual abuse is mandatory for anyone who knows of it [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Believe the child, and call 1098, the 24x7 Child Helpline linked to the emergency number 112 [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].
household-rules-prevent-child-abuse.hg:
Pune mein ek nau saal ki bachchi ka ek aam din sochiye. Subah saat baje school van. Shaam paanch baje tuition. Dance class se lene aane wala driver. Cousin ki shaadi ke liye raat ko ruke hue ek uncle. Inmein se koi bhi intezaam usne nahi chuna; sab badon ne kiya. Yeh baat isliye maayne rakhti hai, kyunki asli sawaal yeh hai ki bachchon ko nuksaan kaun pahunchata hai. 2024 mein India mein police ne POCSO ke under bachchon par penetrative sexual assault ke 44,126 cases darj kiye. Inmein se 3,658 cases mein accused family ka hi koi sadasya tha, aur 16,668 mein koi family friend, padosi, employer ya doosra jaan-pehchaan wala. Sirf 1,492 cases mein accused koi anjaan insaan tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh guide inhi intezaamon ke baare mein hai, aur un rules ke baare mein jo bade inke liye bana sakte hain.

## Rules bachchon ke liye nahi, badon ke liye kyun hain

Body-safety lessons bachchon ko sikhate hain ki "na" kaho, wahan se nikal jao aur kisi ko batao. Yeh zaroori hain, lekin isse saari zimmedari kamre ke sabse chhote insaan par aa jaati hai. 2024 mein penetrative sexual assault ke victim bachchon mein se 831 chhe saal se chhote the aur 3,438 ki umar 6-12 saal thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Chhote bachche bahut kam bata paate hain, isliye yeh ginti asal sankhya se kam hi hai. Chhe saal ki bachchi us van ko mana nahi kar sakti jo uske parents ne book ki hai, ya us tutor ko jise woh fees dete hain.

Sarkar ki 2007 ki Study on Child Abuse mein nikla ki aadhe abusers bachche ke jaan-pehchaan wale the ya bharose ki position mein the, aur zyadatar bachchon ne kisi ko kuch nahi bataya [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

Grooming un cheezon par chalti hai jo badon ko dikh sakti hain. US ki nonprofit Darkness to Light ke red flags yeh hain: kisi ek bachche par special attention, gifts, chhoona ya hug karna, hamdard listener banna, family ki madad ki offer, aur internet ke zariye pahunch [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. Inmein se zyadatar ke liye akele mein waqt, koi gift ya koi secret chahiye, aur yeh kise milega, yeh bade tay karte hain.

Sabse pehli chetavani shayad sirf bachche ke bartaav mein badlaav ho: bure sapne, phir se bistar geela karna, kisi ek insaan se ajeeb sa darr ya uske saath akele rehne se katraana. Darkness to Light ke mutabik aise sanket physical sanketon se zyada common hain [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. Ghar ka ek rule, ki kisi bachche ko aise insaan ke saath jaane ke liye majboor nahi kiya jaayega jiske saath woh nahi jaana chahta, is chetavani ko action mein badal deta hai. Warna hum bas itna kehte hain, "Uncle ke saath badtameezi mat karo."

## Akele mein waqt: tuition, coaching aur 'special' attention

Home tuition dining table par honi chahiye, ya aise kamre mein jiska darwaza khula ho, jab ghar mein koi aur adult ho jo bina kisi fixed time ke beech-beech mein aata-jaata rahe. Agar class tutor ke ghar par hai, toh pata kariye ki wahan aur kaun rehta hai, aur bachche ko darwaze se khud lekar aaiye. Kisi ek bachche ko akele mein "extra help", class ke time ke baad ya teacher ke flat par, us list ka pehla red flag hai; yeh madad group mein aur class ke time mein hi maangiye.

Akele mein waqt ab phone par bhi milta hai. UNICEF chetavani deta hai ki online abuser koi aisa bhi ho sakta hai jise bachcha jaanta ho, aur woh aksar pehle bachche ya uske ghar walon ka trust jeetta hai [[unicef-keeping-children-safe-online-2026]]. Tutor, coach aur driver bachchon ko nahi, parents ko message karein; class ke groups mein ek parent zaroor ho; raat ko phone bedroom ke bahar charge hon.

Ghar par, koi bhi adult bina planning ke kisi ek bachche ke saath "special" akela waqt nahi bitayega, aur koi aapke bachchon ko aise gifts nahi dega jinke baare mein aapko pata na ho. Surprise theek hai, kyunki sabko jaldi pata chal jaata hai; parents se chhupaya gaya secret theek nahi.

## Nahana, sleepovers aur raat ko rukne wale mehmaan

Jab bachche khud naha sakein aur toilet ja sakein, toh unhe darwaza band karke khud karne dijiye. Jab kisi chhote bachche ko madad chahiye, toh woh parent ya ek tay caregiver de, koi aaya hua rishtedaar ya bada cousin nahi. Body parts ke sahi naam sikhaiye, taaki bachcha theek-theek bata sake ki kya hua.

Shaadiyan, tyohaar aur lambe family visits woh waqt hain jab hamare ghar sabse zyada bhare hote hain aur nigrani sabse kam hoti hai, aur bachche jahan jagah mile wahin so jaate hain. In raaton ke liye ek rule banaiye: bachche apne parents ke saath ya apni umar ke bachchon ke saath soyenge, aise kamre mein jahan bade jhaank sakein, aur kisi adult mehmaan ke saath ek bistar par kabhi nahi.

Kisi dost ke ghar sleepover se pehle poochhiye ki raat ko ghar mein aur kaun hoga: bade bhai, uncles, staff. Bachche ko bataiye ki woh kisi bhi waqt call kar sakta hai aur aap use lene aa jayenge, koi sawaal nahi poochha jaayega.

Beton ko bhi betiyon jitne hi rules chahiye: 2007 ki sarkari study mein sexual abuse report karne wale bachchon mein 52.94% ladke the [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Us sample mein kaam karne wale aur sadak par rehne wale bahut se bachche the, jinmein ladke zyada hote hain, lekin yeh yaad dilata hai ki ladke apne aap surakshit nahi hote.

## Driver, gharelu staff aur school van

Police data mein driver, van staff ya gharelu kaamgaron ki alag ginti nahi hoti [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

School van ke liye driver aur attendant ke naam aur number jaaniye, aur operator se poochhiye ki kya har trip par ek doosra adult bhi saath hota hai. Pata kariye ki sabse aakhir mein kis bachche ko utaara jaata hai, kyunki woh bachcha har safar ka aakhri hissa driver ke saath akele bitata hai. Agar woh aapka bachcha hai, toh route, seat ya pick-up badaliye. Chhote bachche peeche baithein.

Ghar par, koi driver ya gharelu kaamgar band darwaze ke peeche kisi bachche ke saath akela adult na ho, school jaane wale bachche ko na nahlaye, aur aapko bataye bina bachche ko bahar na le jaaye. Police verification sirf record check karta hai, irade nahi. Aur yeh rules aapke ghar mein kaam karne walon par shak karne ke liye nahi hain: yeh ghar aaye uncle aur bharose wale padosi par bhi utne hi laagu hote hain.

## Kisi par ilzaam lagaye bina rules kaise laayein

Har rule ko ghar ki policy ki tarah rakhiye, kisi insaan ke baare mein faisle ki tarah nahi: "Hamare ghar mein tuition dining table par hoti hai." Ise sab par laagu kariye, shuruaat un logon se jin par aap sabse zyada bharosa karte hain, kyunki data ke hisaab se khatra wahin hai.

Bachchon ko bhi rules bataiye, taaki koi rule toote toh unhe pata chale: "Koi bhi bada tumse humse secret rakhne ko ya apne saath akele rehne ko nahi kahega. Agar koi aisa kahe, toh humein batana. Tum kisi musibat mein nahi padoge."

Agar bachcha achanak tuition jaane se mana kare, van se pehle roye ya kisi ek rishtedaar se katraye, toh zabardasti mat kariye. Pehle intezaam badaliye, phir aaram se open questions poochhiye. Darkness to Light chetavani deti hai ki aise sanket bachpan ke kisi aur stress jaise bhi dikh sakte hain; inpar dhyaan dena zaroori hai, seedha nateeja nikaalna nahi [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]].

Agar bachcha bataye ki kuch hua hai, toh baat ab rules ki nahi rahi. POCSO ke under, jise bhi bachche ke sexual abuse ka pata ho, uske liye report karna zaroori hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Bachche par bharosa kariye, aur 1098 par call kariye, jo 24x7 Child Helpline hai aur emergency number 112 se judi hai [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].

how-child-grooming-works-red-flags.en:
In 2024, police in India registered 44,126 cases of penetrative sexual assault on children. In 16,668 of them, the accused was a family friend, a neighbour, an employer or another known person [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. These are not strangers who broke in. They are people families let in, trusted with a house key or an hour alone with a child. Our "stranger danger" data story shows who abuses children. This one shows how they get that close, through grooming, and how to interrupt it.

## Grooming is a process, not a moment

Darkness to Light, a US child-protection nonprofit, defines grooming as a deliberate process by which offenders gradually build and keep a secret sexual relationship with a child. On the surface, it says, grooming can look like a close relationship between the adult, the child and even the child's caregivers [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. That is the design: each step, alone, looks like kindness.

The goal is silence. India's 2007 government study on child abuse found that half of the abusers were people the child knew or people in a position of trust, and that most children told no one [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

## Stage by stage: choosing, befriending, testing, isolating, silencing

Grooming follows no fixed script, but it is easier to spot when you see it in stages. Consider a hypothetical. A ten-year-old boy lives in a Patna lane with his mother, who works long shifts. A neighbour who runs the mobile shop at the corner, "uncle" to every child in the lane, takes an interest.

- **Choosing.** He picks the child who is alone after school, hungry for attention and least likely to be believed.
- **Befriending.** He listens. He gives a cricket bat, a mobile recharge, games on his phone. The boy feels chosen.
- **Testing.** Tickling that goes on after the boy says stop, a hand that stays too long, a "joke" about bodies, a video no child should see. Each step checks two things: will the boy object, and will anyone notice?
- **Isolating.** Free maths coaching at uncle's flat, rides on his scooter: time alone that the family itself approves of.
- **Silencing.** "This stays between us." The gifts become a debt. The boy fears he will be blamed, or that his mother will lose a neighbour she relies on.

The boy in this example is not an exception. In the 2007 study, whose sample included many working and street children, boys made up 52.94% of the children who reported sexual abuse. The abuse children reported began as early as age five, gained momentum from ten and peaked between 12 and 15 [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

## Why the family is groomed too

One of Darkness to Light's six red flags is an adult who offers to help the family [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. UNICEF describes the same move online: abusers often first win the trust of the child or a caregiver, and only then manipulate the child into sharing sexual images or videos [[unicef-keeping-children-safe-online-2026]].

In an Indian home, grooming the family can look like a string of favours: a loan when the rent is late, a lift to the hospital, a job lead for an older brother, an offer to "keep an eye" on the children. Each favour buys two things: access to the child, and a family that will struggle to believe, or to complain about, the man who helped them. When a child finally speaks, that goodwill is the first thing the child has to argue against.

## The six red flags in Indian homes and neighbourhoods

Darkness to Light's six red flags [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]], as they can look here:

1. **Special attention to one child:** asking for her by name, picking him for the extra class, favouring one sibling.
2. **Gift giving:** chocolates, cash, a phone or a data recharge, especially gifts parents are not told about.
3. **Touching or hugging:** lap-sitting, tickling and wrestling "games", hugs the child tries to slip out of.
4. **A sympathetic listener:** taking the child's side against parents and teachers until he is the only adult the child confides in.
5. **Offers to help the family:** tuition, school pick-ups, babysitting, money.
6. **Access through the internet:** gaming chats, direct messages, a second account. On gaming platforms, offenders can pull a child into a high-risk grooming conversation within 19 seconds of the first message, and within 45 minutes on average, according to risk-intelligence data cited by WeProtect [[weprotect-gta-2023]].

One flag proves nothing; these are indicators, not evidence. A cluster aimed at one child is what to watch. Online, Indian law already names the pattern: Section 67B of the IT Act punishes enticing children into online sexual relationships, with up to five years in prison on a first conviction [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Worldwide, the US-based NCMEC received 1.4 million reports of online enticement of children in 2025 [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]].

## How to interrupt without accusing anyone

You need no proof to change the rules, and rules accuse no one. Grooming runs on access, secrecy and trust; every stage has a counter-move.

- **Spread the special attention.** "Thank you for helping him with maths. Could you take the whole group on Sundays?"
- **Route gifts and favours through you.** "In our family, gifts for children come through us." "Thank you, I'll drop him myself." Accept the help that does not need your child.
- **Back the child's "stop".** If a child wriggles out of a hug or tickling, say it out loud: "He said stop, so we stop." Children learn that "no" counts when adults enforce it.
- **Be the listener first.** A groomer moves into the space where nobody else is listening. Ask open questions every day, and never punish what a child tells you.
- **One rule for everyone,** relatives and old family friends included, so nobody is singled out.
- **Watch the reaction.** Someone who respects a boundary says "of course". Someone who argues, sulks or quietly works around it has told you something.

If a child tells you something has happened, this is no longer about rules. Under POCSO, anyone who knows of child sexual abuse must report it [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Call 1098 or 112 [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]], and report online grooming at cybercrime.gov.in or on 1930 [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].
how-child-grooming-works-red-flags.hg:
2024 mein India mein police ne bachchon par penetrative sexual assault, yaani child rape, ke 44,126 cases register kiye. Inmein se 16,668 cases mein accused family friend, padosi, employer ya koi aur jaan-pehchaan wala tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh koi stranger nahi the jo zabardasti ghar mein ghuse. Yeh woh log hain jinhe families khud andar aane deti hain, jinhe ghar ki chaabi ya bachche ke saath ghanta bhar akele rehne ka bharosa milta hai. Hamari "stranger danger" wali data story batati hai ki bachchon ka abuse kaun karta hai. Yeh story batati hai ki woh itne kareeb pahunchte kaise hain, yaani grooming se, aur ise roka kaise jaaye.

## Grooming ek pal ki baat nahi, poora process hai

Darkness to Light, US ki ek child-protection nonprofit, grooming ko ek soch-samajhkar kiya gaya process maanti hai, jismein abuser dheere-dheere bachche ke saath sexual abuse ka silsila shuru karta hai aur use secret banaye rakhta hai. Sanstha kehti hai ki upar se yeh kisi adult, bachche aur yahan tak ki parents ke beech ek close rishte jaisa dikh sakta hai [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. Yahi iski chaal hai: har step, alag se dekhein toh, kindness jaisa lagta hai.

Maksad hota hai chuppi. Sarkar ki 2007 ki child abuse study mein nikla ki aadhe abusers aise log the jinhe bachcha jaanta tha ya jo bachche ke liye bharose aur zimmedari wali jagah par the, aur zyadatar bachchon ne kisi ko kuch nahi bataya [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

## Step by step: chunna, dosti, parakhna, akela karna, chup karana

Grooming ki koi fixed script nahi hoti, lekin stages mein dekhein toh ise pehchanna aasaan hota hai. Ek hypothetical situation sochiye. Patna ki ek gali mein das saal ka ek ladka apni maa ke saath rehta hai. Maa lambi shifts mein kaam karti hai. Nukkad par mobile ki dukaan chalane wala ek padosi, jise gali ka har bachcha "uncle" kehta hai, us mein interest lene lagta hai.

- **Chunna.** Woh aisa bachcha chunta hai jo school ke baad akela rehta hai, jise attention ki bhookh hai, aur jiski baat par sabse kam yakeen kiya jaayega.
- **Dosti.** Woh uski baatein sunta hai. Cricket bat deta hai, mobile recharge karata hai, apne phone par games khelne deta hai. Bachche ko lagta hai ki woh special hai.
- **Parakhna.** Gudgudi jo bachche ke "bas" kehne ke baad bhi nahi rukti, ek haath jo zaroorat se zyada der tak tika rehta hai, body ko lekar koi "mazaak", koi aisa video jo kisi bachche ko nahi dekhna chahiye. Har step do cheezein parakhta hai: kya bachcha virodh karega, aur kya kisi ka dhyaan jaayega?
- **Akela karna.** Uncle ke flat par free maths coaching, scooter par ghumana: yaani akele mein waqt, jise khud ghar wale theek maante hain.
- **Chup karana.** "Yeh baat hum dono ke beech rahegi." Gifts ab ehsaan ban jaate hain. Bachche ko darr lagta hai ki blame usi par aayega, ya maa ek aise padosi ko kho degi jis par woh depend karti hai.

Is misaal wala ladka koi anokha case nahi hai. 2007 ki study mein, jiske sample mein kaam karne wale aur sadak par rehne wale bahut se bachche the, sexual abuse report karne wale bachchon mein 52.94% ladke the. Bachchon ne jo abuse bataya, woh paanch saal ki umar mein bhi shuru ho jaata tha, das saal ke baad tezi se badhta tha, aur 12 se 15 saal ki umar mein sabse zyada tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

## Poori family ki grooming kyun hoti hai

Darkness to Light ke chhe red flags mein se ek hai: aisa adult jo family ki madad ki offer karta rahe [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. UNICEF online duniya mein bhi yahi chaal batata hai: abusers aksar pehle bachche ya uske ghar walon ka trust jeette hain, aur uske baad hi bachche ko manipulate karke usse sexual images ya videos bhijwaate hain [[unicef-keeping-children-safe-online-2026]].

Hamare gharon mein family ki grooming ehsaanon ki ek lambi line jaisi dikh sakti hai: rent late ho toh udhaar, hospital jaana ho toh gaadi, bade bete ke liye naukri ki baat, ya "bachchon ka dhyaan main rakh lunga" wali offer. Har ehsaan do cheezein khareedta hai. Ek, bachche tak pahunch. Doosri, ek aisi family jiske liye us aadmi par shak karna ya uski complaint karna mushkil hoga jisne unki madad ki thi. Jab bachcha aakhirkaar bolta hai, toh use sabse pehle isi ehsaan se ladna padta hai.

## Ghar aur mohalle mein chhe red flags

Yeh hain Darkness to Light ke chhe red flags [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]], aur hamare yahan yeh aise dikh sakte hain:

1. **Kisi ek bachche par special attention:** use naam lekar baar-baar bulana, extra class ke liye usi ko chunna, bhai-behnon mein se ek ko hi favour karna.
2. **Gifts dena:** chocolate, paise, phone ya data recharge, khaaskar aise gifts jinke baare mein parents ko bataya nahi jaata.
3. **Chhoona ya hug karna:** god mein bithana, gudgudi aur kushti wale "games", aise hug jinse bachcha chhootkar bhaagna chahe.
4. **Hamdard listener banna:** parents aur teachers ke khilaaf bachche ka saath dena, jab tak bachcha sirf usi se dil ki baat na kehne lage.
5. **Family ki madad ki offer:** tuition, school pick-up, bachchon ko sambhalna, paise.
6. **Internet se pahunch:** gaming chats, direct messages, ek doosra account. Gaming platforms par abusers pehle message ke 19 seconds ke andar kisi bachche ko high-risk grooming conversation mein kheench sakte hain, aur average 45 minutes mein. Yeh data ek risk-intelligence firm ka hai, jise WeProtect ne quote kiya hai [[weprotect-gta-2023]].

Koi ek flag kuch saabit nahi karta; yeh ishaare hain, sabut nahi. Dekhna yeh hai ki kahin kai flags ek hi bachche par toh nahi tike. Online wale hisse par India ka kanoon pehle se saaf hai: IT Act ka Section 67B bachchon ko online sexual relationship mein phansaane ko crime maanta hai, aur pehli conviction par paanch saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Duniya bhar se US ki sanstha NCMEC ko 2025 mein bachchon ki online enticement ki 1.4 million reports mili [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]].

## Kisi par ilzaam lagaye bina ise kaise rokein

Rules badalne ke liye sabut nahi chahiye, aur rules kisi par ilzaam nahi lagate. Grooming teen cheezon par chalti hai: bachche tak pahunch, secrecy aur trust. Iske har step ki ek kaat hai.

- **Special attention ko baant dijiye.** "Maths mein madad ke liye thank you. Kya aap Sunday ko saare bachchon ko saath padha denge?"
- **Gifts aur ehsaan apne through hone dijiye.** "Hamare ghar mein bachchon ke gifts hamare haath se jaate hain." "Thank you, hum use khud chhod denge." Woh madad le lijiye jismein aapke bachche ki zaroorat na ho.
- **Bachche ke "bas" ka saath dijiye.** Agar bachcha hug ya gudgudi se chhootna chahe, toh sabke saamne kahiye: "Usne bas kaha, toh bas." Bachche tabhi seekhte hain ki unki "na" matter karti hai, jab bade use maankar dikhate hain.
- **Sabse pehle aap listener baniye.** Groomer usi jagah ghusta hai jahan koi aur sunne wala nahi hota. Roz open questions poochiye, aur bachcha jo bataye uske liye use kabhi saza mat dijiye.
- **Sabke liye ek hi rule,** relatives aur purane family friends bhi shaamil, taaki kisi ek par ungli na uthe.
- **Reaction dekhiye.** Jo insaan boundary ki respect karta hai, woh kahega "haan, bilkul". Jo behas kare, rooth jaaye ya chupke se raasta nikaale, usne aapko kuch bata diya hai.

Agar bachcha bataye ki kuch hua hai, toh baat rules ki nahi reh jaati. POCSO ke under, jise bhi bachche ke sexual abuse ka pata hai, use report karna hoga [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. 1098 ya 112 par call kariye [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]], aur online grooming ki complaint cybercrime.gov.in par ya 1930 par kariye [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].

india-no-child-abuse-survey-since-2007.en:
In its 2007 Study on Child Abuse, the Ministry of Women and Child Development did something India has not done since: it ran a national study of child sexual abuse that asked children themselves. Researchers surveyed 12,447 children across 13 states, and 53.22% reported one or more forms of sexual abuse [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Nineteen years later, no national survey of child sexual abuse has followed it. What we know about the scale rests on police registers, global estimates and that one old study, which was never built to measure the whole country.

## The 2007 study: what it found, and why it is not a national rate

Of the children surveyed, 21.90% reported severe forms of sexual abuse, and 5.69% said they had been sexually assaulted [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Half of the abusers were people the child knew or who held a position of trust [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Boys made up 52.94% of the children who reported abuse, and 9 of the 13 states found a higher share among boys than girls [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

Of the children who had been sexually assaulted, 72.1% had told no one, and only 3.4% had gone to the police [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Among young adults who had been sexually assaulted in childhood, only 26.8% had ever told anyone [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

But 53.22% does not mean half of India's children. The study used purposive, non-random sampling and deliberately included street children, working children and children in institutions. Its definitions were broad: "other forms" included forcible kissing, sexual advances during travel and exposure to pornography [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. It was a warning light, not a measurement. That same year, several states banned or refused to implement a new school sex-education curriculum [[reuters-nbc-india-states-ban-sex-ed-2007]], a story we tell separately. The government never went back to measure abuse nationally.

## Since then: police FIRs as a stand-in

Without a survey, the national conversation runs on NCRB's *Crime in India*. In 2024, police registered 69,191 POCSO cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That number measures a chain: a child tells, an adult believes the child, the family goes to the police, and the police register an FIR. Every link can break; the 2007 study showed how rarely the chain even starts.

Consider a 12-year-old in Kanpur, abused by a tuition teacher, who tells no one. A survey might reach her years later; a police register never will.

The two sources disagree most about boys. In 2024's police data they were 892 of 44,567 child victims of penetrative sexual assault [[ncrb-cii-2024]], against more than half of the children who reported abuse in 2007. Both figures are distorted, in opposite directions: the 2007 sample included many working and street children, who are disproportionately boys, while police data depends on boys and their families coming forward. Only a representative survey could settle it; our story on boys missing from POCSO data explores the gap.

## Rising FIRs: more abuse or more reporting?

POCSO registrations rose from 53,874 in 2021 to 63,414 in 2022 and 67,694 in 2023 [[ncrb-cii-2023]], then to 69,191 in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], about 28% in three years. NCRB itself says "rise in crime" and "increase in registration of crime by police" are "clearly two different things" [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]].

A rise can mean more children telling and more police registering, or more abuse, and the table cannot tell which. A repeated survey can, because it counts abuse whether or not anyone went to the police.

The gap can be enormous, as child marriage shows. In 2023-24, 20.1% of women aged 20-24 told the National Family Health Survey they had married before 18 [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]; in 2024, police registered 1,499 child marriage cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Police data is not a smaller copy of reality but a different measurement, as our story on surveys and police records shows for adult women.

## What UNICEF's 2024 estimate rests on

In October 2024, UNICEF published its first global estimates of sexual violence against children. More than 370 million girls and women alive today, about 1 in 8, were raped or sexually assaulted before 18; for boys and men, the estimate is 240 million to 310 million, around 1 in 11 [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]]. In Central and Southern Asia, which includes India, the figure is 73 million girls and women, or 9%, against 22% in Sub-Saharan Africa and 34% in Oceania [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]].

These estimates rest mainly on nationally representative surveys run between 2010 and 2022 [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]]. They depend on what survivors disclose, so a lower regional share may partly reflect silence rather than safety.

India's main household survey, NFHS, does ask about sexual violence, but its 2019-21 round put those questions to women aged 18 to 49, not to children; 6% said they had ever experienced it [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Those questions are a short module inside a long health survey, and WHO notes that dedicated violence surveys are likely to draw higher disclosure than such modules [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. No national survey since 2007 has been designed to ask children and young people, boys as well as girls, about abuse in childhood.

## What India should measure, and who should ask

A real answer needs a survey built for the question. It must be nationally representative. It should include boys, girls and transgender children; ask about contact, non-contact and online abuse; and record who the abuser was, the child's age when it began, whether the child told anyone and what happened next. And it must be repeated every few years with the same questions, so that India can finally say whether abuse is rising or falling, and where it is worst.

Asking is not neutral. Under POCSO, anyone who knows or suspects that a child is being sexually abused must report it to the police or the Special Juvenile Police Unit [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. A survey of children must plan, before the first question, for what happens when a child discloses: trained interviewers, a counsellor on call, referral to 1098. The ministry that commissioned the 2007 study could commission another, and NFHS shows that India can already run household surveys at national scale.

Until then, every claim about the scale of child sexual abuse in India, including those in this magazine, rests on partial evidence, not a measurement. You do not need a survey to act on the clearest finding of the 2007 study: most abused children tell no one. If a child does tell you, believe them, keep them safe, and call 1098 or 112.
india-no-child-abuse-survey-since-2007.hg:
2007 ki Study on Child Abuse mein Ministry of Women and Child Development ne woh kaam kiya jo India ne uske baad kabhi nahi kiya: child sexual abuse par ek national study, jismein seedha bachchon se poocha gaya. 13 states mein 12,447 bachchon ka survey hua, aur unmein se 53.22% ne bataya ki unke saath kisi na kisi tarah ka sexual abuse hua tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. 19 saal baad bhi, child sexual abuse par uske baad koi national survey nahi hua. Is problem ka scale hum jitna bhi jaante hain, woh police registers, global estimates aur isi ek purani study pe tika hai, aur yeh study kabhi poore desh ko naapne ke liye bani hi nahi thi.

## 2007 ki study: kya mila, aur yeh national rate kyun nahi hai

Survey kiye gaye bachchon mein se 21.90% ne severe tarah ke sexual abuse ki baat batayi, aur 5.69% ne kaha ki unke saath sexual assault hua tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Abuse karne walon mein aadhe aise log the jinhe bachcha jaanta tha ya jin pe bharosa kiya jaata tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Abuse batane wale bachchon mein 52.94% ladke the, aur 13 mein se 9 states mein ladkon ka hissa ladkiyon se zyada nikla [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

Jin bachchon ke saath sexual assault hua tha, unmein se 72.1% ne kisi ko kuch nahi bataya tha, aur sirf 3.4% police tak gaye the [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Jin young adults ke saath bachpan mein sexual assault hua tha, unmein se bhi sirf 26.8% ne kabhi kisi ko bataya tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

Lekin 53.22% ka matlab yeh nahi ki India ke aadhe bachchon ke saath aisa hua. Is study mein bachche random tarike se nahi chune gaye the. Jaan-boojhkar street children, kaam karne wale bachche aur institutions mein rehne wale bachche shaamil kiye gaye the. Definitions bhi kaafi broad thi: "other forms" yaani 'doosri tarah' ke abuse mein zabardasti kiss karna, safar mein sexual chhedchhad ki koshish aur pornography dikhana bhi gina gaya tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Yeh study ek warning light thi, poori measurement nahi. Usi saal kai states ne schools ke naye sex education curriculum par ban lagaya ya use lagu karne se mana kar diya [[reuters-nbc-india-states-ban-sex-ed-2007]]; yeh story humne alag se batayi hai. Sarkar phir kabhi laut kar national level par abuse naapne nahi gayi.

## Tab se: police FIRs hi paimana ban gayi

Survey na hone ki wajah se national debate NCRB ki *Crime in India* report pe chalti hai. 2024 mein police ne 69,191 POCSO cases darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh number asal mein ek poori chain ko naapta hai: bachcha kisi ko bataye, woh adult bachche ki baat maane, family police ke paas jaaye, aur police FIR darj kare. Is chain ki har kadi toot sakti hai, aur 2007 ki study ne dikhaya ki yeh chain aksar shuru hi nahi hoti.

Sochiye, Kanpur ki ek 12 saal ki bachchi hai. Uska tuition teacher uska abuse karta hai, aur woh kisi ko nahi batati. Saalon baad shayad koi survey us tak pahunch jaaye. Police register kabhi nahi pahunchega.

Dono sources mein sabse bada farak ladkon ko lekar hai. 2024 ke police data mein penetrative sexual assault ke 44,567 child victims mein sirf 892 ladke the [[ncrb-cii-2024]], jabki 2007 mein abuse batane wale bachchon mein aadhe se zyada ladke the. Dono numbers ulti dishaon mein jhuke hue hain: 2007 ke sample mein kaam karne wale aur street children bahut the, jinmein ladkon ka hissa zyada hota hai, jabki police data is pe tika hai ki ladke aur unki families aage aati hain ya nahi. Sach in dono mein se kiske zyada kareeb hai, yeh sirf ek representative survey hi bata sakta hai; POCSO data se gayab ladkon pe humari story is gap ko aur detail mein dekhti hai.

## FIRs badhi: abuse badha ya reporting?

POCSO ke darj cases 2021 mein 53,874 the, 2022 mein 63,414 aur 2023 mein 67,694 [[ncrb-cii-2023]], aur 2024 mein 69,191 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], yaani teen saal mein lagbhag 28% ki badhat. NCRB khud kehta hai ki "rise in crime" aur "increase in registration of crime by police" "clearly two different things" hain, yaani crime badhna aur police ka zyada case darj karna saaf taur pe do alag baatein hain [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]].

Is badhat ka matlab ho sakta hai ki zyada bachche bol rahe hain aur police zyada cases darj kar rahi hai, ya phir abuse badha hai. Table yeh farak nahi bata sakti. Ek baar-baar repeat hone wala survey bata sakta hai, kyunki woh abuse ko ginta hai, chahe koi police tak gaya ho ya nahi.

Yeh gap kitna bada ho sakta hai, child marriage se samjhiye. 2023-24 mein National Family Health Survey mein 20-24 saal ki 20.1% women ne bataya ki unki shaadi 18 se pehle ho gayi thi [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]; wahin 2024 mein police ne child marriage ke sirf 1,499 cases darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Police data reality ki chhoti copy nahi, balki ek alag measurement hai, jaisa humari surveys aur police records wali story adult women ke liye dikhati hai.

## UNICEF ka 2024 ka estimate kis pe tika hai

October 2024 mein UNICEF ne pehli baar duniya bhar mein bachchon ke saath sexual violence ka estimate jaari kiya. Aaj zinda 37 crore (370 million) se zyada ladkiyon aur women ke saath 18 saal se pehle rape ya sexual assault hua, yaani lagbhag har 8 mein se 1 ke saath. Ladkon aur men ke liye yeh estimate 24 se 31 crore (240 se 310 million) ke beech hai, yaani lagbhag har 11 mein se 1 [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]]. Central aur Southern Asia mein, jismein India bhi aata hai, UNICEF 7.3 crore (73 million) ladkiyon aur women ko ginta hai, yaani 9%, jabki Sub-Saharan Africa mein yeh 22% hai aur Oceania mein 34% [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]].

Yeh estimates zyadatar un nationally representative surveys pe tike hain jo 2010 se 2022 ke beech alag-alag deshon mein hue [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]]. Yeh is pe depend karte hain ki survivors survey mein kitna batate hain, isliye kisi region ka kam number kuch had tak safety ka nahi, chuppi ka nateeja bhi ho sakta hai.

India ka sabse bada household survey, NFHS, sexual violence ke baare mein poochta hai, lekin 2019-21 ke round mein yeh sawaal 18 se 49 saal ki women se poochhe gaye, bachchon se nahi. Inmein se 6% ne kaha ki unke saath kabhi sexual violence hua hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Yeh sawaal ek lambe health survey ke andar ka chhota sa hissa hain, aur WHO kehta hai ki jo surveys sirf violence pe bane hote hain, unmein aise chhote modules ke mukable log zyada khulkar bata sakte hain [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. 2007 ke baad se koi bhi national survey is tarah nahi bana ki woh bachchon aur young logon se, ladkon aur ladkiyon dono se, bachpan mein hue abuse ke baare mein pooche.

## India ko kya naapna chahiye, aur kaun pooche

Asli jawab ke liye aisa survey chahiye jo isi sawaal ke liye bana ho. Woh nationally representative ho, sirf shelter homes ya street children tak limited nahi. Usmein ladke, ladkiyan aur transgender bachche, sab hon. Woh touch wale, bina touch wale aur online abuse, teeno ke baare mein pooche. Woh record kare ki abuse kisne kiya, shuru hote waqt bachche ki age kya thi, kya bachche ne kisi ko bataya, aur phir kya hua. Aur woh har kuch saal mein unhi sawaalon ke saath repeat ho, taaki India finally bata sake ki abuse badh raha hai ya ghat raha hai, aur sabse bura haal kahan hai.

Poochna bhi apne aap mein ek zimmedari hai. POCSO ke under, jise bhi pata ho ya shak ho ki kisi bachche ka sexual abuse ho raha hai, use police ya Special Juvenile Police Unit ko batana hi hoga [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Isliye bachchon se baat karne wale survey ko pehla sawaal poochne se pehle hi tay karna hoga ki agar koi bachcha kuch bataye toh aage kya hoga: trained interviewers, call pe available counsellor, aur 1098 se jodne ka intezaam. Jis ministry ne 2007 ki study karwayi thi, woh aisi study dobara karwa sakti hai, aur NFHS dikhata hai ki India national level par household survey pehle se kar sakta hai.

Tab tak India mein child sexual abuse ke scale pe har claim, is magazine ke claims bhi, adhoore saboot pe tika hai, asli measurement pe nahi. Lekin 2007 ki study ki sabse saaf baat pe action lene ke liye kisi survey ki zaroorat nahi: abuse jhelne wale zyadatar bachche kisi ko nahi batate. Agar koi bachcha aapko bataye, toh uski baat pe bharosa kijiye, use safe rakhiye, aur 1098 ya 112 pe call kijiye.

khatna-female-genital-cutting-girls-indi.en:
In December 2017, India's Ministry of Women and Child Development told the Supreme Court that "there is no official data or study which supports the existence of FGM in India" [[guardian-fgm-india-study-2018]]. Bohra campaigners rejected that. Nearly nine years later, the petition that drew the reply is still undecided, no Indian law names the practice, and in February 2026 a UN committee was still asking India how common it is [[cedaw-india-loipr-2026]]. This investigation is about the girls in that gap.

## What khatna is, and who it is done to

Female genital mutilation, also called cutting, means any procedure that removes or injures a girl's external genitals for non-medical reasons [[who-fgm]]. In India it is best known as khatna, the cutting practised in the Dawoodi Bohra community [[scobserver-sunita-tiwari-fgm-case]]. It is done to children. At a Supreme Court hearing on 7 May 2026, Senior Advocate Siddharth Luthra spoke of the genital cutting of seven-year-old girls [[scobserver-sabarimala-day13-2026]].

Defenders call it "a symbolic form of circumcision", as counsel for the review petitioners did that day. Justice Joymalya Bagchi replied that male circumcision could not be equated with genital cutting involving the clitoris [[scobserver-sabarimala-day13-2026]]. A remark from the bench is not a ruling, but it names what the euphemism hides.

No official body can say how many Indian girls are cut. In an online survey by Sahiyo, a group of Bohra women campaigning against khatna, 80% of 385 respondents said they had undergone it, and 82% said they were unlikely to continue it on their daughters [[sahiyo-khatna-survey-2017]]. The sample was self-selected and only about a third lived in India, so it cannot measure prevalence. It does show the challenge comes from inside the community.

Worldwide, more than 230 million girls and women alive today have undergone FGM [[unicef-fgm-estimates-2024]], and about 4 million girls are cut every year, more than 2 million before the age of five [[un-sdg-report-2025-goal5]].

## Before the Supreme Court since 2017

In 2017 a public interest petition, Sunita Tiwari v. Union of India, asked the Supreme Court to ban khatna as a violation of girls' rights to equality, non-discrimination and bodily autonomy under Articles 14, 15 and 21. Community members call it religious practice protected by Articles 25 and 26 [[scobserver-sunita-tiwari-fgm-case]]. In September 2018 it was sent to a larger bench [[sc-sunita-tiwari-order-2018]]. In November 2019, when a five-judge bench split 3:2 to send wider religious-freedom questions to a larger bench, the petition was still pending, with applications from individual Bohra women to join it [[ht-fgm-seven-judge-bench-2019]].

A nine-judge bench began hearing those questions on 7 April 2026, with the khatna petition tagged to them [[scobserver-sabarimala-reference-2026]], and reserved judgment on 14 May [[scobserver-sabarimala-day16-2026]]. As of mid-November 2026, no verdict had come. A girl who was seven when the petition was filed is 16 now.

No specific Indian law bans FGM, though around 59 countries prohibit it [[scobserver-sabarimala-day13-2026]]. UNFPA counts India among countries where FGM can be prosecuted under other laws [[unfpa-fgm-faq-2026]], but no Indian statute names it and the Supreme Court has not ruled on it. This is general information, not legal advice.

## 'No official data': how a practice stays invisible

The 2017 reply was not a slip; it is how the system works. India's crime statistics count offences registered with the police, and there is no offence called FGM. No offence means no column where a cut girl could appear, and an empty column lets officials say there is no evidence.

Yet in 2018 the Attorney General told the court the Union opposed khatna as a violation of fundamental rights [[toi-fgm-five-judge-bench-2018]]. A state that opposes a practice it has never counted cannot know whether its opposition works.

The global count has the same hole. UNICEF's 230 million comes from 31 countries with data [[unicef-fgm-topic-page]], and India, which says it has none, is unlikely to be one of them.

In February 2026 the UN's women's rights committee, CEDAW, asked India for data on how common FGM is, and for "any plans and time frame" for a law against it. India's report is due on 3 February 2027 [[cedaw-india-loipr-2026]].

## The medicalisation myth: a doctor does not make it safe

FGM is not only done by traditional cutters. About one in four survivors worldwide, some 52 million women and girls, were cut by health personnel [[unicef-fgm-topic-page]]. To a family that wants to keep a custom and lower the risk, a clinic can look like a careful compromise.

WHO rejects that compromise. It says FGM has no health benefits; that it can cause pain, bleeding and infection at the time, and later problems with periods, sex, childbirth and mental health; and that it opposes every form of FGM, including when health workers carry it out [[who-fgm]].

Not every survivor has every harm. But the harm of a "small nick" is not only medical. A healthy part of a child's body is cut, for no medical reason, at the request of the adults she trusts most, at an age when she cannot say no. A clinic can lower the risk of infection. It changes nothing else.

## For survivors and parents: help, and saying no

Consider a 19-year-old who hears the term "female genital cutting" in a college lecture and realises it describes something done to her at seven. If that is you: it was not your fault, and your body is not "ruined". A gynaecologist can examine you privately and treat any pain or scarring. Anger, grief and love for the family who arranged it can all exist at once. Tele-MANAS, the Health Ministry's free, round-the-clock helpline, offers counselling on 14416 [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

If you are a parent being pressed by elders, you are not alone in refusing. The decision about your daughter's body is yours, and you can leave it as it is.

If you fear a girl is about to be cut, call the Child Helpline on 1098, which runs 24x7 and is linked to the 112 emergency system [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].

Talk about khatna as what it is: harm to a child's body, not a stick to beat a faith or community with. Some of the strongest voices against it are Bohra women, and mockery from outside protects no girl.
khatna-female-genital-cutting-girls-indi.hg:
December 2017 mein India ki Ministry of Women and Child Development ne Supreme Court ko bataya: "there is no official data or study which supports the existence of FGM in India", yaani aisa koi official data ya study nahi hai jo India mein FGM ke hone ko support kare [[guardian-fgm-india-study-2018]]. Bohra campaigners ne is baat ko reject kiya. Lagbhag nau saal baad bhi us petition ka faisla nahi hua hai jis par yeh jawab diya gaya tha, koi Indian law is practice ka naam nahi leta, aur February 2026 mein ek UN committee abhi bhi India se pooch rahi thi ki yeh kitna common hai [[cedaw-india-loipr-2026]]. Yeh investigation us gap mein phansi ladkiyon ke baare mein hai.

## Khatna kya hai, aur kiske saath hota hai

Female genital mutilation, jise cutting bhi kehte hain, ka matlab hai koi bhi aisa procedure jisme bina kisi medical reason ke ladki ke bahari genitals ka koi hissa hataya jaaye ya use chot pahunchayi jaaye [[who-fgm]]. India mein ise zyadatar khatna ke naam se jaana jaata hai, jo Dawoodi Bohra community mein kiya jaata hai [[scobserver-sunita-tiwari-fgm-case]]. Yeh bachchon ke saath hota hai. 7 May 2026 ko Supreme Court ki ek hearing mein Senior Advocate Siddharth Luthra ne saat saal ki ladkiyon ki genital cutting ki baat ki [[scobserver-sabarimala-day13-2026]].

Iske supporters ise "a symbolic form of circumcision", yaani circumcision ka ek symbolic roop kehte hain, jaise usi din review petitioners ke counsel ne kaha. Justice Joymalya Bagchi ne jawab diya ki male circumcision ki tulna aisi genital cutting se nahi ki ja sakti jisme clitoris shaamil ho [[scobserver-sabarimala-day13-2026]]. Bench ka remark ruling nahi hota, lekin yeh us cheez ka naam le leta hai jise euphemism chhupata hai.

Koi official body nahi bata sakti ki India mein kitni ladkiyon ki cutting hui hai. Sahiyo, jo khatna ke khilaaf campaign karne wali Bohra women ka group hai, ke ek online survey mein 385 respondents mein se 80% ne kaha ki unka khatna hua tha, aur 82% ne kaha ki woh shayad apni betiyon ke saath yeh nahi karengi [[sahiyo-khatna-survey-2017]]. Sample self-selected tha aur usmein se sirf lagbhag ek-tihai log India mein rehte the, isliye isse prevalence naapi nahi ja sakti. Lekin yeh zaroor dikhata hai ki challenge community ke andar se aa raha hai.

Duniya bhar mein aaj zinda 230 million se zyada ladkiyan aur women FGM se guzar chuki hain [[unicef-fgm-estimates-2024]], aur har saal lagbhag 4 million ladkiyon ki cutting hoti hai, jinme se 2 million se zyada paanch saal ki umar se pehle [[un-sdg-report-2025-goal5]].

## 2017 se Supreme Court ke saamne

2017 mein ek public interest petition, Sunita Tiwari v. Union of India, ne Supreme Court se khatna ban karne ki maang ki. Petition kehti hai ki yeh Articles 14, 15 aur 21 ke tahat ladkiyon ke equality, non-discrimination aur bodily autonomy ke rights ka ulanghan hai. Community ke log ise Articles 25 aur 26 se protected religious practice kehte hain [[scobserver-sunita-tiwari-fgm-case]]. September 2018 mein case ek badi bench ko bhej diya gaya [[sc-sunita-tiwari-order-2018]]. November 2019 mein jab five-judge bench ne 3:2 se religious freedom ke bade sawaal ek larger bench ko bheje, tab bhi petition pending thi, aur kuch Bohra women ne bhi case mein judne ke liye applications di thi [[ht-fgm-seven-judge-bench-2019]].

Ek nine-judge bench ne 7 April 2026 se in sawaalon ki sunwai shuru ki, aur khatna petition unke saath tagged thi [[scobserver-sabarimala-reference-2026]]. 14 May ko judges ne judgment reserve kar liya [[scobserver-sabarimala-day16-2026]]. November 2026 ke beech tak koi verdict nahi aaya tha. Jo ladki petition file hone ke waqt saat saal ki thi, woh ab 16 ki hai.

Koi specific Indian law FGM ko ban nahi karta, jabki lagbhag 59 countries ise prohibit karti hain [[scobserver-sabarimala-day13-2026]]. UNFPA India ko un countries mein ginta hai jahan FGM ko doosre laws ke tahat prosecute kiya ja sakta hai [[unfpa-fgm-faq-2026]], lekin koi Indian statute iska naam nahi leta aur Supreme Court ne is par faisla nahi diya hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## 'No official data': ek practice kaise nazar se gaayab rehti hai

2017 ka jawab koi galti nahi tha; system aise hi kaam karta hai. India ke crime statistics sirf police mein register hue offences ginte hain, aur FGM naam ka koi offence hai hi nahi. Offence nahi, toh koi column bhi nahi jisme cutting jhel chuki ladki dikh sake, aur khaali column officials ko yeh kehne deta hai ki koi saboot nahi hai.

Phir bhi 2018 mein Attorney General ne court ko bataya ki Union khatna ka virodh karti hai, kyunki yeh fundamental rights ka ulanghan hai [[toi-fgm-five-judge-bench-2018]]. Jo state kisi practice ka virodh karti hai par use kabhi ginti nahi, woh jaan hi nahi sakti ki uska virodh kaam kar raha hai ya nahi.

Global ginti mein bhi yahi chhed hai. UNICEF ka 230 million ka figure un 31 countries se aata hai jahan data hai [[unicef-fgm-topic-page]], aur India, jo kehta hai ki uske paas data hai hi nahi, shayad unmein shaamil nahi hai.

February 2026 mein UN ki women's rights committee, CEDAW, ne India se FGM kitna common hai iska data maanga, aur poocha ki iske khilaaf law ke liye "any plans and time frame", yaani koi plan aur time frame hai ya nahi. India ki report 3 February 2027 ko due hai [[cedaw-india-loipr-2026]].

## Medicalisation ka myth: doctor ke karne se yeh safe nahi ho jaata

FGM sirf traditional cutters nahi karte. Duniya bhar mein lagbhag har chaar mein se ek survivor, yaani kareeb 52 million women aur ladkiyon, ki cutting health personnel ne ki thi [[unicef-fgm-topic-page]]. Jo family custom bhi nibhana chahti hai aur risk bhi kam karna chahti hai, use clinic ek samajhdaari bhara compromise lag sakta hai.

WHO is compromise ko reject karta hai. WHO kehta hai ki FGM ka koi health benefit nahi hai; ki isse us waqt dard, bleeding aur infection ho sakta hai, aur baad mein periods, sex, childbirth aur mental health se judi problems ho sakti hain; aur ki woh FGM ke har form ka virodh karta hai, tab bhi jab health workers ise karte hain [[who-fgm]].

Har survivor ko har harm nahi hota. Lekin "chhote se nick" ka harm sirf medical nahi hai. Ek bachchi ke body ka ek healthy hissa kaata jaata hai, bina kisi medical reason ke, un bado ke kehne par jin par woh sabse zyada bharosa karti hai, aur aisi umar mein jab woh na bhi nahi keh sakti. Clinic infection ka risk kam kar sakta hai. Baaki kuch nahi badalta.

## Survivors aur parents ke liye: madad, aur na kehna

Sochiye, ek 19 saal ki ladki college ke lecture mein "female genital cutting" shabd sunti hai aur samajhti hai ki yeh us cheez ka naam hai jo saat saal ki umar mein uske saath hui thi. Agar yeh aap hain: isme aapki koi galti nahi thi, aur aapki body "kharab" nahi hui hai. Gynaecologist privately aapka examination kar sakti hain aur kisi bhi dard ya scarring ka ilaaj kar sakti hain. Gussa, dukh, aur us family ke liye pyaar jisne yeh karwaya, yeh sab ek saath ho sakte hain. Tele-MANAS, Health Ministry ki free helpline jo din-raat chalti hai, 14416 par counselling deti hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

Agar aap parent hain aur ghar ke bade aap par pressure daal rahe hain, toh mana karne wale aap akele nahi hain. Aapki beti ki body ka faisla aapka hai, aur aap use waise hi rehne de sakte hain jaisi woh hai.

Agar aapko darr hai ki kisi ladki ki cutting hone wali hai, toh Child Helpline 1098 par call kijiye, jo 24x7 chalti hai aur 112 emergency system se judi hai [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].

Khatna ke baare mein waise hi baat kijiye jaisa woh hai: ek bachchi ki body ko pahunchaya gaya harm, kisi dharm ya community ko neecha dikhane ka bahana nahi. Iske khilaaf sabse mazboot aawaazon mein se kuch Bohra women ki hain, aur bahar se mazaak udaane se kisi ladki ki hifaazat nahi hoti.

marriage-does-not-end-abuse-case-myth.en:
Consider this situation. A 16-year-old's family files a complaint against a 21-year-old man from the next lane. Within days, elders from both families sit down with one offer: get them married, withdraw the case, and nobody's honour is lost. It sounds like mercy. In law, it adds new offences to the first one, and the girl serves the sentence.

## The myth: marriage restores honour and ends the matter

The idea rests on two beliefs: that abuse stains a family's honour and a wedding cleans it, and that a criminal case is a private quarrel two families can settle.

The Supreme Court has rejected both. Its 2023 Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes calls the belief that marrying the rapist restores a survivor's honour a stereotype, and says: "Marriage is not a remedy to the violence of rape" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. In Aparna Bhat v. State of Madhya Pradesh (2021), the court struck down a High Court bail condition requiring a man accused of sexual assault to ask the complainant to tie a rakhi on him. Courts, it ruled, must not suggest compromise or marriage, and bail conditions must not require or permit contact between the accused and the victim [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]].

## Who the accused are: 'friends' and 'partners'

A wedding can be offered only when the family knows the accused, and in child abuse cases it almost always does. In 2024, police registered 44,126 cases of penetrative sexual assault under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, and in 96.6% of them the accused was someone the child knew [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The biggest group, 22,308 cases or 50.6%, was a friend, online friend or live-in partner "on pretext of marriage". Only 1,492 named an unknown or unidentified person [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The victims were mostly teenagers: 23,497 (52.7%) were aged 16 to 18, and 16,801 were 12 to 16 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. At these ages, a wedding can start to look to adults like a way out.

The "pretext of marriage" row mixes online grooming, false promises and teenage relationships, and NCRB does not separate them. Unlike the adult women in our explainer on Section 69, every victim here is under 18: a child's "yes" does not count in law, and no wedding answers the charge.

## What the law says: child marriage, rape within marriage, no compromise

Under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, a girl is a child until 18 and a boy until 21, and a marriage in which either is a child is a child marriage [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. An adult groom, anyone who performs the ceremony and anyone who promotes or permits it can each get up to two years' rigorous imprisonment and a fine of up to Rs 1 lakh; the offences are cognisable and non-bailable [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. A "settlement wedding" exposes the parents and elders who arrange it to prosecution too.

Nor does a wedding erase the abuse. On 11 October 2017, in Independent Thought v. Union of India, the Supreme Court held that sex with a wife under 18 is rape [[sc-independent-thought-2017]]. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), in force since 1 July 2024, keeps that line: its marital exception covers only wives aged 18 or older [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Silence is not neutral either. Under Sections 19 and 21 of POCSO, anyone who knows of a sexual offence against a child must report it, and failing to do so can mean up to six months in jail [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

## What a 'settlement' does to a girl

First, it moves the main witness into the accused's home. POCSO requires courts to shield a child from the accused while she testifies, with curtains or video links if needed [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. A settlement wedding does the opposite: it puts her under his roof, among relatives whose future depends on her silence.

That pressure reaches the courtroom. In 2024, only 32.3% of POCSO trials ended in conviction: 12,672 convictions against 25,476 acquittals [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB does not record why trials fail, but a girl married to the accused is about the hardest witness a prosecutor can have.

Second, her protection expires on her 18th birthday. From then on, the marital exception means forced sex by her husband is not rape in law [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. As of 19 November 2026, the Supreme Court had not ruled on a challenge to that exception; it said it would fix the final hearing on 9 or 10 December 2026 [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]]. Until it rules, a settlement wedding leaves her, from 18, married to a man the rape law cannot reach.

Third, the marriage itself is a risk. Among ever-married women in NFHS-5 (2019-21) who had faced sexual violence, 82% named their current husband [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Of currently married women married only once, 11.2% first faced physical or sexual violence from their husband within two years of the wedding [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. UNICEF says girls married before 18 are more likely to face domestic violence and less likely to stay in school [[unicef-child-marriage-topic-page]].

## What families should do instead

Go to the system, not to the elders. Child Helpline 1098 is linked to the 112 emergency system [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]. Police must record her statement at home or a place she chooses, as far as practicable through a woman officer, never in uniform, and keep her away from the accused [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Every hospital, government or private, must treat her free [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Support need not come from the accused's family. A victim can apply for state compensation even if no trial takes place [[indiacode-bnss-2023]], and under the national legal services scheme the limits are 50% higher for a minor [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]]. A minor girl made pregnant by rape can get shelter, medical care, legal aid, counselling and education support under a 2023 central scheme [[mwcd-pocso-victim-support-scheme-2023]].

If a wedding is being fixed, tell the district Child Marriage Prohibition Officer; the Supreme Court has directed magistrates to stop child marriages with injunctions [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. If it has already happened, she can ask a district court to annul it until two years after she turns 18 [[indiacode-pcma-2006]].

And if two teenagers truly care for each other, the honest answer is time, not a wedding: she can marry at 18, he at 21. A marriage arranged to close a case protects the accused and the family's name. It does nothing for the girl.
marriage-does-not-end-abuse-case-myth.hg:
Yeh situation sochiye. Ek 16 saal ki ladki ki family agli gali ke ek 21 saal ke aadmi ke khilaaf complaint karti hai. Kuch hi dinon mein dono families ke bade-buzurg baith jaate hain, aur unke paas ek hi offer hota hai: dono ki shaadi karwa do, case wapas le lo, kisi ki izzat nahi jaayegi. Sunne mein yeh reham lagta hai. Lekin law ki nazar mein isse pehle offence ke upar naye offences jud jaate hain, aur saza ladki bhugatti hai.

## Myth: shaadi se izzat bachti hai aur maamla khatam

Yeh soch do baaton par tiki hai. Pehli, abuse se family ki izzat par daag lagta hai aur shaadi use dho deti hai. Doosri, criminal case do families ka private jhagda hai, jise woh aapas mein settle kar sakti hain.

Supreme Court dono baatein reject kar chuka hai. 2023 mein court ne Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes nikali. Usmein saaf likha hai ki rapist se shaadi karwane par survivor ki izzat laut aati hai, yeh ek stereotype hai. Handbook ke shabd hain: "Marriage is not a remedy to the violence of rape", yaani shaadi rape ki violence ka ilaaj nahi hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Phir 2021 ka Aparna Bhat v. State of Madhya Pradesh case hai. Ek High Court ne sexual assault ke ek accused ko is shart par bail di thi ki woh complaint karne wali mahila se rakhi bandhwaye. Supreme Court ne yeh shart cancel kar di. Court ne kaha ki courts compromise ya shaadi ka suggestion nahi denge, aur bail ki koi shart accused aur victim ko milne ke liye majboor nahi karegi, na iski ijaazat degi [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]].

## Accused kaun hain: 'dost' aur 'partner'

Shaadi ki baat tabhi uth sakti hai jab family accused ko jaanti ho, aur bachchon ke abuse ke cases mein lagbhag hamesha aisa hi hota hai. 2024 mein police ne POCSO Act ke tahat bachchon par penetrative sexual assault ke 44,126 cases register kiye, aur inmein se 96.6% mein accused koi aisa tha jise bachcha jaanta tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Sabse bada group tha dost, online dost ya 'shaadi ke bahane' saath rehne wala live-in partner: 22,308 cases, yaani 50.6%. Sirf 1,492 cases mein accused anjaan tha ya pehchana nahi ja saka [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Zyada tar victims teenagers the: 23,497 (52.7%) ki umar 16 se 18 saal thi, aur 16,801 ki 12 se 16 saal [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Isi umar mein badon ko shaadi ek 'raasta' lagne lag sakti hai.

'Shaadi ke bahane' wali yeh row online grooming, jhoothe vaade aur teenagers ke aapsi rishte, sab ek saath mila deti hai, aur NCRB inhe alag nahi karta. Section 69 par hamara explainer un adult women ki baat karta hai jinhe shaadi ka jhootha vaada karke dhokha diya gaya. Lekin yahan har victim 18 se kam umar ka bachcha hai. Law mein uski 'haan' ka koi matlab nahi, aur koi bhi shaadi is charge ka jawab nahi hai.

## Law kya kehta hai: child marriage, shaadi ke andar rape, koi compromise nahi

Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 ke hisaab se ladki 18 saal tak aur ladka 21 saal tak child hai, aur agar dono mein se koi bhi child hai to woh shaadi child marriage hai [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. Adult dulhe ko, shaadi karwane wale ko, aur shaadi ko badhawa dene ya hone dene wale ko, har kisi ko 2 saal tak ki rigorous qaid aur Rs 1 lakh tak jurmana ho sakta hai, aur yeh offences cognisable aur non-bailable hain [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. Matlab 'settlement' wali shaadi karwane wale maa-baap aur buzurg khud bhi prosecution ke daayre mein aa jaate hain.

Shaadi se abuse mit-ta bhi nahi. 11 October 2017 ko Independent Thought v. Union of India case mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki 18 saal se kam umar ki wife ke saath sex rape hai [[sc-independent-thought-2017]]. 1 July 2024 se laagu Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) mein bhi yahi line hai: iska marital exception sirf 18 ya usse zyada umar ki wife par laagu hota hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Chup rehna bhi koi neutral raasta nahi hai. POCSO ke Section 19 aur 21 kehte hain ki jise bhi kisi bachche ke khilaaf sexual offence ka pata ho, use report karna hoga, aur report na karne par chhe mahine tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## 'Settlement' wali shaadi ladki ke saath kya karti hai

Pehli baat, yeh shaadi case ki sabse important witness ko accused ke ghar pahuncha deti hai. POCSO kehta hai ki gawahi ke waqt bachche ko accused ke saamne na aana pade, aur zaroorat ho to parda ya video link lagaya jaaye [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. 'Settlement' wali shaadi iska bilkul ulta karti hai. Ladki usi ki chhat ke neeche pahunch jaati hai, aise rishtedaaron ke beech jinka future uski chuppi par tika hai.

Yeh pressure court tak pahunchta hai. 2024 mein POCSO ke sirf 32.3% trials mein conviction hua: 12,672 convictions, jabki 25,476 cases mein accused bari ho gaye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB yeh record nahi karta ki trials kyun fail hue. Lekin jo ladki accused ki wife ban chuki hai, usse mushkil witness kisi prosecutor ke liye shayad hi koi ho.

Doosri baat, 18th birthday par uski legal protection khatam ho jaati hai. Us din se marital exception laagu ho jaata hai, aur pati ki zabardasti ko law rape nahi maanta [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. 19 November 2026 tak Supreme Court ne is exception ke challenge par faisla nahi diya tha; court ne kaha ki final hearing 9 ya 10 December 2026 ko rakhi jaayegi [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]]. Jab tak faisla nahi aata, aisi shaadi ladki ko 18 ki hote hi ek aise aadmi ki biwi bana kar chhod deti hai jis tak rape law pahunch hi nahi sakta.

Teesri baat, shaadi khud ek risk hai. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein jin ever-married women ne sexual violence jheli thi, unmein se 82% ne apne current husband ka naam liya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Jo women abhi shaadishuda thin aur jinki ek hi shaadi hui thi, unmein se 11.2% ne shaadi ke do saal ke andar pehli baar pati ki physical ya sexual violence jheli [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. UNICEF kehta hai ki 18 se pehle byaahi gayi ladkiyon ke saath domestic violence ka khatra zyada hota hai, aur unka school chhootne ka bhi [[unicef-child-marriage-topic-page]].

## Families iski jagah kya karein

Buzurgon ki baithak mein nahi, system ke paas jaaiye. Child Helpline 1098 ab 112 emergency system se judi hai [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]. Police ko ladki ka statement uske ghar par ya uski pasand ki jagah par lena hota hai, jahan tak ho sake ek mahila officer se, jo uniform mein na ho. Accused ko usse door rakhna bhi police ki zimmedari hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Har hospital, sarkari ho ya private, uska ilaaj free karega [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Madad ke liye accused ki family ke aage haath phailane ki zaroorat nahi hai. Victim sarkar se compensation maang sakti hai, chahe trial ho ya na ho [[indiacode-bnss-2023]], aur NALSA ki scheme mein minor ke liye compensation ki limit 50% zyada hai [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]]. Rape se pregnant hui minor ladki ko 2023 ki ek central scheme se rehne ki jagah, ilaaj, legal aid, counselling aur padhai jaari rakhne mein madad mil sakti hai [[mwcd-pocso-victim-support-scheme-2023]].

Agar shaadi fix ho rahi hai, to district ke Child Marriage Prohibition Officer ko bataiye; Supreme Court ne magistrates se kaha hai ki woh injunction dekar child marriages rukwayein [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. Agar shaadi ho chuki hai, to ladki 18 ki hone ke baad do saal tak district court se use annul karwa sakti hai [[indiacode-pcma-2006]].

Aur agar do teenagers sach mein ek doosre ko chahte hain, to imaandaar jawab shaadi nahi, intezaar hai: ladki 18 par shaadi kar sakti hai, ladka 21 par. Case band karne ke liye karwayi gayi shaadi accused ko bachati hai, family ke naam ko bachati hai. Ladki ko usse kuch nahi milta.

missing-children-india-2024-girls.en:
Every year India's crime statistics carry a line that is easy to skip: children reported missing. For 2024 it reads 98,375, up 7.8% from 91,296 in 2023 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Of those children, 75,603 were girls, 22,768 were boys and 4 were transgender [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. More than three in every four were girls. This is what the count says, what the law requires when a child disappears, and what the number cannot tell a family.

## 98,375: a year's count, and the 7.8% rise

The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) also counts how many missing children were found. In 2024 police traced 98,826 children: 67.1% of the 1,47,175 children on the missing list that year, which combined the 98,375 new reports with 48,800 children still missing from earlier years [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. At the end of the year, 48,349 children remained untraced [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Set the two backlogs side by side. The pool carried into 2024 (48,800) and the pool carried out of it (48,349) are almost the same size. Police traced tens of thousands of children in 2024, yet the backlog barely shrank.

The 7.8% rise needs care. NCRB itself says that a "rise in crime" and an "increase in registration of crime by police" are two different things [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. More reports can mean more children going missing, more families going to the police, or both. The table cannot say which.

## Three in four are girls: what might explain it

Girls dominate the count at both ends. They were 75,603 of the 98,375 children reported missing, and 36,352 of the 48,349 still untraced when the year closed [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. More than three times as many girls as boys were reported missing.

The table does not say why any child went missing, or how many were trafficked [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Without a reason column, the possibilities can only be listed, not measured. A 16-year-old may leave with a boyfriend her family has forbidden. Another may run from a marriage being fixed for her, or from violence at home. A third may be lured by a job offer, or taken for labour, sex or marriage. A younger child may simply be lost in a crowd at a railway station. Each needs a different response, yet each enters the record the same way.

Whatever the mix, the skew is itself a finding. Something in the lives of Indian girls makes them far more likely than boys to be reported missing, and a count alone cannot say what it is.

## The FIR rule for missing children

The law is clearer than most families know. In 2013, in Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India, the Supreme Court directed that every complaint about a missing child be registered as an FIR, with an initial presumption that the child has been abducted or trafficked [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The general rule backs it up. On 12 November 2013, a five-judge Constitution Bench held in Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh that registering an FIR is mandatory when information discloses a cognizable offence, that no preliminary inquiry is permissible in such a case, and that officers who refuse must face action [[sc-lalita-kumari-2013]]. Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), such information can be given at any police station, whatever the area of the offence, or electronically, and the informant must get a free copy of the FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), a police officer who fails to record information about trafficking faces six months to two years' rigorous imprisonment [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Imagine a mother in Patna whose 15-year-old daughter has not come home from tuition. At the police station she is told to wait a day, because girls that age usually come back on their own. Under these rules, that answer is wrong. Her complaint should become an FIR that night, treated from the start as a possible abduction or trafficking, and she is entitled to a free copy. She can also call 112, or the Child Helpline 1098, which is integrated with the 112 emergency system [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].

## Missing and trafficked: where the two numbers meet

The same NCRB report counts 2,297 children as trafficked in 2024: 1,384 boys and 913 girls [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The two tables run in opposite directions. Girls dominate the missing count; boys dominate the trafficking count. And nothing joins them. The missing-children table does not say how many children were trafficked, and the trafficking figures cover only cases reported to anti-human trafficking units.

So a girl who disappears, is moved to another state and is later rescued may appear in one table, in both, or in neither, depending on which office wrote her down. The national data cannot follow a single child from the night she went missing to the day she was found.

## What the count does not tell us

The 2024 figure is a count of reports. It cannot tell us how long each child was gone, what happened to her while she was away, or whether "traced" meant safe. The table records only that a child was traced: not where the child was sent back to, why the child left, or whether anyone asked who took the child away.

Better data is easy to describe: a recorded reason for every case closed, the time it took to trace each child, and a link from each missing report to any trafficking, child marriage or POCSO case that followed. Until then, 98,375 measures how often families went to the police, not what happened to their children.

What a family can do is narrower, and urgent: go to the police at once, insist on the FIR the law already requires, and keep the copy.
missing-children-india-2024-girls.hg:
Har saal India ke crime statistics mein ek line hoti hai jise aasaani se nazarandaaz kar diya jaata hai: laapata report hue bachche. 2024 mein yeh number 98,375 tha, jo 2023 ke 91,296 se 7.8% zyada hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In bachchon mein 75,603 ladkiyan, 22,768 ladke aur 4 transgender bachche the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Har chaar mein se teen se zyada ladkiyan thi. Yeh ginti kya kehti hai, bachcha gayab hone pe law kya maangta hai, aur yeh number kisi family ko kya nahi bata sakta, yahi is article mein hai.

## 98,375: ek saal ki ginti, aur 7.8% ki badhat

National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) yeh bhi ginta hai ki kitne laapata bachche mile. 2024 mein police ne 98,826 bachchon ko dhoondha: yeh us saal ki missing list ke 1,47,175 bachchon ka 67.1% tha, jismein 98,375 nayi reports aur pichhle saalon se ab tak laapata 48,800 bachche shaamil the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Saal ke end mein 48,349 bachche ab bhi nahi mile the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Dono backlogs ko saath rakhkar dekhiye. 2024 mein aaya pool (48,800) aur 2024 se aage gaya pool (48,349) lagbhag barabar hain. 2024 mein police ne das-hazaaron bachchon ko dhoondha, phir bhi backlog mushkil se ghata.

7.8% ki badhat ko dhyaan se padhna hoga. NCRB khud kehta hai ki "rise in crime" aur "increase in registration of crime by police" do alag baatein hain [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. Zyada reports ka matlab ho sakta hai ki zyada bachche gayab hue, ya zyada families police tak pahunchi, ya dono. Table yeh nahi bata sakti ki sach kya hai.

## Har chaar mein teen ladkiyan: iski wajah kya ho sakti hai

Ginti ke dono siron pe ladkiyan haavi hain. Laapata report hue 98,375 bachchon mein 75,603 ladkiyan thi, aur saal khatam hone tak na mile 48,349 bachchon mein 36,352 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Ladkon ke muqable teen guna se bhi zyada ladkiyan laapata report hui.

Table yeh nahi batati ki koi bachcha kyun gayab hua, ya kitne bachchon ki trafficking hui [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Wajah ka koi column na ho, toh sambhaavnaayein sirf ginai ja sakti hain, naapi nahi ja sakti. 16 saal ki koi ladki us boyfriend ke saath ja sakti hai jisse milne se family ne mana kiya ho. Koi doosri apne liye tay ho rahi shaadi se, ya ghar ki hinsa se bhaag sakti hai. Teesri ko naukri ka laalach dekar bulaya ja sakta hai, ya kaam, sex ya shaadi ke liye le jaaya ja sakta hai. Koi chhota bachcha railway station ki bheed mein bas kho sakta hai. Har case ko alag jawaab chahiye, phir bhi record mein sab ek hi tarah darj hote hain.
