Wajah jo bhi ho, yeh jhukaav khud ek nateeja hai. Indian ladkiyon ki zindagi mein kuch aisa hai jo unke laapata report hone ki sambhaavna ladkon se kahin zyada bana deta hai, aur sirf ginti yeh nahi bata sakti ki woh kya hai.

## Laapata bachchon ke liye FIR ka rule

Law utna saaf hai jitna zyadatar families jaanti bhi nahi. 2013 mein Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India case mein Supreme Court ne direction di ki laapata bachche ki har complaint FIR ke roop mein darj ho, aur shuruaat mein yeh maana jaaye ki bachche ka abduction ya trafficking hua hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

General rule bhi isi ka saath deta hai. 12 November 2013 ko paanch judges ki Constitution Bench ne Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh case mein kaha ki agar jaankaari se cognizable offence dikhta hai toh FIR darj karna zaroori hai, aise case mein koi preliminary inquiry allowed nahi, aur mana karne wale officers pe action hona chahiye [[sc-lalita-kumari-2013]]. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ke tahat yeh jaankaari kisi bhi police station pe di ja sakti hai, offence chahe kisi bhi ilaake mein hua ho, ya electronically bhi, aur jaankaari dene wale ko FIR ki free copy milni chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke tahat jo police officer trafficking ki jaankaari darj nahi karta, use chhah mahine se do saal tak ki rigorous imprisonment ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Patna ki ek maa ki kalpana kijiye jiski 15 saal ki beti tuition se ghar nahi lauti. Police station mein use ek din ruk jaane ko kaha jaata hai, kyunki is umar ki ladkiyan aksar khud laut aati hain. In rules ke hisaab se yeh jawaab galat hai. Uski complaint usi raat FIR banni chahiye, shuru se hi mumkin abduction ya trafficking maankar, aur use FIR ki free copy ka haq hai. Woh 112 pe bhi call kar sakti hai, ya Child Helpline 1098 pe, jo 112 emergency system se judi hui hai [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].

## Missing aur trafficked: dono number kahan milte hain

Usi NCRB report mein 2024 mein 2,297 bachchon ko trafficked gina gaya: 1,384 ladke aur 913 ladkiyan [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Dono tables ulti dishaon mein jaati hain. Missing ginti mein ladkiyan zyada hain; trafficking ginti mein ladke. Aur in dono ko koi cheez nahi jodti. Laapata bachchon ki table nahi batati ki kitne bachchon ki trafficking hui, aur trafficking figures sirf un cases ko ginte hain jo anti-human trafficking units tak report hue.

Toh ek ladki jo gayab hoti hai, doosre state le jaayi jaati hai aur baad mein rescue hoti hai, woh ek table mein dikh sakti hai, dono mein, ya kisi mein bhi nahi; yeh is pe nirbhar karta hai ki kis office ne use likha. National data kisi ek bachche ko us raat se, jab woh gayab hui, us din tak follow nahi kar sakta jab woh mili.

## Ginti kya nahi batati

2024 ka figure reports ki ginti hai. Yeh nahi bata sakta ki har bachcha kitne din gayab raha, us dauraan uske saath kya hua, ya "traced" ka matlab surakshit tha ya nahi. Table sirf itna darj karti hai ki bachcha mil gaya: yeh nahi ki use kahan wapas bheja gaya, woh kyun gaya tha, ya kisi ne yeh poocha ki use kaun le gaya.

Behtar data ka khaaka banana mushkil nahi: band hue har case ke liye ek darj wajah, har bachche ko dhoondhne mein laga samay, aur har missing report ka us trafficking, child marriage ya POCSO case se link jo baad mein bana. Tab tak 98,375 yeh naapta hai ki families kitni baar police ke paas gayi, yeh nahi ki unke bachchon ke saath kya hua.

Family jo kar sakti hai, woh chhota hai lekin zaroori: turant police ke paas jaaiye, us FIR pe zor dijiye jo law pehle se maangta hai, aur uski copy sambhaal kar rakhiye.

my-child-would-tell-me-myth.en:
Imagine a mother in Indore whose nine-year-old son tells her everything: the fight at lunch break, the teacher who shouted, the friend who cheated at Ludo. If anyone ever touched him wrongly, she is certain, he would tell her that too. It is the most comforting belief a parent can hold, and India's data says it is usually wrong. Sexually abused children mostly tell no one, including parents they love.

## The myth: closeness guarantees disclosure

The belief treats a close relationship like a smoke alarm: if something burns, it will ring. But it confuses two very different kinds of telling. A child reports a bad mark or a playground fight because nothing about telling it is dangerous. Abuse comes with its own instructions: keep quiet, nobody will believe you, you will be in trouble, you will break the family.

The myth also does quiet damage. Parents who are sure their child would speak stop watching for other signals. And when the child says nothing, they read the silence as proof that nothing happened.

## The truth in numbers: silence is the norm

The last time India's government asked children directly about sexual abuse was in 2007. Its Study on Child Abuse surveyed 12,447 children in 13 states [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Of the children who said they had been sexually assaulted, 72.1% had told no one, and only 3.4% had reported it to the police [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. The silence lasts into adulthood: among young adults in the study who had been sexually assaulted as children, only 26.8% had ever told anyone [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

One finding should give parents hope. Of the few children who did tell someone, most told a parent [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Parents matter enormously. They are just not an automatic alarm.

The study used a purposive sample, not a nationally representative one, and it predates the POCSO Act of 2012. No national survey of child sexual abuse has been done since, so these are the best numbers India has, not exact national rates.

## Why children stay quiet: secrecy, shame, loyalty, missing words

**Secrecy is built.** Darkness to Light, a US child-protection nonprofit, describes grooming as a deliberate process by which an offender gradually builds and keeps a secret sexual relationship with a child, through special attention, gifts, being a sympathetic listener and offering to help the family [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. The secret is the point of the process, not a side effect.

**Words are missing.** In the 2007 study, the abuse children described began as early as age 5 [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. A five-year-old in a home where private parts have only nicknames, or no names at all, may have no way to say what happened.

**Shame grows with age.** The same study found that abuse peaked between ages 12 and 15 [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]], the years when children are most embarrassed about their bodies and most afraid of hearing "why did you go there?"

**Loyalty and fear do the rest.** A child may love the person, need them, or believe that telling will tear the family apart. Boys face an extra wall, because many families assume it cannot happen to them. Yet boys made up 52.94% of the children who reported sexual abuse in the 2007 study [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

The Supreme Court's 2023 Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes tells judges that a survivor who reports late is not therefore lying, and names "lack of familial support or fear of repercussions" among the reasons for delay [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. It was written about women. A child, who depends on adults for food, school and safety, has even more to fear.

## When the abuser is someone the parent trusts

The hardest part for parents is who the abuser usually is. In 2024, police registered 44,126 cases of penetrative sexual assault on children under POCSO, and in 96.6% of them the accused was someone the child knew. The accused was a family member in 3,658 cases and a family friend, neighbour, employer or other known person in 16,668 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The 2007 study pointed the same way: 50% of abusers were known to the child or in a position of trust and responsibility [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

So the closeness a parent relies on often includes the abuser. To tell, a child must accuse someone the parent invited in, praises at dinner, perhaps depends on for money or favours. A child who keeps hearing "Mamaji has done so much for us" draws an obvious conclusion: the truth will not be welcome.

## Making it easier to tell

Closeness still matters, as a safe place to land rather than an alarm. What helps:

- **Give children the words.** Use correct names for all body parts, and say plainly that any touch, photo or secret involving their body is something to tell.
- **Ban body secrets, not surprises.** A surprise is a birthday gift that will be revealed. A secret about touch is never kept, whoever asks for it: uncle, tutor, cousin or coach.
- **Widen the circle.** Name more than one safe adult, so a child who cannot face you still has somewhere to go.
- **Watch, do not wait.** Darkness to Light notes that emotional and behavioural signs of abuse are more common than physical ones: anxiety, sleep problems, unusual fear of a particular person, bedwetting again, changes in mood or in attitude to school [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. They call for attention, not conclusions.
- **Respect the small hint.** "I don't like going to Chacha's house" may be a test. A child who is scolded for half a sentence will not risk the whole story.

If your child does tell you, believe them and act. Under Sections 19 and 21 of POCSO, anyone who knows or suspects that a child has been sexually abused must inform the police or the Special Juvenile Police Unit, and failing to report is punishable [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Call 1098 or 112. This is general information, not legal advice.
my-child-would-tell-me-myth.hg:
Indore ki ek maa ko imagine kijiye. Uska nau saal ka beta use sab kuch batata hai: lunch break ki ladai, teacher ka daantna, woh dost jisne Ludo mein cheating ki. Use poora yakeen hai ki agar kabhi kisi ne bete ko galat tareeke se chhua, to woh yeh bhi zaroor batayega. Kisi bhi maa-baap ke liye isse zyada sukoon dene wala yakeen shayad hi koi ho, aur India ka data kehta hai ki yeh yakeen aksar galat nikalta hai. Sexual abuse jhelne wale zyadatar bachche kisi ko nahi batate, un maa-baap ko bhi nahi jinse woh pyaar karte hain.

## Myth: rishta close hai, to bachcha zaroor batayega

Yeh soch close rishte ko smoke alarm ki tarah dekhti hai: kuch jalega to alarm bajega. Lekin yeh soch do bilkul alag tarah ke batane ko ek jaisa maan leti hai. Bachcha kharab marks ya playground ki ladai isliye bata deta hai kyunki use batane mein koi khatra nahi hota. Abuse apne saath apne instructions lekar aata hai: chup rehna, koi tumhari baat nahi maanega, tum musibat mein padoge, ghar toot jaayega.

Yeh myth chupchaap nuksaan bhi karta hai. Jo parents maan baithte hain ki bachcha khud bata dega, woh doosre ishaaron par dhyaan dena chhod dete hain. Aur jab bachcha kuch nahi kehta, to woh uski chuppi ko is baat ka saboot maan lete hain ki kuch hua hi nahi.

## Numbers ka sach: chuppi hi normal hai

India ki sarkar ne aakhri baar 2007 mein bachchon se seedhe unke sexual abuse ke baare mein poocha tha. Us saal ki Study on Child Abuse mein 13 states ke 12,447 bachchon ka survey hua [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Jin bachchon ne kaha ki unka sexual assault hua tha, unmein se 72.1% ne kisi ko nahi bataya tha, aur sirf 3.4% ne police ko report kiya tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Yeh chuppi badi umar tak chalti hai: study mein jin young adults ka bachpan mein sexual assault hua tha, unmein se sirf 26.8% ne kabhi kisi ko bataya tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

Ek finding parents ko ummeed deti hai. Jin gine-chune bachchon ne kisi ko bataya, unmein se zyadatar ne apne maa ya papa ko bataya [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Parents bahut maayne rakhte hain. Bas woh apne-aap bajne wala alarm nahi hain.

Is study ka sample purposive tha, poore desh ko represent karne wala nahi, aur yeh 2012 ke POCSO Act se pehle ki hai. Tab se bachchon ke sexual abuse par koi national survey nahi hua, isliye yeh India ke paas maujood sabse achhe numbers hain, exact national rates nahi.

## Bachche chup kyun rehte hain: secret, sharm, wafadari, aur shabdon ki kami

**Secret banaya jaata hai.** Darkness to Light, US ki ek child-protection nonprofit, grooming ko ek soch-samajhkar kiya gaya process batati hai, jismein abuser dheere-dheere bachche ke saath ek secret sexual rishta banata hai aur use chhupa kar rakhta hai: special attention dekar, gifts dekar, hamdard sunne wala bankar, aur family ki madad ki offer karke [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. Secret is poore process ka maksad hai, koi side effect nahi.

**Shabd hi nahi hote.** 2007 ki study mein bachchon ne jo abuse bataya, woh 5 saal ki umar se hi shuru ho jaata tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Jis ghar mein private parts ke sirf nicknames hon, ya koi naam hi na ho, wahan paanch saal ke bachche ke paas yeh batane ka koi tareeka hi nahi hota ki uske saath kya hua.

**Umar ke saath sharm badhti hai.** Usi study mein abuse 12 se 15 saal ki umar mein sabse zyada tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Yahi woh saal hain jab bachche apni body ko lekar sabse zyada sharmaate hain, aur sabse zyada darte hain ki unse poocha jaayega, "tum wahan gaye hi kyun?"

**Baaki kaam wafadari aur darr kar dete hain.** Ho sakta hai bachcha us insaan se pyaar karta ho, us par depend ho, ya maanta ho ki batane se ghar bikhar jaayega. Ladkon ke saamne ek aur deewar hoti hai, kyunki bahut si families maan kar chalti hain ki unke saath aisa ho hi nahi sakta. Lekin 2007 ki study mein sexual abuse report karne wale bachchon mein 52.94% ladke the [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

Supreme Court ki 2023 ki Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes judges ko batati hai ki der se report karne wali survivor isliye jhoothi nahi ho jaati. Der ki wajahon mein woh "lack of familial support or fear of repercussions" ginati hai, yaani family ka saath na milna ya nateejon ka darr [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Yeh handbook mahilaon ke baare mein likhi gayi thi. Ek bachcha, jo khane, school aur hifazat ke liye badon par depend hai, uske paas darne ki wajahein aur bhi zyada hoti hain.

## Jab abuser koi aisa ho jis par parents bharosa karte hain

Parents ke liye sabse mushkil sach yeh hai ki abuser aksar hota kaun hai. 2024 mein police ne POCSO ke tahat bachchon par penetrative sexual assault ke 44,126 cases register kiye, aur inmein se 96.6% mein accused koi aisa tha jise bachcha jaanta tha. 3,658 cases mein accused family member tha, aur 16,668 mein family friend, padosi, employer ya koi aur jaan-pehchaan wala [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 2007 ki study bhi isi taraf ishaara karti thi: 50% abusers aise the jinhe bachcha jaanta tha ya jo bharose aur zimmedari ki position mein the [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

Matlab jis closeness par parents bharosa karte hain, usmein aksar abuser bhi shaamil hota hai. Batane ke liye bachche ko us insaan par ilzaam lagana padta hai jise parents ne khud ghar bulaya, jiski dinner par taarif hoti hai, jis par shayad paise ya ehsaanon ke liye depend bhi kiya jaata hai. Jo bachcha baar-baar sunta hai ki "Mamaji ne hamare liye kitna kuch kiya hai", woh seedha nateeja nikaal leta hai: yeh sach koi sunna nahi chahega.

## Bachche ke liye batana aasaan kaise banayein

Closeness phir bhi maayne rakhti hai, alarm ki tarah nahi, balki ek surakshit jagah ki tarah jahan bachcha aakar tik sake. Yeh cheezein madad karti hain:

- **Bachchon ko shabd dijiye.** Body ke har hisse ka sahi naam istemaal kijiye, aur saaf-saaf kahiye ki body se juda koi bhi touch, photo ya secret aisi baat hai jo batani hi hai.
- **Body ke secrets band, surprises nahi.** Surprise woh hai jaise birthday gift, jo baad mein khul jaata hai. Touch ke baare mein secret kabhi nahi rakha jaata, chahe koi bhi maange: chacha, tutor, cousin ya coach.
- **Daayra badhaiye.** Ek se zyada safe adults tay kijiye, taaki jo bachcha aapka saamna na kar paaye, uske paas bhi jaane ki koi jagah ho.
- **Intezaar mat kijiye, dhyaan dijiye.** Darkness to Light ke mutabik abuse ke emotional aur behavioural signs physical signs se zyada common hain: anxiety, neend ki dikkat, kisi khaas insaan se ajeeb sa darr, phir se bistar geela karna, mood mein ya school ke prati ravaiye mein badlaav [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. Yeh signs dhyaan maangte hain, jaldbaazi ke nateeje nahi.
- **Chhote ishaare ki izzat kijiye.** "Mujhe Chacha ke ghar jaana achha nahi lagta" ek test ho sakta hai. Jis bachche ko aadhe vaakya par daant pad jaaye, woh poori kahani sunane ka risk nahi lega.

Agar aapka bachcha aapko bata de, to uska yakeen kijiye aur kadam uthaiye. POCSO ke Section 19 aur 21 ke tahat jise bhi pata ho ya shak ho ki kisi bachche ka sexual abuse hua hai, use police ya Special Juvenile Police Unit ko batana hoga, aur report na karna punishable hai [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. 1098 ya 112 par call kijiye. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

older-sibling-guide-child-abuse.en:
Consider this. You are 19, home for the holidays, and your 12-year-old cousin goes silent whenever one uncle visits. Or your 10-year-old brother tells you, late at night, about something his tuition teacher does, and then makes you swear never to tell. Many abused children tell nobody. In the government's 2007 Study on Child Abuse, 72.1% of children who had been sexually assaulted had told no one, and only 3.4% had told the police. Those who did confide in someone turned mostly to a parent, and next to a brother or sister [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. This guide is for that older sibling or cousin, especially when the adults around you will not act. It is general information, not legal advice.

## Why it may be you they tell

You are closer in age, you share rooms and phones, and you are less frightening than a parent. A child who fears being scolded or disbelieved may test the water with you first.

There is a harder reason. The person hurting a child is almost always someone the child knows, and often someone the family trusts. In 96.6% of the 44,126 cases of penetrative sexual assault on children registered under POCSO in 2024, the accused was someone the child knew. That included 3,658 cases against a family member and 16,668 against a family friend, neighbour, employer or other known person [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. When the accused is an uncle or a family friend, a child may feel that the parents are the last people who will listen.

Do not assume a younger brother is safe because he is a boy. In the 2007 study, boys were 52.94% of the children who reported sexual abuse, in a sample that included many working and street children [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

## Signs to watch in a brother, sister or cousin

Darkness to Light, a US child-protection nonprofit, notes that emotional and behavioural signs of abuse are more common than physical ones. They include anxiety or depression, nightmares and trouble sleeping, unusual fear of a person or reluctance to be alone with them, a return to outgrown habits such as bedwetting, changes in mood or in attitude to school, and sexual knowledge beyond the child's age [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]].

Siblings see what parents miss: whom the child avoids at family functions, who messages them late at night, gifts nobody explains. Grooming usually looks like kindness: special attention to one child, presents, an adult who plays the sympathetic listener or offers to help the family [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]].

These signs can also come from exam stress, bullying or a fight with a friend. They call for a gentle question, not a conclusion. Choose a calm, private moment and keep it open: "You seem upset whenever he comes over. Has anyone done something that made you uncomfortable?"

## 'Promise you won't tell': what to say instead

Abusers often tell children it is "our secret", so a child who finally speaks may beg you to keep it. Do not make that promise. Say instead:

- "I believe you, and I'm glad you told me."
- "It is not your fault, and you are not in trouble."
- "This is too big for us to carry alone. I'll only tell people whose job is to help, and I'll tell you before I do."

Don't ask for details, don't make the child repeat it to relatives, and don't confront the person they named. Later that day, write down their exact words, the date and anything you noticed.

The law is on your side. Section 19 of POCSO puts the duty to report child sexual abuse on any person, a child included. Section 21 punishes a failure to report with up to 6 months in prison or a fine, though a child cannot be punished for not reporting [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. If you are under 18 yourself, the law cannot punish you for staying silent. If you are 18 or older, it can.

## When parents refuse to act: 1098, school, police

Parents may say "he would never do that", "think of the family's name" or "we will handle it ourselves". A parent who knows about the abuse and stays quiet is failing that same legal duty [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Say so calmly. If nothing changes, go around them:

- **Another adult who will act:** an aunt, a grandparent, a teacher or the school counsellor. Teachers and counsellors share the duty to report, and the head of a school who fails to report abuse by a staff member faces up to 1 year in prison and a fine [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].
- **1098**, the Child Helpline [[wcd-childline]], runs 24x7 and is linked with the emergency number 112 [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]. You do not need proof to call: the law asks anyone who knows or suspects abuse to report it [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Give facts: the child's age, where they are, whether they are safe tonight, and their own words.
- **112**, if the child is in danger right now.
- **Any police station.** The law lets you report there wherever the abuse happened [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

After a report, police must record the child's statement at home or at a place the child chooses, by a woman officer where practicable, never in uniform, and must keep the child away from the accused. They must also inform the Child Welfare Committee within 24 hours [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Don't post about it, not even in a family WhatsApp group. Small details can identify a child, and POCSO itself bars media reports from revealing a child victim's name, school, family or neighbourhood [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

## Your own safety and your own feelings

Don't take on the abuser yourself. Threats or violence can put you, the child and the case at risk. If you live with the accused and fear what happens once you speak, tell 1098 that too.

You may feel guilt for not seeing it sooner, rage, or the pull of family loyalty. Some older siblings realise the same person hurt them too. If that is you, you deserve the same help. Tele-MANAS, the government's free mental-health helpline, answers round the clock on 14416 [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

Speaking up may cost you peace at home for a while. Staying silent costs the child far more.
older-sibling-guide-child-abuse.hg:
Socho: tumhari umar 19 saal hai, chhuttiyon mein tum ghar par ho, aur tumhara 12 saal ka cousin ek khaas uncle ke aate hi bilkul chup ho jaata hai. Ya tumhara 10 saal ka bhai raat ko tumhe batata hai ki uske tuition teacher kya karte hain, aur phir kasam dilata hai ki kisi ko mat batana. Abuse jhelne wale bahut se bachche kisi ko nahi batate. Sarkar ki 2007 ki Study on Child Abuse mein, jin bachchon ke saath sexual assault hua tha, unmein se 72.1% ne kisi ko nahi bataya tha, aur sirf 3.4% ne police ko bataya tha. Jinhone kisi ko bataya, unhone zyada tar mummy-papa ko bataya, aur unke baad bhai ya behen ko [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Yeh guide usi bade bhai, behen ya cousin ke liye hai, khaas kar tab jab aas-paas ke bade kuch nahi karte. Yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahi.

## Bachcha tumhe hi kyun bata sakta hai

Tum umar mein bachche ke kareeb ho, kamra aur phone share hota hai, aur bachche ko tumse utna darr nahi lagta jitna mummy-papa se. Jo bachcha daant khaane ya yakeen na kiye jaane se darta hai, woh pehle tumse baat karke dekhta hai ki kya hoga.

Ek aur, zyada kadwi wajah hai. Bachche ko nuksaan pahunchane wala lagbhag hamesha koi aisa hota hai jise bachcha jaanta hai, aur aksar aisa jis par family bharosa karti hai. 2024 mein POCSO ke tahat bachchon par penetrative sexual assault ke 44,126 cases register hue, aur inmein se 96.6% mein accused koi aisa tha jise bachcha jaanta tha. Inmein 3,658 cases family member ke khilaaf the, aur 16,668 family friend, padosi, employer ya kisi aur jaan-pehchaan wale ke khilaaf [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jab accused koi uncle ya family friend ho, toh bachche ko lag sakta hai ki mummy-papa hi sabse aakhir mein uski baat sunenge.

Yeh mat maano ki chhota bhai ladka hai isliye safe hai. 2007 ki study mein sexual abuse report karne wale bachchon mein 52.94% ladke the, aur us sample mein kaam karne wale aur sadak par rehne wale bachche bhi kaafi the [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

## Bhai, behen ya cousin mein kin signs par nazar rakhein

Darkness to Light, America ki ek child-protection nonprofit, kehti hai ki abuse ke emotional aur behavioural signs physical signs se zyada common hote hain. Jaise anxiety ya depression, bure sapne aur neend ki dikkat, kisi khaas insaan se ajeeb sa darr ya uske saath akele rehne se katraana, chhooti hui aadatein laut aana jaise bistar geela karna, mood ya school ke prati ravaiye mein badlaav, aur umar se aage ki sexual jaankari [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]].

Bhai-behen woh dekh lete hain jo mummy-papa se chhoot jaata hai: family functions mein bachcha kisse bachta hai, raat ko use kaun message karta hai, kaun se gifts aa rahe hain jinka koi hisaab nahi. Grooming aksar meharbani jaisi dikhti hai: kisi ek bachche par khaas dhyaan, tohfe, hamdard ban kar sunne wala bada, ya family ki madad karne ki peshkash [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]].

Yeh signs exam ke stress, bullying ya kisi dost se ladai ki wajah se bhi ho sakte hain. Inka matlab hai pyaar se ek sawaal poochna, koi nateeja nikaal lena nahi. Koi shaant, private waqt chuno aur sawaal khula rakho: "Jab woh aate hain, tumhara mood bigad jaata hai. Kya kisi ne kuch aisa kiya jisse tumhe ajeeb ya bura laga?"

## 'Promise karo kisi ko nahi bataoge': iski jagah kya kahein

Abuser aksar bachchon se kehte hain ki yeh "hamara secret" hai, isliye jo bachcha aakhirkaar bolta hai, woh tumse raaz rakhne ki minnat kar sakta hai. Yeh promise mat karo. Iski jagah kaho:

- "Mujhe tum par yakeen hai, aur achha kiya jo tumne mujhe bataya."
- "Ismein tumhari koi galti nahi hai, aur tum kisi musibat mein nahi ho."
- "Yeh baat itni badi hai ki hum dono akele nahi utha sakte. Yeh sirf unhe bataya jaayega jinka kaam madad karna hai, aur kisi ko bhi batane se pehle tumhe pata hoga."

Bachche se details mat poocho, use rishtedaaron ke saamne baat dohrane ko mat kaho, aur jiska naam liya gaya hai usse confront mat karo. Usi din baad mein uske exact shabd, date aur jo bhi tumne notice kiya, sab likh lo.

Kanoon tumhare saath hai. POCSO ka Section 19 child sexual abuse report karne ki zimmedari har insaan par daalta hai, bachche par bhi. Section 21 report na karne par 6 mahine tak ki jail ya fine ki saza deta hai, lekin report na karne par kisi bachche ko saza nahi di ja sakti [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Agar tum khud 18 se kam ho, toh chup rehne par kanoon tumhe saza nahi de sakta. Agar tum 18 ya usse zyada ke ho, toh de sakta hai.

## Jab mummy-papa kuch na karein: 1098, school, police

Mummy-papa keh sakte hain "woh aisa kabhi nahi kar sakte", "family ki izzat ka socho" ya "hum khud sambhal lenge". Jo parent abuse ke baare mein jaante hue bhi chup rehta hai, woh bhi wahi kanooni zimmedari tod raha hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Yeh baat shaanti se kaho. Agar phir bhi kuch na badle, toh unke bina aage badho:

- **Koi aur bada jo kuch karega:** mausi, bua, chachi, dadi-nani, teacher ya school counsellor. Teachers aur counsellors par bhi report karne ki zimmedari hai, aur jo school head kisi staff member ke abuse ko report nahi karta, use 1 saal tak ki jail aur fine ho sakta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].
- **1098**, yaani Child Helpline [[wcd-childline]], 24x7 chalti hai aur emergency number 112 se judi hui hai [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]. Call karne ke liye saboot nahi chahiye: kanoon har us insaan se report karne ko kehta hai jise abuse ka pata ho ya shak ho [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Seedhi baatein batao: bachche ki umar, woh abhi kahan hai, aaj raat safe hai ya nahi, aur usne apne shabdon mein kya kaha.
- **112**, agar bachcha abhi isi waqt khatre mein hai.
- **Koi bhi police station.** Kanoon ke hisaab se tum wahan report kar sakte ho, chahe abuse kahin bhi hua ho [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Report ke baad police ko bachche ka statement ghar par ya bachche ki chuni hui jagah par record karna hota hai, jahan tak ho sake woman officer se, aur officer uniform mein nahi hona chahiye. Bachche ko accused se door rakhna bhi police ki zimmedari hai. Police ko 24 ghante ke andar Child Welfare Committee ko bhi khabar deni hoti hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Iske baare mein kahin post mat karo, family WhatsApp group mein bhi nahi. Chhoti-chhoti details se bachche ki pehchaan khul sakti hai, aur POCSO khud media reports mein child victim ka naam, school, family ya mohalla batane par rok lagata hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

## Tumhari apni safety aur tumhare apne jazbaat

Abuser se khud mat bhido. Dhamki ya maar-peet tumhe, bachche ko aur case ko khatre mein daal sakti hai. Agar accused tumhare saath ek hi ghar mein rehta hai aur darr hai ki bolne ke baad kya hoga, toh yeh baat bhi 1098 ko batao.

Ho sakta hai tumhe guilt ho ki pehle kyun nahi dekha, gussa aaye, ya family ki wafadari tumhe peeche kheenche. Kuch bade bhai-behenon ko yeh ehsaas bhi hota hai ki usi insaan ne unhe bhi nuksaan pahunchaya tha. Agar tumhare saath bhi aisa hua hai, toh tum bhi utni hi madad ke haqdaar ho. Tele-MANAS, sarkar ki free mental-health helpline, 14416 par din-raat jawaab deti hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

Bolne se kuch waqt ke liye ghar ka sukoon chhin sakta hai. Chup rehne ki keemat bachcha kahin zyada chukata hai.

online-crimes-against-children-cseam-tre.en:
Three numbers from the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) look like a story with a plot. Police registered 1,171 cases of sexually explicit material depicting children as cyber crimes against children in 2022, 1,499 in 2023 and 1,099 in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. A rise, then a fall to below where it began. It is tempting to read that as abuse growing and then shrinking. The numbers cannot carry that meaning.

Start with the name. In September 2024 the Supreme Court told Indian courts to stop saying "child pornography" and to use "child sexual exploitation and abuse material" (CSEAM) instead [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Each image records a real child being abused. The question here is how India counts those records.

## 1,171, 1,499, 1,099: the three-year curve

In 2024 these cases made up 63% of the 1,753 cyber crimes against children that police recorded [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A second NCRB table, which counts IT Act cases by section, shows the same shape: cases under Section 67B, the law against child sexual abuse material, went from 1,166 to 1,472 to 1,036 [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. Two tables, slightly different totals, one curve.

So something real moved in the records. But in this crime an FIR often begins far from the child: in a technology company's scanning software, a report to a clearinghouse in the United States, or a complaint typed into a government website. When any link in that chain speeds up or slows down, the count moves with it.

## What NCRB counts as a cyber crime against a child

NCRB counts FIRs, not images, tips or complaints. When one FIR covers several offences, only the one with the maximum punishment is counted [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. So when a child is sexually assaulted and the abuse is also recorded, the case is counted in the POCSO tables whenever POCSO carries the heavier charge. POCSO has its own line for abuse material too: 500 cases in 2024 under Sections 14 and 15, for using children to make such material or storing it [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The result is a record scattered across two laws and several tables, under a heading that still says "cyber pornography", the framing the Supreme Court rejected [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]].

## 2019: a portal and a pipeline of tips

Two steps taken in 2019 built the pipeline behind these numbers. On 26 April 2019 NCRB signed an agreement with the US-based National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) to receive its CyberTipline reports [[pib-wcd-ccpwc-2024]]. On 30 August 2019 the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, cybercrime.gov.in, began as a pilot with a specific focus on crimes against women and children, including child sexual abuse material [[pib-mha-i4c-launch-2020]].

As the Supreme Court described the route, platforms report to NCMEC, NCMEC passes reports to NCRB, and NCRB forwards them to the states through the portal [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. By 31 March 2024, more than 69.05 lakh such reports had reached states and union territories [[pib-wcd-ccpwc-2024]]. Separately, about 1.94 lakh complaints about child sexual abuse material and rape or gang-rape content had been filed on the portal by 30 April 2024 [[pib-wcd-ccpwc-2024]].

Now set one year's tips against one year's FIRs. In 2024 NCMEC linked 2,252,528 reports to India, 1,521,666 of them with enough information for police action [[ncmec-cybertipline-by-country-2024]]. Police registered 1,099 cases.

Consider what a single tip must survive. A platform flags an upload traced to a phone in a small town. The report goes to the US, returns to NCRB and lands with a district cyber cell, which must find a real person, seize a device and decide to register an FIR. A tip can stop at any step. NCMEC itself warns that its country figures do not measure how much abuse happens in a country; they mostly reflect uploads detected by US platforms [[ncmec-reports-by-country-2025]].

## Why 2024 fell: fewer crimes, or fewer reports?

Line up the two series. Every year, the NCRB count moved the same way as NCMEC's reports for India [[ncmec-reports-by-country-2025]].

| Year | NCMEC reports linked to India | NCRB cases of child sexual abuse material |
|---|---|---|
| 2022 | 5,675,324 | 1,171 |
| 2023 | 8,923,738 | 1,499 |
| 2024 | 2,252,528 | 1,099 |

The 2024 drop was not India's alone. Worldwide, NCMEC's reports fell from 36.2 million in 2023 to 20.5 million in 2024; NCMEC said large platforms had begun "bundling" related reports and some were reporting less, not that the crimes had stopped [[ncmec-2024-in-numbers-2025]]. Counted as separate incidents, 2024 came to 29.2 million [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]].

Three years are not proof, and tips are not the only bottleneck. In 2024 police had 2,356 Section 67B cases to investigate, chargesheeted at a rate of 69.3%, and still had 48.1% under investigation at year's end [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Courts had 2,885 such cases; trials ended in only 156, with 57 convictions, and 94.5% were still pending [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

So a falling count can mean fewer tips, slower cyber cells or cases filed under another law. On its own, it cannot mean children are safer.

## What a real measure would look like

A count built around children would publish the whole pipeline, state by state: tips received, tips investigated, FIRs, people charged and, above all, children identified and helped. Today the tips surface as a running total in an answer to Parliament, and the FIRs as a yearly count in NCRB's tables. Neither source shows what happened to the tips in between.

It would count platforms too. The Supreme Court ruled in 2024 that platforms which report abuse material to NCMEC must also report it to India's Special Juvenile Police Unit or local police [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. How many such reports arrive, and what happens to them, deserves a published number.

It should expect the count to rise. In February 2026 large platforms' duty to "endeavour to deploy" automated tools that find child sexual abuse content became a duty to "deploy appropriate technical measures" [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. More detection means more tips. If FIRs climb next, that may be the system working better, not more children being hurt.

And it would ask children. A survey that asks young people directly, as the government's 2007 Study on Child Abuse did, would show what no FIR count can [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Until then, read every swing in this line as a report on police and platforms. It captures a tiny fraction of what is detected, and nothing of what is not.
online-crimes-against-children-cseam-tre.hg:
National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) ke teen numbers dekhkar lagta hai jaise koi kahani chal rahi ho. Bachchon ke khilaaf cyber crimes mein, police ne bachchon ko sexually explicit tarah se dikhane wale material ke 2022 mein 1,171 cases darj kiye, 2023 mein 1,499 aur 2024 mein 1,099 [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. Pehle badhat, phir giravat, aur woh bhi shuruaat wale number se neeche tak. Mann karta hai ise aise padhein ki abuse pehle badha aur phir ghat gaya. Lekin yeh numbers itna bada matlab nahi utha sakte.

Shuruaat naam se karte hain. September 2024 mein Supreme Court ne India ki courts se kaha ki "child pornography" kehna band karein, aur uski jagah "child sexual exploitation and abuse material" (CSEAM) kahein [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Har aisi image ek asli bachche ke abuse ka record hai. Yahan sawaal yeh hai ki India in records ko ginta kaise hai.

## 1,171, 1,499, 1,099: teen saal ka curve

2024 mein police ne bachchon ke khilaaf 1,753 cyber crimes darj kiye, aur unmein se 63% yahi cases the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB ki ek doosri table, jo IT Act ke cases ko section ke hisaab se ginti hai, wahi shape dikhati hai. Section 67B, yaani child sexual abuse material ke khilaaf wala law, uske cases 1,166 se 1,472 hue, aur phir 1,036 [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. Do tables, thode alag totals, lekin curve ek hi.

Toh records mein kuch na kuch sach mein hila. Lekin is crime mein FIR aksar bachche se bahut door shuru hoti hai: kisi tech company ke scanning software mein, United States ke ek clearinghouse ko gayi report mein, ya kisi government website pe type ki gayi complaint mein. Is chain ki koi bhi kadi tez ya dheemi ho, ginti bhi uske saath hilti hai.

## NCRB bachche ke khilaaf cyber crime kise ginta hai

NCRB FIRs ginta hai, images, tips ya complaints nahi. Jab ek FIR mein kai offences hote hain, toh sirf woh gina jaata hai jiski saza sabse zyada hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Isliye agar kisi bachche ka sexual assault hua aur us abuse ko record bhi kiya gaya, toh jab bhi POCSO ka charge bhaari ho, case POCSO ki tables mein gina jaata hai. POCSO mein abuse material ki apni alag line bhi hai: 2024 mein Sections 14 aur 15 ke under 500 cases, yaani bachchon ko aisa material banane mein use karna, ya aisa material store karna [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Nateeja yeh hai ki record do laws aur kai tables mein bikhra hua hai, aur ek aisi heading ke neeche hai jo ab bhi "cyber pornography" kehti hai. Yeh wahi framing hai jise Supreme Court reject kar chuka hai [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]].

## 2019: ek portal aur tips ki pipeline

In numbers ke peeche ki pipeline 2019 ke do kadamon se bani. 26 April 2019 ko NCRB ne US ki sanstha National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) ke saath agreement sign kiya, taaki uski CyberTipline reports India ko milein [[pib-wcd-ccpwc-2024]]. 30 August 2019 ko National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, yaani cybercrime.gov.in, pilot ke roop mein shuru hua. Iska khaas focus women aur bachchon ke khilaaf crimes pe tha, jismein child sexual abuse material bhi shaamil tha [[pib-mha-i4c-launch-2020]].

Supreme Court ne yeh raasta aise samjhaya: platforms NCMEC ko report karte hain, NCMEC reports NCRB ko deta hai, aur NCRB unhe portal ke through states ko bhej deta hai [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. 31 March 2024 tak aisi 69.05 lakh se zyada reports states aur union territories tak pahunch chuki thi [[pib-wcd-ccpwc-2024]]. Iske alawa, 30 April 2024 tak portal pe child sexual abuse material aur rape ya gang-rape content ki lagbhag 1.94 lakh complaints darj ho chuki thi [[pib-wcd-ccpwc-2024]].

Ab ek saal ki tips ko usi saal ki FIRs ke saamne rakhiye. 2024 mein NCMEC ne 2,252,528 reports India se jodi, jinmein se 1,521,666 mein itni jaankari thi ki police action le sake [[ncmec-cybertipline-by-country-2024]]. Police ne 1,099 cases darj kiye.

Sochiye, ek tip ko kitne padaav paar karne padte hain. Ek platform kisi upload ko flag karta hai, jo ek chhote shehar ke kisi phone tak trace hota hai. Report US jaati hai, NCRB ke paas wapas aati hai, aur phir district ke cyber cell tak pahunchti hai. Wahan kisi ko asli insaan dhoondhna hai, device seize karna hai, aur tay karna hai ki FIR darj ho ya nahi. Tip kisi bhi step pe ruk sakti hai. NCMEC khud warning deta hai ki uske country figures yeh nahi naapte ki kisi desh mein kitna abuse hota hai; yeh zyadatar US platforms ke pakde gaye uploads dikhate hain [[ncmec-reports-by-country-2025]].

## 2024 mein ginti kyun giri: kam crimes, ya kam reports?

Dono series ko saath rakhkar dekhiye. Har saal NCRB ki ginti usi direction mein chali jis direction mein India ke liye NCMEC ki reports chali [[ncmec-reports-by-country-2025]].

| Saal | India se judi NCMEC reports | Child sexual abuse material ke NCRB cases |
|---|---|---|
| 2022 | 5,675,324 | 1,171 |
| 2023 | 8,923,738 | 1,499 |
| 2024 | 2,252,528 | 1,099 |

2024 ki giravat sirf India ki nahi thi. Duniya bhar mein NCMEC ki reports 2023 ke 36.2 million se girkar 2024 mein 20.5 million reh gayi. NCMEC ne kaha ki bade platforms ne judi hui reports ko "bundle" karna shuru kar diya tha aur kuch platforms kam report kar rahe the; aisa nahi tha ki crimes ruk gaye the [[ncmec-2024-in-numbers-2025]]. Alag-alag incidents ke hisaab se ginein, toh 2024 ka aankda 29.2 million banta hai [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]].

Teen saal ka data koi saboot nahi hai, aur tips akeli rukawat bhi nahi hain. 2024 mein police ke paas investigate karne ke liye Section 67B ke 2,356 cases the. Chargesheet ka rate 69.3% raha, aur saal ke end mein bhi 48.1% cases investigation mein hi the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Courts ke saamne aise 2,885 cases the. Trial sirf 156 mein poora hua, 57 mein conviction hua, aur 94.5% ab bhi pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Toh girti ginti ka matlab kam tips ho sakta hai, dheeme cyber cells ho sakte hain, ya kisi doosre law ke under darj hue cases. Akele is number se yeh nahi kaha ja sakta ki bachche ab zyada safe hain.

## Ek sahi measure kaisa dikhega

Bachchon ko centre mein rakhkar banayi gayi ginti poori pipeline ko state-wise publish karegi: kitni tips aayi, kitni ki jaanch hui, kitni FIRs hui, kitne logon pe charge laga, aur sabse zaroori, kitne bachchon ki pehchaan hui aur unhe madad mili. Abhi tips Parliament mein diye gaye ek jawaab mein running total ki tarah dikhti hain, aur FIRs NCRB ki tables mein ek saalana ginti ki tarah. Dono mein se koi source yeh nahi dikhata ki beech mein un tips ka kya hua.

Aisi ginti platforms ko bhi ginegi. Supreme Court ne 2024 mein faisla diya ki jo platforms abuse material ki report NCMEC ko karte hain, unhe India ki Special Juvenile Police Unit ya local police ko bhi report karna hoga [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Aisi kitni reports aati hain, aur unka kya hota hai, iska bhi ek published number hona chahiye.

Aur aise measure ko yeh maan kar chalna chahiye ki ginti badhegi. February 2026 mein bade platforms ki duty badli. Pehle unhe child sexual abuse content pakadne wale automated tools "endeavour to deploy" karne the, yaani lagane ki koshish karni thi. Ab unhe "deploy appropriate technical measures" karna hai, yaani sahi technical measures lagane hi hain [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. Zyada detection ka matlab zyada tips. Agar iske baad FIRs badhti hain, toh ho sakta hai system behtar kaam kar raha ho, yeh nahi ki zyada bachchon ko nuksaan pahunch raha hai.

Aur aisi ginti bachchon se poochegi. Ek survey jo young logon se seedha sawaal kare, jaise sarkar ki 2007 ki Study on Child Abuse ne kiya tha, woh dikhayega jo koi FIR count nahi dikha sakta [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Tab tak is line ke har utaar-chadhaav ko police aur platforms ke kaam ki report ki tarah padhiye. Jo material pakda gaya, yeh line uska bas ek chhota sa hissa dikhati hai, aur jo pakda hi nahi gaya, uska kuch bhi nahi.

online-friend-meeting-teen-safety.en:
In 2025, the US-based National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) received 1.4 million reports of online enticement of children, a 158% rise on 2024. More than 800 of them described an offender who travelled to meet a child in person [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]]. Each began as a conversation on a screen. This guide is for teenagers thinking of meeting someone they know only from a phone, and for the parents they may or may not tell.

## From chat to meeting: what the 800 reports show

The 800 are a small slice of 1.4 million, and that is the point. Most of the reports describe no journey at all, and more than 80,000 concerned sextortion [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]]. The meeting is the step where online abuse can become physical.

Read the rise with care. Part of it reflects a 2024 US law, the REPORT Act, which requires platforms to report online enticement [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]]. More reports do not prove more crime. These are also global figures from a US clearing house. India's crime statistics have no separate count of offenders who met a child they first contacted online.

## Inside NCRB's 'online friends' column

The closest Indian number sits in NCRB's table of who the accused was in POCSO penetrative-assault cases. In 2024, the largest group, 22,308 of 44,126 cases (50.6%), fell in a single column: friends, online friends or live-in partners "on pretext of marriage" [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The table does not separate the three. An adult who groomed a 14-year-old online, a man who promised a 16-year-old marriage and a classmate in a teenage relationship all sit in one column.

Older teenagers dominate the record. Of 44,567 child victims of penetrative assault in 2024, 23,497 (52.7%) were 16 to 18 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], an age of more independence and first relationships. NCRB does not say how many of these cases began online. Boys are in this data too: 892 of the victims were boys [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. One line does not move. POCSO protects everyone under 18, so anything sexual with a child is an offence, whatever the child agreed to [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

## Signs an online friendship is grooming

UNICEF warns that online abusers may be strangers or people the child already knows, and that they often win the trust of the child, or of a parent, before manipulating the child into sharing sexual images or videos [[unicef-keeping-children-safe-online-2026]]. Indian law treats the build-up as a crime: Section 67B of the IT Act punishes enticing a child into an online sexual relationship, with up to five years in prison on a first conviction [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].

Consider this situation. A 15-year-old boy in Pune has chatted for two months with a "girl from the next school" he met on a gaming server. Her camera never works. She sends him game credits, says nobody understands him like she does and asks him to keep her a secret. Then she suggests meeting at "my cousin's flat" and offers to pay for his cab.

Every warning sign is in that story:

- **Secrecy:** "Don't tell anyone about us."
- **A move somewhere private:** from a game or comments to a private or disappearing-message app.
- **Speed and flattery** that make you feel chosen.
- **Gifts and money:** recharges, game credits, cab fare.
- **Questions about your routine:** when your parents are out, where you will be alone.
- **Pressure to meet alone or send photos,** then sulking, guilt or threats when you say no.
- **A story that does not add up:** an age that shifts, a camera that never works.

## Rules for any first meeting, agreed in advance

Not meeting is the safest choice for anyone under 18. If you are going anyway, agree these rules before the day:

1. **A trusted adult knows** who, where and when, and has seen the profile.
2. **Public, busy, daytime:** a café or a mall, never a home, hotel, car, empty park or "a friend's place".
3. **Your own transport,** so you can leave at any moment. No pickups or cabs paid for by them.
4. **Bring someone:** a friend, or an adult who stays nearby.
5. **Share your live location,** and agree a code word that means "call me and get me out".
6. **Any change means you leave:** a different person from the one in the profile, a second venue, a "quick stop" somewhere private.

A real friend will accept all six. Someone who argues against them, especially against an adult knowing, has told you what you need to know.

Parents: rules only work if your teenager tells you about the meeting. Promise a no-questions pickup at any hour, and keep it. Banning the phone or punishing honesty teaches a child to hide the next chat.

## If a meeting has already happened: what to do now

If it felt wrong, or the person is now pushing for more, tell a trusted adult. Block the account but do not delete the chats: screenshots, usernames, profile links and payment details are evidence. Report at cybercrime.gov.in or on 1930 [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].

If you were sexually assaulted:

- **Get safe, then call 112 or the Child Helpline 1098,** which runs 24x7 and is linked to 112 [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].
- **Go to any hospital.** Every hospital, public or private, must give a survivor of a POCSO offence immediate free treatment [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Ask about medicines quickly.** Emergency contraception can be used up to five days after unprotected sex and works better the sooner it is taken [[who-ec]]. HIV prevention medicine (PEP) should start as soon as possible, and no later than 72 hours after exposure [[who-pep]].
- **Know what happens next.** Under POCSO, anyone who learns that a child has been abused, including a doctor or counsellor, must report it to the police [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. They cannot promise total secrecy. You are the one who was harmed, not the one in trouble.

Agreeing to meet someone is not agreeing to what they did. In the weeks after, Tele-MANAS (14416) offers free counselling at any hour [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].
online-friend-meeting-teen-safety.hg:
2025 mein US ke National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) ko bachchon ke online enticement, yaani online fuslaane, ki 1.4 million reports mili, jo 2024 se 158% zyada thi. Inmein se 800 se zyada reports mein offender bachche se milne khud travel karke pahuncha tha [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]]. Har ek ki shuruaat screen pe ek baatcheet se hui thi. Yeh guide un teenagers ke liye hai jo kisi aise insaan se milne ki soch rahe hain jise woh sirf phone pe jaante hain, aur un parents ke liye bhi, jinhe shayad woh bataayein, shayad nahi.

## Chat se mulaqat tak: 800 reports kya dikhati hain

1.4 million mein 800 bahut chhota hissa hai, aur asli baat yahi hai. Zyadatar reports mein milne ke liye kisi safar ka zikr hi nahi hai, aur 80,000 se zyada reports sextortion ki thi [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]]. Mulaqat woh step hai jahan online abuse physical ban sakta hai.

Is badhotri ko dhyaan se padhiye. Iska ek hissa 2024 ke ek US kanoon, REPORT Act, ki wajah se hai, jo platforms ke liye online enticement report karna zaroori banata hai [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]]. Zyada reports ka matlab zaroori nahi ki crime bhi zyada hua. Yeh ek US clearing house ke global figures bhi hain. India ke crime statistics mein aise offenders ki koi alag ginti nahi hai jo kisi bachche se online contact ke baad usse milne pahunche.

## NCRB ka 'online friends' wala column

Sabse kareebi Indian number NCRB ki us table mein hai jo batati hai ki POCSO ke penetrative assault cases mein accused kaun tha. 2024 mein sabse bada group, 44,126 mein se 22,308 cases (50.6%), ek hi column mein tha: friends, online friends ya "on pretext of marriage", yaani shaadi ke bahane, live-in partners [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Table in teeno ko alag nahi karti. Ek adult jisne 14 saal ke bachche ko online groom kiya, ek aadmi jisne 16 saal ki ladki se shaadi ka waada kiya, aur teenage relationship wala ek classmate, sab ek hi column mein baithe hain.

Record mein sabse zyada bade teenagers hain. 2024 mein penetrative assault ke 44,567 child victims mein se 23,497 (52.7%) 16 se 18 saal ke the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh woh umar hai jab azaadi badhti hai aur pehle relationships bante hain. NCRB yeh nahi batata ki inmein se kitne cases online shuru hue. Is data mein ladke bhi hain: victims mein 892 ladke the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Ek line kabhi nahi hilti. POCSO 18 se kam umar ke har insaan ko protect karta hai, isliye kisi bachche ke saath kuch bhi sexual offence hai, chahe bachche ne haan kaha ho [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

## Online dosti grooming hai, iske signs

UNICEF ki warning hai ki online abusers anjaan bhi ho sakte hain aur bachche ke jaan-pehchaan wale bhi. Woh aksar pehle bachche ka, ya maa-baap ka, trust jeette hain, aur phir bachche ko manipulate karke sexual photos ya videos share karwaate hain [[unicef-keeping-children-safe-online-2026]]. Indian kanoon is taiyaari ko hi crime maanta hai: IT Act ka Section 67B kisi bachche ko online sexual relationship mein fuslaane pe pehli conviction mein paanch saal tak ki jail ki saza deta hai [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].

Ek situation sochiye. Pune ka ek 15 saal ka ladka do mahine se ek "bagal wale school ki ladki" se chat kar raha hai, jo use ek gaming server pe mili thi. Uska camera kabhi kaam nahi karta. Woh use game credits bhejti hai, kehti hai ki koi use utna nahi samajhta jitna woh samajhti hai, aur kehti hai ki uske baare mein kisi ko na bataye. Phir woh "meri cousin ke flat" pe milne ko kehti hai aur cab ke paise dene ki offer karti hai.

Is kahani mein har warning sign maujood hai:

- **Secrecy:** "Hamare baare mein kisi ko mat batana."
- **Kisi private jagah shift karna:** game ya comments se kisi private ya disappearing-message app pe.
- **Tezi aur tareefein,** jo tumhe special feel karaayein.
- **Gifts aur paise:** recharge, game credits, cab ka kiraya.
- **Tumhari routine ke sawaal:** parents kab bahar hote hain, tum kab akele hote ho.
- **Akele milne ya photos bhejne ka pressure,** aur mana karne pe roothna, guilt trip ya dhamki.
- **Kahani jo jud nahi rahi:** umar jo badalti rehti hai, camera jo kabhi chalta hi nahi.

## Pehli mulaqat ke rules, pehle se tay

18 se kam umar mein na milna hi sabse safe choice hai. Agar phir bhi ja rahe ho, to yeh rules mulaqat ke din se pehle tay karo:

1. **Ek trusted adult ko pata ho** ki kisse, kahan aur kab mil rahe ho, aur usne profile dekhi ho.
2. **Public, bheed wali jagah, din mein:** koi café ya mall. Kabhi ghar, hotel, car, sunsaan park ya "ek dost ki jagah" nahi.
3. **Apna transport,** taaki tum kabhi bhi nikal sako. Unki bheji pickup ya unke paise wali cab nahi.
4. **Kisi ko saath le jao:** koi dost, ya koi adult jo aas-paas rahe.
5. **Live location share karo,** aur ek code word tay karo jiska matlab ho "mujhe call karke yahan se nikaalo".
6. **Kuch bhi badla to nikal jao:** profile wale insaan ki jagah koi aur aaye, doosri jagah chalne ki baat ho, ya kahin private "bas thodi der" rukna ho.

Ek sachcha dost yeh chhe ke chhe rules maan lega. Jo inke khilaaf bahas kare, khaas kar kisi adult ko batane ke khilaaf, usne tumhe woh bata diya hai jo jaanna zaroori tha.

Parents: rules tabhi kaam karte hain jab aapka teenager aapko mulaqat ke baare mein bataye. Kisi bhi waqt "bina sawaal" pickup ka waada kijiye, aur use nibhaiye. Phone chheen lena ya sach bolne pe saza dena bachche ko agli chat chhupana sikhata hai.

## Agar mulaqat ho chuki hai: ab kya karein

Agar kuch galat laga, ya woh insaan ab aur aage badhne ka pressure daal raha hai, to kisi trusted adult ko batao. Account block karo par chats delete mat karo: screenshots, usernames, profile links aur payment details sab evidence hain. Report cybercrime.gov.in pe ya 1930 pe karo [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].

Agar tumhare saath sexual assault hua hai:

- **Pehle safe jagah pahuncho, phir 112 ya Child Helpline 1098 pe call karo,** jo 24x7 chalti hai aur 112 se judi hai [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].
- **Kisi bhi hospital jao.** Har hospital, sarkari ho ya private, ko POCSO offence ke survivor ka turant aur free ilaaj karna hota hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Dawaiyon ke baare mein jaldi poochho.** Emergency contraception unprotected sex ke paanch din tak li ja sakti hai, aur jitni jaldi lo utna behtar kaam karti hai [[who-ec]]. HIV se bachane wali dawa (PEP) jitni jaldi ho sake shuru honi chahiye, aur exposure ke 72 ghante ke andar hi [[who-pep]].
- **Aage kya hoga, yeh jaano.** POCSO ke tahat jis kisi ko bhi pata chale ki kisi bachche ke saath abuse hua hai, doctor ya counsellor bhi, use police ko report karna hota hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Woh poori secrecy ka waada nahi kar sakte. Nuksaan tumhara hua hai, musibat mein tum nahi ho.

Kisi se milne ke liye haan kehna, usne jo kiya uske liye haan kehna nahi hai. Aane wale hafton mein Tele-MANAS (14416) kisi bhi waqt free counselling deta hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

only-rape-counts-child-abuse-myth.en:
Consider this situation. A 10-year-old in Lucknow tells her mother that her tuition teacher touches her in ways she does not like, and has told her to keep it between them. The family is uneasy. Then someone says what families often say: he only touched her, nothing really happened, why ruin a man's name and the girl's future over it? The tuition continues. That sentence rests on a myth, that only rape counts as child sexual abuse. The law, the data and children's own reactions all say otherwise.

## The myth: if it was not rape, it was not abuse

The myth grades abuse by what happened to the body, and only the most extreme act counts. Part of it is the old idea of "izzat": if the girl is still a "virgin", the family has lost nothing worth reporting. Part of it is relief. "Only touching" lets adults skip the hardest step, which is acting against someone they know.

The child hears something else: what happened to my body does not matter, and telling achieved nothing. Next time, there is no reason to tell.

## More than a third of POCSO cases are not rape cases

In 2024, police registered 69,191 cases under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Of these, 44,126 (63.8%) were for penetrative or aggravated penetrative sexual assault, what most people would call child rape. The rest were other crimes: 20,845 (30.1%) for sexual assault or aggravated sexual assault without penetration, 3,502 for sexual harassment, 500 for using children to make, or storing, sexual abuse material, and 218 under sections covering abetment, attempt, failure to report and false complaints [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

So more than one in three POCSO cases in 2024 were not about penetrative assault. These are the cases the myth would erase, and they are a floor, not a full count. NCRB records each case once, under its most serious offence, so touching that came before a rape disappears into the rape figure. And if families treat touching as nothing, those cases are the least likely to reach a police station at all.

## Touch, exposure, photos: what the 2007 study counted

When the government asked children directly, in its 2007 Study on Child Abuse, it did not limit the question to rape. Of 12,447 children across 13 states, 53.22% reported one or more forms of sexual abuse, 21.90% reported severe forms, and 5.69% reported being sexually assaulted [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. The severe forms included fondling, forcing a child to exhibit private parts and nude photography. The other forms included forcible kissing, sexual advances during travel and exposure to pornography [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

The sample was purposive, not national, so these are not prevalence rates for India. But the pattern is plain: most of what children described was not sexual assault in the study's narrowest sense. A rule that only rape counts would have told most of them that nothing happened.

Global estimates show the same gap. UNICEF estimates that more than 370 million girls and women alive today, about 1 in 8, were raped or sexually assaulted before 18. Counting non-contact abuse, such as online or verbal sexual abuse, the figure rises to about 650 million, or 1 in 5 [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]]. For boys and men, the estimate rises from 240 to 310 million to between 410 and 530 million [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]].

## Sexual intent, not skin: what POCSO says

POCSO protects every child under 18, boys and girls alike [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], and it does not stop at penetration. Sexual assault without penetration is a separate offence, punished under Sections 8 and 10, and so is sexual harassment of a child, punished under Section 12; police count each of these separately [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Courts have had to defend that range. In January 2021 the Bombay High Court held that touching a child over her clothes was not sexual assault because there was no skin-to-skin contact. On 18 November 2021 the Supreme Court set that ruling aside: "the important ingredient for constituting the offence of sexual assault under POCSO is sexual intent and not skin to skin contact with the child" [[barandbench-satish-2021]].

Nor does the law treat these as lesser complaints. Under Section 29, a Special Court must presume that a person prosecuted for sexual assault committed it unless the contrary is proved, exactly as it does for penetrative assault [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

## The harm a child carries, and how to respond

Darkness to Light, a US child-protection nonprofit, notes that emotional and behavioural signs of abuse are more common than physical ones: anxiety or depression, sleep problems and nightmares, unusual fear of a person, bedwetting again, changes in mood or in attitude to school [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. None of these depends on whether there was penetration. A child who was "only touched" can be a child who stops sleeping, or refuses to go back to tuition.

If a child tells you about any of it:

- **Name it.** Say "that was wrong, and it was not your fault", never "thank god nothing happened".
- **Stop the access** at once, whoever the person is.
- **Report.** The POCSO duty to report covers every offence under the Act, not only rape, and failing to report can mean up to six months in prison or a fine [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Call 1098 or 112.
- **Keep listening, without pushing.** A child may share part of what happened first, to see how you react.
only-rape-counts-child-abuse-myth.hg:
Yeh situation sochiye. Lucknow mein 10 saal ki ek ladki apni maa ko batati hai ki uska tuition teacher use aise chhoota hai jo use achha nahi lagta, aur usne kaha hai ki yeh baat dono ke beech hi rahe. Family pareshaan hoti hai. Phir koi woh baat keh deta hai jo families aksar kehti hain: usne bas chhua hi to tha, asal mein kuch hua nahi, ek aadmi ka naam aur ladki ka future kyun kharab karna? Tuition chalti rehti hai. Yeh baat ek myth par tiki hai, ki bachchon ke sexual abuse mein sirf rape hi gina jaata hai. Law, data aur khud bachchon ke reactions, sab kuch aur kehte hain.

## Myth: rape nahi hua, to abuse bhi nahi hua

Yeh myth abuse ko is hisaab se naapta hai ki body ke saath kya hua, aur sirf sabse extreme cheez ko hi abuse maanta hai. Iske peeche ek hissa 'izzat' wali purani soch ka hai: agar ladki ab bhi 'virgin' hai, to family ka koi aisa nuksaan nahi hua jise report kiya jaaye. Ek hissa raahat ka bhi hai. "Bas chhua tha" kehkar bade sabse mushkil kadam se bach jaate hain, yaani kisi jaan-pehchaan wale ke khilaaf action lene se.

Bachcha isse kuch aur sunta hai: meri body ke saath jo hua uska koi matlab nahi, aur batane se kuch nahi badla. Agli baar batane ki koi wajah hi nahi bachti.

## POCSO ke ek-tihaai se zyada cases rape ke nahi hain

2024 mein police ne Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act ke tahat 69,191 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Inmein se 44,126 (63.8%) penetrative ya aggravated penetrative sexual assault ke the, jise zyadatar log child rape kehte hain. Baaki doosre crimes the: 20,845 (30.1%) bina penetration wale sexual assault ya aggravated sexual assault ke, 3,502 sexual harassment ke, 500 bachchon se sexual abuse material banwane ya use store karne ke, aur 218 un sections ke tahat jo abetment, attempt, report na karne aur jhoothi complaint se jude hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Yaani 2024 mein POCSO ke har teen mein se ek se zyada cases penetrative assault ke nahi the. Yahi woh cases hain jinhe yeh myth mita dena chahta hai, aur yeh poori ginti nahi, sirf neeche ki had hai. NCRB har case ko ek hi baar, uske sabse gambhir offence ke under ginta hai, isliye rape se pehle hua chhoona rape ke figure mein hi kho jaata hai. Aur agar families chhoone ko kuch maanti hi nahi, to aise cases ke police station tak pahunchne ki sambhavna sabse kam hoti hai.

## Touch, body dikhana, photos: 2007 ki study ne kya gina

2007 ki Study on Child Abuse mein jab sarkar ne seedhe bachchon se poocha, to sawaal sirf rape tak seemit nahi tha. 13 states ke 12,447 bachchon mein se 53.22% ne sexual abuse ka ek ya zyada roop bataya, 21.90% ne gambhir roop bataye, aur 5.69% ne kaha ki unka sexual assault hua tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Gambhir roopon mein fondling, bachche se zabardasti private parts dikhwana aur nude photography shaamil the. Baaki roopon mein zabardasti kiss karna, safar ke dauraan sexual advances aur pornography dikhana shaamil the [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

Sample purposive tha, national nahi, isliye yeh India ke prevalence rates nahi hain. Lekin pattern saaf hai: bachchon ne jo bataya, uska zyadatar hissa study ke sabse sankare matlab mein sexual assault nahi tha. 'Sirf rape gina jaayega' wala rule inmein se zyadatar bachchon ko yahi kehta ki kuch hua hi nahi.

Duniya bhar ke estimates bhi yahi farq dikhate hain. UNICEF ka estimate hai ki aaj zinda 370 million se zyada ladkiyon aur mahilaon, yaani lagbhag 1 in 8, ka 18 saal se pehle rape ya sexual assault hua. Online ya verbal sexual abuse jaise non-contact abuse ko bhi ginein, to yeh figure lagbhag 650 million, yaani 1 in 5, tak pahunch jaata hai [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]]. Ladkon aur mardon ke liye yeh estimate 240 se 310 million se badhkar 410 se 530 million ho jaata hai [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]].

## Skin nahi, sexual intent: POCSO kya kehta hai

POCSO 18 saal se kam umar ke har bachche ko bachata hai, ladkon aur ladkiyon dono ko [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], aur yeh penetration par aakar ruk nahi jaata. Bina penetration wala sexual assault ek alag offence hai, jiski saza Section 8 aur 10 mein hai, aur bachche ka sexual harassment bhi, jiski saza Section 12 mein hai; police in sabko alag-alag ginti hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Courts ko is range ka bachaav karna pada hai. January 2021 mein Bombay High Court ne kaha ki kapdon ke upar se bachchi ko chhoona sexual assault nahi hai, kyunki skin-to-skin contact nahi hua. 18 November 2021 ko Supreme Court ne yeh faisla palat diya: "the important ingredient for constituting the offence of sexual assault under POCSO is sexual intent and not skin to skin contact with the child", yaani POCSO mein sexual assault ka sabse zaroori hissa sexual intent hai, bachche ki skin se skin ka contact nahi [[barandbench-satish-2021]].

Law in cases ko halki shikayat bhi nahi maanta. Section 29 ke tahat Special Court ko maan kar chalna hota hai ki jis par sexual assault ka case chal raha hai, usne offence kiya hai, jab tak ulta saabit na ho, bilkul waise hi jaise penetrative assault mein [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Bachcha jo zakhm saath lekar chalta hai, aur aapko kya karna chahiye

Darkness to Light, US ki ek child-protection nonprofit, kehti hai ki abuse ke emotional aur behavioural signs physical signs se zyada common hain: anxiety ya depression, neend ki dikkat aur bure sapne, kisi insaan se ajeeb sa darr, phir se bistar geela karna, mood mein ya school ke prati ravaiye mein badlaav [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. Inmein se koi bhi sign is baat par depend nahi karta ki penetration hua ya nahi. Jis bachche ko "bas chhua gaya", woh aisa bachcha bhi ho sakta hai jiski neend ud jaaye, ya jo tuition wapas jaane se inkaar kar de.

Agar koi bachcha aapko inmein se kuch bhi bataye:

- **Use naam dijiye.** Kahiye "woh galat tha, aur usmein tumhari koi galti nahi", kabhi yeh nahi ki "shukar hai kuch hua nahi".
- **Pahunch turant band kijiye**, chahe woh insaan koi bhi ho.
- **Report kijiye.** POCSO mein report karne ki duty Act ke har offence par laagu hai, sirf rape par nahi, aur report na karne par chhe mahine tak ki jail ya jurmana ho sakta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. 1098 ya 112 par call kijiye.
- **Sunte rahiye, zor daale bina.** Ho sakta hai bachcha pehle poori baat ka sirf ek hissa bataye, yeh dekhne ke liye ki aap kaise react karte hain.

pocso-2024-by-the-numbers.en:
In 2024, police in India registered 69,191 cases under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Behind that one figure sit many more: who the children were, who the accused were, what police did and what courts decided. Here is each key number, mostly from NCRB's *Crime in India 2024*, with what it means and what it hides. For the wider count of crimes against children, from kidnapping to child marriage, read our companion piece on all of them.

## Cases and rate: 69,191 and 15.6 per lakh children

**69,191 cases, 70,132 children.** That is the number of POCSO FIRs, and the children named in them [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *What it hides:* NCRB counts each FIR once, under its most serious offence, the "principal offence rule" [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A case that also involves a crime with a heavier punishment, such as murder, may be counted under that crime instead.

**15.6 per lakh children.** The rate per 1,00,000 children [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *What it hides:* it is worked out on the child population of the 2011 Census, a count 13 years older than the crimes.

**53,874 to 69,191.** Cases rose from 53,874 in 2021 to 63,414 in 2022, 67,694 in 2023 and 69,191 in 2024, about 28% in three years [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. *What it hides:* a rising count can mean more abuse, or more families willing to report and police willing to register. The data cannot tell which.

**36.9% of crimes against children.** POCSO was the second-biggest head; only kidnapping and abduction, at 40.0%, was bigger [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**44,126 penetrative assaults.** The cases split across the Act like this [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| POCSO sections | Offence | Cases |
|---|---|---|
| 4 and 6 | Penetrative or aggravated penetrative sexual assault | 44,126 (63.8%) |
| 8 and 10 | Sexual assault or aggravated sexual assault | 20,845 (30.1%) |
| 12 | Sexual harassment | 3,502 |
| 14 and 15 | Using a child to make, or storing, sexual abuse material | 500 |
| 17 to 22 | Abetment, attempt, failure to report, false complaints | 218 |

## Victims: girls, boys and ages

**43,675 girls, 892 boys.** These were the 44,567 child victims of penetrative assault [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *What it hides:* boys are about 2% here, yet in the government's 2007 study boys were 52.94% of the children who reported sexual abuse [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. The gap says more about who gets reported than about who gets abused, a story we tell separately.

**831 under six.** Of the same 44,567 victims, 831 were under six and another 3,438 were aged 6 to 12, so 4,269 were under 12 in all. Then 16,801 were aged 12 to 16, and 23,497, or 52.7%, were 16 to 18 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *What it hides:* very young children rarely disclose, so the under-12 counts are minimums. The bulge at 16 to 18 may partly reflect cases from teenage relationships and elopements, which NCRB does not count separately.

## Who the accused were

**96.6% known to the child.** In 42,634 of the 44,126 penetrative-assault cases, the accused was someone the child knew [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**3,658, 16,668, 22,308 and 1,492.** Family members; family friends, neighbours, employers or other known persons; friends, online friends or live-in partners "on pretext of marriage"; and, last, unknown or unidentified people [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *What it hides:* the table covers only Sections 4 and 6. Its biggest column mixes adults who groom children with sexual relationships between teenagers, which POCSO treats as an offence when either one is under 18.

## Police: chargesheets and the open files

**95.3% chargesheeted.** Of the POCSO cases police disposed of in 2024, they filed a chargesheet in 95.3% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *What it hides:* the rate divides chargesheets by cases disposed of. It says nothing about how strong the evidence was.

**21,256 still open.** At the end of the year, 21,256 POCSO cases were still under investigation: 23.7% of the 89,658 cases police had to investigate [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Under the BNSS, in force since July 2024, police get two months to finish investigating penetrative and other sexual assault on a child [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. *What it hides:* cases registered late in the year may still be within that deadline, so not every open file is late. And the law sets no consequence for missing the deadline.

## Courts: convictions and the backlog

**32.3% convicted.** Trials ended in 12,672 convictions, 25,476 acquittals and 1,101 discharges [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The rate was up from 29.0% in 2023 [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. For penetrative assault alone it was 30.2% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *What it hides:* acquittals often follow children or families turning hostile, compromises, disputes over proof of age and cases arising from teenage relationships. A single rate cannot separate them.

**2,86,903 waiting.** At the end of 2024, 2,86,903 POCSO cases were pending trial, 87.7% of all POCSO cases before the courts that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]], up from 2,62,089 a year earlier [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. For penetrative assault alone, 1,70,455 cases were waiting [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *What it hides:* Section 35 of POCSO asks a Special Court to record the child's evidence within 30 days and to finish the trial within a year, as far as possible [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. With nearly nine in ten cases still pending at the end of the year, that promise is out of reach for most children.

Put together, the 2024 record sketches the road ahead for a family that files a POCSO complaint. When police close the investigation, they will almost certainly file a chargesheet. The trial may well outlast its one-year target. If it ends, the chance of a conviction is about one in three.

And every NCRB figure above starts at a police station. In the government's 2007 study, 72.1% of children who said they had been sexually assaulted had told no one [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. No table counts them.
pocso-2024-by-the-numbers.hg:
2024 mein India ki police ne Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act ke tahat 69,191 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Is ek number ke peeche kai aur numbers hain: bachche kaun the, accused kaun the, police ne kya kiya aur courts ne kya faisla diya. Yahan har zaroori number hai, zyadatar NCRB ki *Crime in India 2024* report se, aur saath mein yeh bhi ki uska matlab kya hai aur woh kya chhupa leta hai. Kidnapping se lekar child marriage tak, bachchon ke khilaaf saare crimes ki poori ginti hamare ek aur article mein hai.

## Cases aur rate: 69,191 cases, har ek lakh bachchon par 15.6

**69,191 cases, 70,132 bachche.** Yeh POCSO FIRs ki ginti hai, aur unmein darj bachchon ki [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *Yeh kya chhupata hai:* NCRB har FIR ko ek hi baar ginta hai, uske sabse serious offence ke naam par, jise "principal offence rule" kehte hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Agar kisi case mein isse bhaari saza wala crime bhi juda hai, jaise murder, to woh case us crime mein gina ja sakta hai.

**Har ek lakh bachchon par 15.6.** Yeh POCSO cases ka rate hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *Yeh kya chhupata hai:* yeh rate 2011 ki Census ki bachchon ki aabaadi par nikala gaya hai, yaani aabaadi ka woh number in crimes se 13 saal purana hai.

**53,874 se 69,191.** Cases 2021 mein 53,874 the, 2022 mein 63,414, 2023 mein 67,694 aur 2024 mein 69,191: teen saal mein lagbhag 28% ki badhat [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. *Yeh kya chhupata hai:* badhti ginti ka matlab zyada abuse bhi ho sakta hai, ya yeh ki zyada families report karne lagi aur police case register karne lagi. Data se pata nahi chalta ki asli wajah kaunsi hai.

**Bachchon ke khilaaf crimes ka 36.9%.** POCSO doosra sabse bada head tha; isse bada sirf kidnapping aur abduction tha, 40.0% ke saath [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**44,126 penetrative assaults.** POCSO ke alag-alag sections mein cases is tarah bante the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| POCSO sections | Offence | Cases |
|---|---|---|
| 4 aur 6 | Penetrative ya aggravated penetrative sexual assault | 44,126 (63.8%) |
| 8 aur 10 | Sexual assault ya aggravated sexual assault | 20,845 (30.1%) |
| 12 | Sexual harassment | 3,502 |
| 14 aur 15 | Bachche se sexual abuse material banwana ya use store karna | 500 |
| 17 se 22 | Uksaana, koshish, report na karna, jhoothi complaint | 218 |

## Victims: ladkiyan, ladke aur umar

**43,675 ladkiyan, 892 ladke.** Yeh penetrative assault ke shikaar 44,567 bachche the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *Yeh kya chhupata hai:* yahan ladke lagbhag 2% hain, jabki sarkar ki 2007 ki study mein sexual abuse report karne wale bachchon mein 52.94% ladke the [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Yeh gap is baare mein zyada batata hai ki kiska abuse report hota hai, is baare mein kam ki kiska abuse hota hai. Is par hamara ek alag article hai.

**6 saal se chhote 831.** Inhi 44,567 victims mein se 831 bachche 6 saal se chhote the aur 3,438 bachche 6 se 12 saal ke, yaani 12 se chhote kul 4,269. Phir 12 se 16 saal ke 16,801 the, aur 23,497 yaani 52.7%, 16 se 18 saal ke the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *Yeh kya chhupata hai:* bahut chhote bachche shayad hi kabhi bata paate hain, isliye 12 se chhote bachchon ki ginti ko kam se kam ginti samjhiye. 16 se 18 wala bada number kuch had tak teenage relationships aur ghar se bhaagne wale cases se aa sakta hai, jinhe NCRB alag se nahi ginta.

## Accused kaun the

**96.6% bachche ke jaan-pehchaan wale.** Penetrative assault ke 44,126 cases mein se 42,634 mein accused koi aisa tha jise bachcha jaanta tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**3,658, 16,668, 22,308 aur 1,492.** Yeh ginti is order mein hai: family members; family friends, padosi, employers ya koi aur jaan-pehchaan wala; friends, online friends ya "shaadi ke bahane" live-in partners; aur aakhir mein anjaan log ya jinki pehchaan nahi hui [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *Yeh kya chhupata hai:* yeh table sirf Section 4 aur 6 ki hai. Iske sabse bade column mein bachchon ko groom karne wale adults aur teenagers ke beech ke sexual rishte, dono mile hue hain. Agar dono mein se koi bhi 18 se kam hai, to POCSO aise rishte ko bhi offence maanta hai.

## Police: chargesheets aur khuli files

**95.3% mein chargesheet.** 2024 mein police ne POCSO ke jin cases ko dispose kiya, unmein se 95.3% mein chargesheet file ki [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *Yeh kya chhupata hai:* yeh rate chargesheets ko dispose kiye gaye cases se divide karke nikalta hai. Saboot kitne strong the, iske baare mein yeh kuch nahi batata.
