**21,256 ab bhi khuli.** Saal ke end mein POCSO ke 21,256 cases ki investigation chal hi rahi thi: un 89,658 cases ka 23.7% jinki jaanch police ko karni thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. July 2024 se laagu BNSS ke tahat police ko bachche par penetrative aur doosre sexual assault ki investigation do mahine mein poori karni hoti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. *Yeh kya chhupata hai:* saal ke aakhri mahinon mein register hue cases ho sakta hai abhi deadline ke andar hon, isliye har khuli file late nahi hai. Aur deadline miss karne par kanoon mein koi consequence tay nahi hai.

## Courts: saza aur atke hue cases

**32.3% mein saza.** Trials ka nateeja raha 12,672 convictions, 25,476 acquittals aur 1,101 discharges [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 2023 mein yeh rate 29.0% tha [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. Sirf penetrative assault ke cases mein yeh 30.2% raha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *Yeh kya chhupata hai:* kai cases mein accused isliye bari hote hain kyunki bachcha ya family apne bayaan se palat jaati hai, compromise ho jaata hai, umar ke saboot par jhagda hota hai, ya case teenagers ke rishte se nikla hota hai. Ek akela rate in sabko alag nahi kar sakta.

**2,86,903 intezaar mein.** 2024 ke end mein POCSO ke 2,86,903 cases trial ke intezaar mein the, us saal courts ke saamne rahe saare POCSO cases ka 87.7% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Ek saal pehle yeh number 2,62,089 tha [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. Sirf penetrative assault ke 1,70,455 cases atke the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *Yeh kya chhupata hai:* POCSO ka Section 35 kehta hai ki Special Court bachche ka bayaan 30 din mein record kare aur jahan tak ho sake, ek saal mein trial khatam kare [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Jab saal ke end mein lagbhag 10 mein se 9 cases atke hon, to zyadatar bachchon ke liye yeh waada poora hona mushkil hai.

Sab milake, 2024 ka record us family ke aage ka raasta dikhata hai jo POCSO complaint karti hai. Police investigation poori karegi to lagbhag pakka chargesheet file karegi. Trial ek saal ke target se aage khinch sakta hai. Aur trial khatam ho bhi jaaye, to saza hone ka chance lagbhag teen mein ek hai.

Aur upar NCRB ka har number police station se shuru hota hai. Sarkar ki 2007 ki study mein jin bachchon ne kaha ki unke saath sexual assault hua, unmein se 72.1% ne kisi ko nahi bataya tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Un bachchon ko koi table nahi ginti.

pocso-acquittals-reverse-burden-paradox.en:
Indian criminal law usually makes the prosecution prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt. POCSO turns that around. Section 29 tells a Special Court to presume that a person prosecuted for sexually assaulting a child committed the offence, unless the contrary is proved [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Yet in 2024, courts acquitted the accused in 25,476 POCSO cases and convicted in 12,672, with 1,101 more discharged: a conviction rate of 32.3% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Two acquittals for every conviction. This investigation follows a case from the police station to the verdict to find where it breaks. It is general information, not legal advice.

## A law that presumes guilt, and a two-to-one acquittal rate

The presumption covers the core offences: penetrative and non-penetrative sexual assault, and their aggravated forms [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. But it only tilts the scales once a case is standing in court. It cannot replace a child's account once it is withdrawn, prove an age when the documents are disputed, or make up for a weak investigation. When those fail, the presumption has nothing to rest on.

The rate has edged up. In 2023, courts convicted in 29.0% of POCSO trials, with 11,087 convictions against 25,803 acquittals [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. For penetrative sexual assault alone (Sections 4 and 6), the 2024 rate was 30.2% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

An acquittal is not a finding that a child lied. It means the case was not proved. NCRB does not record why a trial failed, which is itself part of the problem.

## From 95.3% chargesheeted to 32.3% convicted

Police filed chargesheets in 95.3% of the POCSO cases they disposed of in 2024, while 21,256 were still under investigation at the end of the year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That looks like a strong pipeline. It is not the same as strong evidence: a chargesheet says a case is ready for trial, not that it will survive one.

The two rates also describe different cases. The vast majority of the 2024 convictions came in cases carried over from earlier years [[ncrb-cii-2024]], and the queue behind them is long: 2,86,903 POCSO cases were pending trial at the end of 2024, 87.7% of all POCSO cases before the courts that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. POCSO asks courts to record a child's evidence within 30 days and to finish the trial within a year where possible [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. But the queue is growing: a year earlier, at the end of 2023, it stood at 2,62,089 [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. While the backlog keeps growing, the one-year promise is the exception, and the waiting years are where cases leak.

## Hostile witnesses: when the accused is family

In 96.6% of the POCSO penetrative-assault cases registered in 2024, the accused was someone the child knew [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In 3,658 cases it was a family member; in 16,668, a family friend, neighbour, employer or other known person [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Consider this situation. A 12-year-old in Kanpur tells her teacher about her father. An FIR is filed, he is arrested, and the household loses its main income. Over the next two years, relatives tell her mother the family will be ruined and that a "settlement" can still be arranged. When the girl finally reaches the witness box, she says she does not remember. The prosecution declares her hostile, and the presumption has nothing left to stand on.

NCRB cannot say how many acquittals follow this path. But acquittals often follow a child or family turning hostile, and the structure explains why: the child must testify against someone the child depends on. The Supreme Court ruled in 2021 that judges must never suggest compromise or marriage in sexual-offence cases [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. Nothing in that ruling reaches the pressure applied at home.

## Age proof, delay and the teenage-relationship cases

POCSO protects everyone under 18 [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], so many trials turn on a document. If the court doubts the school certificate or the birth record, the POCSO charge can fall even when little else is disputed. Delay compounds the problem: a 16-year-old who filed a complaint may be an adult, married or living elsewhere by the time she is called to testify.

The largest group of accused complicates the picture. In 2024, 22,308 of 44,126 penetrative-assault cases (50.6%) fell in one NCRB column, friends, online friends or live-in partners "on pretext of marriage", and 23,497 child victims (52.7%) were aged 16 to 18 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. This group mixes adults who groom children with relationships between teenagers, some of them cases that follow an elopement. Under 18, consent has no legal effect. But when she tells the court the relationship was her choice and will not testify against the boy, such cases often end in acquittal.

NCRB does not separate these cases. So nobody can say how often courts convict adults who prey on children, the number that matters most.

## What raises convictions without convicting the innocent

Lowering the standard of proof is not the answer; the presumption already tilts the trial. What fails is everything around the courtroom.

- **Record the child's evidence fast.** The 30-day rule is already in Section 35 [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Every month of delay is a month of pressure.
- **Make the courtroom bearable.** Questions go through the judge, the child must not see the accused while testifying, and the hearing is held in camera with a trusted adult present [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. These rules matter most for a child testifying against a parent.
- **Cut the family's dependence on the accused.** Every state must run a victim compensation scheme, and compensation is available even when a trial ends in acquittal [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Investigate as if there were no presumption.** Collect age documents on day one and preserve medical and digital evidence. That protects the child and an innocent accused alike.
- **Count honestly.** Separate teenage-relationship cases, and record why trials end in acquittal.

The presumption is POCSO's strongest tool. It works only if the child's account survives long enough to reach a verdict.
pocso-acquittals-reverse-burden-paradox.hg:
Indian criminal law mein aam taur pe prosecution ko guilt reasonable doubt se pare saabit karna hota hai. POCSO ise ulat deta hai. Section 29 Special Court se kehta hai ki jis insaan pe bachche ke sexual assault ka case chal raha hai, maan kar chalo ki offence usi ne kiya hai, jab tak ulta saabit na ho [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Phir bhi 2024 mein courts ne 25,476 POCSO cases mein accused ko acquit kiya aur 12,672 mein convict kiya, aur 1,101 aur cases mein accused discharge hue: conviction rate 32.3% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Har conviction ke saamne do acquittals. Yeh investigation ek case ko police station se verdict tak follow karti hai, yeh dhoondhne ke liye ki woh kahan tootta hai. Yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahi.

## Guilt maanne wala kanoon, aur do-ek ka acquittal rate

Yeh presumption core offences pe lagta hai: penetrative aur non-penetrative sexual assault, aur unke aggravated roop [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Lekin yeh tarazu tabhi jhukata hai jab case court mein khada ho. Bachche ka bayaan wapas le liya jaaye to yeh uski jagah nahi le sakta, documents pe vivaad ho to umar saabit nahi kar sakta, aur kamzor investigation ki bharpaai nahi kar sakta. Jab yeh cheezein fail hoti hain, to presumption ke paas tikne ko kuch nahi bachta.

Rate thoda upar aaya hai. 2023 mein courts ne 29.0% POCSO trials mein conviction diya tha, 11,087 convictions ke saamne 25,803 acquittals [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. Sirf penetrative sexual assault (Section 4 aur 6) mein 2024 ka rate 30.2% tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Acquittal ka matlab yeh faisla nahi hai ki bachche ne jhooth bola. Iska matlab hai ki case saabit nahi hua. NCRB yeh record hi nahi karta ki trial kyun fail hua, aur yeh khud problem ka hissa hai.

## 95.3% chargesheet se 32.3% conviction tak

2024 mein police ne jin POCSO cases ko dispose kiya, unmein se 95.3% mein chargesheet file ki, jabki saal ke end mein 21,256 cases ki investigation ab bhi chal rahi thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh ek mazboot pipeline lagti hai. Lekin yeh mazboot evidence ke barabar nahi hai: chargesheet ka matlab hai ki case trial ke liye taiyaar hai, yeh nahi ki woh trial jhel paayega.

Dono rates alag-alag cases ke baare mein bhi hain. 2024 ke convictions ka bahut bada hissa pichhle saalon se chale aa rahe cases mein aaya [[ncrb-cii-2024]], aur unke peeche line lambi hai: 2024 ke end mein 2,86,903 POCSO cases trial ka intezaar kar rahe the, yaani us saal courts ke saamne aaye saare POCSO cases ka 87.7% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. POCSO courts se kehta hai ki bachche ka bayaan 30 din mein record ho aur trial jahan tak ho sake ek saal mein poora ho [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Lekin line badh rahi hai: ek saal pehle, 2023 ke end mein, yeh 2,62,089 thi [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. Jab tak backlog badhta rahega, ek saal wala waada exception ban jaata hai, aur intezaar ke yahi saal hain jahan cases haath se nikalne lagte hain.

## Hostile witnesses: jab accused family ka ho

2024 mein register hue POCSO penetrative assault cases mein se 96.6% mein accused koi aisa tha jise bachcha jaanta tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 3,658 cases mein woh family member tha; 16,668 mein family friend, padosi, employer ya koi aur jaan-pehchaan wala [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Ek situation sochiye. Kanpur ki ek 12 saal ki ladki apni teacher ko apne papa ke baare mein batati hai. FIR hoti hai, papa arrest hote hain, aur ghar ki main kamaai band ho jaati hai. Agle do saal rishtedaar uski maa se kehte rehte hain ki family barbaad ho jayegi, aur "settlement" ab bhi ho sakta hai. Jab ladki aakhir witness box tak pahunchti hai, to kehti hai ki use yaad nahi. Prosecution use hostile declare kar deta hai, aur presumption ke paas tikne ko kuch nahi bachta.

NCRB nahi bata sakta ki kitne acquittals isi raaste se aate hain. Lekin acquittals aksar tab hote hain jab bachcha ya family hostile ho jaaye, aur iski wajah structure mein hai: bachche ko unhi logon ke khilaaf gawahi deni padti hai jin par woh nirbhar hai. Supreme Court ne 2021 mein kaha ki judges sexual offence cases mein kabhi compromise ya shaadi ka sujhav nahi de sakte [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. Par woh faisla ghar ke andar daale jaane wale pressure tak nahi pahunchta.

## Umar ka saboot, deri aur teenage relationship wale cases

POCSO 18 se kam umar ke har insaan ko protect karta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], isliye kai trials ek document pe tik jaate hain. Agar court ko school certificate ya birth record pe shak ho, to POCSO ka charge gir sakta hai, chahe baaki baaton pe zyada vivaad na ho. Deri is problem ko aur badhati hai: complaint karne wali 16 saal ki ladki, gawahi ke liye bulaye jaane tak, adult ho chuki ho sakti hai, shaadishuda ya kahin aur rehne wali.

Accused ka sabse bada group tasveer ko aur uljha deta hai. 2024 mein 44,126 penetrative assault cases mein se 22,308 (50.6%) NCRB ke ek hi column mein the, yaani friends, online friends ya "on pretext of marriage" (shaadi ke bahane) live-in partners, aur 23,497 child victims (52.7%) 16 se 18 saal ke the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Is group mein bachchon ko groom karne wale adults bhi hain aur teenagers ke beech ke relationships bhi, jinmein se kuch cases couple ke ghar se bhaag jaane ke baad bante hain. 18 se kam umar mein consent ka koi legal matlab nahi hai. Lekin jab ladki court mein kehti hai ki relationship uski marzi se tha aur ladke ke khilaaf gawahi nahi deti, to aise cases aksar acquittal pe khatam hote hain.

NCRB in cases ko alag nahi karta. Isliye koi nahi bata sakta ki bachchon ka shikaar karne wale adults ko courts kitni baar convict karte hain, jabki sabse zaroori number wahi hai.

## Begunah ko saza diye bina convictions kaise badhein

Saboot ka standard neeche karna jawab nahi hai; presumption pehle se trial ko ek taraf jhukata hai. Fail hota hai courtroom ke aas-paas ka sab kuch.

- **Bachche ka bayaan jaldi record ho.** 30 din ka rule Section 35 mein pehle se hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Deri ka har mahina pressure ka ek aur mahina hai.
- **Courtroom ko sehne layak banaaiye.** Sawaal judge ke zariye jaate hain, gawahi dete waqt bachche ko accused nazar nahi aana chahiye, aur sunwaai in camera ek trusted adult ki maujoodgi mein hoti hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Yeh rules sabse zyada us bachche ke liye maayne rakhte hain jo maa ya baap ke khilaaf gawahi de raha hai.
- **Family ki accused pe nirbharta khatam kijiye.** Har state ko victim compensation scheme chalani hoti hai, aur trial acquittal pe khatam ho tab bhi compensation mil sakta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Aise investigate kijiye jaise presumption ho hi nahi.** Umar ke documents pehle hi din jama kijiye, medical aur digital evidence surakshit rakhiye. Isse bachcha bhi bachta hai aur begunah accused bhi.
- **Imaandari se giniye.** Teenage relationship wale cases alag kijiye, aur record kijiye ki trials acquittal pe kyun khatam hote hain.

Presumption POCSO ka sabse mazboot hathiyaar hai. Yeh tabhi kaam karta hai jab bachche ka bayaan verdict tak tik paaye.

pocso-act-explained-plain-words.en:
In 2024 police in India registered 69,191 cases under a single law, the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, involving 70,132 children [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Many parents have heard the word POCSO. Few have read what it says. Here is the Act in plain words, part by part, set against what happened to those cases. It is general information, not legal advice.

## Who is a child: everyone under 18, boys included

POCSO came into force on 14 November 2012. It defines a child as any person below 18, and protects boys and girls alike [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. The definition says any person, not any girl, so a child of any gender is covered.

Age is the whole test. A 17-year-old is a child in law, and the law does not ask whether the child agreed. A sexual act with a 17-year-old is an offence even if the child said yes. Other Indian laws draw their lines at other ages, which we map in a separate explainer.

The records show how rarely boys reach the system. Of 44,567 children recorded as victims of penetrative sexual assault in 2024, 892 were boys [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That does not mean boys are safe; it reflects how rarely their abuse is reported.

## The offences: touch, penetration, harassment and abuse material

The Act sorts abuse into groups, each with its own punishment section. In 2024 the police caseload looked like this [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| Offence | Sections | Cases in 2024 |
|---|---|---|
| Penetrative and aggravated penetrative sexual assault | 4 and 6 | 44,126 |
| Sexual assault (contact without penetration) and its aggravated form | 8 and 10 | 20,845 |
| Sexual harassment | 12 | 3,502 |
| Using a child for, or storing, sexual abuse material | 14 and 15 | 500 |
| Abetment, attempt, failure to report, false complaints | 17 to 22 | 218 |

"Aggravated" means circumstances the law treats as worse, and the Act lists them one by one. Sexual harassment covers conduct with sexual intent that need not involve any touch.

Two Supreme Court rulings sharpened these definitions. In January 2021 the Bombay High Court held that touching a child over her clothes was not sexual assault because there was no skin-to-skin contact. On 18 November 2021 the Supreme Court set that aside: "the important ingredient for constituting the offence of sexual assault under POCSO is sexual intent and not skin to skin contact with the child" [[barandbench-satish-2021]]. In September 2024 it held that storing or possessing child sexual abuse material, when the circumstances show the intent the law describes, is an offence under Section 15 even if it is never shared. It also told courts to stop calling it "child pornography" [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]].

## Punishments after the 2019 amendment

An amendment in force from 16 August 2019 made the sentences much harsher [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]:

- penetrative sexual assault: at least 10 years, up from 7;
- penetrative sexual assault on a child under 16: at least 20 years;
- aggravated penetrative sexual assault: at least 20 years' rigorous imprisonment, up to imprisonment for the rest of natural life, or death.

Harsher sentences sit alongside one stubborn fact. In 96.6% of the penetrative assault cases registered in 2024, the accused was someone the child knew [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. So the person a family must report is usually someone it knows, an uncle, a neighbour, a tutor or a "friend", who if convicted faces at least 10 or 20 years. Whether that makes families more willing to come forward or less, the police data cannot show.

## Rules that protect the child: reverse burden, secrecy, special courts

**The burden shifts.** In most crimes the prosecution must prove guilt. Under Section 29, when a person is prosecuted for penetrative or sexual assault on a child, the Special Court must presume he committed the offence "unless the contrary is proved" [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. That is not a verdict in advance; the accused can rebut it. Yet courts convicted in only 32.3% of POCSO trials completed in 2024: 12,672 convictions against 25,476 acquittals [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**The child stays anonymous.** Section 23 bars any media report from revealing a child victim's name, address, photograph, family details, school or neighbourhood, unless the Special Court allows it in the child's interest. Breaking the rule can bring 6 months to 1 year in prison, a fine, or both, and the publisher or owner is jointly liable [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. In 2018 the Supreme Court added that FIRs in POCSO cases must not be put in the public domain [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

**Silence is an offence.** Under Sections 19 and 21, anyone who knows of child sexual abuse must report it. Not reporting can mean up to 6 months in prison or a fine, and up to 1 year and a fine for the head of an institution who fails to report abuse by someone working under them [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. A child who stays silent cannot be punished for it.

**A special court, on a clock.** Every district must have a designated Special Court. It must record the child's evidence within 30 days of taking up the case and finish the trial, as far as possible, within one year [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. The trial is held in camera, before a woman judge where practicable [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## What a law cannot do on its own

The clock has not held. At the end of 2024, 2,86,903 POCSO cases were waiting for trial, 87.7% of all POCSO cases before the courts that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. By November 2026 the government counted 779 fast-track special courts, 399 of them only for POCSO cases [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. For most children, the one-year trial is a promise on paper.

The Act is strong in its text. It still depends on people: an adult who believes the child, an officer who registers the FIR without delay, a doctor who examines without judgement, and a court that keeps its own deadlines. Every case in the table above began with someone who refused to stay silent. The law can punish. Only adults who act can make it protect.
pocso-act-explained-plain-words.hg:
2024 mein India mein police ne sirf ek kanoon ke under 69,191 case register kiye, aur in cases mein 70,132 bachche victim ke taur par record hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh kanoon hai Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, yaani POCSO. Bahut se parents ne POCSO ka naam suna hai. Bahut kam logon ne padha hai ki ismein likha kya hai. Yahan hum is Act ko part by part, simple words mein samjha rahe hain, aur saath mein yeh bhi ki un cases ka hua kya. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Bachcha kaun hai: 18 se kam umar ka har insaan, ladke bhi

POCSO 14 November 2012 se lagu hai. Ismein "child" ka matlab hai 18 saal se kam umar ka koi bhi insaan, aur yeh ladkon aur ladkiyon ko barabar protect karta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Definition "koi bhi insaan" kehti hai, "koi bhi ladki" nahi, isliye kisi bhi gender ka bachcha is kanoon ke daayre mein aata hai.

Yahan umar hi sab kuch hai. 17 saal ka teenager bhi kanoon ki nazar mein bachcha hai, aur kanoon yeh poochhta hi nahi ki bachche ne haan kaha tha ya nahi. 17 saal ke bachche ke saath sexual act offence hai, chahe usne haan hi kyun na kaha ho. Baaki Indian kanoon alag-alag umar par line kheenchte hain; un sabko humne ek alag explainer mein map kiya hai.

Records dikhate hain ki ladkon ke case system tak kitni kam baar pahunchte hain. 2024 mein penetrative sexual assault ke 44,567 child victims record hue, jinmein sirf 892 ladke the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Iska matlab yeh nahi ki ladke safe hain; yeh is baat ki jhalak hai ki ladkon ke saath hue abuse ki report kitni kam hoti hai.

## Offences kaun se hain: touch, penetration, harassment aur abuse material

Act abuse ko alag-alag groups mein baant-ta hai, aur har group ka apna punishment section hai. 2024 mein police ke paas aaye cases kuch aise the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| Offence | Sections | 2024 mein case |
|---|---|---|
| Penetrative aur aggravated penetrative sexual assault | 4 aur 6 | 44,126 |
| Sexual assault (bina penetration ke, sexual intent se touch) aur uska aggravated form | 8 aur 10 | 20,845 |
| Sexual harassment | 12 | 3,502 |
| Bachche se sexual abuse material banwana, ya use store karna | 14 aur 15 | 500 |
| Abetment, attempt, report na karna, jhoothi complaint | 17 se 22 | 218 |

"Aggravated" ka matlab hai woh situations jinhe kanoon zyada serious maanta hai, aur Act mein yeh ek-ek karke likhi hain. Sexual harassment mein woh harkatein aati hain jo sexual intent se ki jaayein, bhale hi unmein koi touch na ho.

Supreme Court ke do faislon ne yeh definitions aur clear kar di. January 2021 mein Bombay High Court ne kaha tha ki kapdon ke upar se bachchi ko touch karna sexual assault nahi hai, kyunki "skin-to-skin contact" nahi hua. 18 November 2021 ko Supreme Court ne yeh faisla palat diya: "the important ingredient for constituting the offence of sexual assault under POCSO is sexual intent and not skin to skin contact with the child" [[barandbench-satish-2021]]. Yaani asli test sexual intent hai, skin contact nahi. September 2024 mein court ne kaha ki child sexual abuse material ko store ya possess karna bhi Section 15 ke under offence hai, agar halaat se woh intent dikhe jo kanoon mein likha hai, bhale hi woh kabhi kisi ko share na kiya gaya ho. Court ne yeh bhi kaha ki courts ise "child pornography" bolna band karein [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]].

## 2019 amendment ke baad saza

16 August 2019 se lagu ek amendment ne sazayein kaafi sakht kar di [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]:

- penetrative sexual assault: kam se kam 10 saal, pehle yeh 7 saal thi;
- 16 saal se kam umar ke bachche par penetrative sexual assault: kam se kam 20 saal;
- aggravated penetrative sexual assault: kam se kam 20 saal ki rigorous imprisonment, jo baaki poori zindagi ki jail tak ja sakti hai, ya phir death penalty.

Lekin sakht sazaon ke saath ek sach waisa ka waisa khada hai. 2024 mein register hue penetrative assault ke 96.6% cases mein accused koi aisa tha jise bachcha pehle se jaanta tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yaani family ko aksar kisi jaan-pehchaan wale ki report karni padti hai, jaise chacha, padosi, tuition wale sir ya koi "friend", jise conviction hone par kam se kam 10 ya 20 saal ki saza ho sakti hai. Isse families ke liye aage aana aasaan hota hai ya mushkil, yeh police data nahi bata sakta.

## Bachche ko bachane wale rules: ulta burden, pehchaan chhupana, Special Court

**Burden ulta hai.** Zyadatar crimes mein guilt prove karna prosecution ka kaam hota hai. Lekin Section 29 kehta hai ki agar kisi par bachche ke saath penetrative ya sexual assault ka case chal raha hai, toh Special Court yeh maan kar chalegi ki offence usi ne kiya hai, "unless the contrary is proved", yaani jab tak woh ulta prove na kar de [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Yeh pehle se sunaya gaya verdict nahi hai; accused ise rebut kar sakta hai. Phir bhi 2024 mein jin POCSO trials ka faisla aaya, unmein se sirf 32.3% mein conviction hua: 12,672 convictions aur 25,476 acquittals [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**Bachche ki pehchaan chhupi rahegi.** Section 23 ke hisaab se koi bhi media report victim bachche ka naam, address, photo, family details, school ya mohalla nahi bata sakti. Chhoot sirf tab hai jab Special Court bachche ke interest mein permission de. Rule todne par 6 mahine se 1 saal tak ki jail, fine, ya dono ho sakte hain, aur publisher ya owner bhi barabar ka zimmedar hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. 2018 mein Supreme Court ne yeh bhi kaha ki POCSO cases ki FIR public domain mein nahi daali jaayegi [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

**Chup rehna bhi crime hai.** Section 19 aur 21 ke hisaab se jise bhi child sexual abuse ke baare mein pata hai, use report karna hi hoga. Report na karne par 6 mahine tak ki jail ya fine ho sakta hai. Kisi institution ka head agar apne neeche kaam karne wale ke kiye abuse ko report nahi karta, toh use 1 saal tak ki jail aur fine ho sakta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Haan, agar koi bachcha chup reh jaaye, toh use iski saza nahi di ja sakti.

**Special Court, time limit ke saath.** Har district mein ek designated Special Court honi chahiye. Case lene ke 30 din ke andar use bachche ka statement record karna hota hai, aur jahan tak ho sake, ek saal mein trial khatam karna hota hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Trial in camera, yaani band kamre mein hota hai, aur jahan possible ho, woman judge ke saamne [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Kanoon akele kya nahi kar sakta

Yeh time limit nibhai nahi gayi. 2024 ke end mein POCSO ke 2,86,903 case trial ka wait kar rahe the, yaani us saal court ke saamne jitne POCSO case the unmein se 87.7% atke rahe [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. November 2026 tak sarkar ke hisaab se 779 fast-track special courts chal rahi thi, jinmein se 399 sirf POCSO cases ke liye thi [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. Zyadatar bachchon ke liye ek saal mein trial ka vaada sirf kaagaz par hai.

Act ke words mazboot hain. Lekin yeh kanoon logon ke bharose chalta hai: ek adult jo bachche ki baat par yakeen kare, ek police officer jo bina der kiye FIR likhe, ek doctor jo bachche ko sharminda kiye bina examine kare, aur ek court jo apni hi deadlines maane. Upar ki table ka har case kisi aise insaan se shuru hua jisne chup rehne se inkaar kiya. Kanoon saza de sakta hai. Bachche ko asal mein wahi adults bachate hain jo aage badh kar kuch karte hain.

pocso-quiet-states-bihar-uttar-pradesh.en:
Read India's child sexual abuse map one way and Bihar looks like a remarkably safe place to be a child. In 2024 its police registered 5.2 cases under the POCSO Act for every lakh children, a third of the national rate of 15.6. Uttar Pradesh registered 9.5. Kerala registered 48.0, more than nine times Bihar's rate [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Nothing in the data says a child in Bihar is nine times safer than a child in Kerala. Read with the rest of the evidence, the quiet in the north looks less like safety and more like silence.

## 9.5 and 5.2: the quiet states

The 2024 POCSO rates, in cases per lakh children [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| State | Cases per lakh children |
|---|---|
| Kerala | 48.0 |
| Tamil Nadu | 33.7 |
| India | 15.6 |
| Uttar Pradesh | 9.5 |
| Bihar | 5.2 |

Counts tell a different story. Maharashtra registered the most POCSO cases in 2024, 9,432, followed by Uttar Pradesh with 8,087, Tamil Nadu with 6,969 and Madhya Pradesh with 5,861. Kerala, fifth with 4,513, tops the table only when cases are measured against its child population [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Per child, Uttar Pradesh registers well below the national rate.

Remember what the table measures. A case appears only when someone tells the police and the police write an FIR. Each FIR is counted once, under its most serious offence [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The rates divide by each state's child population in the 2011 Census, which may differ substantially from today's.

## What the quiet hides

Other sources describe a very different Bihar. In the National Family Health Survey of 2023-24, Bihar had the highest share of any state surveyed of ever-married women reporting violence by their husbands, 36.1% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Yet its police registered cruelty by husbands or relatives at 3.0 cases per lakh women in 2024, against 52.8 in Telangana [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Most of what women tell surveyors in Bihar never reaches its police stations.

The same survey found that 34.6% of Bihar's women aged 20 to 24 had been married before 18, the second-highest share in India [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. In law, sex with a wife under 18 is rape [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. Where about a third of young women were married as children, a rate of 5.2 per lakh children measures what reaches the police, not what happens.

Uttar Pradesh shows the same pattern across crimes. It registered more crimes against women than any other state in 2024, 66,398, yet its rate of 58.0 per lakh women was below the national 64.6 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The Muzaffarpur shelter home case shows how abuse can stay out of the count. Abuse at a state-funded girls' shelter home in Muzaffarpur was flagged by a social audit of children's homes that the Tata Institute of Social Sciences did for the state government, submitted in April 2018 [[newslaundry-tiss-audit-bihar-2018]]. In January 2020 a POCSO court in Delhi convicted 19 of the 20 accused [[scconline-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]]. Children living in an institution cannot simply walk into a police station. Someone from outside had to go in and ask.

Silence is the norm, not the exception. In the government's 2007 Study on Child Abuse, 72.1% of children who had been sexually assaulted had told no one, and only 3.4% had gone to the police [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. India has not run a national survey of child sexual abuse since, a gap we examine in a separate investigation.

## Kerala and Tamil Nadu: more abuse, or more reporting?

NCRB itself warns against reading its tables as a safety ranking. More crime registered in a place "is not an indicator of its being comparatively unsafe", it says, and "'Rise in crime' and 'increase in registration of crime by police' are clearly two different things" [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]].

What police write down varies widely from state to state, and from law to law. Kerala's police registered 496 of the 616 cases filed in all of India in 2024 under the Domestic Violence Act [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In figures cited by the Supreme Court in 2024, Tamil Nadu had filed 2,392 FIRs on 8,966 child marriage cases over three years, while Telangana filed 149 on 4,440 [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. Yet Tamil Nadu registered cruelty by husbands or relatives at just 2.2 cases per lakh women in 2024, below even Bihar's 3.0 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. No state writes everything down. None of this proves that Kerala or Tamil Nadu has more abuse, or less. It shows that a high POCSO rate can reflect stronger reporting and registration, not only more abuse.

## 19 metros, 7,508 cases: the city picture

NCRB's 19 metropolitan cities registered 7,508 POCSO cases with girl victims in 2024. Delhi (1,489) and Mumbai (1,331) alone made up 37.6%, followed by Bengaluru (588), Pune (575) and Chennai (437) [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Nationally, police registered 67,809 POCSO cases with girl victims [[ncrb-cii-2024]], so about eight in nine came from outside these metros, from smaller cities, towns and villages. City rates rest on 2011 populations too, and NCRB says they cannot be compared with state rates [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Registered child abuse is mostly not a big-city story.

## Questions to ask of your own state's numbers

A low number is a question, not an answer. Before you read your state's POCSO figure as good news, ask four things.

- **Is it a count or a rate?** A big state can top the count table and still register few cases per child.
- **Did registration get easier?** Bihar's registered crimes against women rose 19.2% in a single year, from 2023 to 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB says rises can follow citizen-friendly steps such as e-FIR facilities or women's help desks [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. A rising POCSO rate in a quiet state may be the first sign that children are being heard.
- **What do surveys say about the same state?** Child marriage and violence at home are measured outside police records.
- **Can a family report without a fight?** Since July 2024, police must record a complaint whatever the place of the crime, a "zero FIR", and may receive it electronically [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Kerala's 48.0 is not a scandal to hide. Bihar's 5.2 is not a record to celebrate. The number that should worry us is the one nobody has written down.
pocso-quiet-states-bihar-uttar-pradesh.hg:
India ke child sexual abuse map ko ek tarah se padhein, toh lagega ki Bihar bachchon ke liye kaafi safe jagah hai. 2024 mein wahan ki police ne har ek lakh bachchon par POCSO Act ke sirf 5.2 case register kiye, jo poore desh ke rate 15.6 ka ek-tihaai hai. Uttar Pradesh mein yeh rate 9.5 tha. Kerala mein 48.0, yaani Bihar se nau guna se bhi zyada [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Lekin data mein kahin nahi likha ki Bihar ka bachcha Kerala ke bachche se nau guna zyada safe hai. Baaki evidence ke saath padhein, toh North India ki yeh shanti safety kam aur silence zyada lagti hai.

## 9.5 aur 5.2: chup rehne wale states

2024 mein POCSO case ka rate, har ek lakh bachchon par [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| State | Har lakh bachchon par case |
|---|---|
| Kerala | 48.0 |
| Tamil Nadu | 33.7 |
| Poora India | 15.6 |
| Uttar Pradesh | 9.5 |
| Bihar | 5.2 |

Total count alag kahani batata hai. 2024 mein sabse zyada POCSO case Maharashtra mein register hue, 9,432, uske baad Uttar Pradesh mein 8,087, Tamil Nadu mein 6,969 aur Madhya Pradesh mein 5,861. Kerala 4,513 case ke saath paanchve number par hai, aur pehle number par tabhi aata hai jab case ko bachchon ki aabadi ke hisaab se dekha jaaye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Har bachche ke hisaab se dekhein, toh Uttar Pradesh ka rate national rate se kaafi neeche hai.

Yaad rakhiye ki yeh table asal mein kya ginti hai. Koi case ismein tabhi aata hai jab koi police ko bataye aur police FIR likhe. Har FIR sirf ek baar gini jaati hai, usmein likhe sabse serious offence ke naam par [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Rate nikaalne ke liye har state ke bachchon ki 2011 Census wali aabadi li jaati hai, jo aaj ki aabadi se kaafi alag ho sakti hai.

## Yeh chuppi kya chhupaati hai

Doosre sources Bihar ki bilkul alag tasveer dikhate hain. 2023-24 ke National Family Health Survey mein, pati ki violence report karne wali ever-married auraton ka share Bihar mein survey hue sabhi states mein sabse zyada tha, 36.1% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Phir bhi 2024 mein wahan ki police ne pati ya sasural walon ki cruelty ke case har lakh auraton par sirf 3.0 register kiye, jabki Telangana mein yahi rate 52.8 tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Bihar ki auratein survey mein jo batati hain, uska zyadatar hissa kabhi police station tak nahi pahunchta.

Usi survey ke hisaab se Bihar mein 20 se 24 saal ki 34.6% auraton ki shaadi 18 se pehle ho gayi thi, jo desh mein doosra sabse ooncha share hai [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Kanoon mein 18 se kam umar ki wife ke saath sex rape hai [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. Jahan lagbhag ek-tihaai young auraton ki shaadi bachpan mein hui ho, wahan har lakh bachchon par 5.2 case ka rate bas yeh batata hai ki police tak kya pahuncha, yeh nahi ki asal mein kya hua.

Uttar Pradesh mein bhi alag-alag crimes mein yahi pattern dikhta hai. 2024 mein wahan auraton ke against crime ke sabse zyada case register hue, 66,398, phir bhi wahan ka rate, har lakh auraton par 58.0, national rate 64.6 se kam tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Muzaffarpur shelter home case dikhata hai ki abuse ginti se bahar kaise reh sakta hai. Muzaffarpur mein sarkari paise se chalne wale ladkiyon ke ek shelter home mein sexual abuse ki baat ek social audit mein saamne aayi, jo Tata Institute of Social Sciences ne state government ke liye kiya tha aur April 2018 mein submit kiya tha [[newslaundry-tiss-audit-bihar-2018]]. January 2020 mein Delhi ki ek POCSO court ne 20 mein se 19 accused ko convict kiya [[scconline-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]]. Kisi institution mein rehne wale bachche yun hi uth kar police station nahi ja sakte. Kisi bahar wale ko andar jaakar poochhna pada.

Chup rehna yahan normal hai, exception nahi. Sarkar ki 2007 ki Study on Child Abuse mein, jin bachchon ke saath sexual assault hua tha, unmein se 72.1% ne kisi ko kuch nahi bataya tha, aur sirf 3.4% police tak gaye the [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Uske baad India ne child sexual abuse par koi national survey nahi karaya; is gap par humne ek alag investigation kiya hai.

## Kerala aur Tamil Nadu: abuse zyada, ya reporting zyada?

NCRB khud kehta hai ki uski tables ko safety ranking ki tarah na padha jaaye. Uske hisaab se kisi jagah zyada crime register hona "is not an indicator of its being comparatively unsafe", aur "'Rise in crime' and 'increase in registration of crime by police' are clearly two different things" [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. Yaani crime badhna aur police ka zyada crime register karna do alag baatein hain.

Police kya likhti hai, yeh har state mein, aur har kanoon ke hisaab se, bahut alag hai. 2024 mein poore India mein Domestic Violence Act ke under 616 case register hue, jinmein se 496 akele Kerala ki police ne register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Supreme Court ne 2024 mein jo data quote kiya, uske hisaab se teen saal mein Tamil Nadu ne child marriage ke 8,966 cases par 2,392 FIR file ki, jabki Telangana ne 4,440 par sirf 149 [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. Lekin 2024 mein Tamil Nadu ne pati ya sasural walon ki cruelty ke case har lakh auraton par sirf 2.2 register kiye, jo Bihar ke 3.0 se bhi kam hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Koi bhi state sab kuch nahi likhta. Isse yeh prove nahi hota ki Kerala ya Tamil Nadu mein abuse zyada hai ya kam. Isse bas itna dikhta hai ki POCSO ka ooncha rate sirf zyada abuse nahi, behtar reporting aur registration ka nateeja bhi ho sakta hai.

## 19 metros, 7,508 case: shehron ki tasveer

NCRB ke 19 metropolitan shehron mein 2024 mein aise 7,508 POCSO case register hue jinmein victim ladkiyan thi. Inmein se 37.6% akele Delhi (1,489) aur Mumbai (1,331) mein the, uske baad Bengaluru (588), Pune (575) aur Chennai (437) [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Poore desh mein aise 67,809 POCSO case register hue jinmein victim ladkiyan thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]], yaani lagbhag nau mein se aath case in metros ke bahar ke the: chhote shehron, kasbon aur gaon ke. City rates bhi 2011 ki aabadi par tike hain, aur NCRB ke hisaab se unhe state rates se compare nahi kiya ja sakta [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Register hone wala child abuse zyadatar bade shehron ki kahani nahi hai.

## Apne state ke numbers se yeh sawaal poochhiye

Kam number ek sawaal hai, jawab nahi. Apne state ke POCSO figure ko achhi khabar maanne se pehle yeh chaar baatein poochhiye.

- **Yeh count hai ya rate?** Bada state count table mein sabse upar hokar bhi har bachche ke hisaab se bahut kam case register kar sakta hai.
- **Kya report karna aasaan hua?** Bihar mein auraton ke against register hue crime sirf ek saal mein, 2023 se 2024 ke beech, 19.2% badh gaye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB kehta hai ki aisi badhat e-FIR ya women help desk jaisi facilities ke baad bhi aa sakti hai [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. Kisi chup state mein POCSO rate badhe, toh yeh pehla sign ho sakta hai ki bachchon ki baat suni jaane lagi hai.
- **Surveys usi state ke baare mein kya kehte hain?** Child marriage aur ghar ki violence police records ke bahar bhi naapi jaati hai.
- **Kya family bina ladaai ke report kar sakti hai?** July 2024 se police ko complaint register karni hi hogi, chahe crime kahin bhi hua ho; ise "zero FIR" kehte hain. Police complaint electronically bhi le sakti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Kerala ka 48.0 koi sharm ki baat nahi jise chhupaya jaaye. Bihar ka 5.2 koi record nahi jiska jashn manaya jaaye. Asli fikr ki baat woh number hai jise kisi ne kabhi likha hi nahi.

pocso-timeline-2012-to-2026.en:
On 14 November 2012, Children's Day, the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act came into force. It defined a child as anyone under 18 and protected boys and girls alike [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Since then the law around it has been rebuilt in bursts, and the dates show a pattern: Parliament has tended to move after crimes that shook the country, and the Supreme Court has often stepped in after lower courts read the law too narrowly. Our POCSO explainer covers what the Act says today; this is how it got there. It is general information, not legal advice.

## 2012-2013: the Act and the age of consent

POCSO was barely a month old when the Delhi gang rape of December 2012 shook the country. The Justice J.S. Verma Committee, set up that month, reported on 23 January 2013 [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. An ordinance followed on 3 February, and the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 made sex with a girl under 18 rape whether or not she consented [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].

That raised the age of consent in the Penal Code from 16 to 18. The Verma Committee had recommended 16; Parliament chose 18 [[prs-madhavan-sexual-offences-2013]]. But the same Act kept the marital exception for wives aged 15 and above, so until 2017 a husband's sex with his 15-, 16- or 17-year-old wife was not legally rape [[indiacode-cla-2013]]. The law said two things at once: a girl under 18 cannot consent, and a husband needs no consent from a wife who is 15.

## 2017-2019: child brides, the death penalty and special courts

That contradiction was fixed by a petition, not by Parliament. On 11 October 2017, in Independent Thought v. Union of India, the Supreme Court read down the exception: sex with a wife under 18 is rape [[sc-independent-thought-2017]].

The next burst came from the street. Amid national protests over the Kathua and Unnao cases, an ordinance in force from 21 April 2018 made the rape of a girl under 12 punishable with death, raised the minimum sentence for rape from seven to ten years, and gave police two months to finish rape investigations [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]]. A POCSO amendment in force from 16 August 2019, which covers boys too, went further: aggravated penetrative sexual assault on a child now carries at least 20 years, up to imprisonment for the rest of natural life, or death [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Sentences rose quickly; courtrooms took longer. The central scheme for fast-track rape and POCSO courts began on 2 October 2019 [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]].

## 2021-2023: a new scheme, a new helpline system, support for pregnant survivors

In January 2021 the Bombay High Court held that touching a child sexually over her clothes was not "sexual assault" under POCSO without skin-to-skin contact. On 18 November 2021 the Supreme Court set that aside: what matters is sexual intent [[barandbench-satish-2021]].

The machinery changed too. Mission Vatsalya replaced the old Child Protection Services scheme from 2021-22, with costs shared 60:40 between the Centre and most states [[mwcd-mission-vatsalya-guidelines-2022]]. Procedures issued in March 2023 tied the 1098 Child Helpline into the 112 emergency system; 1098 then covered 568 districts and was to reach every district [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].

Pregnant girls were the next gap. In 2022 the Supreme Court observed that because a minor's pregnancy must be reported to the police, a girl and her guardian face a choice: a registered doctor and possible criminal proceedings, or an unqualified provider. It ruled that a doctor ending such a pregnancy need not name the girl in that report if she and her guardian ask [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. On 30 November 2023 the women and child development ministry launched a Nirbhaya Fund scheme for minor girls made pregnant by rape: shelter, medical and maternity care, legal aid, counselling and education support under one roof [[mwcd-pocso-victim-support-scheme-2023]].

## 2024: abuse material renamed, new criminal codes

On 1 July 2024 the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam replaced the Penal Code, the CrPC and the Evidence Act [[air-new-criminal-laws-2024]]. The BNSS gives police two months to complete investigations of penetrative and other sexual assault on children under POCSO [[indiacode-bnss-2023]], but sets no consequence for missing the deadline. The BNS wrote the 2017 judgment into the code: the marital exception now covers only wives aged 18 or older [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

On 23 September 2024 the Supreme Court told every court to stop saying "child pornography" and to use "child sexual exploitation and abuse material" (CSEAM) instead, because such images record real abuse. It urged Parliament to amend POCSO to match. In the same ruling it set aside a Madras High Court order that had quashed such a case, holding that storing or possessing this material with the intent the law specifies is itself an offence under Section 15 of POCSO, even if it is never shared [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]].

## 2025-2026: courts extended, gaps still open

On 10 February 2026, ruling on a High Court order that had reduced the charges in a child sexual assault case from attempt to rape to lesser offences, the Supreme Court said efforts to sensitise judges "have not borne the fruit that was expected". It asked a National Judicial Academy expert committee to draft guidelines [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]]. On 4 November 2026 the Union Cabinet extended the fast-track court scheme to 31 March 2031, with Rs 3,788.04 crore and room for up to 850 courts; 779 were working, 399 of them exclusive POCSO courts [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]].

The promises, next to the record:

| The promise | The record |
|---|---|
| Trial within a year, as far as possible (POCSO, 2012) | 2,86,903 POCSO cases awaiting trial at the end of 2024, 87.7% of those before the courts [[ncrb-cii-2024]] |
| Investigation within two months (2018, now BNSS) | 21,256 POCSO cases still under investigation at the end of 2024; NCRB does not say how many were past two months [[ncrb-cii-2024]] |
| Death penalty and higher minimum sentences (2018, 2019) | Conviction in 32.3% of POCSO trials completed in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]] |
| Fast-track courts (2019) | 2,45,579 rape and POCSO cases pending before them on 31 December 2025 [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]] |

Fourteen years of amendments have made these punishments among the harshest in Indian law. What the timeline does not record is the system meeting its own deadlines, and the next burst should not need a new crime to set it off. Meanwhile, the law requires anyone who knows a child is being sexually abused to report it [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. The 1098 helpline and the 112 emergency number both take that call [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].
pocso-timeline-2012-to-2026.hg:
14 November 2012, yaani Children's Day. Isi din Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act lagu hua. Is kanoon mein 18 saal se kam umar ka har insaan bachcha hai, aur yeh ladke aur ladki dono ko barabar protect karta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Tab se yeh kanoon dheere-dheere nahi, jhatkon mein badla hai. Dates ko order mein padhiye toh ek pattern saaf dikhta hai. Parliament aksar tab hila jab kisi crime ne poore desh ko hila diya. Aur Supreme Court kai baar tab aage aaya jab lower courts ne kanoon ko bahut tang nazar se padha. Aaj POCSO mein kya likha hai, woh hamare POCSO explainer mein hai. Yahan kahani yeh hai ki kanoon yahan tak pahuncha kaise. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## 2012-2013: Act aaya, age of consent 18 hui

POCSO ko lagu hue mushkil se ek mahina hua tha, jab December 2012 ke Delhi gang rape case ne poore desh ko jhakjhor diya. Usi mahine Justice J.S. Verma Committee bani, jisne 23 January 2013 ko apni report di [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. 3 February ko ordinance aaya, aur phir Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 ne saaf likh diya: 18 saal se kam umar ki ladki ke saath sex rape hai, chahe uski consent ho ya na ho [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].

Yaani IPC mein age of consent 16 se badhkar 18 ho gayi. Verma Committee ne 16 ki salah di thi, lekin Parliament ne 18 chuni [[prs-madhavan-sexual-offences-2013]].

Par isi Act mein ek bada chhed reh gaya. Marital exception, yaani shaadi wali chhoot, bachi rahi, aur usmein biwi ki umar 15 saal hi rahi. Matlab 2017 tak, agar pati apni 15, 16 ya 17 saal ki biwi ke saath sex karta, toh kanoon use rape nahi maanta tha [[indiacode-cla-2013]]. Sochiye, kanoon ek saath do baatein keh raha tha: 18 se chhoti ladki consent nahi de sakti, lekin 15 saal ki biwi se pati ko consent lene ki zaroorat hi nahi.

## 2017-2019: child brides, death penalty aur special courts

Yeh ulti baat Parliament ne theek nahi ki. Ise ek petition ne theek karwaya. 11 October 2017 ko Independent Thought v. Union of India case mein Supreme Court ne yeh exception badal diya: ab 18 se kam umar ki biwi ke saath sex bhi rape hai [[sc-independent-thought-2017]].

Agla badlav sadak se aaya. Kathua aur Unnao cases ko lekar desh bhar mein protest ho rahe the. Usi mahaul mein 21 April 2018 se ek ordinance lagu hua. Isne 12 saal se chhoti bachchi ke rape par death penalty tak ki saza jodi, rape ki minimum saza saat saal se badhakar das saal ki, aur police ko rape ki investigation poori karne ke liye do mahine diye [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]].

Phir 16 August 2019 se POCSO mein amendment lagu hua, jo ladkon ko bhi protect karta hai. Ab bachche par aggravated penetrative sexual assault ki saza kam se kam 20 saal hai. Yeh baaki ki poori zindagi ki jail tak ja sakti hai, ya death penalty tak [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Sazaayein toh fatafat badhin, par courtrooms der se aaye. Rape aur POCSO cases ke liye fast-track courts ki central scheme 2 October 2019 ko shuru hui [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]].

## 2021-2023: nayi scheme, naya helpline system, pregnant bachchiyon ke liye support

January 2021 mein Bombay High Court ne kaha ki agar skin-to-skin contact nahi hua, toh kapdon ke upar se bachchi ko galat iraade se chhoona POCSO mein "sexual assault" nahi hai. 18 November 2021 ko Supreme Court ne yeh faisla palat diya. Court ne kaha: asli baat sexual intent hai [[barandbench-satish-2021]].

System ka dhaancha bhi badla. 2021-22 se purani Child Protection Services scheme ki jagah Mission Vatsalya aaya, jiska kharcha Centre aur zyadatar states 60:40 mein baant-te hain [[mwcd-mission-vatsalya-guidelines-2022]]. March 2023 ke naye niyamon ne 1098 Child Helpline ko 112 emergency system se jod diya. Tab 1098 ki service 568 districts mein thi, aur ise har district tak pahunchana tha [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].

Agla gap pregnant bachchiyon ka tha. 2022 mein Supreme Court ne ek kadwa sach maana. Kisi minor ladki ki pregnancy ki khabar police ko dena zaroori hai. Isliye ladki aur uske guardian ke saamne do hi raaste hote hain: registered doctor ke paas jaayein aur criminal case ka khatra uthayein, ya kisi jholachhap ke paas jaayein. Court ne kaha ki abortion karne wale doctor ko us report mein ladki ka naam likhne ki zaroorat nahi, agar ladki aur uske guardian aisa chahein [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

Phir 30 November 2023 ko Ministry of Women and Child Development ne Nirbhaya Fund se ek scheme shuru ki, un minor bachchiyon ke liye jo rape ki wajah se pregnant huin. Ismein rehne ki jagah, ilaaj, delivery tak ki care, legal madad, counselling aur padhai ka support, sab ek hi chhat ke neeche milna hai [[mwcd-pocso-victim-support-scheme-2023]].

## 2024: abuse material ka naya naam, naye criminal codes

1 July 2024 se teen naye kanoon lagu hue: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) aur Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam. Inhone IPC, CrPC aur Evidence Act ki jagah li [[air-new-criminal-laws-2024]]. BNSS kehti hai ki bachchon par penetrative aur doosre sexual assault ki POCSO investigation police do mahine mein poori kare [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Lekin deadline toote toh kya hoga, is par kanoon chup hai. BNS ne 2017 wale judgment ko code mein likh diya: ab marital exception sirf 18 saal ya usse badi biwi par lagu hota hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

23 September 2024 ko Supreme Court ne desh ki har court se kaha ki "child pornography" bolna band karein aur uski jagah "child sexual exploitation and abuse material" (CSEAM) kahein, kyunki aisi tasveerein aur videos kisi asli bachche ke saath hue abuse ka record hain. Court ne Parliament se bhi kaha ki POCSO mein yeh badlav kare. Isi faisle mein court ne Madras High Court ka woh order bhi palat diya jisne aise ek case ko khatam (quash) kar diya tha. Court ne kaha ki kanoon mein likhe iraade ke saath aisa material store karna ya apne paas rakhna bhi POCSO ke Section 15 mein offence hai, chahe use kabhi share na kiya gaya ho [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]].

## 2025-2026: courts ki extension, gaps ab bhi baaki

10 February 2026 ko Supreme Court ke saamne ek High Court ka order tha, jisne bachchon ke sexual assault ke ek case mein "attempt to rape" ka charge ghatakar chhote offences mein badal diya tha. Supreme Court ne maana ki judges ko sensitive banane ki koshishon ka "woh phal nahi mila jiski ummeed thi", aur National Judicial Academy ki ek expert committee se guidelines banane ko kaha [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]].

4 November 2026 ko Union Cabinet ne fast-track courts ki scheme 31 March 2031 tak badha di, Rs 3,788.04 crore ke saath aur 850 tak courts ki gunjaish ke saath. Us waqt 779 courts chal rahe the, jinmein se 399 sirf POCSO cases sunte hain [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]].

Ab vaadon ko record ke bagal mein rakhkar dekhiye:

| Vaada | Record |
|---|---|
| Trial jahan tak ho sake, ek saal mein poora (POCSO, 2012) | 2024 ke end mein 2,86,903 POCSO cases trial ke intezaar mein, yaani courts ke saamne aaye cases ka 87.7% [[ncrb-cii-2024]] |
| Investigation do mahine mein (2018, ab BNSS) | 2024 ke end mein 21,256 POCSO cases ki investigation baaki; NCRB yeh nahi batata ki inmein se kitne do mahine paar kar chuke the [[ncrb-cii-2024]] |
| Death penalty aur lambi minimum saza (2018, 2019) | 2024 mein poore hue POCSO trials mein se sirf 32.3% mein conviction [[ncrb-cii-2024]] |
| Fast-track courts (2019) | 31 December 2025 ko in courts mein rape aur POCSO ke 2,45,579 cases pending [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]] |

Chaudah saal ke amendments ke baad bachchon ke abuse ki sazaayein Indian law ki sabse sakht sazaaon mein gini jaati hain. Lekin is timeline mein kahin nahi dikhta ki system apni hi deadlines par khara utra ho. Agle badlav ke liye kisi naye crime ka intezaar nahi hona chahiye.

Tab tak kanoon har kisi se ek baat kehta hai: agar aapko pata hai ki kisi bachche ka sexual abuse ho raha hai, toh report karna zaroori hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. 1098 helpline aur 112 emergency number, dono par yeh call ki ja sakti hai [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].

pretext-of-marriage-pocso-category.en:
In its Crime in India 2024 report, the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) sorts the year's child-rape cases by who the accused was. One column takes half the table. Of 44,126 cases of penetrative sexual assault registered under the POCSO Act, 22,308, or 50.6%, sit under the heading "Friends/Online-Friends or Live in Partners on Pretext of Marriage" [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That is more than the family members (3,658) and the family friends, neighbours and employers (16,668) put together. The number is easy to quote and impossible to read, because nobody can say what is inside it.

## The column that holds half the cases

NCRB's offender table for POCSO sorts the accused into four groups: family members; family friends, neighbours, employers or other known persons; friends, online friends or live-in partners on pretext of marriage; and unknown or unidentified accused, who account for just 1,492 cases, or 3.4% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The third label bundles at least three relationships: a friend, someone met online, and a partner who promised marriage. The table records nothing about the accused's age, or about how the relationship began. A 19-year-old classmate and a 40-year-old man met on a gaming app land in the same cell.

## Three stories in one number

Consider three hypothetical cases that could all end up in this column. What follows is general information, not legal advice.

**Grooming.** A 14-year-old in Nagpur is befriended online by an adult who spends weeks winning her trust before asking for photos and a meeting. UNICEF warns that online abusers, known or unknown, often first earn the trust of a child or a caregiver and then manipulate the child [[unicef-keeping-children-safe-online-2026]].

**A false promise.** A man promises marriage to a 16-year-old, draws her into a sexual relationship, then disappears. If she were an adult, this might fall under Section 69 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which punishes sex obtained by deceit or a false promise of marriage with up to 10 years in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Police registered 1,325 such cases in the section's first six months, July to December 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Because she is under 18, her consent has no value in law: it is rape under Section 63 of the BNS [[indiacode-bns-2023]], and penetrative sexual assault under POCSO [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

**Two teenagers.** A 17-year-old girl and her 19-year-old boyfriend run away together, and her parents go to the police. The 2013 criminal law amendment raised the age of consent from 16 to 18 [[prs-madhavan-sexual-offences-2013]], and the law makes no exception for partners close in age. If they have had sex, then whatever she says, in law he is an accused and she is a victim. A teenage relationship can also be coercive, and being close in age does not make it safe.

The first fits the usual picture of a child abuser. The third is what people imagine when they call POCSO "misused". The second sits in between, and the column cannot tell any of them apart.

## Why the 16-18 age group dominates

Of 44,567 child victims of penetrative assault in 2024, 23,497, or 52.7%, were aged 16 to 18. Another 16,801 were 12 to 16, and 4,269 were under 12 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Two things may tilt the count towards the top end. Young children rarely disclose abuse, so the under-12 figures are best read as minimums. And part of the bulge at 16 to 18 may come from adolescent relationships and elopements, which NCRB does not count separately.

Here is the gap. NCRB prints the victim's age and the accused's relationship in two separate tables. Nobody reading the published tables can tell how many of the 23,497 older teenagers sit in the 22,308 column, or how many of their accused were teenagers themselves.

## What the blind spot does to two public arguments

Police filed chargesheets in 95.3% of the POCSO cases they disposed of in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In court, the outcome looks very different. Trials ended in 12,672 convictions against 25,476 acquittals and 1,101 discharges, a conviction rate of 32.3%; for penetrative assault alone it was 30.2% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Acquittals can follow a child or family turning hostile, a compromise, a dispute over proof of age, or a case that began as a teenage relationship. The data does not say which. So one side reads 32.3% as proof that the system fails abused children, and another as proof that families use POCSO against their daughters' boyfriends. Both are guessing. Meanwhile every kind of case waits in the same queue: 2,86,903 POCSO cases were pending trial at the end of 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The age-of-consent debate runs on the same blind spot. In 2013 the Verma Committee recommended an age of consent of 16, and Parliament chose 18 [[prs-madhavan-sexual-offences-2013]]. People who want it lowered point to the bulge at 16 to 18; people who want it kept point to grooming. Neither side can show from NCRB's tables how big its problem is.

## What better data would record

This does not need a new survey. It needs better columns. NCRB could:

- split the friends-and-partners column into online contacts, partners close in age, and men who promised marriage;
- record the accused's age band, so that a 19-year-old and a 45-year-old stop sharing a cell;
- cross-tabulate the victim's age with the relationship instead of printing them apart;
- note who filed the complaint, and whether the case began as a missing-person or elopement report;
- publish convictions and acquittals by type of relationship.

Better data would not change the law. POCSO treats everyone under 18 as a child [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], and any sexual act with a child remains an offence whatever both people say. But it would show where adults are targeting children, and where the courts' time is going. Until then, 22,308 is a number everyone quotes and nobody can read.
pretext-of-marriage-pocso-category.hg:
Apni Crime in India 2024 report mein National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) us saal ke child rape cases ko is hisaab se baant-ta hai ki accused kaun tha. Ek column aadhi table le leta hai. POCSO Act ke tahat register hue penetrative sexual assault ke 44,126 cases mein se 22,308, yaani 50.6%, is heading ke neeche hain: "Friends/Online-Friends or Live in Partners on Pretext of Marriage", yaani dost, online dost ya shaadi ke bahane live-in partner [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh family members (3,658) aur family friends, padosi aur employers (16,668) ko milaakar bhi zyada hai. Yeh number quote karna aasaan hai aur padhna namumkin, kyunki koi nahi bata sakta ki iske andar kya hai.

## Woh column jismein aadhe cases hain

POCSO ke liye NCRB ki offender table accused ko chaar groups mein baant-ti hai: family members; family friends, padosi, employers ya koi aur jaan-pehchaan wale; friends, online friends ya shaadi ke bahane live-in partners; aur anjaan ya na pehchaane gaye accused, jinke sirf 1,492 cases hain, yaani 3.4% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Teesra label kam se kam teen tarah ke rishton ko ek saath baandh deta hai: dost, online mila koi insaan, aur shaadi ka waada karne wala partner. Table mein na accused ki umar darj hoti hai, na yeh ki rishta shuru kaise hua. 19 saal ka classmate aur gaming app par mila 40 saal ka aadmi, dono ek hi cell mein aa jaate hain.

## Ek number mein teen kahaniyaan

Teen kaalpanik (hypothetical) cases socho, jo sab isi column mein pahunch sakte hain. Aage jo likha hai woh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahi.

**Grooming.** Nagpur ki ek 14 saal ki ladki se online ek adult dosti karta hai, hafton tak uska bharosa jeet-ta hai, aur phir photos aur milne ki maang karta hai. UNICEF chetaavni deta hai ki online abuser, jaan-pehchaan wale hon ya anjaan, aksar pehle bachche ya uske caregiver ka bharosa jeet-te hain aur phir bachche ko manipulate karte hain [[unicef-keeping-children-safe-online-2026]].

**Jhootha waada.** Ek aadmi 16 saal ki ladki se shaadi ka waada karta hai, use sexual rishte mein le aata hai, phir gaayab ho jaata hai. Agar ladki adult hoti, toh yeh Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 69 mein aa sakta tha, jo dhokhe se ya shaadi ke jhoothe waade se banaye gaye sexual sambandh par 10 saal tak ki jail deta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Is section ke pehle chhah mahinon, yaani July se December 2024 mein, police ne aise 1,325 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Lekin kyunki ladki 18 se kam hai, kanoon mein uski consent ki koi value nahi: yeh BNS ke Section 63 ke tahat rape hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]], aur POCSO ke tahat penetrative sexual assault [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

**Do teenagers.** 17 saal ki ek ladki apne 19 saal ke boyfriend ke saath ghar se chali jaati hai, aur uske mummy-papa police ke paas jaate hain. 2013 ke criminal law amendment ne age of consent 16 se badha kar 18 kar di [[prs-madhavan-sexual-offences-2013]], aur kanoon umar mein kareeb partners ko koi chhoot nahi deta. Agar dono ke beech sex hua hai, toh ladki kuch bhi kahe, kanoon ki nazar mein ladka accused hai aur ladki victim. Teenagers ka rishta bhi zabardasti wala ho sakta hai; umar mein kareeb hona use safe nahi banata.

Pehla case child abuser ki aam tasveer se milta hai. Teesra woh hai jo log sochte hain jab woh kehte hain ki POCSO ka "misuse" ho raha hai. Doosra in dono ke beech mein hai, aur column inmein se kisi ko bhi alag nahi kar sakta.

## 16-18 ki umar ka group sabse bada kyun hai

2024 mein penetrative assault ke 44,567 child victims mein se 23,497, yaani 52.7%, 16 se 18 saal ke the. 16,801 bachche 12 se 16 saal ke the, aur 4,269 bachche 12 se kam umar ke [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Ginti ke upar wali umar ki taraf jhukne ki do wajahein ho sakti hain. Chhote bachche abuse ke baare mein bahut kam bata paate hain, isliye 12 se kam umar ke aankdon ko kam se kam ginti samjho. Aur 16 se 18 wale is ubhaar ka kuch hissa teenagers ke rishton aur ghar se bhaagne (elopement) wale cases se bhi aa sakta hai, jinhe NCRB alag se nahi ginta.

Gap yahin hai. NCRB victim ki umar aur accused ke rishte ko do alag tables mein chhaapta hai. Published tables padh kar koi nahi bata sakta ki 23,497 bade teenagers mein se kitne 22,308 wale column mein hain, ya unke kitne accused khud teenagers the.

## Is blind spot ka do public behason par asar

2024 mein police ne jin POCSO cases ka nipataara kiya, unmein se 95.3% mein chargesheet file ki [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Court mein nateeja bilkul alag dikhta hai. Trials 12,672 convictions, 25,476 acquittals aur 1,101 discharges ke saath khatam hue, yaani conviction rate 32.3%; sirf penetrative assault mein yeh 30.2% tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Acquittal kai wajahon se ho sakta hai: bachcha ya family hostile ho jaaye, samjhauta ho jaaye, umar ke saboot par vivaad ho, ya case teenagers ke rishte se shuru hua ho. Data yeh nahi batata ki kis case mein kaun si wajah thi. Isliye ek paksh 32.3% ko is baat ka saboot maanta hai ki system abuse jhelne wale bachchon ko fail kar raha hai, aur doosra paksh ise is baat ka saboot ki familiyaan apni betiyon ke boyfriends ke khilaaf POCSO ka istemaal karti hain. Dono sirf andaaza laga rahe hain. Is beech har tarah ka case ek hi line mein intezaar karta hai: 2024 ke aakhir tak 2,86,903 POCSO cases trial ke intezaar mein the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Age of consent ki behas bhi isi blind spot par chalti hai. 2013 mein Verma Committee ne age of consent 16 rakhne ki sifarish ki thi, aur Parliament ne 18 chuni [[prs-madhavan-sexual-offences-2013]]. Jo log ise ghatana chahte hain, woh 16 se 18 wale ubhaar ki taraf ishaara karte hain; jo ise 18 hi rakhna chahte hain, woh grooming ki taraf. Koi bhi paksh NCRB ki tables se yeh nahi dikha sakta ki uski chinta kitni badi hai.

## Behtar data kya darj karega

Iske liye naya survey nahi, behtar columns chahiye. NCRB yeh kar sakta hai:

- friends aur partners wale column ko alag-alag hisson mein baante: online contacts, umar mein kareeb partners, aur shaadi ka waada karne wale mard;
- accused ki umar ka band darj kare, taaki 19 saal ka ladka aur 45 saal ka aadmi ek hi cell mein na rahein;
- victim ki umar aur rishte ko alag-alag chhaapne ki jagah ek saath (cross-tabulate karke) dikhaye;
- yeh likhe ki complaint kisne ki, aur kya case missing-person ya ghar se bhaagne ki report se shuru hua;
- rishte ke type ke hisaab se convictions aur acquittals publish kare.

Behtar data se kanoon nahi badlega. POCSO 18 se kam umar ke har insaan ko child maanta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], aur child ke saath koi bhi sexual act jurm hi rahega, chahe dono kuch bhi kahein. Lekin isse pata chalega ki adults bachchon ko kahan nishaana bana rahe hain, aur courts ka waqt kahan ja raha hai. Tab tak 22,308 ek aisa number hai jise sab quote karte hain aur koi padh nahi paata.

schools-hostels-homes-abuse-duty.en:
Imagine a 13-year-old boy at a residential school in Dehradun. He tells his house warden that the sports coach keeps him back alone after practice and touches him in ways that frighten him. The warden tells the principal. The principal calls in the coach, "warns" him, and asks the warden to stay quiet until admissions are over. Under the POCSO Act, both adults have now broken the law, the principal more seriously: the head of an institution who fails to report abuse by someone working under them faces up to 1 year in jail and a fine [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. What follows is general information, not legal advice.

## Trust plus access: teachers, wardens, coaches and carers

Institutions give some adults daily, unsupervised access to children and power over them: marks, team selection, hostel privileges, sometimes a child's place to live. That is what grooming needs. The child-protection nonprofit Darkness to Light lists its red flags as special attention to one child, gifts, touching or hugging, acting as a sympathetic listener, offering to help the family, and reaching the child through the internet [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. In a school they look like a "favourite student", free extra coaching, late-night messages or an offer to help with fees.

Police data hides this group. NCRB's table of who the accused was in child-rape cases has no row for teachers, wardens or carers. They fall into a mixed column of "family friends, neighbours, employers or other known persons", which held 16,668 of 2024's 44,126 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Nobody can tell from it how many involved an institution's staff.

## The law: an aggravated offence and a duty to report

Under Section 64(2)(f) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), rape by a relative, guardian or teacher, or by anyone in a position of trust or authority, carries 10 years up to imprisonment for the rest of natural life [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Under POCSO, which protects boys and girls alike, penetrative assault on a child under 16 carries at least 20 years [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Anyone who knows or suspects that a child sexual offence has been, or is likely to be, committed must tell the Special Juvenile Police Unit or the local police. Failing to report can mean up to six months in jail, a fine or both; for the head of an institution who fails to report an offence by a subordinate, up to one year and a fine [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]].

An internal inquiry, a quiet transfer or a resignation does not replace that report. In the Just Rights for Children Alliance judgment of 23 September 2024, the Supreme Court told courts not to show leniency to schools, children's homes, shelter homes, hostels and similar institutions that fail to report [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]].

## Children away from home: what the Bihar audit showed

Children who live in an institution have no parent at the gate each evening. A social audit of Bihar's children's homes by the Tata Institute of Social Sciences, done for the state government and submitted in April 2018, flagged sexual abuse at several institutions, including a state-funded girls' shelter home in Muzaffarpur [[newslaundry-tiss-audit-bihar-2018]]. The audit revealed the sexual abuse of 34 minor girls at that home [[sc-handbook-child-rights-2025]]. On 20 January 2020 a POCSO court at Saket in Delhi, where the Supreme Court had moved the trial, convicted 19 of the 20 accused; 11 were later sentenced to life imprisonment [[scconline-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]].

The girls were in the state's own care, and it took an outside audit to bring the abuse to light. Today Mission Vatsalya, the Centre's child-protection scheme since 2021-22, funds child care institutions alongside Child Welfare Committees and District Child Protection Units [[mwcd-mission-vatsalya-guidelines-2022]]. Paper inspections are no substitute for outsiders who talk to children.

Disabled children face a higher wall. Under Section 92(d) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, anyone in a position to dominate the will of a disabled child or woman who uses it to exploit her sexually faces six months to five years in prison and a fine; rape itself is punished under the BNS [[gazette-rpwd-act-2016]]. When a disabled survivor reports a sexual offence, police must record the complaint at her home or a place she chooses, with an interpreter or special educator, on video [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## What a real child-protection policy contains

Ask your child's school, hostel, coaching centre or children's home for its written child-protection policy. A serious one covers:

- **Who reports, and to whom.** A named person who informs the police the same day, not a committee that decides whether to.
- **Access.** No one-to-one time behind closed doors; coaching, transport and hostel night duty arranged so another adult can see.
- **Contact.** No private social-media chats or late-night messages between staff and individual children.
- **Checks.** Background and police verification for every staff member, including drivers, guards and cooks.
- **The accused.** Kept away from children while the police investigate, just as POCSO requires the police to keep a child away from the accused [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].
- **Privacy.** The child's name, photo and class never shared, including in staff or parents' WhatsApp groups. POCSO bars any media report that reveals a child victim's name, school or family details [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].
- **Training.** Staff taught the grooming signs; children told whom they can tell.

If an institution cannot show you this, ask why.

## If the institution buries a complaint

You do not need the institution's permission, or its inquiry, to go to the police. Any police station must record a complaint wherever the offence happened (a Zero FIR), it can be sent electronically, and you are entitled to a free copy [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Call 1098, the Child Helpline [[wcd-childline]], or 112 if a child is in danger now.

Refusing to record it is itself an offence: up to six months in prison under POCSO [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], and six months to two years under Section 199 of the BNS for a police officer who fails to record a complaint of rape or sexual assault [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. In your complaint, name the head who knew and did nothing; Section 21 of POCSO makes that an offence too. For a children's home, write to the district's Child Welfare Committee as well.

Keep a record of who you told, when, and how they replied. Ask for the accused to be moved, not your child. A child who reported abuse should not lose a school, a team or a home for telling the truth.
schools-hostels-homes-abuse-duty.hg:
Sochiye, Dehradun ke ek residential school mein 13 saal ka ek ladka. Woh apne house warden ko batata hai ki sports coach practice ke baad use akele rok leta hai aur aise chhoota hai ki use darr lagta hai. Warden yeh baat principal ko batata hai. Principal coach ko bulata hai, use "warning" deta hai, aur warden se kehta hai ki admissions khatam hone tak chup rahe. POCSO Act ke tahat, dono adults ab law tod chuke hain, aur principal ne zyada gambhir roop se: jo institution head apne neeche kaam karne wale kisi insaan ka abuse report nahi karta, use 1 saal tak ki jail aur fine ho sakta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Aage jo likha hai, woh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Trust aur access: teachers, wardens, coaches aur carers

Institutions kuch adults ko bachchon tak roz ka, bina nigrani ka access dete hain, aur un par power bhi: marks, team selection, hostel ki suvidhaayein, aur kabhi-kabhi bachche ke rehne ki jagah. Grooming ko yahi chahiye. Child protection par kaam karne wali nonprofit Darkness to Light iske red flags yeh batati hai: kisi ek bachche par khaas dhyaan, gifts, chhoona ya gale lagana, hamdard sunne wala banna, family ki madad ki offer, aur internet ke zariye bachche tak pahunchna [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. School mein yeh "favourite student", free extra coaching, der raat ke messages ya fees mein madad ki offer jaise dikhte hain.

Police data is group ko chhupa deta hai. Child rape cases mein accused kaun tha, is par NCRB ki table mein teachers, wardens ya carers ki koi row nahi hai. Woh "family friends, padosi, employer ya doosre jaan-pehchaan wale" ke mixed column mein chale jaate hain, jisme 2024 ke 44,126 cases mein se 16,668 the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Isse koi nahi bata sakta ki inmein se kitne cases mein kisi institution ka staff shaamil tha.

## Law: aggravated offence aur report karne ki duty

Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 64(2)(f) ke tahat, kisi rishtedaar, guardian ya teacher ka, ya trust ya authority ki position wale kisi bhi insaan ka kiya rape 10 saal se lekar baaki ki poori zindagi ki jail tak ki saza laata hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. POCSO ladkon aur ladkiyon dono ko barabar protect karta hai, aur iske tahat 16 saal se kam umar ke bachche par penetrative assault ki saza kam se kam 20 saal hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Jise bhi pata ho ya shak ho ki kisi bachche ke khilaaf sexual offence hua hai, ya hone wala hai, use Special Juvenile Police Unit ya local police ko batana hoga. Report na karne par 6 mahine tak ki jail, fine ya dono ho sakte hain; aur jo institution head apne subordinate ke offence ko report nahi karta, use 1 saal tak ki jail aur fine [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]].

Internal inquiry, chupchaap transfer ya resignation us report ki jagah nahi le sakte. 23 September 2024 ke Just Rights for Children Alliance judgment mein Supreme Court ne courts se kaha ki jo schools, children's homes, shelter homes, hostels aur aise doosre institutions report nahi karte, un par narmi na dikhayein [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]].
